# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

## 0.1.0-beta.65 (2026-11-27)

- An agent can turn Jev off for its own web tools: `jev: "off"` on `web_search` or `web_fetch` in its `definition.tool_settings` turns it off for both, as `AGENTRUN_WEB_JEV_OFF=1` does for every agent. Its runs' planes carry it at every launch and claim, and no TypeSafe key is handed. `off` is the one value; the server's own tool settings refuse it. The console's agent editor has a Jev switch beside the web tools. <!-- changes/agent-jev-off.md -->
- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) keeps each workspace of the backend in front of it to its own agents, runs and imported template packages. The backend names the workspace in the `AgentRun-Workspace` header with a server token: another workspace's row answers the same `404` as a missing one, lists hold the workspace's rows alone, what the request makes is stamped with it, and an `Idempotency-Key` is the workspace's own. A request in a workspace is served only the run, agent and template routes the serve README's API-only section lists (`403 not_scoped` for any other). `AGENTRUN_WORKSPACE_TOKENS` names the tokens that must always send the header. `GET /v2/capabilities` answers `features.workspaces` (the header, whether this server enforces it, and the operations a scoped request is served), so a proxy can refuse to forward to a server that does not keep workspaces apart. The header is `400` on any other server or credential, and a request without it is served as before. `agentrun-serve workspace-backfill FILE [--apply]` puts agents made earlier in a workspace (on SQLite it adds the workspace columns itself; a Postgres store below migration 0033 is refused, exit 2, never migrated). The store gains a nullable `workspace` on agents, runs and imported templates (Postgres migration 0033, additive: runners of the earlier build keep running). <!-- changes/serve-workspace-tenancy.md -->
- `GET /v2/settings/prices` reads the prices this server meters computer and browser time at, from the same settings its meters read: each computer provider's price per vCPU-second, GiB-second of memory, GB-month of disk and GPU-second of each GPU type a setting names, and each browser provider's price an hour with its billing minimum. Each price is a decimal string with its source: `setting` (the operator's `AGENTRUN_COMPUTE_USD_PER_*` or `AGENTRUN_BROWSER_USD_PER_HOUR_*`), `list` (a built-in list price, or $0 for a provider that bills nothing) or `unpriced` (none set, or a setting that is not a plain decimal). A caller can show estimates and turn a budget of its own into the server's figures. <!-- changes/settings-prices-read.md -->
- Under a recipe that names AgentRun's MCP server per start (`ar` and 6 random hex digits: Cursor's, Antigravity's, any with the title tie), a recipe that lists the MCP configs its agent reads (`mcpConfigs`, new) now has a run keep the name its first start minted and give it again at each later start. Before, a resumed Cursor run asked the host's gate for every call of AgentRun's own tools: Cursor keeps, with its session, the name it was first given and titled the call under it, which the new start no longer spelled, so the title tie read it as another server's. `mcpConfigs` lists the MCP config files the agent reads (`~/path` or `$HOME/path` in its HOME, any other path in its work directory; Cursor's: `~/.cursor/mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`). A recipe that lists none (Antigravity's) still names the server afresh at each start. One that declares a server under the run's name has that name refused at the start: AgentRun's server gets a fresh name, kept from then on, the run gets a notice naming the file, and a call titled under the old name goes to the host's gate as that server's. A config that is no regular file, too large to read (over 1 MiB) or fails to read, or one that does not parse as JSON but names the run's server or holds a `\u` escape, counts as declaring it. The file is never edited. A run that began before this change keeps no name yet: its first start after it mints one, and a resumed Cursor session's calls under the old name ask the gate for the rest of that session. Owner recipes in serve take `mcpConfigs` too. Recipes on the fixed `agentrun` name (Goose's) are unchanged. <!-- changes/acp-run-server-name.md -->

  A proxy-billed recipe with the title tie (which takes Goose's facts) now finds its tools in meta `tools_call` under the run's own server name (`ar3f12ab__look_up`); before, only `agentrun__` names were read as AgentRun's.
- A run whose agent called its learned workflow itself, and that the workflow answered or handed back, now names the revision that ran: `workflow.digest` on GET /runs/{id} and each runs list row, `runs[].digest` on GET /agents/{agent_id}/learning/cost, and `workflow_digest` on its grade. Before, only a run the platform served first did, so such a run read `digest: null` though its `workflow_calls[].digest` named the revision, took no share of that revision's compile and check spend, and was never the run where the workflow took over. It now counts as a served run of that revision wherever a platform-served run does: its share of the spend, the cost page's takeover, and the audit's served-run counts and grade rows. A connected agent's run, whose events keep no call record, still names no digest. <!-- changes/agent-called-run-keeps-digest.md -->
- The console's Claude login row: Turn on, where the login then reads not signed in (after Sign out, say) and the CLI's sign-in can start on this machine, starts that sign-in in the same press, so the browser opens as it did before Sign out existed. A start the server refuses leaves the row on, with its words; a sign-in that already waits (another tab started it) is left alone. Check again reads "Checking…" while it asks and then says "Checked just now.", so a check that finds nothing new still shows it ran. <!-- changes/claude-turn-on-starts-sign-in.md -->
- The console says Decision for an agent New agent's Decision made: its page's Kind and its card read "decision", and New agent's panel and the editor's field are titled Decision, wherever the agent's workflow decides and runs no agent or code (read from the definition; nothing new is stored). An archived agent's card in the Archived list and its page carry a labeled Unarchive. On an agent's page in a narrower window, the Run box's Attach files drop zone keeps its width and "Run with your coding agent" wraps under it, instead of squeezing its words to one a line. <!-- changes/console-decision-unarchive-dropzone.md -->
- A ChatGPT renewal that a stop cuts off after it took its lease no longer hands out the old sign-in's token when the owner signed in again or out meanwhile: the new sign-in's token is sent, or the run is told it is signed out. A run handed back during a runner's stop now ends on a stop or cancel a person sent before that no delivery had passed on yet, at this close, instead of resuming on the next start only to end there. The README says what a second stop signal does while a runner closes, and that a close that never ends needs SIGKILL. <!-- changes/plan-stop-p3s.md -->
- A saved key that holds a "+" (a base64 key body, for one) is now withheld when a run prints it split into string literals joined by "+" (`"ab" + "cd+ef"`), double- or single-quoted, also after prose with an apostrophe ("Here's the key:"); before, it showed on the run's view, its Timeline, the event stream, its export and to an eval's grader. <!-- changes/redact-plus-in-joined-literals.md -->
- A learning run that a follow-up opened again now counts the follow-up's turns as the job's. Its `cost.usd` is everything the run spent except each round's end-of-run turn, its `cost.tools_usd` holds the follow-up's paid calls (`toolsusd/3`), and `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage` serves its `tools`, `browser_time` and other lines (`runusage/5`) instead of `lines: null` with `reason: "reopened"`. The lines at each end are cumulative: they hold the last end's lines and what the follow-up added, so a backend that bills each end bills the difference. Before, `usd` stayed at the first round's figure, `tools_usd` was null and the follow-up's spend was booked as learning (`followup_usd`), so a backend billing the job charged nothing for a follow-up's paid tools. `followup_usd` now holds only end-of-run spend beyond the compile turns. A reopened run's ledger row gets the new figure at its next end; a run that already ended keeps the row it has. <!-- changes/reopened-run-follow-up-is-the-job.md -->
- Checking whether a run's learning round is still going now reads only the newest end in the run's journal: its job's end kept for the look-back, or the run's last end. A claim that waits on another run's round checks it about every 2 s, and a run of a learning agent checks each of its agent's steered running runs as it starts. Before, each check read the run's whole journal, so a long run cost more with every check. The answer is unchanged. <!-- changes/round-open-reads-newest-end.md -->
- A new run now waits on another run's correction only while that run's learning step runs after its job (the compile turn after a follow-up, a grade's words, or a message a person sent during the run's first job), not during the person's follow-up turn itself. A run launched while a follow-up turn is still running starts from its agent's learning as it is then, with no wait. A run launched once the corrected run reads `completed` still waits for the correction, as before, also when a person sends that run another message while its learning step runs (the step still merges the correction first). When the runner loses the run's claim or shuts down during the wait, the wait ends at once and the runner starts nothing, so another runner takes the run over. A run waits at any claim before its first turn: one handed back before that turn waits and reads its agent's learning again on its next claim. A claim that cannot read the run's own row or journal before the wait hands the run back to be tried again, instead of failing it or starting without the wait. The wait polls less often the longer it lasts (250 ms, doubling to 2 s), and starting a learning run reads the commands of the agent's running runs in one query per 50 runs. <!-- changes/seed-wait-learning-end-only.md -->
- Imports now skip hidden paths. A template import from a GitHub source (`POST /v2/templates/import` with `source`) no longer stores a hidden file or folder of the package, such as a committed `.env` or a tool's `.cache/`, the same as an upload. Before, the import kept such a file in the stored package, though no part of the server read it. Now it is skipped unread: never counted against the import's file and byte limits, never shown by a dry run, never stored. A hidden symbolic or hard link still refuses the import (422). The stored template's id and `sha` (the commit read) mean what they did. A package stored before this change keeps any hidden file until it is imported again or deleted. <!-- changes/serve-import-skips-hidden.md -->
- A template eval's link check now counts the links a web call's text holds: those in a fetched part's text (a part past the first lists no links of its own), in each chunk an objective found, and in a native search's text. Before, a link the model read there and cited was reported as `no matching call`. Each `web_search` and `web_fetch` call a run's Web answers also writes one `web_receipt` line to the server's log: `op`, the `provider` that answered, `tries` (each provider asked as `provider:outcome`, a failure's code after a `/`), the `classifier` (`off`, or `ran` or `not_run` with `classifier_in`, `classifier_kept`, `classifier_model` and any error code or skip reason) and `cost_usd`, so the provider chain and Jev's ranking can be audited from the log. The line never holds the URL, the objective or queries, a page's text, an error's message or a key. <!-- changes/serve-web-receipts.md -->
- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) serves `GET /v2/settings/prices` with its token, so the backend in front of it can read the prices its meters use and bound a run's budget in the server's figures before launch. A request without the token is still 401. The read returns this server's settings; a runner started separately meters at the prices in its own environment. <!-- changes/settings-prices-api-only.md -->
- `agentrun template install SOURCE` now works on a server that takes uploads only. Such a server refuses a GitHub source: serve in its API-only profile (422 `input_invalid`, field `source`, reason `not_allowed`) or a server that answers 422 `files_only`. Before, the command printed that refusal and stopped. Now it reads the package from GitHub itself, anonymously, at the commit the ref points to (serve's own reader, exported as `@parcha/agentrun-serve/template-source`). It then uploads the package's folder (`{files}`, as `agentrun deploy DIR` sends one), the same files serve's own import of the source keeps, so the server checks the same package and refuses what that import refuses. A package whose agent.md names another folder than the source's is refused before anything is uploaded, as that import refuses it (an upload is named by its agent.md, so it would otherwise replace an upload of that name). Hidden files and folders are left out, as an upload never keeps them. `--dry-run` is passed through, and the reader keeps serve's import limits. An upload keeps no publisher, so on that path every install needs `--trust` unless it is a dry run, and without it nothing is read. The output's `sha` is the commit that was read, `source` is pinned to it, `publisher` is null, and stderr says the command read GitHub itself. Every other answer is unchanged: a server that takes the source still gets one request, keeps the publisher's trust and pins the commit itself. <!-- changes/template-install-upload-only.md -->
- A pi session opened again in a turn now reads the turn back from its conversation before a call the model made runs, not after: a pi-native tool (bash, web_fetch, a subagent) whose read fails is blocked before it does anything, where before it ran and its result was replaced by an error, inviting the model to run it again. <!-- changes/turn-budget-read-before-call.md -->
  - A session that read its own answer never reads the turn back, so a store that cannot read blocks none of its calls.
  - A call pi reruns after a crash (its intent stored, so the read happens after it) keeps what it did when the read fails, held to the window's bound alone, instead of an error.
  - The words a call gets when its turn could not be read are plain: the store's own error is no longer in the model's transcript. A host tool's call pi runs again after a crash, whose read fails before it runs, says an earlier attempt of it may already have taken effect, never that nothing was done.
  - A tool that nests calls (a code-mode script) whose result's length the session's journal could not keep halts its drive, as an effect's failure does, so the harness is never handed that result.

## 0.1.0-beta.64 (2026-11-26)

**Breaking:**

- A correction appended to an agent's `corrections.md` that would take the file past its cap now drops the oldest lines instead of being refused. If you relied on old corrections staying until an owner removed them, keep your own copy. <!-- changes/corrections-newest-wins.md -->
  The cap is now 8192 bytes (was 2048), and the newest correction always reaches the next run's `# Learned`. The run's learning (`GET /runs/{id}/learning`) gives the number of lines dropped in a new `dropped_lines` field, and its `detail` says it too. A correction whose own line is over 8192 bytes is still refused, and so is an owner's whole-file `PUT .../learning/corrections` over the cap: nothing is dropped for an edit. Before this, one follow-up correction wrapped the way a host wraps it (about 2 KB) filled the file, and every later one was dropped with `too_large`.
- On a server with no Docker box whose runner has no shell (Mode 1), a template update's `dry_run` is now refused for its place as its apply is. That is the `dry_run` of an apply with `agent_id`, the one `agentrun deploy` sends once its lock names the agent. Before, such a plan answered `revise`, `agentrun deploy` printed `~ agent ... revise` and asked to confirm, and the apply then failed with `422` `name a box`. The plan now checks the revision the update would write, so it is refused in the same field (`definition.place`), reason and words as the apply, and `agentrun deploy` stops at the preview. An example is a package that now names `bash`, for an agent with no place. A `dry_run` that lacks keys or a required MCP server lists them in its plan, as before, and checks the place only once they are there. That is the order the apply refuses in: `409` for the keys, then `422` for the place. Before, a fresh plan with keys missing and no place answered `422` for the place first. <!-- changes/no-box-update-plan.md -->

  Upgrading: an update of an agent made earlier keeps its place. An apply with `agent_id` of a package that names no `tools` writes the agent's revision with no tools, on the runner it had, where a fresh apply of the same package is refused.

**Changes:**

- Wrapped has a leak receipt, and the console draws it once the person turns it on. The import already cuts keys and tokens out of what it keeps of each session: the key-shaped values of its environment, the keys saved on the server, and keys of a format secretlint finds. It now keeps on each run how many distinct keys it cut from that run, as a number alone. `GET /v2/wrapped` answers `secrets` by adding up the year's runs from the store: `runs` counted, `runs_holding` (those that held a key) and `removed` (the keys cut, each once a run). <!-- changes/wrapped-leak-receipt.md -->
  - `secrets` is null when no run of the year was counted. Only runs imported here count: a session left out of the import, or imported before this version, is not in it.
  - The card is off until the person checks "Show the leak receipt" on the Wrapped page, and the page offers it only for a year whose keys were counted. It shows the keys cut, the sessions that held one and the sessions checked. It never shows a key, its shape or where it was.
  - A password typed in a command, with no known key format, is not in the count.
- On Goose and Cursor, a permission request for a tool the agent is not given is now refused at once, and the run goes on. Before, the request went to the host's gate like any other, and since there is no grant for a person to approve, the run parked (`parked`, with no summary) on a question nobody could answer usefully. Now the ACP adapter answers it `reject_once` without asking the gate or journaling it, and the run's timeline gets a line saying `tool "<name>" isn't granted to this agent`. ACP's permission answer carries no words, so the agent reads its own vendor's refusal; the line is for the person. A run that parked on such a request before this change is answered the same way when it resumes: the waiting request gets a settled deny in those words, the agent's recovery note says it was refused with no person asked, and the gate is not asked. Under Cursor's and agy's recipes, which give our server a new name at each start, the waiting request's title is read against the name of the start that asked, which the adapter now records with it; a request recorded without that name still goes to the gate, since its title cannot be tied to a server of ours. An agent that calls such a tool without asking now gets those same words from the adapter's MCP server, which said `unknown tool: <name>` before. A tool the agent is given whose setting asks (a write behind the gate) still asks a person and parks as before, and a native call with effects of its own (a shell, an edit) still goes to the gate whatever its title says. claude-agent, codex and pi never asked about such a tool: their tool bridge answers a call of a tool it does not hold `unknown tool: <name>` before the gate. serve's computer claim drops its `refuseKind` hook, which nothing called once every CLI harness got the browser. <!-- changes/acp-ungranted-tool-refused.md -->
- On a Linux desktop, the check of whether computerd's own user could change an app's desktop file asks the kernel too (`faccessat2` as the effective user, no link followed) for each folder on the way and for the file, beside the mode bits, so an ACL entry or a FUSE file system's own rule that lets the user write is seen. `apps.launch` names a refused desktop file from that one check, by the id asked for, and no longer opens every desktop file again to find it: that open followed links and waited forever on a named pipe called `*.desktop`. A refused file is never read, so the name or program it gives finds no app: asked by that name, `apps.launch` answers `not_found`, and by its id, `denied`. `apps.terminate` ends an app this computerd launched though its desktop file is refused now, as when a file of its id was written ahead of it since; before, it answered `denied` and the app ran on to the computer's end. The computer wire spec says that `apps.launch` answers `denied` for such an app and that `apps.list` leaves it out. A correction to the previous release's note on desktop files: refusing an app whose desktop file computerd's own user could change closes the desktop-file route only, not `write` plus apps as a whole. An app reads its config from the user's home, which `write` reaches, so an agent given both can still reach a shell through an app it opens, and the remedy stays granting no apps on such a desktop. The words every offer of a computer's ops carries (`GUI_REACH`), the serve README and the desktop kind skill say that where `write` is granted, `apps.open` reaches what a shell does with or without a URL or a path, since an app reads its config from the user's home. <!-- changes/apps-launch-refusal-kernel-check.md -->
- On a Mode 2 server whose Archil region has no serverless exec (`gcp-us-central1`), the refusal of an agent with `bash` (or another shell tool) and no computer now opens with the rule: "bash needs a box (a sandbox computer): this server's Archil region gcp-us-central1 has no serverless exec, …". Before, it opened "name a sandbox computer: …". The words are the same at its save, at `agentrun deploy`, at each run of one saved before (`409 agent_not_runnable`) and in `capabilities.places.default_reason`. The field, reason and fix are unchanged. The serve and CLI READMEs now say where `bash` runs on such a region: nowhere without a box. Give the agent a sandbox computer, or leave `bash` out of its tools. <!-- changes/archil-no-exec-bash-needs-a-box.md -->
- A learned workflow call's `usd` in a run's `workflow_calls` no longer counts a CLI's own side request on another model (its title or summary helper) booked inside the call's window. That request was already no proof the call spent; now it is no part of the call's price either. <!-- changes/call-cost-side-request.md -->
- On an Archil region with no serverless exec, a run's checkout (`checkout: pull_request` or `checkout: repository`) is made in its computer only when the claim started that computer. A sandbox kept through a wait and taken back, the agent's own persistent computer and a paired computer may already have run the agent's code, so the server hands them no GitHub token: the run gets no `repo/` folder, and it and its timeline are told why up front. A correction to the previous release's note on that checkout: the GitHub App's token is never in the checkout's argv or the environment it starts with; only the fetch's git processes carry it. Every checkout's git, on every mode, now puts the App's Authorization header in the environment of the calls that reach GitHub alone (the fetches, `ls-remote`), never in the script's or any other git call's, copies no template at `git init`, runs no hook, and finds `sh`, `git` and the rest in `/usr/bin` and `/bin` before any other folder. An attached computer's exec whose stdin write fails with an error other than a closed input now closes that stdin, so the program answers at once instead of at the call's deadline. <!-- changes/checkout-fresh-computer-only.md -->
- A CLI harness run that sends no model key (one on a `--faux` start, or one pinned to the faux model) no longer reads the Claude login setting at its claim, nor asks its runner for the login when it runs in a process of its own. Before, only a held run skipped that read. The earlier notes for held and keyless runs said a held Cursor run's key is "never decrypted" and that such runs open no saved model key: the claim still decrypts every sealed secret into the run's redactors, to scrub it from the run's output, but it never reads one for the run or lays it on the run. <!-- changes/cli-keyless-run-no-login-ask.md -->
- A run that sends no model key (held because its model can't run, on a `--faux` start, or pinned to the faux model) now opens no saved key it never sends for anything it lays, hands on or sends, including runs that run inside the runner (the run's redactor still loads the server's saved secrets, so an echo of one is cut from its records). On a `--faux` start, a subagent, learned-workflow or grader tier no longer opens any saved key, and neither does an SDK run's compile turn; that turn is also no longer skipped for want of a gateway key, since the faux model sends none. A run's own model key handed at its start is never read out of its launch, held or sent for a held run or one on a `--faux` start. A run pinned to the faux model keeps it, and a workflow pinned to it is still laid its saved model keys: its subagent tiers, learned workflows and model nodes run on the runner's models. The check that a server holds a gateway key now reads that key alone. A run with decision nodes opens the gateway's key for them only when its decisions would use it. A run's Composio connected-account check now asks Composio nothing for a blank user, which it treats as having no account. <!-- changes/keyless-run-in-runner.md -->
- A tool with a `file` setting now files more of what its server sends, and its summary says more about errors without showing their words. <!-- changes/mcp-filed-results-followup.md -->
  - A protocol-level error is filed like any other answer. This covers a JSON-RPC error, or an HTTP error the client throws. The tool's result is the same summary with `isError: true`. Before, the result showed the first 300 characters of the server's message.
  - An error answer's summary ends with one more line, built from the error's structure and never from its words. The line gives the HTTP status, the JSON-RPC code, and when to retry. The retry time comes from a `retry_after`, `retryAfter`, `retry_after_seconds`, `retry_after_ms` or `retryAfterMs` field of a JSON error (at its top, in its `error` or `data`, or in a JSON-RPC error's `data`), or from the Retry-After header, which wins when both are given. An error answer (`isError: true`) arrives over HTTP 200, so its line names no status, but it still takes the Retry-After of the response that carried it. The status and the Retry-After are the call's own response's, also when other calls to the same server run at the same time. A 429 or 503 with no retry time says to retry later. When the error has none of these, as with a plain-text error, the line says `Error: no status or retry time given.`
  - The tool gate now keeps the agent's own file tools, `web_save` and `browser_upload` out of the folder. 0.1.0-beta.60's notes said the model's own `read`, `grep`, `ls` and `bash` could still open it. Now the gate refuses a call whose path is in a folder one of the agent's `file` settings names, or under it, for these tools: the agent's own `read`, `write` and `edit` (claude-agent's `Read`, `Write` and `Edit` too, a computer script's file ops, and a screenshot's `save_as`), `web_save` (where it saves) and `browser_upload`. The error names the setting. The check reads the path as given and as pi's file tools take it, with one leading `@` dropped, so `@stripe/pages/a.json` is refused. It resolves `./` and `..` against every name the run's file tools take for its folder: its full path, a computer's `/workspace`, and a CLI harness's working folder. It compares each segment as a disk that folds names would, so on a local macOS run `Stripe/Pages/a.json`, a fullwidth spelling, or one with a zero-width or other ignorable character is refused too. It reads no file, so it doesn't follow links.
  - On a computer that mounts the run's folder, while a folder is filed, a script's file ops (`files.read`, `files.list`, `files.write` and `files.stat`) must name a path inside `/workspace`. Any other path is refused, with an error saying a run with a filed folder keeps a script's file ops in `/workspace`. The computer reaches the folder by names no check of the words can follow, such as `/proc/self/root/workspace/...`, `/proc/self/cwd/...` and `/dev/fd/3/...`, so a list of bad paths can't hold. The cost: while a folder is filed, a script's file ops can't read or write the rest of the computer's disk, such as its `Downloads` folder. A computer that doesn't mount the run's folder, and a run with no filed folder, are unchanged. Opening the file on the computer beneath `/workspace` with links refused (`openat2` with `RESOLVE_BENEATH` and `RESOLVE_NO_MAGICLINKS`) is a follow-up.
  - Outside the gate: a tool not on that list, such as `browser_downloads`, which writes into `downloads/`; the computer's screen (input on a terminal app or a file manager, and `apps.open` with a path or a `file://` URL); a link already inside `/workspace`, which a script's file op follows; and a harness's own file reads that never ask the host, such as Cursor's. What still holds from beta.60: `bash`, on the runner or a computer, is not gated by path, so a command, a link it makes, or any program the run starts can still open the folder. Only `bash` set to `deny` stops this: a script's `shell.run` and `processes.start` follow bash's setting, not whether `bash` is among the agent's tools. A template that must keep the model off the answers sets `bash` to `deny`, and gives the run no desktop or sets the desktop kind to `deny`, or runs its skill's code where the model can't read the output. A desktop whose model is handed no screen tools (`surface: code`) still gives its scripts `apps.open` and input ops.
  - The shape names a key only when it reads as a plain name: lowercase words joined by `_` (`has_more`), or camelCase (`pageInfo`), with any leading `_`, at most 32 characters. Keys with digits or capitals after a prefix (`cus_NffrFeUfNV2Hib`, `txn_1Q0001`) and all-capitals keys are counted instead. A key that is data but looks like a plain word, such as a username like `marisol_q`, is still named.

  Upgrading: a runner from 0.1.0-beta.60 up to the release before this one still files a filed tool's answers, but it shows a protocol error's first 300 characters to the model, its error answers' summaries have no status or retry line, and it doesn't refuse the agent's `read`, `write`, `edit`, `web_save` or `browser_upload` in the folder, or a script's file op outside `/workspace`. It raises no error or warning about any of these, so update every runner that can claim the runs of an agent with a `file` setting to this release. What beta.60's notes say of runners from before `file` still holds.
- OTLP redaction now holds a credential-named pair's value in `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` at every boundary, so a line quoting the credential, as written or decoded, no longer prints it or a piece of it when the key and the pairs around it are split at `&`, `;`, comma or space, raw or percent-encoded. The value is held up to each of those after its `=`, and whole to the end, each out of its quotes too. This covers, among others: <!-- changes/otel-encoded-credentials-followups.md -->
  - a credential in a list joined by `%3B`, such as a cookie, including one with a `%20`, quotes or a `%26` in it;
  - a credential with an encoded space in it between pairs joined by different separators, such as `%3B` before it and `%26` after it;
  - the part of a quoted credential before an encoded comma, when the closing quote comes after the comma;
  - a quoted credential with an encoded space in it, followed by another encoded space and the next pair;
  - a credential longer than 4,096 characters with a separator in it, such as `%3B`, ended by a separator of another kind;
  - in a long value, a credential after separators of more than one kind, such as a cookie joined by `; ` or `%3B%20`, or `&flag;api_key=`.

  Not covered, as before: a `+` read as a space, spaces around the `=`, a URL inside a pair's value whose query holds `%3B` or `%26` (its decoded key is held, not the key as written), and a raw comma inside a quoted value, which splits the variable itself (write it `%2C`).

  A malformed header no longer cuts commas, `&`, a literal `%27` or single letters from the tracer's own lines, and a pair like `theme=dark-mode` after an empty first `;` is no longer held.
- A stop no longer loses a ChatGPT plan sign-in to a renewal it cut off: the server's stop, and a runner's (beside the server or in a process of its own). OpenAI may already have spent the refresh token when the stop starts. From the server's stop on, or 4 s into a runner's stop (sooner if its drain ends sooner; a run the drain lets finish may still renew until then), nothing in that process starts a renewal on its store, and one whose lease was still being taken gives the lease back unsent. A renewal already sent gets up to 25 s from then to save its new pair before the store closes, so a runner's renewal is over 29 s after SIGTERM at most, whatever its drain; past that the log says `renewal_drain_cut` with how many were still out. A server with no runner beside it (`--no-runner`) now allows for that wait before its stop exits early: its stop's deadline was 15 s. The shipped Compose files now give the quickstart and the `--no-runner` server 35 s of stop grace, as the runners and the Helm chart had (they gave 15 s); so does the compose file `install.sh --vps` writes, which the DigitalOcean one-click runs (15 s before). The macOS service waits 35 s before launchd kills it (`ExitTimeOut`; launchd's default is 20 s), and the Railway template sets `RAILWAY_DEPLOYMENT_DRAINING_SECONDS` to 35 (Railway's default is 0). A renewal waiting on another process's lease stops waiting, and its log line says `carry=stopping`. When a renewal's write-back fails, the new pair is revoked only if nothing could have written it: the store refused the write unsent (it had closed), logged as `renewed_pair_unsaved` with `write=refused` before the revocation. A runner's renewals now log to its stderr too. On any other failure the row is read back: a pair it holds is kept, and a row still under the renewal's lease is written again. When that write loses, the row is read once more, since a Postgres commit that went unanswered can land late. When the outcome stays open, the pair is kept unsaved, logged as `renewed_pair_unsaved` with `write=unknown` and the store fault's class (`Unanswered` included). A platform that kills the process sooner than that can still cut the wait short: give it at least the 30 s of grace every shipped target gives. <!-- changes/plan-renewal-drain.md -->
- A run whose ChatGPT token needs renewing after its runner has stopped serving renewals (4 s into the runner's stop) is now handed back to resume on the next start instead of ending failed. Before, its next model request got `credential_unavailable` and the run failed, though no refresh was sent and the sign-in stayed saved. While a server or runner stops, a token that will still be valid when the stop ends (its remaining drain plus 25 s) is sent as it is, with no refresh, so most runs never need the hand-back. A runner's close now drains renewals and closes its store even when a step before them throws. A second stop signal while a runner closes (a second `docker stop`, a double Ctrl-C) no longer ends it at once mid-close: it says once that it is already stopping. <!-- changes/plan-stop-handback.md -->
- A command a run's loop refuses after the runner's dispatch took it for now is now written refused, in the runner's process and in a run's own process alike. This covers a row that arrives before the run's harness loop is chosen, as the row that wakes or reopens a run does. Before, the refusal was dropped and the row stayed untaken, so the run was claimed again on every poll, for good. A raise the cap's rule refuses (a retry, or the second of two raises at once) did this to a run parked at its cap. A trigger's message refused in a session on its owner's sign-in did it to a run that ended or was stopped before its first input: each pass started the run's process, opened its secrets and its computer, and wrote a new end, so a `run.ended` webhook and a Slack notice went out on every poll. A refusal that cannot be written now leaves the row for the run's next claim, and is never handed to the loop again. A message that reopens a run in the moment after its end was written, before the runner had finished with that end, is no longer claimed, given back and claimed again: the runner holds the reopen's first claim, starts the run's next turn only once the claim before it has let go, and the end before it still says released. Where runs have users of their own, that turn's process no longer starts while the last one's slot is still reaped, which took back the run's folders and removed its TMPDIR under it. A claim lost while it waits for that, or held by a runner that is closing, starts no turn at all. <!-- changes/refused-outcome-claim-loop.md -->
- `DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}/learning` now answers only once the clock is past the reset's watermark (the millisecond it began), so a run started right after its `204` always learns from what follows the reset. Before, a reset with nothing to wait for could answer in that same millisecond, and a run started at once read as one before the reset: it learned nothing (reason `reset`), an SDK start was refused, and `compile_after` did not count it. The answer waits at most a millisecond more. <!-- changes/reset-answers-after-watermark.md -->
- A run started while another run of its agent is still keeping a follow-up's or a grade's correction now starts from that correction. Before, the run's learning was read when it was started: a host that launched the next run as soon as the corrected run read `completed` (its compile turn can still run for minutes after that) got a run with nothing learned, though the correction merged a moment later. Now the new run's first claim waits for those rounds to end, then reads its agent's learning again. Only rounds already going count: a run that looks back after its job ended, or that runs a follow-up turn. A run that is queued or waiting on a person never delays a new run. The wait lasts at most 3 minutes by default, and a runner sets its own limit with `AGENTRUN_LEARNING_ROUND_WAIT_MS` (`0` for no wait). When the limit passes, the run starts from its agent's learning as it is then and is never refused. A stop or cancel asked during the wait ends it at once. A run claimed again after its first turn keeps the start it ran on. A run started with no such round open starts as before. `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/learning` also gives `seed_failed` (why a run started with nothing learned: `unreadable`, `not_copied` or `other_disk`; null when its learning was read), `seed_waited` (`ended` when the rounds it waited on ended, `timed_out` when the limit passed first; null when it waited on none) and `learned_chars` (the length of the # Learned text it was given). <!-- changes/seed-after-open-round.md -->
- The server's own calls to Docker (whether a daemon answers, at its start and at a run's; which daemon the docker CLI reaches; the data volume's mounts; the Docker host's addresses) now start `docker` with only the variables it reads, as every docker call of the Docker computer does. Before, they got the server's whole environment with its secrets cut out. <!-- changes/serve-docker-probe-env.md -->
- Wrapped's read of the home passes the import an explicit `threads` (the cores less one, at most 8) and a `readAhead` of a quarter of the import worker's heap (512 MiB), instead of taking the import's defaults. So serve's memory for a Wrapped read stays bounded by its own settings when the import's defaults grow. <!-- changes/serve-wrapped-import-threads.md -->
- GET /v2/templates and GET /v2/templates/{template} give each package's `model_tiers_here`: the harness an apply here would make its agent on, and the model its `fast` and `strong` subagents would run on there, null where this server would not use the package's (behind a model gateway, or a model it can't run), with apply's warning as `note`. The console's Free shelf reads it, so on a server behind a model gateway it no longer lists a template as free whose subagents bill on the host's models. <!-- changes/template-tiers-here.md -->
- pi's turn budget now outlasts a process that stops in the turn, as Claude's, Codex's, ACP's and OpenCode's do: a pi session opened again takes the turn back from its conversation (its last answer's usage and calls, and each result handed since) before a call claims, so the calls a resume answers split what their answer left instead of each taking its whole bound. A read of the turn that fails runs no call: the call is an error naming why, and the next call reads again. <!-- changes/turn-budget-resume-pi-scripts.md -->
  - A result goes back to the harness only once its length is in the session's journal (`TurnBudget.kept`): a process that stops right after it was handed no longer loses its part of the turn, which a resumed call would claim again. A length the journal could not keep fails the call instead of handing its result.
  - A result settles at the length it was handed: a result of at most 400 characters, whole under any bound, and a refusal's words now hold what they took, so the calls after them split only what is left.
  - A code-mode script's JSON read too large for its bound is handed as a note alone (`[read cut: this result is M characters of JSON, past the N ...]`), since part of a JSON document does not parse: on a 16k-32k window, a script that parses it fails naming the cut instead of on a character in the middle, and the model reads that it should ask for less. A read that is not JSON keeps its start and its note, as before.
  - A failed call's error refused for a window too small to cut it in keeps its first line (as much as fits beside the note in the 400 characters a result always keeps whole), so the model reads what went wrong.
  - The run's view shows the cap park a run stands at as its runner reads it: a raise entry clears only the park it names. A raise that names none (checked against the run while it worked) no longer hides a park journaled before it.
- A run whose start fails before its own process is up (a store read, the server's settings or its keys) no longer holds a stop or a command sent to it: each now ends at once, saying the run's process is not running, where it used to wait with no end. An agent's tool that the server denies no longer shows `ceiling` on GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}: its `resolved` says `unavailable: denied`, and the deny, not the setting under it, is why nothing runs. <!-- changes/web-ceiling-p3.md -->
- The leak receipt's count holds in more cases. An import stops a run's key tally however the run ends, so a run that throws no longer leaves its tally counting the keys of every later run. `GET /v2/wrapped` adds up only imported runs: a live run's `secrets` metric, or a count that is not a whole number of zero or more, is in no figure. In the console, the receipt is asked for again when the year changes, and its footnote reads "From the N runs counted on import; counts only, no key shown." <!-- changes/wrapped-leak-receipt-followups.md -->
- The server's README no longer says the owner's session binds a per-run Composio server to any user. It binds any user but the preset's shared default `agentrun`, which every caller gets `422 not_allowed` for, as the API reference already says. <!-- changes/serve-readme-owner-binding.md -->
- `POST /v2/runs/{run_id}/messages` takes an optional `said`: the person's own words, when `content` is a host's text around them (a preamble, the earlier report, turn instructions). The model still gets `content` alone; the run's learning keeps `said` as the owner's correction (one line of `corrections.md`) and as the follow-up in its compile turn's traces, so a host's scaffolding never lands under `# Learned`. Learning reads each message whole from the run's own record, never as the Timeline row shows it (cut at 2,000 characters): `said` is kept however long `content` is, and a long message sent with no `said` is kept whole, its last words included, no longer cut at 2,000 characters. A `said` that is not a string (`wrong_type`), empty after trimming (`empty`) or longer than 4,000 characters (`too_long`) is 422 `input_invalid` at `said`, nothing written; it need not appear inside `content`. `GET /v2/capabilities` says a server takes it: `features.messages.said: true`, API-only servers included. The generated clients carry the field. <!-- changes/message-said.md -->
- Agent37 and Modal computers report their size, so their time can be priced: an Agent37 machine carries the vCPUs, memory and disk Agent37's instance answer gives (`resources`, memory and disk in GB), and a Modal computer carries the limits its create set (2 vCPUs and 4096 MB unless the spec asks other sizes), since Modal reads no size back and bills a sandbox by its use up to those limits. A run on either, with `AGENTRUN_COMPUTE_USD_PER_*` prices set for the provider, now books its `compute_time` lines under the run's cap instead of reading them `unpriced`; Agent37's disk is priced too where a disk price is set. <!-- changes/agent37-modal-computer-sizes.md -->
- The tool gate's filed-folder check now covers three more cases. <!-- changes/filed-gate-followups.md -->
  - On a computer that mounts the run's folder, while a folder is filed, a script's file ops (`files.read`, `files.list`, `files.write` and `files.stat`) must name an absolute path inside `/workspace`. A relative path is refused, with an error saying it is not an absolute path: the computer is handed the path as written, so the gate holds only the form it checked. The computer's own file service already refused a relative path, so no script that worked before is refused now.
  - On that computer, a path under the run folder's name on the runner's machine, such as a bind's source folder or a CLI harness's working folder, is refused as outside `/workspace`. Before, the gate took those names as the run's folder, but on the computer they are other folders, and `files.write` could create them on the computer's own disk.
  - A learned workflow's call node is held by its arguments, not only by its tool's name. A `pdf_pages` call node whose path is in a filed folder is refused before it runs, in the gate's words, as the agent's own `read` there is. The gate reads that path as `pdf_pages` opens it, with the function `pdf_pages` itself calls, so `~x/../stripe/pages/a.pdf` and `file:x/../stripe/pages/a.pdf`, which `pdf_pages` normalizes to `stripe/pages/a.pdf`, are refused too, and `@stripe/pages/a.pdf`, which it opens as a folder named `@stripe`, isn't.
  - A screenshot's `save_as` is held as the screenshot saves it, with the kernel's own `savePathOf`. The kernel saves `~x/../stripe/pages/shot.png` and `file:x/../stripe/pages/shot.png` at `stripe/pages/shot.png`, and the gate read them as outside the run's folder, so they were saved in a filed folder. They are refused now, held as `write` in the words a `save_as` in the folder already got (`write can't be called: ...`), so no refusal a caller matches changes its words. A shot saved outside the folder is saved as before.

  The docs now say that keeping the model off a filed answer takes giving the run no desktop, or setting the desktop kind to `deny`. A desktop whose model is handed no screen tools (`surface: code`) still gives its scripts `apps.open` and input ops.

  Upgrading: a runner from 0.1.0-beta.60 up to 0.1.0-beta.63 has neither the `pdf_pages` call node check nor the `save_as` check. It runs a learned `pdf_pages` call node on a path in a filed folder and saves a screenshot's `save_as` into one, with no error or warning, so update every runner that can claim the runs of an agent with a `file` setting to this release.
- POST /runs/{run_id}/messages counts `said` in Unicode code points for its 4,000 limit, as its schema's `maxLength` and a host's own count (Python `len()`) do. An emoji is one character, not two: a `said` of 4,000 emoji is taken, where it was refused as `too_long`. <!-- changes/said-code-points.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.63 (2026-11-26)

- An agent on any CLI harness (claude-agent, codex, opencode, and Goose or Cursor where their owner installed them) now gets the browser, the same way it gets web_fetch. Before, granting `browser` to such an agent came back with "browser runs on pi here; on <harness> it is not bound yet", and a run of an agent whose computer is a browser was refused at its claim with "This agent's computer is a browser, which only the pi harness drives here". Now neither is refused on any of them. The harness is handed the browser's tools (`snapshot`, `run`, `screenshot` and the rest) as host tools. They drive the same session pi's would: the agent's browser computer, or else the vendor its tool plane picks. They use the same live view, the same spend held under the run's cap, and the same release when the run is let go. <!-- changes/browser-on-every-harness.md -->
  - The person can take part as on pi: the agent's `browser_request_handoff` asks them and its call waits, with the run working, its row saying it waits for them in the browser, and its session held, until they hand the browser back; and the person can take the browser over in its live view unasked, while the agent's next browser call waits for them and is then told they had it. Either way the agent's later browser calls drive the same session, and none is made again.
  - A browser call in flight when its runner dies is answered as interrupted ("may or may not have taken effect") when the run resumes on another runner, and is never sent to the browser again; the model goes on from that answer. The next claim takes back the session the run opened, and it is released once when the run ends. Each browser call's memo is its own, so nothing it kept carries into another call.
  - Every browser answer the harness is handed (a page's snapshot text, the hand-over and take-over words) passes through the run's redactor first, as every other host tool's answer does: a secret the run holds that a page shows back reaches the CLI only as `[redacted]`.
  - `subagent` still runs on pi only, and is refused in words on every other harness; `pdf_pages` and `llm` stay a workflow's node tools.
  - `capabilities.tools` lists every harness under the browser's `harnesses`, not `pi` alone.
- The kyb template can screen a name against each sanctions list's own published file. With a shell it saves the file with `web_save` and greps every row, and its answer names the method `full_list_grep` with the list's version where the file or its URL gives one (`unknown` otherwise). Before it reports `no_hit` it has searched each identifier it holds, a short name such as `ADF Ltd` whole as a word, and, where a common name needs narrowing, whole UN records rather than lines, since the UN file keeps each part of a person's name on its own line. It reads a name with another in brackets, such as `ADF (Allied Democratic Forces)`, as both names, so a short name is not passed over as one word inside a longer name. It reads an EU entry's rows whole, the header line first, so a long remark no longer cuts off the name, birth date, documents or citizenship that come after it, and a `;` inside a quoted field shifts no column. Without a shell it screens through the list owners' indexes and records, as before. <!-- changes/kyb-list-files.md -->
- `agentrun share RUN --to URL` publishes an ended run to a share host and prints its link, `<URL>/r/<id>`. It exports the run again with `--restore`, checks the bundle against `--expect SHA` before anything is sent, and posts the bundle byte for byte to `POST <URL>/r/v2/shares`. A bundle whose sha256 changed since the preview page showed it is refused (exit 1), with words saying to open the page again. Before it sends anything, it prints that a share is public: anyone with the link can open it. The preview page's footer now shows the whole command, `agentrun share RUN --to <url> [--restore IDS] --expect SHA`, with `<url>` your share host's address, and how to sign in to it. The page names no default share host. <!-- changes/share-publish-cli.md -->
  - `agentrun login --share URL < TOKEN_FILE` signs in to a share host: the token, read from stdin, is checked at `URL/r/v2/shares` and kept in a `share` entry of the same 0600 config file. The server's `base_url` and `api_key` stay as they were, so every other command still goes where it went, and a later `agentrun login` keeps the share entry. `agentrun logout --share` removes that entry alone; `agentrun logout` still removes the file.
  - A share host's refusal is said in the CLI's own words, never its message or a value: a 422 prints its counts by rule (a rule the bundle's own records don't name counts as `unknown`), a 400 says the host does not take the bundle's format, a 413 gives its numbers, a full quota says to take a share down, and a refused token (exit 4) gives the login command. Publishing with no share login for that address refuses before the export, with the same command.
  - `agentrun share delete URL` takes a share down with the same token (`DELETE <host>/r/v2/shares/<id>`); its page and bundle then answer 410. A share of another token's (exit 4), one the host does not have (exit 1) and one already deleted (exit 0) are each said plainly.
  - `agentrun share RUN` with none of `--to`, `--dry-run` and `--out` still exits 2 and sends nothing; its words now name `--to`. `--to` with `--dry-run` or `--out` is refused.
- On a Linux desktop, `apps.list` leaves out, and `apps.launch` and `apps.terminate` refuse as `denied` naming the file and why, an app whose desktop file computerd's own user could change: on the way to it from `/`, every symbolic link followed, the user owns a folder, a link or the file (`~/.local/share/applications` among them), the mode bits let it write the file or a folder holding one of them, or computerd runs as root. The entry is read from the file that walk checked, opened without following a link and refused if another took its place. An app runs what its desktop file says, so before, an agent given `write` and the apps group, with bash denied and exec off, could write a desktop file there and `apps.launch` it, or shadow a system app's id, and run any command. Apps installed under the user's home, as on a paired machine's `~/.local/share/applications`, are no longer listed, and a computerd that runs as root lists none. <!-- changes/apps-launch-writable-desktop-files.md -->

  The surface's `apps.open` (a script's `computer.apps.open`) refuses a `url` that starts with `-`, after leading whitespace too, as `invalid` before the call leaves it, in computerd's words, so a paired Linux machine on an older computerd doesn't hand it to the app as a flag. The computer README and `AppsLaunchParams.url`'s comment say what a `url` is on Linux. The words every offer of a computer's ops carries (`GUI_REACH`) and the desktop kind skill say that `apps.open` with a path reaches what a shell does for a file the agent wrote too, where `write` is granted.
- On a Linux desktop, `apps.launch` (a script's `computer.apps.open`) refuses a `url` that is neither an absolute URL with a scheme (`https://…`, `file:///…`) nor an absolute path, and starts nothing. Before, computerd put the `url` into the app's argv as it was: one starting with `-`, after leading whitespace too, reached the app as a flag (Chromium's `--renderer-cmd-prefix` runs a command, on a computer whose exec is off), and a relative path reached it as a file. A `url` starting with `-` is refused `invalid` in words of its own: `starts with "-": the app would take it as a flag, not a url`. The macOS and Android daemons already took only a URL with a scheme, handed to the OS rather than to an argv. <!-- changes/apps-open-url-guard.md -->

  The words every offer of a computer's ops carries (`GUI_REACH`) now say that `apps.open` with a URL or a path, not only a `file://` URL, reaches what the shell and the file ops do. serve's README and the desktop kind skill no longer say that every op the gate refuses whatever its arguments is left out of `computer_op`'s list: only the ops held to a tool (the file ops, `shell.run`, `processes.start`) are; apps and raw input stay.
- A server's start lists the ChatGPT plan's models only with an access token OpenAI takes. The start never renews the token itself, so a stop right after it can't spend the refresh token and lose the sign-in. Until a run renews the token, the fallback list stays. Once one has, the server's next read of the sign-in (`GET /capabilities`, which the console reads, or the ChatGPT sign-in page) lists the models while that token is fresh, with no restart. A server's stop now also waits, within its 2 s, for the change its start's model list tells it. A renewal that loses its write-back to a new sign-in, and whose new pair OpenAI doesn't confirm revoked, now carries that pair in the saved row. If another process is renewing that row, it waits for that renewal first. The server's next start revokes the pair. <!-- changes/plan-settle-followups.md -->
- The scrubber now cuts a read of `.env` files named by a glob or a brace, such as `cat .env*`, `head .env.*` or `cat .env.{local,production}`. Before, these printed every file uncut. The dotfile exemption covers only a plain path, so these commands keep their `env` token and their output is an `env-dump` cut. <!-- changes/scrubber-env-globs.md -->

  The env-dump reader now also catches:
  - `process` with `.env` on the next line;
  - the `Environment` property (`systemctl show -p Environment`) and `/etc/environment`;
  - `heroku config` and its subcommands;
  - `ps` with an uppercase `E` (`ps auxE`, `ps -E`).

  A transcript's cut now also starts and ends at a full PS1 prompt: `user@host:~$`, `root@c:/#`, `[user@host dir]$`, with or without a `(venv) ` prefix.

  A shared run's title now has one more env-dump cut. The title is the first message on one line, so `$ printenv` and its `NAME=value` output sat on the same line there and were shared uncut. The export now reads the title as a flattened transcript: after a prompt, when a command that prints the environment is followed by a `NAME=value` word, everything from that word to the next prompt is cut. This covers only that shape. Output that doesn't start with `NAME=` (`printenv NAME`, `echo $NAME`, `cat .env`, `docker inspect`, `heroku config`) is still carried in the title, though the row that holds the same message is cut. Only the title is read this way; a row or file keeps reading `$ env NAME=value command` as a command. A share host reads an uploaded bundle's title the same way.

  A `.env` name in another case (`cat .ENV`, `cat .Env.local`) is now an env-dump. env-file matches only lower-case names, and the exemption used to drop these names anyway.
- A raise that reaches an agentic run's claim while that claim is parking the run again at its cap (a refused raise woke it, and the park is slow, as one that keeps a computer is) now waits for the run's next claim, which resumes the run. Before, the parking claim took the raise and the run was left parked with nothing to wake it. <!-- changes/serve-raise-during-repark.md -->
- A capped workflow run parked at its cap that a claim wakes with no raise that resumes it (a raise the cap's rule refuses, from a race of two raises or a retry) now parks again on the pause it stood at, with nothing written, before any step runs. Before, each such claim ran the held step into the same cap and wrote a new `agentrun.budget` entry. A refused raise's row is left untaken and wakes the run on every poll, so the entries grew without bound. <!-- changes/serve-refused-raise-claim-loop.md -->
- A capped workflow run writes one budget entry per cap in two more cases. A retry of the raise that resumed the run, reaching it once it parked again at the raised cap, is taken and leaves the new pause standing: its raise entry names the pause the raise answered, as an agentic run's does, not the one the run stands at since. A claim of a run paused at its cap whose row reads running (a woken claim lost before its release) parks the run again on its pause, as a claim of the parked run does. Before, each ran the held step into the same cap and wrote another `agentrun.budget` entry. A run's view shows the pause it stands at after such a retry: a raise entry clears only the pause it names. <!-- changes/serve-workflow-raise-retry-lost-claim.md -->
- A tool result is held to the model's context window, not only to the fixed 120,000-character bound: a model with a small window (an Ollama model at 65,536 tokens, a 16k one) is never handed a result that fills its context. <!-- changes/tool-result-window-bound.md -->
  - `boundResult(text, budget?)` takes the model's window (`{ contextWindow, baseInputTokens? }`): a result may take at most a quarter of what the window leaves (`RESULT_WINDOW_SHARE`), at three characters a token (`RESULT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN`), and never more than `HOST_RESULT_MAX_CHARS`. Past that it is cut with a note saying it was cut to fit the window and how to read on; a window too small for any cut refuses the result in words, and a result of at most 400 characters (`RESULT_ALWAYS_WHOLE_CHARS`) always stands whole, so bounding a bound changes nothing. With no window the bound is exactly as before. `resultMaxChars(budget)` gives the bound, and `boundTo(text, max)` cuts to a given bound, saying how (`ResultBound`: the characters kept, the whole length, the bound).
  - `SessionSpec.contextWindow` carries the session model's window, and each harness adapter (Claude, Codex, ACP, OpenCode) takes a `contextWindow` option for when the host passes none; Codex and OpenCode are told that window in place of their 272,000 guess. A Codex script cut off by a crash is answered within the same bound (`recoveryMaxChars`), not `EXEC_RECOVERY_MAX_CHARS`.
  - agentrun-serve puts the run's model window from its catalog on every session, and pi now holds every tool result to it too: a host tool's and a pi-native one's (web_fetch, web_search, the browser's), which before reached the model up to pi's own output limits. What a host tool streams while it runs is held to the bound too (`boundedProgress`), since pi writes a call cut off past its restart limit from that text, without its hooks.
  - A turn's results together fit what the window has left (`TurnBudget`, `ResultBudget.turn`): from what the context already holds (the last request's input tokens and its answer's output, else the session's system prompt and tool schemas counted with o200k), less the room kept for the model's answer (`answerReserve`: a quarter of the window, at most `ANSWER_RESERVE_MAX_TOKENS`, 16,384 tokens), each call the model made takes the smaller of its own bound and what is left over the calls still unanswered, so parallel calls split it, and below the least a cut keeps a result is refused in words. The kernel owns the rule; the session's model proxy reports each answer's facts (`ModelProxyOptions.turn`, its calls counted from the stream by `toolCallsIn`) for Claude, Codex, OpenCode and Goose, and pi and Claude Code on a person's login report them from their own hooks (pi's afterResponse, the login's stream booking). `windowBudget(window, system?)` builds the budget with its turn. A call whose result goes to the harness's own tool rather than the model (`ToolBridgeOptions.outsideTurn`: Codex's code-mode script calls) takes the per-result bound alone, outside the turn's split.
  - The bridge records each cut it hands a harness (`bound:<callId>`, `boundKey`), and a replay of the call is cut by that record. Codex compares a nested call's two records on those lengths, never on the note's words; `boundOf` is gone. A session written before the record still agrees where Codex got the host's bound's cut, as before.
  - On Claude, Codex, ACP and OpenCode, a turn's budget outlasts a process that stops in the turn (a park, a crash): each answer's facts and each result's length as it was handed go to the session's journal as they happen (`journalTurn`, `TURN_STREAM`), and a budget that has read no answer yet takes them back before any call claims (`TurnBudget.restore`). The calls a resume answers split what their answer left, and a result handed before the stop keeps its part. Codex's recovered script outputs claim their room in the turn too and are held to that claim (`ResultBudget.maxChars`). pi's turn budget is not journaled yet: a pi session opened again starts a fresh one, and each result there keeps its per-result bound.
- A run with `checkout: pull_request` or `checkout: repository` on a Mode 2 server whose Archil region has no serverless exec (gcp-us-central1) now gets its checkout: the server's git fetch runs in the run's sandbox computer once it has mounted the run's folder, the same script with the GitHub App's token on the process's stdin, never on its argv or in its environment. Before, the fetch went to Archil's exec, which that region refuses, and the run was told its checkout failed with "Exec is not enabled". A run there with no computer that mounts its folder is told up front that it has no checkout and why, and its timeline names a sandbox computer as the fix. A template whose computer list asks for a shell first (code-review, agent-scout) is applied there with the first sandbox whose keys are set and that mounts the run's folder (E2B, Modal or Agent37 on Archil), so its runs have a shell and their checkout. A computer's exec now takes stdin (process.write). Regions with exec and Mode 1 are unchanged. <!-- changes/archil-no-exec-checkout.md -->
- A CLI run's end-of-run turn (its learning step) now reads the turn's last message as its answer, as a pi run's always has. Before, it ran every message of the turn together, so a claude-agent turn whose stream stalled and was asked again whole stored the stalled part and the whole answer as one. The Claude adapter takes the stream idle limit from its host (`streamIdleMs`, `LOCAL_STREAM_IDLE_MS`) rather than from a route's `fetch`, and serve sets it only for a model on its own machine. <!-- changes/cli-end-of-run-answer.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.62 (2026-11-26)

**Breaking:**

- A script's file ops on a desktop or a phone need their tool among the agent's tools: `computer.files.read`, `files.list` and `files.stat` need `read`, and `files.write` needs `write`, as before. Naming a desktop no longer grants them: an agent that read files through `computer` without `read` in its `tools` is now refused in words (`computer_op files.read needs read among this agent's tools…`), whatever `read`'s setting says, on every desktop, mounted or not. Add `read` to the agent's `tools` to keep them. `computer_op`'s op list and a script's `computer` declarations offer only the ops the gate would let through: not one whose tool the agent is not given, nor one held to a tool set to deny, nor one held to a tool set to ask where no one can approve, nor one `bash`'s policy refuses whatever its command (`bash` set to deny drops `shell.run` and `processes.start`; the read-only policy drops `processes.start`). Both say that input ops on a computer with a terminal app or a GUI file manager, and `apps.open` with a `file://` URL, can do what a shell or the file ops do, whatever `bash`'s, `read`'s or `write`'s setting. `shell.run` and `processes.start` still follow `bash`'s setting, not a grant, so leaving `read` out keeps no file from an agent that has the shell, paired machines included: on a desktop with exec on, `computer.shell.run` reads and writes any file under `bash`'s setting, which allows by default. `computerDeclarations` takes the ops to leave out, and the kernel exports `withoutOps` for computer_op's definition and `GUI_REACH` for the words. <!-- changes/desktop-file-ops-need-grants.md -->
- A harness module's runner gets the run's redactor on its launch (`HarnessLaunch.redact`, required and typed) and no longer among the harness's own options, and every loop the runner makes refuses to start without the runner's redactor that holds keys. Upgrading: a harness module reads the run's redactor from `launch.redact` (required); `extra.redact` is no longer set. <!-- changes/run-keys-redact-followups.md -->
  - A native run's loop, the runner's dispatch loop, a loop the live view wraps and a loop for a run in its own process now each refuse to start without the runner's held redactor, as the adapter, SDK and workflow loops already did. Before this release, a native run's loop given none ran on a redactor of the runner's environment alone, which holds no key a claim opens; the runner always hands its own, so only a caller outside the runner reached that.

**Changes:**

- Render Sandboxes as a computer provider (`render`, subpath `@parcha/agentrun-computer/render`): a Linux sandbox in a Render microVM, over Render's public REST API with no SDK. Settings → Computers shows a Render row that takes `RENDER_API_KEY` and `RENDER_WORKSPACE_ID`, and the server's launcher holds `RENDER_API_KEY` with the other providers' keys, never in the server's environment. `render` is a box the clients' types name. <!-- changes/computer-render-sandbox.md -->
  Its sandboxes dial the server, as Fly Machines and Cloudflare do: Render runs a command with no stdin, so once a sandbox runs, the provider starts `agentrun-dial` in it through one `runs/sync` call, and it fetches the server's daemon and dials the attach route. A server with no public https address (`AGENTRUN_PUBLIC_URL`) refuses a Render computer in words before Render is called. `prepareImage()` imports the box image once into the workspace as a sandbox build named `agentrun-box-<tag>`. Network `none`, `open` and an allow list are init's, as on the other dial providers. Render keeps no labels, so a computer's name gives its own two and the rest live in a file in the sandbox; a listing whose file read fails fails in words. Render has no endpoint that lengthens a running sandbox, so there is no `extend()`, and a sandbox lives at most a day. No mount: a Render computer can't mount the server's run folders.
- `agentrun-serve --share-host` (or `AGENTRUN_SHARE_HOST=1`) starts a share host: a server that answers under `/r/` alone and stores shares in `DIR/shares/`. A share's page is `/r/<id>` (the console's `share.html`, with its asset URLs under `/r/_assets/` and a CSP that loads nothing from any other origin), its stored bytes are `/r/<id>/bundle.json` (`nosniff`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`), and its API is `POST /r/v2/shares`, `GET /r/v2/shares` (the caller's own), `DELETE /r/v2/shares/<id>` and a public `GET /r/v2/health`. Every other address is a 404, the console, `/v2`, MCP and every run, agent, key, computer and trigger route among them. A share host starts no runner and has no owner or console session: its API takes one of its tokens (`AGENTRUN_TOKENS`), whose id owns each share it uploads. <!-- changes/share-host.md -->
  An upload is a run's `agentrun.share/1` bundle exactly as `GET /v2/runs/<id>/export` wrote it: canonical JSON at most 8 MiB, the export's closed fields and caps, each file's size and digest and the document's sha256 checked (a mismatch is `400`). The host then scrubs the whole body, and each of its strings alone, in cut mode with the values it holds (its keys and tokens). A value it finds refuses the upload unless a `restored` record names it exactly (pointer, rule, start, end) and the host's own scrub says its kind may be restored (label, personal, jev; never a key format, a held value or a dump); a restored record naming no value the host finds refuses it too (save a restore of Jev's rule, which the host never runs: taken unchecked, its value still scrubbed, and counted in `restored_unchecked`), and so does a scrub that fails. An upload that needs more than 50,000 string reads is `413` before any scrub. Each distinct string is one read for each context it is read under (a file's path, a workflow call's command), and a call's command is read once for all of its output. Each refusal is `422 input_invalid` with `details.reason` and counts by rule, never a value, and nothing is stored; the host never repairs a bundle. A stored share answers `201 {id, url, sha256}`, its id 128 random bits in base32 and its URL on `AGENTRUN_PUBLIC_URL` (never a Host header; a share host on an address other than loopback needs it to start). A token keeps at most 100 shares (`403 forbidden`, `details.reason: share_quota`, past it); shares never expire. Only the token that made a share deletes it (`204`); its bytes go, and its page and bundle then answer `410`. Run one replica with `DIR` on a persistent volume: the quota and the share index are the one process's.
  A share page draws no image at all: not a run's file and not a provider's URL, in a workflow's graph or in a report.
  The host re-reads a file's content with its path and a workflow call's output with that call's command. A Timeline row's output it re-reads without its call's context, since a bundle carries no calls, so the host's check of a row is the context-free rules' alone. The export still cuts the row with its call's context.
  The share page has not yet been drawn in a real browser: its HTML, CSP and assets were fetched from a real console build on a loopback share host.
- Wrapped has a cache section, and the console draws its cache grade card. The import now analyzes each Claude Code, Codex and pi session's cache as it imports it, the same way `agentrun-import --cache` does, and keeps the numbers on the run: the cache read and whole prompt behind its hit rate, its breaks by cause, what they cost above a cache read, and how many have no known price. `GET /v2/wrapped` answers `cache` by adding up the year's runs from the store, so it reads no session file again. <!-- changes/wrapped-cache-card.md -->
  - `cache` is null when no run of the year was analyzed. Only runs imported here count: a session left out of the import, or imported before this version, is not in it.
  - The card shows a grade from the hit rate (A+ from 97%, then a step every three points down to D from 60%, F under that), the hit rate, what breaks cost, how many there were, and breaks by cause. The cost is "Unknown" when no break could be priced, and the foot line counts the breaks left out of it.
  - `@parcha/agentrun-import` exports `fileCache`, `sessionBreaks` and `conversationOf`: the per-file analysis, the join `cacheHome` uses, and which subagent files are one conversation (a Codex subagent's thread that goes on in another rollout is one). Another reader of a session's files gets the same breaks.
- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) now serves an ended run's share bundle (`GET /runs/{id}/export`, with its `?restore=`) to its token: before, it answered `404` and `agentrun share` failed against it. The bundle is the full server's, cut by the same scrubber, and a run that has not ended is still `409`. The share preview page stays the console's, which this profile refuses: use `agentrun share RUN --out FILE` there. <!-- changes/api-only-share-export.md -->
- On a Mode 2 server whose Archil region has no serverless exec (`gcp-us-central1`), a new agent that names `bash` (or another shell tool) and no computer is refused at its save or deploy and told to name a sandbox computer, instead of being saved with a shell that never runs (every bash call failed with "Exec is not enabled"). A new agent that names no tools is not refused: it saves on the runner with no tools, as Mode 2 always saved it. An agent already saved with `bash` and no computer is now refused at each run, `409 agent_not_runnable` at `definition.computer` in the same words, and no run starts; this holds for runs started by hand, by a schedule and by a trigger, and is intended: bash cannot run there, so give the agent a sandbox computer or remove `bash` from its tools. Capabilities' `places.default_place` is null there with a `default_reason` saying why, bash shows unavailable, and `GET /v2/computers` gives the no-computer choice no shell. Servers on Archil's AWS regions, and on a region serve doesn't know, are unchanged. <!-- changes/archil-no-exec-no-shell.md -->
- A package's composio trigger written with no `config` reads as `config: {}`, the config of an event whose schema needs no field (Slack's new channel): `agentrun deploy` no longer refuses it, and an apply makes, and a re-apply keeps, the trigger with the empty config. `POST /v2/triggers` still takes `config` as given; its refusal of one left out now says to send `{}` for such an event. <!-- changes/composio-trigger-config-default.md -->
- A run whose kept computer can't be taken back no longer shows the provider's refusal to the person. Before, a resumed run's timeline could read "The sandbox kept before could not be taken back: the computer … does not match this provider, so attach refuses it and it is left as it is: HostConfig.Mounts: …", with host paths and Docker's settings in it. Now it says why in serve's own words. When the runner that parked the run is gone: "The sandbox wasn't kept: the runner that kept it is gone." When that runner is still there, it says that runner ends it. Otherwise: "The sandbox wasn't kept: it couldn't be taken back." Each goes on to say the run has a new sandbox. The provider's full words go to the runner's log. When the new claim deletes that kept machine, its kept row is marked ended at once, so the run's end removes the row instead of leaving it marked ending until a janitor's pass. <!-- changes/computer-keeper-gone-words.md -->
- The janitor's pass over left Archil credential removes is bounded as a whole, and a failed leave is logged and tried again. <!-- changes/computer-night-followups-2.md -->
  - The pass over the `archil_revoke:<run>` rows now has one bound for the whole pass, the kept delete bound. Once it passes, the remove being asked is cut, and the rows not yet asked stay for the next pass, reported in one line. Before, each row had its own bound, so N hanging rows held the provider sweep and the next wake for N bounds.
  - Each pass starts after the last row the previous pass asked, wrapping around to the first, so a row whose remove hangs is retried last on the next pass and the rows after it are asked first. Every row is asked within as many passes as there are rows.
  - When a run's claim ends and the store refuses to write the left row, the runner now logs `run <id>'s Archil mount credential remove could not be left for the janitor, so it lapses at its ttl: …`, and a later leave writes the row. Before, the failure was dropped, and the rejected write was cached, so no later leave could write the row.
