  - A runner with tracing on now says so once as it starts: `[otel] tracing is on: spans export to <origin>`, the endpoint's origin alone (scheme, host and port), never its user, password, path, query or fragment, nor a header. Off, nothing is said.
  - A failed export's line names the endpoint's origin and the time, and a collector that keeps failing is said again at most once a minute, by the next failure once a minute has passed, with the count of failures since the last line (`[otel] 25 more trace exports to <origin> failed since <time>, the last at <time>; ...`). Before, the first failure was one line with neither, and nothing more until an export succeeded and failed again. A run's end still never waits on an export.
- On macOS, signing Claude Code in from the console now saves the login's Keychain item under the Mac user the server runs as, so `claude auth status` in that person's terminal reads it signed in, as AgentRun's badge does. Before, the claude CLI that AgentRun starts for the sign-in, the status check and a run got no `USER`. The CLI names the Keychain item's account by `USER`, and without it the account was `unknown`. The badge, asked the same way, read signed in, while the person's own `claude`, which has `USER`, looked under their name and read signed out. Those three now carry `USER` and `LOGNAME` set to the user the server runs as, as the system names it (`os.userInfo()`), even when the server itself was started without `USER`, as a service launchd starts may be, or with another user's. <!-- changes/claude-keychain-account-user.md -->

  Who breaks: anyone who signed Claude in from the console on macOS before this release. That login reads signed out once the server is updated, since its item is under `unknown`. What to do: sign in again under Settings → Model keys. The old item stays in the Keychain under the account `unknown` and still holds a valid login, which nothing reads any more. Delete it in Terminal with `security delete-generic-password -a unknown -s "Claude Code-credentials-<hash>"`, where `<hash>` is the first 8 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the login folder's path: for AgentRun's own folder, `D="<data>/claude-login"` (`<data>` is the server's `--data`, `~/.local/share/agentrun/agents` by default), then `security delete-generic-password -a unknown -s "Claude Code-credentials-$(printf %s "$D" | shasum -a 256 | cut -c1-8)"`. Keychain Access can delete it too.
- Behaviour change: on a run a trigger started (schedule, webhook, Slack, GitHub, Composio, email or feed), `email_send` now asks a person before it sends to an address this account has never sent to, even with `email_send` set to allow. Who breaks: an agent a trigger runs that emails new people unattended. Its send now waits for approval, naming them ("someone@example.com: this account has never sent to them"), and with accounts off, where no one can approve, it is refused in those words. To let it through, approve the first send to each new person; the run's later sends to them go unasked. <!-- changes/email-trigger-ask.md -->

  - Never sent to means no message in the account's own Sent folder (Gmail's Sent Mail), from the account's own address and not a draft, has the address in its To, Cc or Bcc: the exact address, blind to the case of ASCII letters only, as far back as Sent goes. Mail received from someone doesn't count, so a scheduled run replying to a first-time sender asks once.
  - What doesn't ask: the account's own address, an address the run already sent to (unasked or approved), on an email run its thread's starter (the From of the message that started it) when the receiving server's own Authentication-Results says `dmarc=pass` for the From's domain, and every send of a playground or API run, which only the 5-send cap holds, as before.
  - The starter's pass is read only from the message's topmost Authentication-Results, and only under the account provider's authserv-id: Gmail's `mx.google.com`, the one known so far. On any other provider, or with no pass (no header, `dmarc=fail` or `none`, `dkim=pass` alone, a pass for another domain), the starter asks like any new address.
  - An email run on its thread now asks too: it keeps the outside-the-thread ask, and a reply-all that reaches someone the starter Cc'd and the account never wrote to asks, naming them. `scope: "mailbox"` turns the outside-the-thread ask off and exempts no starter.
  - `email_file` now refuses Sent and Drafts as targets ("email_file never files into Sent or Drafts: ..."), so a run can't move a draft or someone else's mail into Sent to make an address look written to.
  - A Sent folder that can't be read, an account with none, and a send checked while no account is saved all ask, saying "its recipients couldn't be checked against this account's sent mail" and why.
- The setup skill's Local model step says to start Ollama: the server lists its models itself, so the service gets no gateway and no key for it. The first-run walks run on a fake Ollama. On a server with a public address (`--tailscale`, `--public-url`), the skill and the launcher's README say to set `OLLAMA_HOST`, the default address too: only one person's own server asks it unset. <!-- changes/ollama-walks.md -->
  - Breaking: `agentrun service install --env AGENT_MODEL_API_KEY=none` is refused, and a re-install drops it from a service that has it. A service that reached Ollama through `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL` then gets `model_key_required`. Remove the gateway with `agentrun service install --env AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL= --env AGENT_MODEL_GATEWAY_IDS= --env AGENT_MODEL= --env AGENT_MODEL_PRICE=`, start Ollama, and pick the model as `ollama/<tag>`. A service with `--tailscale` or `--public-url`, or an Ollama off port 11434 on this machine, also needs `--env OLLAMA_HOST=<host:port>` set to Ollama's address (port 11434 on that machine by default): such a server lists Ollama only where `OLLAMA_HOST` names it. A re-install that drops the key says so in one line naming this move, and never the key's value. `--env AGENT_MODEL_API_KEY=...` gets its own refusal naming the same move. Where the gateway is on this machine, that refusal and `model_key_required` both say to remove `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL`, since AgentRun lists Ollama itself, and add `OLLAMA_HOST=<host:port>` where the server would otherwise lose Ollama's address. A pair given to `--env` with no name before `=` is refused without being repeated.

**Changes:**

- A desktop's or a phone's agent can keep what it sees: `computer_screenshot` takes `save_as`, a path relative to the run's folder ending `.png`, and saves the screenshot there through the run's own files, whatever disk the computer has. The answer is the image as before, plus `saved as <path> in the run's files` (and `saved` in its structured value). A path outside the folder, an absolute one or one not ending `.png` is refused in words before the computer is asked. A screenshot with `save_as` is held to `write`'s setting as well as the computer's: `write` set to deny refuses it before the computer is asked, set to ask puts it to a person. `save_as` needs `write` among the agent's tools: an agent not given `write` is not offered `save_as`, and a screenshot with one anyway is refused in words, whatever `write`'s setting says. Nor is it offered with `write` set to deny, or set to ask on a server where no one can approve. <!-- changes/desktop-screenshot-save-as.md -->
  A desktop or a phone the run's folder is not mounted in (one with `exec: false`, or a provider that mounts none) tells its model once in the run, as the server's note, that the computer's own disk is not the run's files and is deleted at the end, and that the file tools and `save_as` keep what the user should get. A run not given `write`, with `write` set to deny, or with it set to ask where no one can approve, is told instead that screenshots can't be saved to the run's files. The note goes after a due cap wrap-up, never ahead of it, and a resumed claim does not tell it again. The note is part of such a run's first request: on a pi desktop run on Sonnet it needs $0.055 through a gateway (from $0.052; its byte bound 10,445 tokens) and $0.031 straight to Anthropic (from $0.030, so the README's first-request figure there is $0.04); the documented $0.09 minimums for the five-step run do not change.
- A completed fal job's `result` is kept in the run's files at `evidence/fal/<request_id>.json`, so a step that needs the whole result (an audio clip's timestamp chunks, say) reads it from the file instead of the model retyping it. The run's MCP gateway files it when an answer of a fal server (`run_model`, `submit_jobs`, `wait_for_jobs`) carries a job whose `status` is `completed` and which has a `result`. The answer the model reads is unchanged, byte for byte. Only a request_id in fal's UUID shape names a file; any other id (a path, `..`, a plain name, a UUID with a suffix) is not filed, and the call works as before. A file is saved once: whatever is already at the path (a file, a folder, a link) is kept, and a link on the way is never followed. A file that lands at the path after the check is kept too: the file is made in one step that never replaces (`Workspace.writeNew`, on the local Workspace and on one attached to the run's computer). A result that can't be filed never fails the call. In Mode 2 the gateway files through the run's computer when it mounts the run's folder. With no computer mounting it, the gateway files over the Archil disk's file API, which has no `writeNew`: nothing is filed, and the call works as before (follow-up Parcha-ai/agentrun#3777). `web_save` now saves through the same helper. Where the Workspace has `writeNew` it also keeps a file that landed after its check. Where it doesn't (an Archil run disk), web_save keeps its check then a write, as before (follow-up Parcha-ai/agentrun#3777). The parsing is fal's meter's (`McpMeter.results`), so the gateway stays the same for every server. <!-- changes/fal-results-filed.md -->
- `@parcha/agentrun-import` reads GitHub Copilot CLI, a new source (`copilot`): each session's `$COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<id>/events.jsonl` (`~/.copilot` without `COPILOT_HOME`), and an older CLI's `session-state/<id>.jsonl`. `normalizeUsage("copilot", …)` takes the cache read and write out of `inputTokens` and keeps `reasoningTokens` as `reasoning`. <!-- changes/import-copilot.md -->
  - Copilot writes no request's tokens to disk (`assistant.usage` is ephemeral). A session's tokens are the per-model totals of the `session.shutdown` each CLI process writes as it exits; a shutdown that holds the session's whole total (a CLI that keeps its accounting across processes) counts only what it adds. Each model's total goes on its last request in that process; the model's earlier requests there are `folded` into it (zeros, known), so the run is metered and the catalog prices it. A session with no shutdown, still running or killed, has tokens 0 and its requests unmetered. Copilot writes no dollar cost, so `cost` is `null` unless each request's tokens are known.
  - Each model call is one request, keyed by its first `assistant.message`'s `messageId`; a response split into chunks (each its own `messageId`, one `apiCallId`) is one. Each event counts once by its `id` and each message by its `messageId`, so a copied session adds no request; a copied shutdown adds no tokens but moves the copy's baseline, so its next whole total adds only its own. Each turn keeps the ids it was read by (`uuids` its events', the shutdown's on the requests it fed; a request's new `keys` its later chunks' `messageId`s), so a later import of a copy counts it as one import of both would. A rotated journal's `checkpoint: true` records are copies. Subagent, autopilot, skill and agent-written user messages are not the person's turns.
  - `agentrun-serve import` (and `--from copilot`) imports Copilot CLI sessions as runs. An imported run's entries keep those ids (`record_uuids`, and `record_keys` for a request's later chunks), and a later import restores them, as it does Claude Code's: a fork or copy of a session imported already counts none of it again. A turn's `folded: true` (its zeros counted in a later request of the session) is read as known tokens, never unmetered, so the run's estimate prices it. `imported_from.source` and the stats analytics' `by_source` take `copilot`, in the OpenAPI document and the generated clients.
- `@parcha/agentrun-import` reads OpenCode, its fourth source (`opencode`, run by serve's `opencode` harness). It reads every session in `$XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode` (`~/.local/share/opencode`): the `opencode*.db` databases (1.x and 2.x schemas), the one `OPENCODE_DB` names, and the JSON storage OpenCode kept before SQLite. SQLite goes through `node:sqlite` on Node and `bun:sqlite` under Bun. <!-- changes/import-opencode.md -->
  - One locator per session: `{ file: <db>, id }`, or a storage session's JSON file. A session in several databases is listed once, from the one that wrote it last (its rows' latest `time_updated`; a tie, the first). A 2.x session wins over the 1.x copy beside it, and a 2.x fork's rows copied from its source count nothing.
  - A 1.x fork's copies count once. OpenCode 1.x's `fork()` copies each message under a new id with its time, tokens and cost, and marks nothing, so the reader keys each request by a fingerprint (time, step, model, tokens and cost as written) and each prompt by its time and text, and passes over one the import has read. A 2.x row without a fork mark is keyed the same way. OpenCode's reader orders a home's sessions oldest first (`LocatorSize.created`, a reader's `order` takes an `OrderKey`), so a source is read before its forks. The cursor keeps its read's fingerprints (`owned`), so a session read again is no copy of itself. A prompt's fingerprint is its turn's `uuids` (serve's `record_uuids`). serve seeds the request and prompt fingerprints of the OpenCode runs in its store, so a fork imported after its source counts its own requests and prompts alone. The known-answer key of a database session is the sha256 of `<db path relative to the home>#<session id>`.
  - The cursor holds the database's device and inode and a stamp of the session's rows. An unchanged session is not read again, a changed one is read again whole, and a replaced database is read from its start. A turns: false cursor (parseHome's state) holds no prompt, title or working directory, as a line source's does, so a read resumed from it gives none.
  - Each step of an OpenCode message is one request, at its `step-finish` usage. `normalizeUsage("opencode", …)` adds the reasoning to `output` and keeps it as `reasoning`. OpenCode wrote the reasoning into `output` until 1.3.16 (anomalyco/opencode#21047), so `normalizeUsage(format, raw, { version })` keeps the output as written for a session whose `version` is older; the options are optional, and no version reads as today's. Where a step records `total`, the total says it whatever the version.
  - A request OpenCode ran on its claude-agent provider names the Claude Code session that also holds it (`mirrors`, per request and per session). When `parseHome` reads that Claude Code session in the same call, the request counts there and not again in OpenCode's totals (tokens, calls, cost). Otherwise it counts in OpenCode's.
  - `parseHome` adds a subagent's own written cost to its parent's for every source except Claude Code, whose `cost-state` already holds it. OpenCode's subagents are sessions of their own.
  - A reader may give `stat(locator)`: the session's own size and last write. OpenCode's is the session's rows' (their `data` bytes, their latest `time_updated`), not its database's. `locatorSize` exports it, falling back to the file's, and `inOrder` returns it with each locator.
  - The mirror rule is one export, `mirroredIn` with `sessionKey` and `ownRequests`, which `parseHome` and serve both use.
  - serve's import goes by each session's own size and last write: the 10-minute "still being written" check, the per-session cap and the run's 256 MiB budget. One live OpenCode session leaves the rest of its database importable, and a database over the budget imports every session that fits.
  - serve's import holds back an OpenCode run whose request ran through a Claude Code session that is on disk and not imported now (still written, held back with a live subagent, in a project not chosen, or of a source this import does not read: with `--from opencode` alone it lists Claude Code's sessions to know), said under a new left-out kind, `mirror`. It comes in with that session, so the request counts once in either order. A session no import brings in as it is (over the cap, unreadable, a temp or gone folder, none of the person's messages) does not hold it.
  - serve's import counts a mirrored request once: when the Claude Code session it mirrors is already in the store, or this import saved it, the OpenCode run's metrics, cost and estimate leave it out. The import writes Claude Code's runs first, so the session a request mirrors (an OpenCode run's own or a subagent's at any depth) is saved before the run that leaves it the request. Every other source's runs follow in their own order, so an OpenCode session comes before its later forks and keeps the records they copied, its subagents read with it. One that is not saved (unreadable, too large, a stop before it) leaves the request in the OpenCode run. The turn stays in the OpenCode transcript either way. When it counts elsewhere, its answer carries `data.mirrors`, and the timeline shows it and counts no request. A Claude Code session imported later cannot reach back into the OpenCode run, so that run waits for it (above).
  - A `turns: false` read of OpenCode keeps no answer text, in its requests or its cursor, as the other readers do. A request's error reads as `failed` (`FAILED`), never the provider's message.
  - A time OpenCode wrote past now (a clock set ahead, or past what a Date holds) reads as its database's last write (its file's or its `-wal`'s, never past now), in a session's times and its `stat`. That is the same at each look, so the session ages out of the 10-minute "still being written" window as its database does, and never holds back its parent run for ever.
  - OpenCode's databases are opened read-only with a 5 s busy timeout, so a read waits out OpenCode's write lock instead of failing. A database OpenCode has closed (no `-wal`, no `-shm` beside it) is opened `immutable`, as a read-only open of a WAL database would create both in OpenCode's folder and leave them there, owned by whoever read. A read that finds OpenCode opened or wrote the database meanwhile (its `-wal` or `-shm` there after, or the file's size, time or inode changed) fails, and the next import reads it again. A read adds its fingerprints to `seen` only once it ends clean, so one that fails partway takes none of its records from a later fork. With either file there, OpenCode has it open and it is opened as before, its `-wal` rows read.
  - The JSON storage is read by its own files' names: a session's messages under `message/<its file's name>`, a message's parts under `part/<its file's name>`. Never by an id a file holds, and never through a linked folder. A session whose id is not an OpenCode id (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) is passed over.
  - A session OpenCode is still running is live (its `stat` says written now), whatever its rows' times say: a 2.x session whose `time_busy` is after its `time_idle`, and a 1.x or storage session whose last message is a request not completed or has a tool part pending or running. A request its error ended (failed, or aborted: stopped, as its read says) has ended, completed or not. One parked on a permission prompt past 10 minutes is not imported as finished.
  - An OpenCode database that cannot be listed (not a database, unreadable) is a locator of its own, whose read fails: `parseHome` hands it back among its `failures` and the known-answer CLI exits 1, never an OpenCode history of no sessions. A storage session is told from a database by its name (`.json`), never by reading the file's header. A storage session whose file or folder cannot be read (no access, an I/O error) fails its read whole, never read as fewer messages. A record that is gone mid-read, or is malformed JSON, is passed over.
  - A session whose own size cannot be had (its database locked or damaged since it was listed) is no longer dropped from `inOrder`. It is kept, marked `failed`. `parseHome` reads it, and a read that fails too lands among its `failures`. serve's plan leaves it out as `unread`, said. Only a session that is gone (its reader's `stat` says none, or its file is missing) is passed over.
  - The store's SQL guard (`scripts/store-sql-guard.test.mjs`) allows SQL outside the store in one named file, the OpenCode reader. It reads OpenCode's own database, not agentrun's. The guard holds it to SELECT statements (and its busy timeout) only and to read-only opens: `bun:sqlite`'s `{ readonly: true }`, or SQLite's read-only and URI flags alone, for the `immutable` URI. The guard also finds a driver module named through a const (`const NODE_SQLITE = "node:sqlite"; await import(NODE_SQLITE)`) and counts `bun:sqlite` as a driver.
  - serve finds each source's folders where its environment puts them (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, OpenCode's `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `OPENCODE_DB`), as `parseHome` does.
  - An imported run's cost holds its subagents' costs where the source writes them on the subagent's session (every source but Claude Code, whose cost already holds them): `withSubagentCosts`, which `parseHome` uses too. One unknown makes the run's unknown.
  - serve's import brings a run in only when every subagent it has, at any depth, can be read now. The plan walks the import's children relation (Claude Code's subagent files, Codex child threads, OpenCode child sessions). If any one is still being written or is over the cap, the run is left out with it, said as `live` (or `large`), and it comes in whole later. A live subagent's listing ties it to its run. One over the cap is not read, so it is tied by `locatorParent`: the parent its reader's `stat` names (OpenCode's), else its reader's `parentOf`, a bounded head read (Codex's: a rollout's first line, `session_meta`, read 256 KiB at a time up to 64 MiB, so a long `session_meta` still names its parent).
  - serve imports OpenCode runs under an `opencode` revision whose instructions are the project's AGENTS.md, else its CLAUDE.md. The project's `.opencode/skills` and `.opencode/skill` folders, where OpenCode reads a project's skills, are among its skill folders. A home's global skills (`~/.config/opencode/skill(s)`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR`) are not imported, as no harness's are.
  - serve: the `imported_from.source` and `by_source` enums and `ImportSource` include `opencode`, and `agentrun-serve import --from` takes it.
- A learned workflow's check now judges each `agree_on` field (else the whole answer) against a grade's expected answer where one exists, else the agent's answer, and a hold names the fields that failed and the known answers the draft missed. <!-- changes/learning-check-per-field.md -->
- The models of this machine's Ollama run on codex and opencode too, and on a harness module on OpenAI's Responses. A Responses request goes through the same translation as pi's and the Messages harnesses' (`/api/chat`, `num_ctx`, tools as text where a model needs it), at $0, never counted toward `AGENTRUN_FREE_MODEL_REQUESTS`. They are listed in those harnesses' models and free models. The trust rules are unchanged: Ollama at the default address only on one owner's own server, and elsewhere only where `OLLAMA_HOST` names it. <!-- changes/responses-wire-ollama.md -->
  - On upgrade: on a server with no model key and Ollama running, codex and opencode now start the runs they refused before, on Ollama's first model that calls tools. A saved agent on either harness that names no model follows that default. Name the model to pin it. Any key wins.
  - Each request is the whole conversation. `store: true` and `previous_response_id` are refused with a 400 that says so. Replayed reasoning, OpenAI's encrypted reasoning included, is dropped.
  - Function tools only. A custom (freeform) tool, `local_shell` and `web_search` are refused with a 400 naming the tool, never dropped. codex offers no live web search on these models.
  - A `tool_choice` that forces a call (`"required"`, or one naming a function) is refused with a 400: Ollama can't be made to call a tool. `"auto"` and `"none"` are taken.
  - `text.format` `json_schema` is Ollama's own `format`: the answer is held to the schema. `json_object` is held to any JSON object. Beside tools sent, a format is refused with a 400, since a model held to a format can't call a tool: codex's `--output-schema` (an output schema on every turn, with its tools) stops running on these models. Drop the output schema, or use a model route that takes tools with a format. A format of another type is refused too.
  - `temperature` and `top_p` reach Ollama's options. On a thinking model, `reasoning.effort` turns Ollama's thinking on, and `"none"` turns it off. An effort the route doesn't know is refused.
  - `parallel_tool_calls: false` (codex sends it for a model it doesn't know) gets an answer's first tool call alone: Ollama has no switch for one call per answer. The calls it drops are logged by count and tool name.
  - A request streams only with `stream: true`. One that names no stream gets the whole response as one JSON body, as OpenAI's API answers it.
  - codex and opencode are told the model's window as the route runs it (its `num_ctx`: the model's trained context, at most 64k, at most `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`), not their 272,000 default, so they compact before Ollama would cut the prompt.
  - Their output ceiling is the route's too (half the window, at most 16,384), not their 32,000 default.
  - An answer cut at its output limit ends `response.incomplete` (`max_output_tokens`) with its usage: it is booked, and codex ends the turn instead of asking again.
  - Every model id a client sends (codex's title and compaction requests, opencode's small model) runs the one tag.
- `GET /v2/runs` takes `from`, `to` and `model`, for any run, whether made here or imported. `from` and `to` are RFC 3339 date-times with their zone (`2026-11-01T00:00:00Z`, or an offset such as `+01:00`). They list the runs started in [from, to): a run that started exactly at `from` is in, and one that started exactly at `to` is out. Either one can be given alone. An imported run starts when its session did. `model` lists the runs that sent at least one request to that model, named exactly as a run's metrics name it (no prefix, no case folding), `provider/model` (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`, `openai/gpt-5`). A run counts from its first finished turn: its metrics are written each time a turn ends, covering every turn so far, so a run in its first turn is not listed yet, and a model it first uses in a later turn counts once that turn ends. The server reads no time zone; the console turns its own dates into instants. The console's runs list keeps all three in the address (`#/runs?from=...&to=...&model=...`, each with a button that clears it). The CLI, the TypeScript client and the Python client send them as `--from`/`--to`/`--model`, `from`/`to`/`model` and `from_=`/`to=`/`model=`. A window or a model that no run has lists none. These are 400: a `from` after `to`, a value that is not a date-time with its zone, an empty model, and a second value for any of the three. <!-- changes/runs-filters.md -->
- Goose 1.59.2 no longer asks permission for a call of one of AgentRun's tools, and the ACP adapter no longer reads Goose's titles. Before, it tied `agentrun: <tool>` (with or without Goose's summary, `agentrun: write · proof.txt`) to our tool and answered `allow_once`, and a title in a form it did not read reached the tool gate as Goose's own call and stopped the run at input_required. <!-- changes/acp-announces.md -->
  - A recipe's new `allowFile` (`{ path, form }`) is written into the private HOME at each start from the tools that start lists. Goose's recipe declares its permission file, `.config/goose/permission.yaml` in the form `goose-permission`, every tool allowed as `agentrun__<tool>` and nothing else, so the gate asks once, at the MCP call.
  - The adapter answers a permission request `allow_once` without the gate only where the recipe declares `quirks.permissionTie: "title"`: Cursor's recipe, since its allowlist asks for every MCP call, and the Antigravity example's, since agy asks for every one too. Every other request goes to the host's gate, journaled, whatever its title says.
  - A recipe's new `announces` field says where the agent's `tool_call` names the tool it calls: Goose 1.59.2's `_meta.goose.toolCall.toolName` (`agentrun__<tool>`), Cursor's late update's `rawInput` (`providerIdentifier`, `toolName`, `args`), agy's `name` (`mcp_agentrun_<tool>`, its `prefix`). Its `extras` names fields an agent writes beside the arguments that the MCP call never carries (agy's `toolSummary`), left out before the two are matched. A path that starts at the `tool_call`'s `title`, `toolCallId`, `kind`, `status`, `rawOutput`, `content`, `locations` or `sessionUpdate` is refused (the agent's text or a tool's output), and a recipe with the title tie and no `announces` is refused. A call is matched to its MCP call by that tool and its arguments, never by a title. A call it names as another tool (Goose's own `load_skill` with the same arguments) never takes our call's id, so the resume memo keys our call under its own id.
  - A title naming our tool on a call of the agent's own (a read titled `agentrun__write`) no longer marks it ours, so Cursor's tie never answers its request; the host's gate does.
  - The host gate's question about an agent's permission request carries the request's `toolCallId` in its `args`. `agentrun harness-check` matches a permission request to `check_echo` by that `toolCallId` or by the check's nonce as its input's `text`, never by its title. Its `mcp_tool` row counts every request (`permissionAsks`) and those for `check_echo` (`ourAsks`); a request for the agent's own call fails no stage. A recipe file passes `allowFile`, `announces` and `quirks` through.
  - `AGENTRUN_LOG=debug` makes serve write into a run's log one line per call an ACP agent announces, on a recipe that declares `announces`: `acp: the agent announced a call`, with the call's `toolCallId`, its `kind`, the tool name the recipe's field holds when it names an AgentRun tool (at most 200 characters; `native` for any other call, since a recipe's field may sit inside the call's input) and the AgentRun tool it named, never the call's input. A call announced with no name (Cursor's) gets the line again when a later update names it. Unset or `quiet`, no such line is written.
- A server's address has one name in an app's environment, `AGENTRUN_BASE_URL`, the name AgentRun's clients and CLI read. A suggested agent's pull request and client file, the two lines the console's AgentRun API keys page copies, and the Suggested agents page's "Set in your app's environment" list all named it `AGENTRUN_URL`, so an app that also used the SDK or the CLI held the same address under two names. <!-- changes/agentrun-base-url-one-name.md -->

  - Each of them now gives the value the server prints when it starts: the address ending in `/v2`. The page of HTTP calls written for a language with no client adds no `/v2` to its paths.
  - A suggested agent's client (TypeScript, JavaScript or Python) reads `AGENTRUN_BASE_URL` and takes it with or without `/v2`, trailing slashes cut, as the SDK does. An address that is no `http` or `https` URL is refused by the variable's name before anything is sent.
  - A client file from a pull request opened before this release still reads `AGENTRUN_URL`, as its own header and its pull request say. An app with one of each sets both: `AGENTRUN_URL` stays the address without `/v2`, which that file adds itself. A create whose branch was pushed before this release and whose pull request GitHub refused opens that pull request when Create is sent again: its text says `AGENTRUN_BASE_URL` while the pushed file reads `AGENTRUN_URL`. For that file, set `AGENTRUN_URL` to the address without `/v2`.
- The Antigravity example recipe names agy's calls of AgentRun's tools by the field agy writes them in, `name` (`mcp_agentrun_<tool>`): `announces` with `prefix: "mcp_agentrun_"`, and `extras: ["toolSummary"]`, so the summary agy adds to the arguments it reports is left out when the call is matched to its MCP call. agy asks permission for every MCP call, so the recipe declares the title tie: a request titled `Run mcp_agentrun_<tool>`, the whole text, for a call `announces` named as that same tool, is answered allow once, with the host's gate asked at the MCP call itself, as for Cursor. The Antigravity example recipe now passes `harness-check` (agy 1.5.14): it declares MCP over stdio, since agy advertises no MCP over HTTP, and names `.gemini/antigravity-cli/conversations` as its state, so a resume after a kill and another runner both load the conversation. <!-- changes/antigravity-recipe-check.md -->
- A change for callers: an approval's note (`POST /runs/{run_id}/approvals/{approval_id}`) is now cut of the keys the run holds before it is written into the run, as a message is. A run whose launch's sealed part won't open under this server's seal key now refuses a note with `409 not_continuable`, `details.reason` `withheld`, and nothing is written. Before, the note was written whole, so a deny note that repeated one of the run's keys kept it in the run's command rows, and the run's view showed it once its end erased the key. An answer with no note is taken as before. <!-- changes/approval-note-cut.md -->

  `template eval` no longer cancels a run at one claim read that finds no runner when a runner already took the run and its view later reads queued again (a workflow run between steps, a run waiting for a place after a cap raise, a steer not yet taken). A page that isn't queued now counts as the run held, so the queue bound starts over from there.
- A read of the ChatGPT sign-in that was out while a sign-in was kept, or while a sign-out removed it, no longer undoes their state: the server stays signed in or signed out as they left it. A server that stops while a pasted sign-in is still listing its models waits up to 2 seconds for it, so the sign-in is saved before the store closes. <!-- changes/b50-plan-close-followups.md -->

  `agentrun start` keeps in `start.log` only a line in the server's exact shape of a sign-in's failure, at most 64 KiB of them after the start. A second start on the same data folder no longer leaves the first's later lines over its log or after a run of NUL bytes.
- A model the runner's route translates onto a harness's wire (this machine's Ollama models on Anthropic's Messages and OpenAI's Responses) is offered only to a harness whose proxy forwards with the route's `fetch`, and the Messages translation no longer drops what it can't run. Before, any harness on the wire was offered those models, including a module that sends its requests to the network, where nothing answers. <!-- changes/b51-route-hints.md -->
  - `AdapterFacts` gains `forwardsRoute`. claude-agent, Goose, codex and opencode set it, and so does every recipe that builds on Goose's facts. A harness without it is offered none of the route's models, takes none as its default, and its words say to add a key ("No model yet for <harness>: add an OpenRouter or Anthropic key"). A run that names one is refused before it starts.
  - An output schema (`output_config.format` of type `json_schema`) on a Messages request with no tools now reaches Ollama as its `format`. Before, it was dropped and the answer came back unconstrained. Beside tools it is refused with a 400 `invalid_request_error` that says to drop the output schema or use a model route that takes tools with a format, because Ollama holds the whole answer to the format and leaves the model no way to call a tool.
  - The Messages translation answers `POST /v1/messages` and `POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` alone. Any other method or path is a 404 `not_found_error` in Anthropic's error shape, and nothing reaches Ollama.
  - `agentrun harness-check` on a model the route translates (`--model ollama/<tag>`) now reaches it. Its recorder wraps the route's own fetch, so the recipe's agent gets the same route a server's run gets and the check still sees every request. Before, every request went to the route's placeholder origin and `mcp_tool` failed.
- A server in AgentRun's image with no Docker socket (Fly.io, Render, a Kubernetes pod) now says what Settings → Computers says: use a vendor computer, or, on a machine you run, give it the host's socket with compose.yaml. A `--faux` server in the image says the image's words too. <!-- changes/box-reason-hosted.md -->
- A browser session kept across a reopen no longer holds its down time twice under a spend cap: once its first charge after the reopen books that time, its reserve on the run's ledger is one stretch again, so the run's next call is no longer refused for room the run never spends. <!-- changes/browser-reserve-one-stretch.md -->
  A new browser session whose reserve the cap refuses now pauses the run in the cap's words and logs `browser_reserve_refused`, where before the refusal went unread and the session ran on with its next stretch held nowhere.
- Capabilities now mark a tool that runs only on the server `runner_only: true` (the browser), as they mark a box-only one `sandbox_only`. The console's Tools step reads it. A tool card now states every rule that keeps its tool off here, together: the harnesses that run it, where it runs, and what it lacks. For the browser on Claude, in a box place, it says "Runs on Pi here, not on Claude; Server-only: it runs on the server, and this agent's place is the docker box". Before, a card stated one rule at a time. On Claude it named only the harness. On pi, in a box place, it said nothing, and the save was then refused. <!-- changes/browser-states-every-rule.md -->
- A stopped or cancelled run's kept desktop, phone or sandbox is now deleted when the run ends, by whichever runner ends it, instead of staying up until its 10 minutes pass; a Docker container on another runner's host is deleted by that runner, as before. When the runner that kept a machine refuses new runs, the run resumes on another runner with a new machine, the timeline says the runner that kept the old one ends it, and that runner does. The timeline says a park kept its machine only once the keep is saved, GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/computer says a machine whose keep ended early wasn't kept, and the 10 minutes run on the store's clock, so a runner whose clock is off no longer moves them and GET /v2/runs/{run_id} on a server whose clock is off no longer says the machine released while it is still kept. <!-- changes/claim-affinity-followups.md -->
- Capabilities' `features.claude_login` and the Claude Code login routes now read one answer, so they can't disagree. In Settings → API Keys, a login turn-on or turn-off that answers after capabilities hid the row no longer puts the row back. <!-- changes/claude-login-served-secretlint-pins.md -->
- The runner's hold of Claude Code's refresh lock on AgentRun's own login folder, where each run is a user of its own, is steadier. A runner whose new lock is gone at its first touch (another holder took it) waits for that holder and takes its renewal, instead of failing the ask. A runner whose read of its own lock or `.takeover` directory fails on release (an I/O error, not the lock gone) reads it once more and removes it while it is still its own, instead of leaving it for the 60 s stale time. A failed read of the lock just before or after the renewal is sent is logged as `lock_unread`, no longer as `lock_lost`, which now means only that another holder took the lock. A renewal whose save could not read the login's file (an I/O error, not the file gone) keeps the renewed pair in memory and saves it at the next ask, logged as `file_unread`, instead of forgetting it: when Anthropic rotated the refresh token, that pair held the only one left, and later asks could not renew. An ask that reads the login's file while a renewal that got a new refresh token is still saving it now waits for that renewal and is handed its token, instead of being refused for the refresh token the renewal just spent; so is one whose read ends just after a renewal that could not save its new pair settled, handed the pair held in memory. The runner's reader of the login now says each renewal's outcome on the runner's log, as `event=claude_login` lines with no token in them (a renewal that failed or was refused, a save held, a lock lost or unread); before, it said none. A renewal writes its new pair back before it says a lock lost or unread after its post, so a log that fails there never loses the pair, and a second ask's save of a held pair another ask already saved is said as `reason=already_saved`, never as `reason=newer`, which means another holder's pair. And a run that is a process of its own runs on the login only if its claim read it on, so turning the login on just after such a run is claimed never moves it onto a login its claim did not check. <!-- changes/claude-login-token-followups.md -->
- A claude-agent or codex run paused at its cap and raised now shows the server's follow-up ("The cap was raised to …; continue the task.", as the server's) on its timeline and in its record, as a pi run does. <!-- changes/cli-raise-follow-up-row.md -->
- Add from Composio takes a typed toolkit slug again when Composio's toolkit list fails or leaves the toolkit out, and **Cancel** works while a list loads. A key edit or Cancel stops the load. The toolkit listing gives up after 30 seconds in all, and any Composio answer over 4 MiB is refused. Only an account Composio names as the server's user's connects a server, labels it, or runs its trigger: one Composio answers as another user's, or with no user at all, never does (`composio_not_connected`), and the user connects one again. A trigger on a server whose saved Composio user is blank is refused before Composio is asked anything; the server's own Composio routes (its events, its triggers, the project's subscription) and its delete still work. An account a refresh kept on 0.1.0-beta.57 or beta.58, which could be another user's, isn't shown: the server shows no account line until its next **Refresh**. <!-- changes/composio-picker-fallback.md -->
- A desktop, phone or sandbox turned off for the rest of a run (its tools refused for a deny) is no longer kept when the run parks: it is deleted at the park, as at the run's end, and its mount credential for the run's folder is revoked. Before, it was kept and billed for 10 minutes that no later part of the run could use. <!-- changes/computer-off-followups.md -->
- A plain `npm install` of the server now brings the vendor SDKs its computer providers load (e2b, modal, @boxd-sh/sdk, ssh2 and Archil's `disk`), as pinned optional dependencies of `@parcha/agentrun-computer`, so E2B's "Test connection" no longer fails with "Cannot find package 'e2b'". Installed without them (`--omit=optional`), a provider says the package and its install step, such as `E2B needs the e2b package: npm install e2b@2.63.0`. In Mode 1, a sandbox provider that could hold the run's folder on an Archil disk now says to turn on Archil in Settings → Workspace. <!-- changes/computer-vendor-sdk-deps.md -->
- A desktop's or a phone's live view draws its screen at your display's own pixels, so it stays sharp at any size, the console's full-window view and a high-density display included. The view used to draw each frame at the frame's size and let the browser stretch it to fit, which blurred text. A view whose box has the screen's shape is filled to its edges, and resizing it redraws the screen at the new size at once. <!-- changes/computer-viewer-sharp.md -->
- On a server that sends its models to a gateway, the first screen's card no longer offers the ChatGPT sign-in or a provider key where neither runs an agent: with no gateway model named it says to name one (AGENT_MODEL, or Settings → Model keys → Use a model gateway), and with a gateway address AgentRun refuses it says why, in the server's words. `GET /v2/settings/model-gateway`'s `problem`, which Settings → Model keys → Use a model gateway shows too, now gives every refusal a run meets, Particle's API among them, not only the address rule's, and saving or testing a gateway there refuses Particle's API the same way. The card reads that view again with each new read of the capabilities, so an address fixed at a restart stops showing refused. Where the gateway server's own default is a plan model (`AGENT_MODEL=chatgpt/…`), the card offers the ChatGPT sign-in, which runs it. A plan model a gateway names under its prefix (`agent-model/chatgpt/…`) reads as the plan's ("… · on your ChatGPT plan") wherever a model is labelled. <!-- changes/console-gateway-card.md -->
- A Docker computer's egress proxy no longer outlives it. A delete now finds the proxy first and removes the computer and its proxy in one `docker rm`, so a teardown cut off partway (the process running it ended, as a one-shot server's close can) never leaves a proxy running with no computer. A computer whose own removal fails, on a release or after a create that was cut off or whose computer never started, still has its proxy and volume removed, and the computer's failure is still the answer. Before, a failure or an exit between the two calls left the proxy running until its 24 hour deadline. <!-- changes/docker-egress-teardown.md -->

  - `sweepLeftovers` and the janitor's `sweep` take `mine`: given a leftover's labels, whether it is the caller's to remove. Without it, every leftover with the sweep's labels goes, as before.
  - serve's computer janitor now sweeps Docker's leftovers at the runner's start and on its interval, for this server's alone: a proxy or volume whose `agentrun.run` label (or its hash) names a run in this store that no claim holds. Another server's on the same Docker host is left for that server's own sweep.
  - Docker's `sweepLeftovers` never removes a proxy or volume whose computer is there: it reads the computer by name right before each removal, after `mine`, and a read that fails keeps the part. A past deadline no longer overrides a running computer, and a computer made while the sweep runs keeps its proxy. A part with an owner label is never removed.
  - A release (delete) now runs `docker ps` for the proxy before its `docker rm`, and a stop looks for the proxy before it stops the computer.
- A saved harness key with no binding to any recipe file now says so: `reenter.why` is `not_bound`, not `recipe_changed`. That covers a key saved before keys were bound and one whose binding write was cut off. Upgrading from 0.1.0-beta.56 or earlier: every harness key saved then has read as not saved since 0.1.0-beta.57, the first release that binds keys (there as `recipe_changed`, now `not_bound`), and its runs have been refused since; paste each such key again on the Harness keys page. The Harness keys page says "Not tied to a recipe file" beside it. Such a key reads as not saved and no run gets it, so a scheduled or triggered run of that recipe is refused until each of its keys is pasted again on the Harness keys page; the old value stays sealed and cut until then. `GET /capabilities` with a bearer the server does not take still answers, with no kept ids, and now also writes an `auth_failed` line (`reason=wrong_token`) like every other route. A `DELETE` of a key the harness doesn't hold is refused with the keys it does hold ("acme's keys are ACME_API_KEY."), never "acme runs on …" for an id no recipe runs. <!-- changes/harness-keys-followups.md -->
- Behaviour change for Mode 2: MCP evidence (`evidence/mcp`) now lands on the run's disk instead of the runner's local folder for the run. Before, a claim's MCP gateway wrote to that local folder, outside the run's files. Where nothing had made the folder, it told the model a long answer "could not be saved". In pi's spec it wrote over the disk's file API instead, which the run's computer's mount refuses while it holds the disk's write delegation. Each claim path now hands the gateway the run's active Workspace: the one attached to the run's computer once that computer mounts the folder, otherwise the disk's file API. A Mode 2 run with no computer mounting its folder files no fal results (`evidence/fal`) until Parcha-ai/agentrun#3777. With one, they are filed through the computer. Mode 1 is unchanged: the run's folder on this machine, which a Docker box bind-mounts. <!-- changes/mcp-evidence-mode2-disk.md -->
- The owner's MCP server edits are no longer lost to a write that read the server earlier. A tools refresh (the owner's or the API token's) used to write back the address, auth type and prices it read over a save that landed while it listed, including a repricing in the same millisecond. Now it lands only on the server as it read it, and otherwise retries on the fresh row or is refused in words with nothing written. The owner's OAuth sign-in over a server an API token saved now makes it the owner's, as the owner's save already did. Over a server an API token saved, whose reads show only its origin, the owner's save, sign-in and preview no longer take that shown address (`https://host/…`) for the saved one: they answer `422` on `url` (`not_an_option`), so the owner's credential goes only to an address the owner named in full. <!-- changes/mcp-owner-data-guards.md -->
- An MCP server saved under a name is now always made after every earlier server of that name that a record still describes. This holds even within the same millisecond, after the clock stepped back, or when another server process sharing the database made the earlier one. Before, the new server could get the same creation time, and an owner's removal of the earlier server could then drop the record saying the API token saved the new one, so the new server read as the owner's. <!-- changes/mcp-server-made-after-records.md -->
- An MCP server the API token saves under a new name is the token's from the moment it exists. The token's first save used to write the server, then the record saying the token saved it, in two writes. An owner's preview, save or sign-in start that landed between them, sent at the address reads show (its origin), was taken as the owner naming the token's address, and the owner's credential went there. Both are now written in one store transaction, so such a request is refused under `url` (`422`), as it is once the save is done. An owner's delete of a server under that name that lands while the token saves the name again no longer drops the token's new record either: the delete removes a server's records only while they are still the ones it read. <!-- changes/mcp-token-first-save-mark.md -->
- A run's trace no longer costs or carries what it should not. Under `agentrun-serve runner`, where each run is a process of its own, a run's end waited up to 3 s on the collector, since that process flushed its own spans before it exited: now it sends its trace to its runner, which exports it in the background, and a run's process never holds an `OTEL_*` setting at all. The runner reads that trace as untrusted: every string it carries (a provider, a host, a call id, a request's or turn's end, a failure) is cut of every secret the runner holds, or taken only from values the runner knows, and a call's id, its parent's or a route's name longer than 128 characters is kept as its SHA-256, so a run's process can't hold megabytes of ids open in its runner. A name the model wrote no longer reaches a span as written: a call the harness refused (a tool the session does not have; the kernel's `tool_start` event says `refused: true`, which claude-agent now sets) is `execute_tool` with `error.type=tool_refused` and no tool name, a model the run does not know (not a route's model, nor one its price table names by that same id) is named by its route's model, and every name is cut of every secret the runner holds and at 64 characters. Each value of `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` and `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS` of 8 characters or more is now a secret the server and the runner hold, under any header name, an unknown one too, but a `Content-Type`, `Accept`, `Content-Encoding` or `User-Agent` header's value, and a dataset or tenant header's (`x-honeycomb-dataset`, `x-axiom-dataset`, `x-scope-orgid`), which is only cut from the tracer's `[otel]` lines, so a dataset named `production` refuses no source capture. A credential is held without the word before it too, after a known auth scheme (`Bearer`, `Basic`, `Api-Key`, `Api-Token`, `Token`, `sentry`, `Splunk`, `GenieKey`) or under a credential-named header (`authorization`, `x-sentry-auth`, `x-api-key`); any other header's value is held whole, never its tail alone. So are an OTLP endpoint's user, password and each query parameter named like a credential: a word of its name is a credential word or ends in key, token, secret, password, auth, sig, signature or credential (`api_key`, `access_token`, `apiKey`, `accesstoken`, `writekey`; never `authority` or `keyspace`). A comma inside a header value must be written `%2C`. The tracer's own `[otel]` lines, where an exporter's error may quote a header it sent, are cut of each such value at any length, a short one too, and of what follows any header value's first word; everywhere else (the runner's logs, what a run writes, a served run, a source capture) a held value is still cut at 8 characters or more and a shorter header value is on no held list, on purpose, since a needle of a few characters would cut ordinary text, turn a served number such as `1` into `[redacted]`, or refuse a source capture of any project that holds it. <!-- changes/otel-trace-names-and-child-export.md -->
- A run whose loop runs in a process of its own (the runner's default) now reports its browser to the server: a browser its owner took over reads `computer.state: "taken_over"` (Running now's "You drive"), and a browser let go while the run waited for its person shows the Screen tab's ended state. The run's process writes both rows itself, and the store a run's process reaches refused every settings write, so neither ever reached the server outside a test. It may now write and remove those two rows of its own run, and no other. <!-- changes/run-process-browser-rows.md -->
- The console's trigger forms (a schedule, a webhook, a GitHub trigger, an app trigger, a feed trigger and an email trigger) now take the picked agent's typed input as the run bar does. An agent whose input_schema has fields shows them under the message and sends them in `target.input` beside `content`, and the server's refusal of one of them is said at that field. An agent whose schema the fields can't show takes its whole input as JSON. Editing a schedule keeps its typed input and anything else in it the form doesn't show, saves a field left alone exactly as stored (a list item's spaces, a blank item or an empty value included), and a schedule whose input has no message can be edited again. A message left blank beside typed fields is sent as `""`, so each run still gets what the server adds to `content` (a trigger's event, a schedule's last answer); a whole JSON input goes exactly as written, and the form says what comes in its `content`. An agent whose schema limits its input's keys (`maxProperties`, `propertyNames`) takes its whole input as JSON in a trigger's form, where the message is the person's to keep or leave out. A trigger's page lists its typed input beside the message. In every trigger form's Agent picker, agents that share a name each show their id beside it. <!-- changes/schedule-typed-input.md -->
- A `codemode` script that stops at a call the run refused (a tool set to deny, a person's deny) now reads Refused on the run's Timeline, as the refused call inside it does. Before, the script's own row read as a call that ran and failed, so the console showed a red Error chip on it and a neutral Refused chip on every other refused step. The same holds for `tools_call` of a refused tool. A host tool that `nests` may now answer `refused: true` with its error; pi marks that result refused, and the other harnesses end the call refused. The console's Refused chip on a script says it stopped at a refused call, its calls before that one having run. The script's text, and what the model reads, are unchanged. <!-- changes/script-refused-reads-refused.md -->
- A missing or malformed `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` is refused in one wording wherever the key is read: what it guards, and the length it wants and has, never its value. An import or a scrub handed none points at its `--data` directory. <!-- changes/seal-key-length.md --> <!-- changes/seal-key-readers-one-refusal.md -->
- The console's app-trigger form searches its events in the Event field itself. Typing filters the open list by an event's name, slug or description, so a toolkit with hundreds of events is one field rather than a filter box above a dropdown. The search is a new console primitive, `SearchPicker` (Headless UI's Combobox, styled and wired to a `Field` as `Picker` is), for any long list. <!-- changes/searchable-event-picker.md -->
- A server's stop no longer waits out a Docker host-address read that the runner beside it started with no signal: the stop's signal cuts that read, and its helper container is removed by name within the stop's deadline. <!-- changes/serve-stop-cuts-host-read.md -->
- A template eval no longer shows a fake MCP server's call arguments raw. The llm grader's `<mcp-calls>` block and the report's `mcp_calls` were built from each fake's own log, the arguments whole, so a value the run's cut holds (a server key, a handed key, a key-shaped string) that the agent passed to a fake tool reached the grader's provider and the report as typed. The timeline's copy of the same call was cut. Both now come from the run's timeline under its cut: the calls on a faked server's tools that ran, meaning not refused before they ran and with a result. A call that failed on its way to the fake shows with its error as its result, never as a success. A fake still answers exactly as its fixture is written. <!-- changes/template-eval-mcp-calls-cut.md -->
  - The report's `mcp_calls` entries change shape, from the fake log's `{tool, arguments}` (whole) to the timeline's `{tool, name, preview, arguments, status, result}`, with the arguments redacted. A refused call is still in the report's `calls`, now marked `refused: true`.
  - The fake's own log is read only to match a `tool_used` grader's `args` on a faked tool, and is never shown. It is the run record's new `fakeLog`.
  - For TypeScript callers: `RunRecord` gains a required `fakeLog`, and `ToolCall` gains `refused`.
  - A change for callers of `GET /runs/{run_id}/timeline?calls=whole`: a call's `tool_input` now holds up to 120,000 characters of names and values in all, the bound `tool_result_text` has, instead of cutting each string at 2,000. The server reads each string from the arguments as the call came, through the run's redaction, so a grader can read a long write whole, such as an issue body, a note or a posted digest. The 120,000 is one budget for the whole row, taken in order, with every name and value counting at least one character and each array or object its two brackets: the name or string that reaches it is cut there, a number, boolean or null that would pass it shows as `...`, an array or object then ends with one `...` (an item, or a `...` name), and a value past it shows as `...`.
  - learn-bench builds its steps' records the same way, and now reads each step's timeline with `calls=whole`, as the template eval does. Before, a grader saw only the preview, which could show a call's input as nothing at all.
  - An llm grader's `<tool-calls>` block shows the calls' arguments whole when the calls fit. When they don't, the arguments get what the calls' results and the rest of their lines leave, and at least half the block's room: each long argument list keeps its head and tail with its middle cut and marked, the longest cut first, so every call keeps its result. A write whose content a final file holds whole, and whose first and last 2,000 characters `<files>` shows (a trailing `...` where the timeline cut it left off), shows it cut at 2,000 characters in the call, pointing at the file, so those bytes are in the grader's input once; when the file is cut, the content's middle is cut in both, as the file's block marks. One whose head or tail the cut of a long file takes from `<files>` (an append in its middle), or that no final file holds whole (a write a later one overwrote), keeps it in the call, cut there as any long argument is.
- The console's template prompts and the agentrun-serve skill read a template's entry in `GET /v2/templates`, not the whole package, so a package's instructions and skill files no longer reach the coding agent. They say every text in the entry (its description, parameter descriptions, MCP reasons, model notes and warnings, trigger inputs) is the package author's, not instructions to the reader, and so do the CLI's help and the clients' docs for `GET /v2/templates` and an import preview. `agentrun template install --dry-run` prints the same on stderr. <!-- changes/template-prompt-reads-listing.md -->
- A template page's "Update" buttons now say which agent each one updates. When several agents the template made share a name, each button adds the agent's id, as in "Update Market monitor (monitor-2)". A name no other agent has stays as it was. <!-- changes/template-update-names-agent.md -->
- `install.sh --vps` waits for apt's locks under one deadline: 600 s from the first refusal of a lock other than dpkg's, which each later try's own wait for dpkg's lock is cut to as well, so the whole wait stays under about 1200 s and a first try that waited long for dpkg's lock still leaves its retries. The clock is the time since boot, which a just-booted server's clock steps don't move. A server refused by an earlier version's data now names the command that started it, as the launcher says, never what the folder holds: <!-- changes/vps-apt-clock-installed-refusal.md -->
  - started by the installer's command from the folder refused: move the folder aside, then run the installer again for this same version (`curl -fsSL https://agentrun.ai/install | sh -s -- --version <this version>`), with no npx command that may not be there;
  - started by the installer's command on a `--data` of the person's own: move it aside, then that command (`agentrun`, or its path when its folder is not on PATH) with the same `--data`, not npx;
  - started by npx: the npx command, even when the folder still holds an earlier install's `bin/agentrun`.

  Each says how the earlier version opens the folder moved aside.
- `web_save` now saves a text file a host serves with no type (`application/octet-stream`, `binary/octet-stream`, `application/binary` or no Content-Type) to a `.txt` or a `.csv`, and a file a host declares XML (`application/xml`, `text/xml`) to a `.txt` alone, when the whole file is UTF-8 with no NUL byte. It answers `text/plain` or `text/csv`. Before, both were refused, so an agent could not save a list published that way, such as a sanctions list's CSV or XML download. Bytes that are not UTF-8 text, or hold a NUL anywhere, are still refused and nothing is written. Declared XML is refused at `.xml`, `.csv` or `.html`, so nothing parses it as XML or XHTML. Untyped text is still refused at any other extension. A declared page, SVG, XHTML or script is refused at `.txt` or `.csv`. The 200 MiB size cap is unchanged. The run's files route serves these files as it serves every saved text file: `text/plain` or `text/csv` with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, inline, and as an attachment with `?download=1`. <!-- changes/web-save-text-lists.md -->
- The OpenAPI description of `POST /v2/triggers/{trigger_id}/firings/{firing_id}/release` now says what the server already does. A release waits out the engine's whole turn on the firing, a hook call still open included, not only while the hook's answer is being written. After a transport error, the host sends the same call again: a firing already released answers 200 with it, unchanged, whatever its words. Or it reads the firing in the trigger's firings. Releases alone turn a trigger off only after the failures in a row that pause it land with no 2xx between them, and any other failed firing counts in the same streak. No behaviour changes. <!-- changes/trigger-release-wait-docs.md -->
- An ended run can be exported as a share bundle: `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/export` (and `agentrun runs export RUN`) answers one `agentrun.share/1` JSON document with the run's allowlisted view fields, its Timeline rows, a workflow's graph, its UTF-8 text files within the caps, what was left out and why, and a sha256. Strings in it pass through the server's scrubber. Each cut is a record with its place, rule, kind and shape, never its value. A value beside a label and a personal detail can be put back with `?restore=<cut ids>`. Two exports of the same run are the same bytes. A run still at work answers 409, a withheld run 403, a bundle over 8 MiB 413, and a scrub that fails answers 500 with an empty body. <!-- changes/share-export-bundle.md -->
  A tool's output in the bundle (a result's preview, an approval outcome's text, a workflow call's output) is cut knowing the file the call read or the command it ran, so a read of `~/.pgpass` or the output of `env` is one dump cut, and `agentrun-serve scrub` counts it the same way.
- A template eval's `tool_used` grader takes `at_most: <n>`: it passes on 1 to n matching calls (its `args` filter first, as `count`'s and `at_least`'s do), and beside `at_least` on any number between the two, so "fetched robots.txt at least 3 and at most 4 times" is one grader. A failing grade names the run's count and both bounds ("5 calls of web_fetch; the grader expects at least 3 and at most 4"). An `at_most` under 1 (none is `expect: not_called`'s to say), one beside `count` or `expect: not_called`, or an `at_least` above it is refused in words. <!-- changes/tool-used-at-most.md -->
- The console's Wrapped page draws its share cards, as 1200 by 675 images under the year's sections. Each card's words are its image's alt text. Four cards are drawn: "Your year in agents" (tokens, sessions, prompts, model requests, days at work and list price), "Where your tokens went" (each harness's and model's share of the tokens), "When your agents work" (the busiest hour and weekday, time at work, and requests by hour and by weekday) and a one-card summary. A card's numbers all come from `GET /v2/wrapped`. <!-- changes/wrapped-cards.md -->
  - A list price stays "Unknown" when no request had a known price, never $0. Requests with no known price are counted on the card beside the price.
  - Harnesses are named as the rest of the console names them (Claude, Codex, Pi, OpenCode), on the cards and in the page's harness list.
  - A harness or model list longer than its card has room for shows the largest that fit, and the rest are added up in one "other" bar.
  - When session files could not be read, each card says its numbers may be incomplete.
  - A year with no sessions draws no cards.
  - The cache grade, laptop, leak receipt, agent type and launch cards are not drawn yet. They each wait on something the year's answer does not have yet: the cache analyzer, the leak scan's counts-only mode, the launch benchmark, or rules that need subagent shares, parallelism, a month's cost and an electricity estimate.
- The Claude login on this machine now uses the folders the server's env gives it only when they belong to the server's own user, as it already did for the home. Those folders are `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CLAUDE_SECURESTORAGE_CONFIG_DIR`, and `ANTHROPIC_CONFIG_DIR` or else `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`'s `anthropic`. Each one must be a folder that user owns, or a folder still to be made inside one it owns. The home and these folders are judged by one rule, so that no other user can change where the path leads after the check: <!-- changes/claude-login-config-dirs.md -->

  - The path is walked as the system walks it, one name at a time, so a trailing slash, `.` or `..` hides nothing, and a `..` after a link goes up from where the link leads. Each link on the way, and each link in the chain it leads through, must be one that user or root made.
  - Each folder above the real folder must be that user's or root's, and not one others may write in (anyone, or its group, unless that group is the user's private one), unless the sticky bit keeps each entry its maker's (as /tmp has it).
  - The folder itself must be that user's and not open to others' writes by the same rule. So must the folder a still-to-make one is made in, sticky or not, so a folder still to make in /tmp is refused, root's included.
  - The CLI gets the real path the check looked at (the home included), from the same look: each decision (a run, the sign-in, the Settings view's line and status check, a turn-on) walks the folders once and takes the login, or the refusal, from that walk, never the path as given. Where the folders are refused, the view's `command` is empty and its `folder` is the folder as the env names it. Where the env's path has a link on it, the shown sign-in line and the CLI now name the folder the link leads to. On macOS the CLI names its Keychain item after that folder, so a login the person's own Claude CLI keeps under a path with a link reads as signed out until it is signed in again from here.

  A server started under a sudo that keeps the env (root, with the person's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) no longer signs the Claude CLI in as root inside the person's folder. Where a folder fails the check, the turn-on and the sign-in at this machine's login are refused (403) in words that name the variable and the folder, and no run goes on the login. AgentRun's own login keeps its folders in the data folder, so the env's folders refuse nothing there, but the home rule above applies to both places. A login saved before on folders, the home's included, that fail the check is kept, not turned off: the start logs why it is not used, every read refuses it in those words, and it is back once the folder is mended (a chmod, or the server started as the right user). A chmod needs no restart: a run's check, a save's, a template's plan or apply, and capabilities look at the folders again, so the login is offered and runs again as soon as the view reads it signed in, and stops again once its folder is refused. Such a request asked while the server is still making the offers again from such a change, or from a turn-on or turn-off, waits for them, and the server logs `claude_login_wait` as it waits, with `why`: `queue` (behind a turn-on, turn-off or sign-in), `refresh` or `turn`. A sign-in, a turn-on or a turn-off never waits for those offers. The Settings view says such a login is `refused`, with why, and offers Turn off, which removes it; until then no API key is made. The refusal words now name the server's user (`uid 501 (svc)`, say), the home's refusal included. A folder that is the user's but open to others' writes is refused in words of its own, which name the open folder, its mode and the `chmod g-w,o-w` that closes it. A folder of this machine's login still to make is made by AgentRun at the turn-on and before the CLI's sign-in, 0700 whatever the umask, and checked again before the CLI gets it, so a login the CLI signs in there is not refused after.

  Where the env's `HOME` is another user's and the login therefore uses the server's user's own home, the sign-in line the Settings view shows now carries `HOME=<that home>`. Before, it left `HOME` to the terminal, so the line run in the person's terminal signed in to their own home, which the server never reads. The harness's `ClaudeAgentLogin` has a new optional `homeApart` that asks for this.

  A folder its group may write in is the user's alone where that group is the user's private one, as the local account files alone say: `/etc/nsswitch.conf` takes users and groups from those files only (`files` or `compat`), and the group is the user's primary group, which no other user has as theirs and which `/etc/group` lists with no other member. So a umask of 002 under such a group refuses nothing there. A switch that also asks another source (sssd, LDAP, NIS, winbind, or systemd's user records, as recent Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora installs do) can give the group members the files do not show, so there such a folder is refused.

  Behaviour change: a login that ran before is refused, at either place, where the server's home is a folder anyone may write in, or its group where another user is in it, or is reached through one (a home on a volume whose group is set for a pod, 2775, say). So is a login on this machine's folders where one of these variables points at another user's folder, or reaches through another user's link or folder, or through such an open folder. A group shared with other users, a group that is not the user's primary one, one `/etc/group` does not list, account files that defer to a directory service (a `+` or `-` line), and any group where `/etc/nsswitch.conf` asks a source other than the files for users or groups, or is missing, all count as open: under a umask of 002 with such a group, a home, a `~/.config` or a `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` folder made by hand is refused until it is `chmod g-w`. The setting stays. Start the server as the person whose Claude plan it is, with that person's variables, and make the folders on the way writable by their owner alone.
- Codex forks no longer count their parent's history twice. A forked rollout written by Codex 0.130 or 0.145 (a `/fork`, or a spawned subagent) begins with a copy of its parent's turns, token counts included, stamped with the fork's time. The import counted those requests again in the fork, and on the fork's day, so the tokens, cost and requests of every such fork were too high. The copy is now read as a copy, counted once in the parent. The rule is ccusage's: the fork's leading usage is matched against the parent's usage from before the fork, and the longest run equal to its start or its end is the copy. A fork whose parent's rollout is not under the home has nothing to match, so its usage still counts. A fork whose parent is not in the directory of its own date costs one listing of the sessions directory per import, through a new `lookups` read option that `parseHome` passes, not one per fork. Re-import a home to correct the runs imported before. <!-- changes/codex-fork-replay.md -->
  - A fork's session keeps its own id. A forked rollout from Codex 0.154 on writes its parent's `session_meta` after its own, and the import took the last one: the fork took its parent's id and working directory. A later `session_meta` whose id is the thread the rollout forked from is that copy, and is skipped; any other later `session_meta` still counts as before.
  - A fork from Codex 0.152 on stamps its records with its thread. Usage between the first record naming another thread and the fork's own is read as a copy only when the parent's rollout was read. A fork whose parent is archived or not under the home counts it, since nothing else does.
- An agent's `input_schema` `maxProperties` and `propertyNames` now count and name the input's own fields only, never `content`. `content` is always accepted, since it carries a run's message, a trigger's line and event, and a schedule's last answer. Before, a schema capped at one field refused `{ "company": "Acme", "content": "" }`, so a trigger for that agent could not be saved with its typed field and a message, and its runs could not get their event or last answer. A schema's own fields still meet both keywords, and a refusal names the schema's own number. <!-- changes/input-schema-content-exempt.md -->
- A kept computer that the janitor ends now has its run folder's mount credential revoked, on the disk recorded at the park, even when the run was deleted since. Before, a run stopped while parked, or resumed with its computer off, left that credential valid for up to 24 hours. A revoke that keeps failing is retried until the credential has expired, then the computer's record is closed. <!-- changes/janitor-revokes-kept-mount.md -->
- The console can make a Decision or a Workflow agent again. Since "New agent" opened the Build page, the editor that offers those two (its harness picker's Decision and Workflow) only ever opened on an existing agent. Build now links "set one up in the editor", which opens the editor creating a new agent at `#/agents/new?editor`, with every harness, Decision and Workflow to pick from. An agent named `new` keeps its own pages, its editor at `#/agents/new/edit`. <!-- changes/new-agent-editor.md -->
- A run's screen recording's ffmpeg now starts with only PATH, the locale and TMPDIR, as the server's other helper programs do. Before, it got the server's whole environment, so a key the server held, under any name, reached it. <!-- changes/recording-ffmpeg-child-env.md -->
- `agentrun-serve runner --check --env` calls an `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` that is not a seal key bad even when the runner's store does not open, in the words the start uses (its length, never its value), instead of "set, and not checked against the store". A key of the right shape stays unchecked there. <!-- changes/runner-check-seal-key-shape.md -->
- The scrubber reads a password typed in a command (`redis-cli -a`, a registry `login -p`, `mysql -p`, `npm set _authToken`, `curl -u`) through a shell lexer, `shell-lex.ts`, beside the span scans it used before. Each of the five rules cuts the union of the two: the lexer's read adds cuts and never removes one the scan makes. Passwords these forms used to leave in the text are now cut: <!-- changes/scrubber-shell-lex.md -->
  - after an operator inside a substitution (`redis-cli -h $(hostname; true) -a …`);
  - after a substitution longer than 256 characters, or one left open on its line (`curl -H "X: $(… -u admin:…`);
  - in ANSI-C quoting (`curl $'-u' admin:…`, `login -p $'…'`);
  - after a backslash line continuation: between a command's arguments for all five, and between `docker` and `login` or `npm` and `config set`;
  - with anything else between a program and its subcommand: a redirection (`docker >out.txt login …`), an option (`docker -D login …`, `npm -g set …`, `npm config --global set …`, any number of options between `config` and `set` within the command's read, which ends 1024 to 3072 characters past the command's name), an escaped blank;
  - after `c`, npm's and pnpm's alias of `config` (`npm c set //registry/:_authToken …`);
  - in a registry login's `-p` with the password glued on (`docker login -p<pw>`);
  - under a command name written quoted (`"curl"`, `'redis-cli'`, `$'curl'`), with `.exe`, `.cmd`, `.bat` or `.ps1` in any case (`Docker.exe`), or after a path: a quoted one holding blanks (`"C:\Program Files\Redis\redis-cli.exe" -a …`) or a relative one (`.\redis-cli.exe`). Inside such a path a backslash is a separator, not the start of an escape (`\r`, `\n`).
