A quoted path ends at its closing quote on the line, and where a path keeps an escape, the same text read with every escape blanked stands beside it, so a path read never leaves what the escape read cuts;
  - after a non-ASCII blank (NBSP, the ideographic space, the other Unicode spaces) before or after a flag, a value or a subcommand;
  - inside a substitution nested in `${…}` or `$"…"`;
  - in a curl `-u` password glued to `&`, `(`, `)`, `<` or `>`, however long.

  A fixed corpus (`test/fixtures/scrub-differential`) records which characters the scrubber on main cut in each row, and a test requires each of them cut still and every row's password gone, but for two rows it names with the reason (a backslash before a name outside a Windows path, `\redis-cli`, reads as an escape). Once the lexer's cuts alone cover the scans' on every row, a later change can delete the scans.

  The lexer's work is counted: it reads each character of a text at most 8 times, and at most 12 when commands are named inside quotes the lexer pairs. The readers hand out one command's words at a time, so what they hold stays one command's however long the text. The tests assert those counts, bound each timed rule's CPU against main's span scan for it, timed in the same call, and bound its wall time, after a full collection, against its own on a quarter of the text.
- A server in a container that writes no `/.dockerenv` or `/run/.containerenv`, which its cgroup names (a Kubernetes pod, an LXC system container), now knows it runs in a container: one that reaches a Docker refuses Docker computers with that reason, instead of mounting paths the Docker host doesn't have; its Docker messages say they are the container's; and it no longer offers its pod's addresses as where another machine reaches it. The server reads its own cgroup for this the way computer's Docker provider already did, through `containerSigns`, which `@parcha/agentrun-computer` now exports. <!-- changes/serve-pod-is-a-container.md -->
- Editing a trigger in the console and picking another agent now starts that agent's input afresh. Before, the trigger's stored input came along: keys the new agent's form has no field for were sent, so a schema that refuses extra keys answered "Remove target.input.<key>" with no field to clear it, and one that allows them got the old values unseen. <!-- changes/trigger-edit-agent-switch.md -->
- serve's test suite waits less: a test server's timeline long poll reads every 100 ms instead of every second, the end-of-run cost read's bound is a test option for native and SDK runs as it already was for adapter runs, and the slowest cases wait on events or a shifted clock instead of real timeouts and leases. No case was removed and no assertion was weakened. <!-- changes/serve-test-suite-faster.md -->
- A held run (`hold: true`) refused its model at its create no longer answers `422 model_key_required` for a missing key on a server whose model gateway holds none: it makes no model call, so it opens and holds its computer. A `model_key` handed with such a run is refused (`422 input_invalid` at `model_key`) as never used. Its claim on a harness recipe billed to its vendor's plan opens none of the keys saved for that harness in Settings → Harness keys, and a runner that starts each run in a process of its own hands that process none; the claim still holds its computer, where the recipe hands a saved key under another name too, and in a run's own process with no owner sign-in. Nor does its claim open the credentials of the MCP servers it is granted, fal's included: nothing can call them, so it carries no MCP tool. A run whose launch's `hold.refused` can't be read (a corrupt row) is held all the same: its start and its messages are refused (`409 agent_not_runnable`) in words that name that field, and its claim opens no model key. <!-- changes/held-run-no-model-key-or-harness-keys.md -->
  A launch whose `hold.minutes` isn't a number (a corrupt row) keeps its hold and its refusal, and waits the default 30 minutes; before, it dropped the whole hold, so the run could start and its claim open its model's keys.
- A Claude Code or pi request that failed, read with `turns: false`, keeps its error as `failed` (as OpenCode's does), never its text: the totals a home's import holds no longer carry a provider's error words. A source named twice in the CLI's `--sources` is read once, where it printed every session twice. Each reader has `idOf(locator)`, the id a read gives a session no record names, and serve's remote history probe takes its ids from it: a pi session whose `session` record names no id is exported under the id its read gives it, no longer skipped as changed. A pi-ai that fails to load now fails `builtinCatalog` and `priceRequests` with its reason, where it priced nothing and said nothing why. <!-- changes/import-untangle-44.md -->
- The console's New race form now offers a harness that runs here but lists no models, such as Cursor on its own sign-in, on its default model (`cursor/default`). Before, the form left it out. <!-- changes/race-plan-harness-default.md -->
- The server serves a share preview of an ended run at `/share/<run_id>`, for the owner's session alone (the owner's sign-in with accounts, the printed link's session without; any other browser gets a 401 page that says to sign in first). `/share/<run_id>?launch=<code>` opens the session as `/?launch=<code>` does and lands on the page without the code; a wrong code gets the 401 page. The page is the console's second entry, `share.html`, under the console's CSP. It reads the run's export (`GET /v2/runs/<run_id>/export`) and nothing else, so it shows exactly what a share would publish: the run's Report, Timeline, a workflow's graph and its files as text, drawn from the bundle alone. <!-- changes/share-preview-page.md -->
  A panel lists the scrubber's cuts by kind with their counts, each with where it sits (`/rows/3/text 9–30`), and one value's cuts in a step's summary and text side by side. A value beside a label and a personal detail each have a switch that exports the run again with that value put back; the other cuts can't be put back. The footer says nothing was sent and shows the bundle's sha256 and the `agentrun share <run> --restore <ids> --expect <sha256>` command that will publish exactly that bundle. A run that has not ended, a withheld run and an export that failed closed each show their reason and nothing of the run. The console now draws every `[redacted:<rule>]` marker as a chip.
- serve's stalled-read, lookup-timeout and cut-turn cases no longer wait out real timers: the end's metrics bound is armed on an injected timer (`endPatchTimer`, one option for the native, SDK and adapter loops in place of two `endPatchMs`), so each stall runs out the moment the case moves a fake clock, and the cases wait on the runner's end event, the turn's own abort and `follow`'s new `done` predicate instead of sleeps and wall-clock loops. <!-- changes/serve-tests-no-real-timers.md -->
- An agent's box can now be any computer provider whose sandbox can hold the run's folder, not only Docker, Daytona and Modal: `e2b`, `agent37`, `morph`, `cloudflare`, `fly`, `boxd` and `groundbox` are boxes too, and a place may name any of them (`"place": {"mode": "sandbox", "box": "e2b"}`). To enable one, list it in `AGENTRUN_BOXES` (`AGENTRUN_BOXES=docker,e2b`) and set the keys its provider requires, in the server's environment or in Settings → Computers (`E2B_API_KEY` for E2B); the box is offered once they are set, and nothing asks the vendor at the start. A vendor's box holds the run's folder on Archil or as a synced folder, so its runs need Archil turned on in Settings → Workspace, as a Daytona or Modal box's did. Which providers are boxes is read from their descriptors, so Orgo (desktops alone), the phone, the hosted browsers and smol cloud are not. A boxd box has no network: capabilities say so in its `places.boxes` entry. With no box ready, the start's banner and `bash`'s reason now name each box `AGENTRUN_BOXES` lists with its reason, and the rest at once. <!-- changes/boxes-from-provider-descriptors.md -->
- A new browser session whose reserve the spend cap refused is now asked for its reserve again at its next charge, so once the cap is raised its next stretch is held on the run's ledger. Before, the refused reserve was never asked again and the session ran on with nothing held for it, even after a raise. <!-- changes/browser-reserve-asked-again.md -->
- Claude Code's login on this machine, after a chmod of its folders, follow-ups to the config-folders change (#3759): <!-- changes/claude-login-followups.md -->

  - A request that finds the login's folders changed (a run's check, a save's, capabilities) swaps the login in one turn on the sign-ins' queue and makes the offers again outside it. A sign-in, a turn-on or a turn-off asked meanwhile no longer waits for that probe of the offers; a run, save or capabilities request still waits for it.
  - Where making the offers again fails after the login was swapped, the next request makes them again, rather than going on with the offers made from the login as it was.
  - A template's plan and apply (`POST /v2/templates/{name}/apply`, with or without `dry_run`) now look at the login's folders first too, so the harness they pick and the model choice they check agree with a run's check right after a chmod.
  - A request that finds the login as it is waits for a turn-on's or turn-off's offers still being made, and `claude_login_wait` is logged with `why` (`queue`, `refresh` or `turn`) for each wait. Once its wait ends, it goes on only if no later turn-on or turn-off started meanwhile and the offers it waited for were made. Where a later one started (its probe drops the earlier one's), it waits for that one too; where another request's making of the offers failed, it makes them again itself. A template's apply asked as a turn-on lands no longer picks its harness by the offers made before both. After 3 such waits a request is refused as `unavailable` (503, retryable), in words that say to ask again.
  - A login folder its group may write in is allowed where that group is the user's private one, as the local account files alone say: `/etc/nsswitch.conf` takes users and groups from those files only (`files` or `compat` on its `passwd` and `group` lines, and on `initgroups` where it has one), and the group is the user's primary group, which no other user has as theirs and `/etc/group` lists with no other member. A umask of 002 under such a group no longer refuses the login. Where the switch also asks another source (sssd, LDAP, NIS, winbind, or systemd's user records, as the `files systemd` that recent Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora installs have), or there is no `/etc/nsswitch.conf`, the group can have members the files do not show, so the folder is refused as before. So are a group another user is in, one that is not the user's primary group, one `/etc/group` lacks, account files with a `+` or `-` line, and a folder anyone may write in, all in the same words.
- Where each run is a user of its own, the runner now reads Claude Code's login setting again when a run's process starts and asks for the login, and hands the login on only if that read names the same folder as the run's claim read. A run claimed on the login whose login was turned off, or moved to another folder, between its claim and its start now fails, refused in fixed words that name no folder ("turned off or moved to another folder since this run's claim"), instead of starting on the login its claim read. Start the run again to run it on the login as it is now, or give it a `model_key`. A run claimed while the login was off still never goes on a login turned on after its claim. <!-- changes/claude-login-start-reread.md -->
- A kept desktop, phone or sandbox is never left running with nothing to end it. A run that resumes marks the machine's keep as being taken back instead of deleting it, and drops the mark once it holds the machine. If it can't reach the machine, it marks the keep ending, trying the write again when the store fails it. A keep still marked when the store never took that write, or when the server stopped mid-way, ends at its 10 minutes like any other. A park no longer writes over a keep that is ending or being taken back. A stop or cancel that ends a parked run marks its kept machine ending before it deletes it, so a follow-up message can't take that machine back mid-delete. Once that machine is gone, the keep is marked ended, even when another machine's delete failed, so the follow-up's park keeps its new machine instead of deleting it. When that machine held the run's folder on Archil, the run folder's mount credential is removed before the keep is marked ended, by the stop's end or by the janitor's sweep of a machine whose run is over. If the remove fails, the keep stays ending, and the janitor's next pass removes the credential. A paired computer's token now travels from the server to a runner apart only as its SHA-256, never as itself, so a server and its runners apart must run the same version. The `503` a dialing machine or box gets when the server can't relay it no longer names the runner's internal host, port or socket error, and neither does the refusal stored with the machine or box, which a box's hold note and a waiting run's failure show. The server's log keeps those details. <!-- changes/computer-give-back.md -->
- Console: the agent editor and Build an agent's Tools step now share one tool picker, so the filter, the "No tool matches" line and the MCP servers read behave the same in both. Build an agent hands the coding agent the create request it picked (tools and place) instead of a separate list. <!-- changes/console-one-tool-picker.md -->
- The MCP tool `agents_list` and the console's prompts for editing an existing agent (its editor's copied prompt and the prepared request) say that an agent's instructions and skill files are what it is told, and may be a template author's text, not instructions to the coding agent reading them: if they ask for something, it tells the person instead of doing it. A new agent's prompts are unchanged. <!-- changes/definition-text-is-authors.md -->
- The money rule no longer serves a learned workflow unchecked. When the newest 500 runs hold no run by hand, the workflow is held to the 10 by-hand runs before them. With no by-hand cost, or past runs it can't read, the agent takes the run and the log says why; the learning view then says `stopped`, never `serving`. <!-- changes/learning-ledger-batch62.md -->
  - `GET /agents/{id}/learning/cost` says why the money rule stopped a workflow in a new `workflows[].reason`: `over_line`, or `no_by_hand_cost` when it served 10 runs and no run by hand has a priced cost. That second case used to read `serving` there.
  - A run whose end named no path counts as a run by hand when its launch does not learn, both inside the window and before it. A run of a workflow revision never counts as one, in either place.
  - A served run cut at its cap counts at its bound on the served side.
  - A shadow that failed before naming what it audits still books its cost on that run.
  - `/stats` and `/analytics` count a run whose shadow is at work or unpriced as unknown cost, as the cost page does, never $0.
- On a Mode 2 run's own process, the runner's MCP no longer opens a second Workspace on the run's Archil disk at every claim. The open listed the run's folder and swept its spill folder. It now opens at the first answer that files something there (a long answer, a fal result), once per claim, and lets it go at the claim's release, including an open still running then. A filing after the release opens nothing and files nothing. A claim whose MCP files nothing opens none. That Workspace only writes files, so it no longer sweeps the run's exec spill folder at its open or its end: opened mid-run, a sweep could delete the output of a command the run was still running. `openRunWorkspace` takes `sweep: false` for such a Workspace; every other caller still sweeps. The gateway's `work` may now return a Promise, which it awaits before filing. A Workspace that can't be opened files nothing, as a failed write does: the long answer says it could not be saved, and a result is left out. <!-- changes/mcp-mode2-disk-opened-lazily.md -->
- A slow Ollama listing no longer hides Ollama's models for 30 seconds. A listing that missed its 2-second deadline (while Ollama loaded a model, say) or got a wrong-shaped answer was kept as "no models", so codex, opencode, claude-agent and pi had no default, and a run naming no model was told to start Ollama while it ran. Now such a listing keeps the earlier models and is asked again at once. A stopped Ollama lists none. <!-- changes/ollama-failed-listing.md -->
- `agentrun-serve eval-template` no longer hangs at exit after it has printed its result (about 1 run in 160). The command now lets Node exit normally instead of calling `process.exit`, which could stop the V8 worker threads while a background compile was waiting for a garbage collection. <!-- changes/queue-flakes.md -->
  A pull request's CI now always runs the tests that scan the whole repository (`TREE_WIDE` in `scripts/test-affected.mjs`: entry-points, typebox-out, doc-checkpoint, check-doc-anchors). Before, a pull request that broke one of their policies passed its own checks and failed first in the merge queue, along with every group queued behind it.
  Four flaky serve tests are fixed. Capture-git's fixture repository no longer runs git auto-maintenance. `raw()`'s SQLite statements run on a worker, so a write never blocks the commit it waits for. Runner-command-wake and graph-redact now count work instead of timing a window.
- In the console's trigger forms, an agent whose `input_schema` has `maxProperties` or `propertyNames` now gets its typed fields, with the message beside them, like any other agent. The forms had fallen back to whole JSON for these schemas: typed fields always carry the message, and such a schema used to refuse `content` with them. Serve now counts and names only the input's own fields against both keywords, never `content`. <!-- changes/trigger-fields-own-cap.md -->
- A server now takes a computer's daemon or driver that speaks protocol 0.2 or any later 0.x, not only 0.2 exactly: a minor step from 0.2 on only adds, and the hello's groups and features say what each side has, so a 0.3 driver pairs with and attaches to a 0.2 server. A 0.1 driver is still refused, because 0.2 replaced its `apps.ui_tree` with `ui`: pairing it says "update the driver on <computer>, then pair with the same code", and its attach is answered 426 with "update the driver on <computer> (the download is on the console's Computers page)", so update the driver on that computer. Another major, or a version of another shape, is refused as before. Every refusal now names the side to update, where pairing and the attach 426 used to say "update whichever is older": the server, for a driver newer than it, else the driver. A hosted daemon's drifted protocol now reads "hello: the daemon speaks protocol 1.0, and this provider 0.2", or "protocol none" when its hello names none. The conformance case `health.declared` still takes only the suite's own protocol version. <!-- changes/computer-protocol-minor-step.md -->
- `web_fetch` on `auto` (the default) now reads through Parallel's extract on any server that holds a Parallel key (`PARALLEL_API_KEY`, set or saved). Parallel gets each URL, with the run's session id and model id, and bills each page to the server's Parallel key. The guarded direct fetch is behind it. Before, `auto` on such a server was the direct fetch. A server with no Parallel key is unchanged (keyless Firecrawl). To keep every URL on the server, pick `kernel` for `web_fetch` (`PUT /v2/settings/tools` or an agent's `tool_settings`). GET /capabilities' `why` says which one a run gets. <!-- changes/serve-web-fetch-parallel-first.md -->
  - Both tools' `auto` order is one table, `DEFAULT_WEB_ORDER`, exported with `autoWeb`. Swapping its ids puts another provider first.
- serve's web tools now run Jev by default on any server that already holds a TypeSafe key (`TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, set or saved), and that sends run content to TypeSafe. Each `web_search` sends TypeSafe its objective and each result's URL, title and snippet. Each `web_fetch` given an objective sends TypeSafe the page's text, up to 1,000,000 characters in chunks, and the objective. A fetch with no objective sends nothing. TypeSafe bills every request to the server's TypeSafe key. To keep the old behaviour, set `AGENTRUN_WEB_JEV_OFF=1` on the server. Jev (`jev-1.14.0`) scores each search result against the objective and reorders the results by that score (rerank+label). It keeps every result, gives each a `relevance` (0 to 1), and adds a `sift` line saying how they were ranked, or why not. Each Jev request is held on the run's spend cap at Jev's published price and settled at the cost Jev reported, never above the hold. A server with only an OpenRouter key runs no web ranking. GET /capabilities' `why` for each tool says what it sends TypeSafe, or that Jev is off. <!-- changes/serve-web-jev.md -->
  - A Jev failure leaves the results as the provider gave them, with a `sift` line saying it did not run.
  - A `web_fetch` given an objective has Jev pick the chunks of the page most likely to hold it (`found`), its requests held and booked as a search's are. One with no objective is never judged: it asks Jev nothing, its page is whole and its answer has no `sift` field. In web, a fetch given a decider but no task now comes back with no `sift` field (it said "not run (no task given); this part is whole"); its classifier record still says `skipped: "no task"`.
  - serve's `web_destinations` start line gains `classifier`: `"jev jev-1.14.0 rerank+label"`, or `off`. It never holds a key.
  - `AGENTRUN_WEB_JEV_OFF=1` on the server turns Jev off for every run created while it is set, on every runner host: the run's plane carries it (`jev: "off"`) and keeps it at every later launch, so a runner started without the switch hands no TypeSafe key and runs no Jev for that run. A runner's own switch can add off, never remove it.
  - The runner hands TypeSafe's key to a run only when one of its web tools is the run's own and Jev is not turned off, as it hands Parallel's: `web_fetch` wherever it runs, and `web_search` on Parallel, keyless Firecrawl or Exa, or pi's hosted search, never a harness's own search inside its CLI (codex's, claude-agent's), where no Jev call can happen. A codex run on its own search with `web_fetch` still gets the key, for the fetch.
  - web: `jevWebDecider` builds this decider from what it is handed (the key, `jevProvider`, a price, a fetch), never from the environment, and `null` gives none. `Pay` gains an optional `charged`, the cost a request reported once it was answered, which `decisionPay` passes for each decision request.
  - web: a decision request's line in `receipt.cost` is now what it was charged: the cost its provider gave (reported, or estimated where it reported none, the line's `basis` says which), never above its hold, and the hold where it gave none. It was the hold, which the cap also booked; now that the cap books the charge, the line follows it, so receipt and ledger say one figure. `DecisionPay`'s `costOf` now returns the answer's `Cost` (`usd` and `basis`).
  - web: `webFetchText`'s line for a provider that gave no page before the direct fetch now reads "Parallel gave no page (answered 500); this one was fetched directly.": it no longer says the provider was picked, which under `auto` it was not.
  - web: `Pay` gains an optional `settled`, told whether the cap's settle of an answered request was written. `decisionPay` moves a decision request's line to its charge only once that settle is written; when it fails, the cap keeps the hold and so does the line, its `basis` saying the settle failed and naming the charge it would have booked. A $0 unbilled line follows the same rule. `unmetered` never calls `settled`, so with no cap the lines are as before.
- Each run writes one start line naming where its web tools go: `event=web_destinations search="exa (keyed) > firecrawl-keyless (keyless) > exa-keyless (keyless)" fetch="parallel (keyed, no key) > firecrawl-keyless (keyless, rate-limited until 12:01 UTC) > direct"`. It gives each tool's order, whether each provider is keyed (and whether the run holds its key) or keyless, and any hold known when the run's Web is made. It never includes a key. The line comes from `Web.destinations()` (new), `destinationsWords` and `destinationsLine`. serve writes it once per run's Web, which is now made as web_fetch is bound for every run, not only one whose web_fetch asks a keyed provider. <!-- changes/web-destinations-line.md -->
- `web_search` asks for an `objective` and a few keyword `queries`. The objective is what the agent wants to find out, in a sentence, at most 1,000 characters. There are up to 5 queries, and each is cut at 200 characters. The tool's description asks for a goal-style objective and 1 to 3 short queries. <!-- changes/web-search-objective.md -->
  `query` is deprecated. It is now optional in the schema and marked deprecated, and the schema requires `objective`, so a model's call that gives `query` alone is refused before it runs. A workflow's call node, and `Web.search` in `@parcha/agentrun-web`, still take a `query` alone, as the objective and its only query. Each provider is sent what it takes:
  - Parallel gets the objective as `objective` and the queries as `search_queries`. Where the run names a model, Parallel also gets that model's bare id as `client_model`. `excerpt_settings` is no longer sent.
  - Exa, keyed and keyless, gets the objective as its query.
  - Firecrawl, keyed and keyless, is sent up to 3 of the queries at once. Each request asks for its share of the results and a markdown scrape of each one. The results are merged by URL, and each snippet is the page's markdown. Keyless Firecrawl is also sent the objective, because its tool requires one. Keyed Firecrawl now costs 1 more credit for each result it scrapes. When the queries meet more than one rate limit, the run's breaker holds the longest wait any of them named; a quota still wins over any rate limit.
  - Native search gets the first query.

  A search's answer now carries `objective` and `queries`, and no longer carries `query`. In a receipt from `@parcha/agentrun-web`, `asked` is the search's objective, and a new `queries` field holds the queries. Jev ranks results against the objective.
  `web_fetch` takes an `objective`. In `@parcha/agentrun-web` the option is `FetchOptions.objective`. `lookingFor` stays as an alias, and `objective` wins when both are given. With no classifier in the run, the answer is the part asked for, unchanged. Before, it said `looking_for not applied (no classifier in this run)`.
  `Web.search` takes a string or `{ objective, queries?, n? }`. `WebConfig.client` (`{ model?, session? }`) is sent to the providers that take it, and only when given. `SearchOptions.session` gives one search its own session, in place of the Web's. Parallel's extract, `web_fetch`'s read, is now sent the same `session_id` and `client_model` as its search, and `FetchOptions.session` gives one fetch its own session. The server now gives each run's Web one random 32-hex session, never made from the run's id, so Parallel gets the same `session_id` on all of a run's searches and fetches.
  The descriptions the model reads of `web_search` and `web_fetch` no longer name a provider, and are the same whichever provider answers. Which provider answers is still in capabilities. The trade: `web_fetch`'s description tells the model that a URL may be sent to a third party, but not which one. The answer's `via` and the call's receipt name that party, and the set of providers is the server's choice, which the model cannot act on. `@parcha/agentrun-web` exports both tools' descriptions and parameter schemas (`WEB_SEARCH_DESCRIPTION`, `WEB_SEARCH_PARAMETERS`, `WEB_FETCH_DESCRIPTION`, `WEB_FETCH_PARAMETERS`), and the server builds its two tools from them.
- A keyless provider's limit now holds it for the whole server, not only the run that met it. Keyless Firecrawl and keyless Exa run on the host's free allowance, so when one run is rate-limited or out of quota, the next run should not pay another refusal to learn it. <!-- changes/web-server-holds.md -->

  - `createWeb` takes `holds` (new `Hold`: provider, tool `search`, `fetch` or `key`, kind and end). Each hold seeds the matching breaker the first time it is used: the Web's own breakers and the breakers a call brings alike. A hold that has already ended is ignored. `onHold` receives each limit that leaves a breaker holding.
  - serve keeps the keyless holds in memory (`web-holds.ts`), with the server as the only writer. A run's own process reports each hold over its channel to the runner. A new run gets the current holds in its spawn environment (`AGENTRUN_SERVE_WEB_HOLDS`), which carries hold data only, never a key. The run's start line and its first call already see them. Each hold is logged as `event=web_provider_held`.
  - A hold whose limit names no end is kept for an hour (`ENDLESS_HOLD_MS`). A restart forgets every hold, so the first run after a restart pays at most one refusal to learn it again. Keyed providers' holds stay with the run.
  - `GET /capabilities` adds `held` to `web_search` and `web_fetch`. It is read live on each answer and lists each hold on a provider the tool resolves to, with its kind, its end and words such as `rate-limited until 12:01 UTC`. When nothing holds the tool, the field is absent.

  Known limit: a runner in its own process (`agentrun-serve runner`) keeps its runs' holds in its own memory, so that server's `/capabilities` does not see them.
- A run now records every learned workflow call it made, and why its first choice did or did not serve. `GET /runs/{id}` and each runs list row carry `workflow_calls`: one entry per call, the platform's before the agent's first turn and the agent's own alike. Each entry has its `workflow`, its `digest`, its `caller` (`platform` or `agent`), its `outcome` (`answered`, `handed_back`, `failed`, or `refused` for a call refused before any node ran, by the tool or at its gate when an ask is declined or the cap is wrapping up) and the `usd` its nodes booked. `usd` is null when that is not known or another call ran beside it, a sibling subagent's on pi included. The same runs also carry `first_choice`, the reason the platform ran a learned workflow first or did not, for example `served`, `none_fit`, `not_promoted`, `cost_stop`, `no_by_hand_cost` (10 served runs and no by-hand cost to hold them to, so the agent takes the run and its `learned_workflow` tool leaves that workflow out) or `past_unread`. Both fields are null where `path` is. SDK runs keep no call record, so their `workflow_calls` is empty. The money rule now counts a run whose agent called a workflow, not only one the platform served: a run the platform served first is charged to that workflow alone, a run only the agent called to each workflow it ran, and a refused call to none. A run whose first call was refused names no workflow: its `path` and `workflow` are the agent's. A workflow over its by-hand cost stops whoever made its calls: it no longer runs first, the agent's `learned_workflow` tool leaves it out, and the run records `cost_stop`. When the agent's past runs can't be read, the money rule fails closed: nothing runs first (`past_unread`), the tool runs no learned workflow, and the learning view reads every workflow as cost-stopped. A run claimed again after a crash still keeps what its workflow did first, its answer or its handback, even when that claim can't read the past. Runs that ended before this release recorded no calls; the money rule charges each as its `path` and `workflow` say, as before, so a workflow stopped today stays stopped. The learning ledger keeps each run's calls, through a new additive column on SQLite and Postgres. `path` and `workflow` read as before. <!-- changes/workflow-calls.md -->
- Claude Code's login on this machine no longer counts a group-writable folder's group as the user's private group when `/etc/group` gives that group a password (anything but `x`, `!`, `*` or empty), since anyone who knows it may join the group; the refusal names the group and the password. An `x` there is not refused: it means any password the group has is in `/etc/gshadow`, which a server without privileges cannot read, so the check does not. A gshadow password or member set with `gpasswd` is not seen; remove it with `gpasswd -r` or `gpasswd -d`. Nor when the account files hold a second account with the user's name or uid, or an id after blanks, which the system still reads. The serve README now says that a user removed from the group keeps it in sessions already open. <!-- changes/claude-login-private-group-accounts.md -->

  A run's check, a save's, a template's plan or apply and capabilities, after finding the login changed, no longer go on by the offers made before it when a model key's save, a harness key's or a new Ollama listing made the offers again meanwhile and that probe failed or is still out: they wait for that probe, or make the offers themselves.
- A Composio save's account lookup and a run's account check ask Composio for ACTIVE connected accounts alone (`statuses=ACTIVE`). A user's started, expired or turned-off accounts no longer count toward the lookup's 10 pages, so an API-only token's save is no longer refused (`403`) for them, and a run's ACTIVE account behind them is found. On an API-only server, a run's binding (`mcp_auth.<server>.connected_account_id`) names an ACTIVE account of its user: one that is only started, expired or turned off is `422` `not_allowed`, nothing started, and the refusal now reads "Composio lists no such ACTIVE account of that user for the server's toolkit". <!-- changes/composio-active-accounts-only.md -->
- A run's browser rows hold to the claim, and the janitor removes the Archil credentials a refused remove left. <!-- changes/computer-night-followups.md -->
  - A run's process removes its browser take or ended-wait row only when no later claim of the run wrote it, and only while the row is the one it read. Before, the remove checked only the key, so a claim still closing could clear the row of the claim that holds the run now, and the Screen tab read no take.
  - The computer janitor logs `the computer janitor removed no mount credential of run <id>: …` when it ends a kept Archil computer whose row names no disk, saying the credential lapses at its ttl. Before, it ended the row without a word.
  - A run's end that keeps no computer and whose Archil credential remove fails now leaves `archil_revoke:<run>`, and the janitor's next pass removes the credential, then the row. Each remove is bounded and its Archil calls are cut when the bound passes. Before, it was only logged and the credential stood until its 24-hour ttl.
- A stopped run's end no longer deletes the machine a follow-up message took back. When a follow-up queued the run again and its claim took the kept desktop, phone or sandbox back before the stop's end ran, that end deleted the machine from under the follow-up's turn. A run's end now lets nothing go once a later claim has the run, or when it can't read the run to tell, and says so in the runner's log; that claim lets the run's machines go at its own end, and otherwise the run's next end or the computer janitor does. On E2B, Daytona, Modal, Morph, Browserbase, Kernel and the phone harness the janitor ends only a machine a park kept: another machine left there runs until the vendor's own lifetime ends it. A keep that lapsed no longer haunts the run: the run's end removes its ended keep, so a follow-up message no longer says again that the desktop wasn't kept because its 10 minutes passed. That needed a janitor pass before, which never runs under `--faux`. A follow-up whose take-back of the kept machine a stopped run's end beat no longer says the machine wasn't kept because its 10 minutes passed when they hadn't; it says it's a new one. A paired computer's files note no longer tells the model the computer is deleted when the run ends; it says what's saved there stays on it. A computer that gives the run no shell (a desktop, phone or browser that doesn't mount the run's folder) now says so in its own words in GET /v2/computers, instead of "No computer on this server". A provider whose machines dial the server, on a runner in a process of its own, now names both fixes when it refuses: give the runner `AGENTRUN_PUBLIC_URL`, or run the server and its runner in one process. <!-- changes/computers-followup.md -->
- Flatten the console navigation into Agents, Templates and Runs. Agents opens the agent list with a direct Connect agent action and a primary New agent action that opens the editor. Coding-agent creation is available from the editor. Remove the standalone Build landing page; existing new-agent links now open the full editor, and links carrying an initial brief still populate it. Agent cards have an outlined Settings icon as their last action, opening configuration directly without a coding-agent prompt. Archive and Unarchive are available as accessible icon buttons on the right of Settings for managed and connected agents. Settings shows an agent-name breadcrumb back to the agent page and marks Settings as the current location, preserving unsaved-change protection. It omits its redundant Settings action while keeping the shared editing controls aligned. Replace the console, sign-in and setup wordmark and favicon with transparent SVG paths based on the supplied AgentRun artwork; the logo uses theme-aware lettering without a background in either theme. Demo mode keeps complete skill files by revision, rejects stale edits, clears removed optional settings when a revision is saved, and keeps each run’s original model labels when agent settings change. Managed agent pages have a Settings button in the header for instructions, workflows, tools, skills, model configuration and revision history. Model & runtime uses compact runtime and thinking pickers, groups model controls, and separates run behavior; unavailable runtimes explain why directly in their dropdown options, with complete setup instructions also available on demand. Learning has its own settings section explaining corrections, reusable workflows and review. Saved runtime, model, thinking and learning choices remain intact. New and existing agents use one editor with the same runtime, model, thinking, computer, tool, skill and learning controls; Decision and Workflow remain available through a separate Agent type choice when creating, keeping the runtime choices consistent with Settings. Both use the same named settings menu with a mobile section picker, without numbered steps or Previous/Next controls. Tools and Skills have separate settings sections. Saved skill names stay visible when their files are unavailable, including demo templates; skill edits stay disabled until the complete files are loaded so a new skill cannot silently replace missing ones. Custom skills can be created and edited with their supporting files; a revision-scoped skill-file read preserves the complete file set, and saves use the loaded revision’s ETag. Connected agents expose detected skills with reported source paths, project and machine; backend SDK connections explain that their skills inventory is unavailable. Edit agent stays in the top-right toolbar and includes the current settings draft. The Tools card’s Edit action opens Settings at Tools, and existing editor links continue to work. Saving keeps the page's current revision in sync, and leaving unsaved edits still asks first. Native and backend SDK agents keep editing in their original source. <!-- changes/console-agent-editor.md -->
- Console: Settings → MCP servers → Add from Composio: the Toolkit field is a search box over Composio's toolkits. Type part of a name or slug (gma, slack) and the list narrows to the toolkits that match, where finding one meant scrolling hundreds. <!-- changes/console-composio-toolkit-search.md -->
- In AgentRun's image with no Docker socket at the start, a Docker daemon that answers later now shows in Settings → Computers as no Docker here, naming the vendor computers that fit each kind (and Archil's step in Mode 1), instead of the start's words, which pointed at that same page. <!-- changes/docker-no-socket-computers-row.md -->
- No run on a `--faux` start is handed a model key any more. Before, an agent's process got its revision's model's key, a workflow run got the key of its host model (`AGENT_MODEL`, or the default a saved key gives), and any run could get a model gateway's key, whether the gateway was set where the server starts or saved in the console. The faux model sends no key, so these were real keys the run never used; a run now holds only the keys its tools run on. <!-- changes/faux-run-no-model-key.md -->
- An `llm` grader on a run with large final files now sees what the run sent. Before, the files took about three quarters of the grader's 120,000 characters, and a quarter of that went to a package's own skills copied under `.agents/skills` and a render tool's cache. The two call lists split what was left by their whole sizes, so a fake MCP server's 36 calls got about 2,900 characters and each argument list was cut to about 15. A media template's rubric that checks each clip's prompt then failed "cannot be verified", or passed with no prompt in its input at all. <!-- changes/grader-evidence.md -->
  - Final files under a folder whose name starts with `.` are tool state. `finalFilesOf` reads them after the run's own files, and `fitFiles` lists them by path and size before it cuts a file of the run's own.
  - The files never take more than leaves the calls' arguments half the room (or all they need). The fake servers' list gets at least half of what the calls are left (or all it needs).
  - A `<cuts>` note, ahead of the evidence, counts each cut: tool-state files listed by name, files cut, calls' arguments and results cut, calls left out, MCP argument lists cut. It tells the grader that what a cut left out was not seen. A list cut to its heads with no call dropped no longer says "and 0 calls in the middle".
  - New: a `tool_used` grader's `args_file` names a JSON list the run writes in its work folder. Each entry must be carried by a call of its own (a one-to-one matching, as `args` matches), and the calls must number the list's length or `count`. A missing, malformed or non-list file fails the grader, saying which. `args_file` beside `expect: not_called`, `at_least` or `at_most` is refused. The list is read under the run's cut, at most 262,144 bytes (the most a cut read answers); an entry's `[redacted]` stands for one character or more of the value a call sent there. Arrays, and the objects inside them, are compared whole, as without the cut.
- A save now refuses an `input_schema` whose `propertyNames` refers to something outside the schema's `$defs` and `definitions`, such as `{ "$ref": "#/properties/name" }`. The refusal is a 422 at `definition.input_schema.propertyNames`, naming the reference. `propertyNames` and `maxProperties` are checked against the input's own fields in a schema of their own, which keeps only the definitions, `$id` and `$schema`. A reference to anything else compiled there as `false`. So the save passed, and then every run that gave a field of its own was refused with "input.name schema is false". The save now checks what a run's start checks: the schema in force compiles, and each `$ref` that `propertyNames` reaches names a value, an anchor or an `$id` in that schema. A reference that names a definition is followed into it, so a definition that refers on to `#/properties/name` is refused too. A definition that no reference names, such as one nested inside the named definition, never applies and is not checked. Only schemas are read: a `$ref` key inside an annotation's value, such as `examples`, is data and saves. <!-- changes/input-schema-own-fields-refs.md -->
- A Jev that answers 402 (out of credit) is now `payment_required`, a new `DecisionProviderErrorCode`, booked at $0 with a $0 line. It was `http`, booked at the hold on every request. A workflow's decision node books it at $0 too. <!-- changes/jev-held-on-refusal.md -->
  - web: once a Web's decider refuses its key (`auth`) or its account (`payment_required`), it is held for the rest of that Web: later searches and fetches send it nothing. A search's `sift` reads "not run (held); these results are unsifted", and a fetch's reads "objective not applied (held); this part is in page order". serve makes one Web per run, so Jev is held for the rest of the run. An outage (5xx or a timeout) is unchanged: booked at the hold, and asked again on the next search.
- OTLP redaction catches more credential names and the credentials inside a header value. A query parameter or header named `apiKey2` or `token2`, a lowercase compound starting with a credential word (`tokenvalue`, `passwordhash`, `jwtpayload`), `jwt`, `session`, `sessionid` and names ending in `passwd`, `pwd` or `authorization` are now named like credentials, so an OTLP endpoint's such parameter is held; `tokens`, `sessions` and `sessioncount` are not, and every name ending in `key` is held as before. Inside any `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` value, a credential-named `name=value` pair's value, read over the whole value with a URL's query and fragment included (a cookie's `session=<token>`, `?region=us;session=<token>`, `#access_token=<token>`, sentry's `sentry_key=<key>` without the comma after it), and the user, password and key parameters of every URL in it (a DSN's `https://<key>@host/1`, a URL nested in another's query or path, a scheme-relative or slash-escaped one; a quoted URL ends at its closing quote, an unquoted one is also read past a quote to the next space, and its password is read whole as RFC 3986 reads it, with any `;`, `&`, `=`, `,`, `'` or `@` in it, as written and decoded) are held and cut from the tracer's `[otel]` lines alone, where before only the whole value was, so an exporter's error quoting the token alone printed it; a harmless pair such as `theme=dark` is left. A credential with a raw `;` in it, as an endpoint's or a header value's query parameter or pair (`?api_key=<key;rest>`), is held whole as well as split at the `;`, so a line quoting it is cut with nothing after the `;` left. The tracer's `[otel]` lines cut held values that overlap or touch as one `[redacted]`, as the runner's redactor does, where before a value starting inside an earlier one showed its tail. A value with thousands of `@` reads at most 16 of its userinfo's readings, and a header value's later URL queries are read while 4,096 characters of them fit, so the tracer still starts at once. The serve README lists every word. <!-- changes/otel-credential-names-and-header-pairs.md -->
- A Browserbase saved sign-in now waits one settle window after the session that saved to it ends, 10 seconds, everywhere: the next session of the same run that saves to it, the next run's save, and whether Settings shows it as held. Before, a second saving session in the same run could open on it after 5 seconds while the server still held it for 10, so it could open on a profile Browserbase was still writing back. The window is the Browserbase provider's own (`capabilities().browser.profiles.settleMs`), and the server reads it from the provider's descriptor rather than keeping a number of its own. <!-- changes/sign-in-settle-one-window.md -->

  The server now creates and removes saved sign-ins through the browser provider itself, so those calls need the provider's own keys (Browserbase's project id too), and a missing key or a non-https base URL fails in the provider's words instead of a vendor 401 or "unreachable". A Browserbase connection behind `BROWSERBASE_CONNECT_BASE_URL` now goes through that gateway wherever it is opened, not only on the browser tool's attach, and that gateway must be `wss:` or `https:`, since every session's signed URL rides it: a `ws:` or `http:` one, loopback included, now fails the Browserbase provider in words naming the variable, so set it to the gateway's wss or https URL. A provider descriptor gains an optional `profiles: { settleMs }` for a browser that keeps saved sign-ins; the sweep's usage text lists the providers the shared machine-host adapter takes from the registry. An attach conformance run against a driver on another protocol now reads "its driver speaks protocol X, and this server Y".
- The API token no longer binds a per-run Composio server to a Composio user the owner connects on the install: the user any preset server the owner saved calls as or its kept account stands on (not one the token saved, and not a per-run one; for a preset saved before the install recorded what a save made at Composio, the user its saved address names), the default `agentrun` and the tool-listing user, in any letter case. On a start (`POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/runs`, a launch hook's firing start included), an inline start (`POST /v2/runs`) and a message (`POST /v2/runs/{run_id}/messages`), the token's `mcp_auth.<server>` binding of one is `422 input_invalid` at `mcp_auth.<server>.composio_user_id` (`not_allowed`), and nothing is written. The owner's users are read at each request, so a user the owner connects later is refused from then on. The owner's session binds any user. On an API-only server, where every caller is the token, the same users are refused. Each binding is now sealed with who handed it (`by`, the token or the owner's session, a new field of the stored launch seal), and each claim reads the owner's users again: a token's binding of a user the owner has connected since has its calls of that server answered, unsent, that the user is the owner's, until a message hands `mcp_auth` again or a new run starts. <!-- changes/token-composio-owner-users.md -->

  Upgrading: a run in flight across the upgrade whose binding names a user the owner connects here was sealed with no mark, so its calls of that server are refused at its next claim in the same words, until its binding is handed again on a message (from the owner's session, for the owner's user) or a new run starts. There is no other migration step. A per-run server still lends the install's Composio key to whoever starts a run, and a token can still name a user the owner connected directly at Composio, outside this install: save one only where the token's callers own that Composio project's users.
- Every web_fetch fallback to the guarded direct fetch tells the model why. Each provider asked ahead of it (Parallel, keyed Exa, keyed Firecrawl, keyless Firecrawl) puts its reason on the page under its id, and `webFetchText` adds a line for it in the order asked: "keyless Firecrawl was picked for web_fetch and gave no page (rate-limited until 12:01 UTC); this one was fetched directly." Where no provider read the page the line says so; a page a provider behind it read carries no reason, as for Parallel. A provider held by a breaker, or one that met a limit on this read, is said by the hold: rate-limited or out of quota, until the minute it lifts (UTC), or for the rest of the run (`holdingWords`, `Reader.holding`). Parallel's other reasons and its line are unchanged; its held reason now names the hold instead of "held by its limit", and a 402 on its extract reads "out of quota for the rest of this run". The server's log lines are unchanged. The registry adds `AHEAD`, `providerName` and a `keyless` mark on keyless Firecrawl and keyless Exa. The direct fetch's refusal of a page that is not text is typed refused/GUARD (the guard's refusal), not not_text. <!-- changes/web-fallback-reasons.md -->
- One provider contract and one registry. Each provider is one `WebProvider` object in its own file (`defineProvider`: its id, label, key variable, the tools it serves, what its fetch does on a miss, its settings check, and `make`, the provider for one Web), registered once in `providers/registry.ts` (`PROVIDERS`). `createWeb` makes each provider an order names once per Web and asks it through one loop per tool: `searchInTurn` for web_search, and one read loop in `fetch.ts` for web_fetch, where each turn is recorded on the receipt as it is taken. `ProviderId`, `SearchProvider`, `FetchProvider`, `KeyedProvider`, a search's `provider`, a page's `via` and `ProviderSettings` are read from the registry, and `keys`, `endpoints`, `send` and `settings` are keyed by its ids. Every fetch provider sits behind the one breaker (`readerOf` on `searchBreaker`); keyless Firecrawl's and the keyed providers' own fetch breakers (`firecrawlFetch`'s, `keyedFetch`) are gone. web_search's breakers and web_fetch's stay separate per tool, as before; a refused key is refused for both tools, which share the provider's one client. `webFetch` and `webRead` take `readers` by provider id in place of `parallel`, `firecrawl` and `keyed`; `parallelReads` makes Parallel's. serve reads the registry for each resolution's chain, the fakes it names under --faux, the keys it reads for a run and the search tool's description. <!-- changes/web-provider-registry.md -->

  Deliberate changes (the first two and the last in receipts and errors alone):
  - An empty query is answered "web_search needs a query" before any provider is asked, for every order. Parallel used to answer it itself, leaving a failed turn on the receipt.
  - web_fetch's turns are recorded in the order the providers were asked. A keyless Firecrawl read that gave no page is a turn on the receipt even where no direct fetch follows, with the limit it met.
  - "not tried: this run holds no Parallel key" is said where Parallel's turn is reached. It used to be added to every page of an order naming Parallel, so a page a provider ahead of Parallel read said Parallel gave none and the page was "fetched directly". No serve order puts a provider ahead of Parallel.
  - An order naming an id no provider has, or a provider for a tool it does not serve, throws in `createWeb`. An unknown search provider used to be asked as keyless Exa.

  The breakers' scope is the base's: `test/breaker-scope.test.mjs`, written against the base, pins it for keyed Exa, Parallel and keyless Firecrawl (a refused key holds both tools; a quota or rate limit holds only the tool that met it).

  A reason Parallel gave no page is said only on a page the guarded direct fetch answered, or on the answer that none read it. With an order such as `[parallel, exa, direct]`, a page Exa read after Parallel failed used to carry `parallel` and a line telling the model it was fetched directly; it now carries neither, and Parallel's turn stays on the receipt.

  A logged provider's failed fetch turn with no error words now leaves `error` off the receipt's turn instead of writing an empty one. A call stopped mid-read keeps on its receipt the turns taken before the stop.
- A quota of a provider's whole key holds both of its tools. Each provider marks what its quota covers on the typed failure (`Failure.covers: "key"`): a 402 (the key's credit spent) on keyed Exa, keyed Firecrawl or Parallel, search or extract alike, and keyless Firecrawl's daily limit and its `KEYLESS_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` and `KEYLESS_ACCESS_NOT_AVAILABLE` (the host's keyless allowance). A rate limit, and `KEYLESS_TOOL_NOT_AVAILABLE`, still hold only the tool that met them. `createWeb` keeps one key breaker per provider beside each tool's own (`withKeyBreaker`): a key-wide quota met by either tool trips it, and both tools are held, unsent, until it lifts. Parallel's extract now answers a 402 with that quota (it used to hold nothing); a 429 on an extract still holds nothing. A search given its own breakers keeps a key's quota in them (`keyLimits: "call"`, the default with `breakers`), so a call node's search still holds nothing after; serve's agent web_search passes `keyLimits: "web"`, so its key's quota holds the run's web_fetch too. <!-- changes/web-quota-scope.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.58 (2026-11-25)

**Breaking:**

- `agentrun deploy` no longer checks a package with the server bundled beside the CLI before it sends it, and `agentrun-serve check-upload` is gone. The target's import is the check: a package the target refuses exits 2 in the target's own words (its 422 `input_invalid`), with nothing applied, and a package the target accepts deploys even when an older CLI's server would have refused it. A script that ran `agentrun-serve check-upload` should deploy and read the exit code and refusal instead. A refused `category` names the value it got: `category is one of engineering, security, sales, marketing, research, finance, operations, compliance, personal, not "productivity"`. `agentrun deploy DIR` with a hidden file in the folder (a `.DS_Store`, a `.env`) no longer throws a TypeError; it names the hidden paths it leaves out, as before. <!-- changes/deploy-import-is-the-check.md -->

**Changes:**

- Learning cost now has a single source of truth, a ledger. The store writes one ledger row for each run, plus spend rows for each compile, check and audit, filed under the workflow version they were for. An agent's cost page (`GET /agents/{id}/learning/cost`), a run's cost (`GET /runs/{id}`) and the launch's money rule all read one summary of those rows, so they agree on every figure. The money rule had its own cost formula and its own by-hand baseline; both are deleted. <!-- changes/learning-ledger.md -->
  - New fields, all additions: a run's `cost` and the cost page's `runs[]` gain `compile_usd`, `followup_usd`, `shadow_usd` and `share_usd`, the parts that make up the run's `learning_usd`. `runs[]` also gains `not_served`: `"cost_stop"` when the money rule stopped the workflow, `"cut"` when a restart cut the workflow's call and the run was handed back (the summary counts that in `hand_backs.cut`, never `back`), or null. Existing fields keep their names and meaning.
  - The money rule's by-hand side is now the job's own cost, without the run's compile turns, follow-ups or audit. It is still the mean over the same runs as the served side: the agent's newest 500 runs on no named disk since its learning's reset. Before, it was the all-in mean. The line where a workflow counts as over the by-hand cost moves to match.
  - Two changes to which runs the by-hand side counts. First, the fallback is gone: when the window holds no `agent` run with a known cost, by-hand is null and the workflow keeps serving. Before, it fell back to the runs before the workflow first ran. Second, runs with learning off now count as by-hand runs anywhere in the window: a run that does not learn is on the `agent` path. Before, such runs were left out once any `agent` run was known.
  - The cost page shows two by-hand figures over different runs, and their descriptions now say which: `workflows[].by_hand` is the money rule's window, and `summary.before` is every run the series counts before the takeover.
  - A revision's compile spend stays on that revision even when no promote record names it. Such a revision now shows on the bill at the default K instead of falling into unattributed.
  - Postgres stores apply migration 0028, which adds the `learning_ledger` and `learning_spend` tables and is additive. On SQLite a server adds them at its start, and a runner waits for that server. Some runs have no ledger row, or a stale one: a run that ended before the upgrade, or one that a runner or server of the earlier version ended again or healed. A row records the run's epoch at the end that wrote it, and every end moves the epoch, so a grade's correction round counts as a new end even though it keeps the run's end time. Each such run gets its ledger row worked out from its run row when it is read.
  - Purging a run deletes its ledger rows. Its cost stays on the run's tombstone, where `/usage` and `/stats` read it.
- A paired computer works under a runner in a process of its own (`--no-runner`; the image's default `server-and-runner`) when the runner knows the server's public address (`AGENTRUN_PUBLIC_URL`), the relay a dial provider's machines already take. A run's claim writes the computer's route, one settings row per computer naming the runner, its process, the run and the hold's end, by compare-and-set. A route held by a live run on a live runner refuses the claim (`<name> is held by run <run> on runner <runner>: one run at a time`); one whose runner is gone or restarted, or whose run is final (completed, failed or cancelled), is taken. Once a second the server closes a paired computer's socket that is not where its route says (close 1001), and the driver's redial lands there: relayed to the run's runner, or on the server itself once the run releases it or its hold ends. A redial to a stale route is `503` in words the server keeps on the route. A run on the runner beside the server takes a route of its own too, so a runner apart's claim for another run is refused in the same words while it holds the computer, which stays on the server. A run cancelled, failed or whose claim is lost while it holds a paired computer lets it go as it ends. The run's create waits for the computer about 80 s and fails in words naming the runner when it does not arrive. `GET /v2/computers` lists a paired computer's `held_on` (the runner its run's hold is on) and `hold_note` (the server's note of a refused relay, or that it is attached nowhere), and Settings → Computers shows both on its row. `runs_refused` on a pairing code, the pair answer and a paired computer is null once a runner relays, and names both fixes until one does. <!-- changes/paired-computer-relay.md -->
- `GET /v2/runs` takes `source`: `source=claude-code` (or `codex`, ... a source's name as the run's `imported_from.source` holds it) lists only the runs imported from that source, and `source=live` the runs made here, not imported. It is the link behind "open these sessions as runs": the console's runs list keeps it in the address (`#/runs?source=claude-code`, with a button that clears it), and the CLI, the TypeScript client and the Python client send it as `--source`, `source` and `source=`. A name no run holds lists none; a second `source`, or a value that is not a lowercase name, is 400. <!-- changes/runs-source-filter.md -->
- Wrapped links each harness's numbers to the runs of every source behind it (`#/runs?source=<source>`), and says "not imported yet", with the import command, for a source with no imported runs. `GET /v2/wrapped`'s harness rows gain `sources` (the sources read for that harness: several can share one), so the console needs no copy of the source-to-harness table. The page also holds the registry of the nine prototype cards (what each reads and waits on) and a renderer seam; with no renderer it shows no cards section. <!-- changes/wrapped-open.md -->
- More follow-ups to the Claude login on this machine (Settings → Model keys), and to the server's probe of the harness offers. <!-- changes/claude-sign-in-followups-2.md -->
  - A tool key's save or delete while the offers held are behind the inputs, and the probe out was made from the inputs read now (a turn-on of the login, say), waits for that probe's turn and starts no probe of its own while it lands. The turn ends when the probe lands or fails, or when a later probe overtakes it; the change then reads the inputs again: landed, it composes the capabilities; failed, it probes for itself; overtaken, it goes by the later probe. So it never answers `500` for another request's failed probe once its key is stored, never waits on a dropped probe, and its key always shows in the capabilities it answers after. Before, it started a probe that dropped the one out, so the save answered only after a whole probe of its own. The server logs `harness_offers_wait` as it waits.
  - A probe of the offers that fails leaves no probe out when it was the latest one, so a later change back to the inputs the offers held were made from reuses them. Before, that change probed again.
  - The Playground's "No model yet" bar is gone while the login is on and reads signed in, no agent is picked (no agents yet, or the agents still being read), and the server's default place is the runner, where a first agent on Claude Agent runs on the login. The bar's ChatGPT and key offer goes with it, whatever harness the first agent will use. On a server whose default place is a box, or before its places are read, the bar stays: a first agent there runs in the box on the model keys. Before, a Playground with no agents offered ChatGPT or a key though an agent on Claude Agent would run on the login.
  - A run of an agent on Claude Agent in a box, refused for its model while the login is on, on a model the login runs (Anthropic's own, `anthropic/<id>`, or none named), says that the login runs agents on the runner only, names the box, and says that moving the agent to the runner runs it on the login. Its `409 agent_not_runnable` carries a new `details.login_on_runner: true` (additive), and the Playground offers "Move it to the runner" there, which saves the agent's definition with its computer set to none and its box-only tools dropped, as the agent's Computer step does, and names the tools it dropped. Which tools run only in a box is the capabilities' word: a move taken before they are read, or after their read failed, reads them itself, and while that read fails it saves nothing and says so. The Computer step, with no tools read, refuses a pick that puts the agent on the runner, in words, and changes nothing. Before, either saved the agent on the runner with bash still granted, and its next run was refused there. The offer is the refused agent's: it shows only while that agent is picked and moves only that agent. After the move, a revision picked in the Playground becomes the one the move saved, so the next request runs on the runner. An agent already on the runner is not saved again. The login still runs agents on the runner only. An agent on any other model (an OpenRouter one, Anthropic's through OpenRouter included) is offered no move: on the runner it still needs its provider's key, which its refusal names. Serve puts a run on the login and makes the offer by one rule.
  - A run's check of the login takes the Settings view's signed-in answer from a runner in a process of its own on the same data folder (`agentrun-serve --no-runner` beside `agentrun-serve runner`). The answer is kept in the data folder's `claude-login-answers/`: one file per login (0600, in a 0700 folder), named by a hash of the machine's id and the login, holding only the time; a signed-out answer removes it. A run's check reads it only as a regular file of at most 32 bytes, never through a link, and a FIFO there is no answer rather than a held check. A note tightens a wider folder to 0700 and never writes through a link at its name. On disk, an answer outlives a server restart for up to its 10 minutes. Before, it was in the server process's memory, so such a runner refused a first run whose two checks timed out right after Settings read signed in.
  - A sign-in whose CLI is a script naming an interpreter that is not there (`#!/path`, or `#!/usr/bin/env <program>` with the program on no folder of the sign-in's PATH) fails at its start, in words that name the interpreter. Before, the parent watch's exit 127 read as the CLI's own exit. The `#!` line is read as the kernel reads it, as bytes, so an interpreter under a folder whose name is not ASCII (a home folder named `José`, say) is found.
  - `parentWatched` throws a `RangeError` at the call for a `termGraceMs` the parent-watch shim would refuse (anything but a whole number of ms from 1 to 2^31 - 1), whichever watch is asked for. Before, the shim exited 2 at spawn, which read as the child's own exit.
  - The status check reads an answer that is already in the CLI's output when the drain's second ends, though the server's event loop was held up past that second. Before, the loop ran the drain's timer before its reads, and the check read `no_status`.
- The agent editor's tools step, with no MCP server saved, links to Settings → MCP servers instead of only naming it. On a server that sends its models to a gateway, unless its own default model is one of the plan's (`AGENT_MODEL=chatgpt/…`), the ChatGPT plan row and the first screen's sign-in no longer say Codex and pi agents run on the plan: there an agent with no model named runs on the gateway, and the plan runs only an agent that names one of its models (`chatgpt/…`). <!-- changes/console-tools-link-gateway-plan.md -->
- A fal job priced by its settings (Kling v3, Veo 3 and 3.1, Ideogram, Nano Banana, sync-lipsync v2, Fabric) is held and booked at no less than its tier's rate on fal's model page when get_pricing states a rate other than the one its tiers were decided at. Before, the tier's ratio was applied to whatever get_pricing stated, so if fal lowered Kling v3 pro from $0.14 to $0.112 a second, a default job (audio on, $0.168 a second on the model page) was held and booked at $0.1344 a second, about 20% under its bill, with nothing to show it. The basis now says so when it happens: get_pricing's rate, the rate the tiers were decided at, and the model page's rate the job is held at. A raise on get_pricing still scales the ratio up. <!-- changes/fal-price-drift.md -->
  A price of $0 from get_pricing is no price: such a job is refused unsent under a cap and, with no cap, booked as an unknown charge, never $0. Before, it was held and booked at $0.
  Jobs sent at once on one endpoint share one get_pricing call, and an error or no answer from get_pricing is asked once more before a job is called unpriceable. Before, calls sent together each asked get_pricing, and one error answer among them refused that job under a cap ("its get_pricing answered an error") although the price had just been read for the others.
  When the call that sent a shared read stops before fal answers (its deadline, or its run's abort), a job whose own call is still live reads the price again with its own call rather than taking the stopped call's empty answer.
- A burst of saves granting monid endpoints no longer loses grants to monid's rate limit. A save's read of monid's listing or an inspect that monid refuses for its rate (429), fails (5xx) or leaves unanswered past the request's limit is sent again after monid's Retry-After (250 ms at least), at most 20 times and for up to 20 s of waits, inside 45 s of the save's start, and only then refused, in the same words as before. One server's saves share those reads: saves that arrive together read the listing once and each endpoint once, each waiting on the other's read no longer than its own 45 s, and a read that answered is reused for 60 s. A refusal monid gives as sent (401, 403, 404), or monid out of reach, still refuses the grant at once. <!-- changes/monid-save-burst-reads.md -->
- A race's lanes are the console's own agents, no longer inline runs on external agents the Agents list could only read. Each lane makes an agent `race-<label>-<n>-<pick>` (POST /v2/agents) and starts its run, labeled and capped as before, on that agent's first revision (POST /v2/agents/{id}/runs), so a resend after a lost answer never runs an edited agent. A lane picked again after a refusal archives the agent it had. A refused last lane can be removed (its agent archived), and the race opens once every lane left has a run. <!-- changes/race-lanes-console-agents.md -->
- A run that grants the subagent tool now gives its subagent tiers only the saved model keys of the models those tiers run on (the revision's `model_tiers`, else `AGENT_MODEL_FAST` / `AGENT_MODEL_STRONG`), or the gateway's key behind a gateway. That holds whether the run has a process of its own, which is now handed only those keys, or routes its tiers in the runner. It used to hand every saved model key. A replay's or audit run's grader now reads only its fast tier's model's key, and reads none when no fast tier is set. A runner with no seal key gives its tiers only their models' keys from its environment. A tier whose provider has no saved key fails on that tier with words saying so, and never falls back to another key. <!-- changes/subagent-tier-keys-only.md -->
- `template eval`: the read of a run's timeline page now stops at the run's deadline and at the eval's stop (Ctrl-C), as the read that asks whether a runner holds it does. A page that stalls is given up on after 15 s and asked again. Before, a server that stalled a page held the eval until fetch's own 300 s timeout, past the deadline, and the run then ended "unknown", not cancelled as timed out. A read that the deadline ends now ends the wait at once, with no further page read. A deadline that has already passed sends no read, and a cancel at the deadline that fails still ends the run timed out. `evalTemplate` refuses a `runTimeoutMs` or `queueTimeoutMs` that isn't a number of milliseconds over 0 (NaN, 0, below 0, Infinity) with a RangeError, before anything runs. Before, NaN left the wait with no deadline, and a fraction of a millisecond threw from the claim read. <!-- changes/template-eval-page-read-deadline.md -->
- `GET /v2/wrapped` is 403 on a server that has an API key made in the console for an app (Settings → AgentRun API keys), as on one that takes a second API token: the key's holder no longer reads the machine user's year. Once the keys are revoked, the owner reads it again. <!-- changes/wrapped-api-keys.md -->
- Where each run is a user of its own (the image, `run_isolation: "uid"`), a claude-agent run now runs on the Claude login in AgentRun's own login folder instead of failing at its claim. The runner, as the server's user, reads the login's access token from that folder and hands the run's CLI that token alone, in `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`: never the folder and never the refresh token, so the run's CLI never renews the login. The runner reads the folder again when the run starts and whenever Anthropic refuses the token mid-run, so a renewal your own Claude CLI wrote there is picked up. The runner also renews the login itself, in the CLI's place, when a token has less than five minutes left and after Anthropic refuses one mid-run: it sends the pinned CLI's own refresh request, holds the CLI's own refresh lock on the folder, reads the file again under it (a renewal by the CLI or another runner is taken, and nothing is sent twice), and writes the answer back to that folder's `.credentials.json` alone, atomically at mode 0600, every other field kept. It holds the lock as the CLI does, by the directory it made and the mtime it set (to the microsecond; on a filesystem that keeps whole seconds alone, any mtime in that second, as the CLI reads its own lock there), so a lock another holder took over while the runner was paused is never touched or removed, and nothing is sent under it. Runners take the lock one at a time, a dead one included, through a short-lived `.takeover` directory beside it, so two runners never hold it at once, unless a runner stalls past the 60 s stale time inside a takeover or between its last check of the lock and its removal of it (every lock that expires has these gaps). The CLI does not see that directory: between a runner and the CLI the lock is as safe as the CLI's own, and where the CLI's second lock beside the login folder can be made, it keeps the two from both sending. If the write back fails, the runner keeps the new pair in memory: later asks get its token, send nothing (the old refresh token is spent and never sent again) and try the write again, under the same lock and after reading the file again, so a newer pair another holder wrote is kept; once that token has less than five minutes left and is still unsaved, the run fails in words that say the renewal could not be saved and what to fix. A held token Anthropic refuses is never handed again: the ask fails while its pair is unsaved, and once the pair is saved the runner renews from it. One ask sends at most one renewal and nothing retries it. A renewal that fails, a refresh token Anthropic refused included, fails the run at its start, and ends the turn mid-run, in words that say to open the Claude CLI once to renew the login; a token refused mid-run that the runner had no way to renew ends the turn in words that say to run the claude CLI once on this login to renew it. No token is in the runner's log or in any error, and each token handed is cut from the run's journal, messages and rows as the runner writes them. A command the run's CLI starts can read the token, as the run's own user can. Under per-run users, a run on this machine's own Claude login (`~/.claude`, or the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` AgentRun was started with) still fails at its claim. So does a login run while another runner on the same data folder runs its login runs under the server's user, and the error names that runner. A login kept in a form the runner does not read fails in words too. For each of these, set `AGENTRUN_RUN_USER=same` or give the run a `model_key`. `claudeAgentAdapter({ login })` in `@parcha/agentrun-harness-claude` also takes `{ token(), refused?(sent) }`, a host's reader of the login's access token: on the CLI's request for a newer token it tells the host which token was refused, then answers from `token()`. The pinned CLI's refresh request, lock and write back are exported as `CLAUDE_LOGIN_REFRESH` (and `loginRefresh` from `/facts`), and a test reads each of them in the installed CLI. <!-- changes/claude-login-per-run-users.md -->
- Claude Code's login on this machine now uses a home the server's own user owns: the server's `HOME` when that user owns it, else that user's own home. A server started under a sudo that keeps `HOME` no longer signs Claude Code in as root inside the person's home, leaving files their own CLI can't read, and a service account that inherited someone's `HOME` no longer reads that person's login as its own. Where the server's user owns neither, Settings says why, the turn-on and the sign-in are refused in those words, and a login saved before is turned off at the start. <!-- changes/claude-login-owned-home.md -->

  The refusal of a box agent on Claude Agent that names no model, while the login is on, offers the move to the runner by the model the agent would run there: the host's default for Claude Agent, `AGENT_MODEL` first. Where that is Anthropic's own, the refusal now says the login runs agents on the runner only and carries `details.login_on_runner`, as it does for an agent that names Anthropic's model itself. Before, the refusal named a key and offered no move. Where it is an OpenRouter model, no move is offered, since the moved agent would still need OpenRouter's key.
- A fal job priced by its settings (Kling v3, Veo 3 and 3.1, Ideogram, Nano Banana, sync-lipsync v2, Fabric) can't be priced when get_pricing states its endpoint in another unit than the one its tiers were decided in (per second, minute or image): under a spend cap it is refused unsent, and without one it is booked as an unknown charge. Before, the tier's ratio and its model-page rate were applied in the new unit, so sync-lipsync v2 stated per second would have been held and booked at its per-minute rate for every second (60 times its bill), and one 4K Nano Banana 2 image stated per megapixel at $2.72 against the $0.16 fal bills. <!-- changes/fal-price-unit.md -->
