- A server whose computerd build for its Docker's architecture is not there (built with `npm run build` but not `npm run build:daemon -w @parcha/agentrun-computer`) says so at its start and doesn't offer Docker. Its `boxes` line, the start's banner and capabilities give the reason with the command that builds it ("no daemon for Docker's amd64 at …: run npm run build:daemon -w @parcha/agentrun-computer, then restart AgentRun"). A run that needs a Docker computer or the Docker box is refused at its start with that reason, and a new agent runs on the runner. Before, Docker was offered and every Docker run failed at its computer's create, a fraction of a second in. As with the server's other Docker checks, it is decided once at the start, so a build made later takes a restart. A daemon of another machine, or a layout whose paths Docker lacks, is still said first. <!-- changes/serve-docker-daemon-missing.md -->
  The start's probe of Docker (`docker version`) now names the daemon's architecture with its version, so the check asks Docker nothing more. A server with `AGENTRUN_BOXES` not listing docker still asks Docker nothing.
  `@parcha/agentrun-computer/docker` exports `dockerDaemonOf(arch, dir?)`: the daemon file a Docker computer binds for that architecture, and the words when it is missing. Docker's `create()` takes its daemon there, so it and a server's start check name the same file in the same words.
- Wrapped: a failed read, a long read, a refusal, and a model's price, each said as they are. <!-- changes/wrapped-states.md -->
  - A read of the year that fails (the worker ended, or ran out of memory on a large home) is kept for a minute, like a read that worked. Each ask in that minute is `500 internal`, and the next ask after it reads again. The server logs the failure once, as it fails, `agentrun-serve: the read of this machine's session history for <year> failed: …`. Before, the failure was dropped with no log, often after its ask had already answered 503, so each new ask started another full read and got another 503.
  - Each of `GET /v2/wrapped`'s `models` has `unpriced_requests` (additive): how many of the model's requests its `cost_usd` leaves out. `wrappedHome`'s models carry `unpricedRequests` to match. The console marks "priced only" on the model that has unpriced requests, and shows "no known price" for a model none of whose requests were priced. Before, every model was marked "priced only" once any request of the year was unpriced, and an unlisted model showed "$0.00 priced only".
  - The console's Wrapped page keeps reading through a `503` (a home still being read): it keeps its skeleton, asks again after the server's `retry_after_ms`, and stops when the page closes. Before, it showed "The server is busy" with a Retry button.
  - A `403` on the Wrapped page shows the server's reasons as the why, and the next step is to open Wrapped on one owner's own server. Before, it said to sign in as the server's owner, which fixes none of these refusals.

## 0.1.0-beta.57 (2026-11-24)

**Breaking:**

- API-only (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`): list the origin of every per_run MCP server the API token saved in `AGENTRUN_API_ONLY_MCP_ORIGINS` before upgrading, or token-saved per_run servers are refused. Every API-only start now holds the list it starts with (an empty one when the setting is unset), and a run that grants a token-saved per_run server at an origin off it fails with nothing sent, as does an agent's save that pins it. The start logs one line, `api_only_mcp_off_list`, with the count and names of those servers. Or re-save it from the owner's signed-in session with API-only off, which makes it the owner's and leaves the save closed: a server saved from the owner's session is not governed by the list, whenever it was saved. <!-- changes/api-only-mcp-origins-upgrade.md -->
- TypeScript client: `runs.files(id, { signal })` becomes `runs.files(id, params, { signal })` (`params` may be `undefined`). `runs.files` takes the listing's new `cut` parameter before its request options, so a call that passes options second would lose them without an error. There is no compat shim. <!-- changes/template-eval-grader-cut-names.md -->

  A template eval's llm grader no longer sees a held value through a file's name. The eval read each file's text under the run's cut, but named every file by its path as the run wrote it, in the `<file path>` block, the "Not shown" list and the list of names when every text is left out. A run that named a file by a key (`cache/<key>.json`, `media/<key>.mp3`) put the key in the grader's prompt. The eval now lists the run's files with `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/files?cut=run`, new here: each file also has its `name`, its path under the run's own cut, made the same way as a cut read's text (each value the cut holds and each secret shape replaced by `[redacted]` in place). Every file gets a name whatever its type, so a grader can still be told about an audio file or an image the run made. The grader's prompt names files by these names alone, and a call is pointed at the file it made by name. A server that doesn't know the listing's `cut` lists no names; the eval then shows each text file it read in a `<file>` block with no path and counts the rest ("and 2 files not named"), never naming one by its path. A run whose cut can't be read is `403 forbidden`, as the listing already was; any other `cut` is `400 bad_request`. Without `cut`, the listing is unchanged. The TypeScript and Python clients and the CLI take the new parameter (`agentrun runs files RUN_ID --cut run`, `client.runs.files(runId, { cut: "run" })`, `client.runs.files(run_id, cut="run")`).
- After this upgrade, a Claude login on this machine that was turned on before it reads "turned on for another machine" (`other_machine`) once, and its runs ask for a key until it is turned on again. Turn it on again under Settings → Model keys. The setting now names the machine by an id the server makes once in its data folder (`machine-id`, 0600) in place of the hostname, which changed with a laptop's network; a setting saved before has no id. <!-- changes/claude-login-machine-id.md -->

**Changes:**

- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) can now take a per_run MCP server save from its token, at origins its operator names in `AGENTRUN_API_ONLY_MCP_ORIGINS` (comma-separated, for example `https://mcp.example.com`). A backend in front of the server can save its gateway (`PUT /v2/settings/mcp-servers/{name}` with `"auth": {"type": "per_run"}`) on a fresh install or after a store reset, without turning API-only off for the save. Runs still bring their own credential in `mcp_auth`, and the server keeps none. A body that carries a credential is `403`, and so is a save over a server the token did not save or one that seals a credential. A per_run body at any other origin, any other auth type and a Composio server's name are the profile's `404`. Each refusal comes before anything is sent to the address. With the setting unset or blank, the save is a `404` as before. A loopback origin still needs `AGENTRUN_MCP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK=1`. A wildcard entry stops the start. The list also holds after the save: drop an origin and restart, and a run that grants a server the token saved there sends it nothing and fails in words saying why. <!-- changes/api-only-mcp-origins.md -->
- A run's browser that its owner took over in the live view now reads `computer.state: "taken_over"` on GET /v2/runs/{run_id} and GET /v2/computers/running, as a desktop or a phone does, so Settings → Computers → Running now shows "You drive" for it. Before, a browser always read `ready` there while its owner had it. The run's process keeps one setting per run while the take is live, writes it in order, and removes it as the take ends, as the process starts (a take a crashed process left), and at the run's end. <!-- changes/browser-take-over-you-drive.md -->
- The owner can now make API keys for their apps in the console, under Settings → AgentRun API keys. Before, the only credentials were the tokens the server was started with (`AGENTRUN_TOKEN`, `AGENTRUN_TOKENS` or `DIR/.token`), so there was no way to get an `AGENTRUN_API_KEY` from the console. <!-- changes/console-api-keys.md -->
  - `POST /v2/settings/api-keys` with `{name}` answers the key once, as `api_key` (`ar_key_` and 32 random bytes). `GET /v2/settings/api-keys` lists each key's name, when it was made and when it was last used, never a key. `DELETE /v2/settings/api-keys/{api_key_id}` revokes one: the next request that carries it is `401`.
  - A key opens what a token opens on `/v2` and `/mcp`. It is never the setup code.
  - Making and revoking are secret writes: the owner's signed-in session alone. A token, or a key, gets `403 forbidden` with the console page in `details.console_url`.
  - The server keeps a keyed hash of each key, never the key. A key that turns up in a run's text, a shared transcript or a learned note is cut by its shape (`ar_key_` and 43 or more base64url characters, a capital or a digit among them), whatever stands before it, since the server holds no value to cut it by.
  - A key is one more caller that starts runs, as a second token is. A server with Claude Code's login on makes no key, and a server with a key refuses to turn that login on until the key is revoked (`403 forbidden`, in words, each way). On a server started with `--harness-sign-in` a key opens nothing, and is still listed so its owner can revoke it. An API-only server takes no key and serves none of these routes.
  - A row under the keys' name in the store that is no key's (damaged, or another version's) opens nothing and counts toward the limit. The list names it in `unreadable`, the console shows it with Remove, and `DELETE` with its id removes it.
  - A server keeps at most 50 keys; the next create is `409 api_keys_full`. Capabilities say `features.api_keys`. A request a key opened is logged with `api_key=<id>`.
  - The CLI gains `agentrun api-keys list`. A suggested agent's pull request and the Playground's code pane now link to the page that makes a key.
- Console: the Build an agent page has a Tools step. Before the agent is created, pick its tools with the Detailed editor's own cards, the MCP servers saved in Settings (a Composio Gmail server, say) among them, and where it runs (on the server or in a sandbox box). The picks go on the playground's create request (`definition.tools`, `definition.place`) and into the coding-agent prompt. A step left alone sends the same request as before: no tools, no place. <!-- changes/console-build-tools-step.md -->
- Settings → MCP servers → Add from Composio picks the toolkit from the list Composio offers (**Load toolkits**, then a picker by name and slug) instead of a typed slug, and a saved Composio server's row says whether its account is connected and which account it is once you press **Refresh**. <!-- changes/console-composio-toolkit-picker.md -->
  - `POST /v2/settings/mcp-servers/composio/toolkits` `{api_key}` answers `{toolkits: [{slug, name}]}`, every page of Composio's list (at most 20 pages and 8 MiB; a cursor Composio repeats ends it), sorted by name. It stores nothing and is the owner's session alone (403 to the API token), as the actions listing is.
  - A refresh of a Composio server reads its account at Composio, and every read of the server then carries `composio_account: {state, labels?, checked_at}`: `connected` with each account's label (its alias, else the name Composio shows, else its word id; never its id or a token), `pending`, `expired`, `none`, or `unknown` when Composio didn't answer. An account Composio answers as another user's is never the server's. The API token sees it too, in a server's full read, and a label may be an email. A per-run server, a toolkit that needs no sign-in, and a server saved before its save recorded what it stands on have none.
  - The picker takes no free entry: a toolkit Composio doesn't list can't be typed in the console (the API still takes any slug).
- The console's Templates and Build pages list the marketplace's templates beside this server's own (GRE-4834), as `GET /v2/marketplace/templates` answers them: this server's packages first, then the marketplace's others under the same search. Install opens the install page (the package read whole, its publisher trusted once) when the list names a source, else the template's marketplace page. <!-- changes/console-marketplace.md -->
  - The two pages list what the marketplace lists, in its order. The bundled `agent-scout`, which the Suggested page runs and the marketplace does not list, is no longer on either page; the API playground and `GET /v2/templates` still list it. A card's title is its display name up to its first parameter ("Code review", not "Code review: …/…"), and a card the marketplace lists reads the marketplace's one-line summary.
  - A marketplace card leads with its harness's icon and lists its harnesses, as this server's cards do, when the list gives them.
  - A marketplace that fails, or that the server could not read just now, is said on both pages with Try again; this server's own templates stay listed.
- The console starts a race at `#/races/new` (New race, on the Runs list's toolbar): one task, a cost cap per lane, and 2 to 4 lanes, each a harness and a model this server runs. Start sends one inline run per lane (POST /v2/runs) with the labels the race view reads (`race`, `lane`, `harness`, `model`), then opens `#/races/<label>` once every lane has a run. <!-- changes/console-race-start.md -->
  - Each lane is an agent of its own (external id `race-<label>-<n>`), with one revision per harness and model, so changing a lane after a refusal makes a new revision rather than a conflict.
  - Each lane gets the tools a new agent gets on this server: every tool its harness runs here, plus the shell where the server's default place is a box. An inline run is granted no tools of its own, so a lane without them could not touch a file. A lane names no place, so the server puts it where it puts that new agent: in the box only with the shell (pi), and on the runner for an adapter harness such as codex or claude-agent, where Claude Code's login works and no box starts.
  - Each lane stays in the Agents list as an inline agent; DELETE removes one.
  - A lane the server refuses shows the server's words in its own place, and the other lanes start anyway. Start again sends only the lanes left, each under the Idempotency-Key its first request had, so no lane starts twice.
  - A lane whose answer never came whole (a lost answer, a timeout, a 5xx, a start the server is still making) may have started, so it says so and keeps its harness, model and the race's task and cap. Start again sends the same request under the same key, and the server answers with the run if it made one. Only a refusal lets a lane change.
  - Lanes are seeded when capabilities first name a harness that runs, so a race never starts with fewer than two.
  - A new race's label is its start time (UTC, to the minute) and twelve random hex characters, so two races started in the same minute never share a race page.
- The console's Dev tools tab says which attempt a cost line was made in, and what a run's repeated requests cost. Where an attempt at a turn was cut (its runner drained, crashed or lost its lease, or the turn was tried again) and another took the turn over, the model requests the cut one had sent and not finished were sent again. Each line of Cost by line then names its attempt, the repeated ones as "requests cut before they answered, sent again"; "Requests sent twice" under the split gives the server's own sum (`infra_usd` on `GET /runs/{id}/usage`) with its share of the run's cost, or "at most" that sum with no share where a line is a ceiling; and What stands out lists it after what failed. A run none of whose attempts was cut reads as before. <!-- changes/dev-tools-attempts-redone-work.md -->
- The console's Dev tools tab says when a run stopped short for its budget, and how much of its cap its cost is. What stands out leads with it for a run whose `stopped_for` is `budget` (it wound down near its cap, named as it was set) or that had tool calls refused for its budget (`budget_refused_calls`): how many were refused, unrun. Refused calls name no amount, since a call refused before a raise met an earlier cap. The Cost tile says the run's cost against its `max_cost_usd` ("84% of its $0.75 cap"), "at most" that share where the cost is a ceiling. A run that stopped short with no request and no call in its trace (a CLI harness's) says so too. A run with no cap, or one that never came near it, reads as before. <!-- changes/dev-tools-budget-stop.md -->
- The console compares runs at `#/compare?runs=<id>,<id>`: two to four runs' Dev tools figures side by side, a column a run in the order the address names them. It shows each run's model requests, tool calls, failures, tokens, share of input read from cache, cost and time, then each tool's calls and time and each model's requests, tokens and cost. With two runs it also says the second against the first. A figure a run's trace does not carry is said as not known, with no difference: a CLI harness's requests, tokens and model time, and a model it recorded no request to. Nor is a difference said of a figure that is not exact: "at least" for a run whose trace is its first 2,000 requests and calls, whose requests did not all report tokens, or a time where a request's or a call's length was not recorded, "at most" for a cost that counts a cut request at what was held for it. Each run and its trace are read once, when the page opens. <!-- changes/dev-tools-compare-runs.md -->
  - A race's page links to it ("Compare in figures") once it has two lanes, in the lanes' order.
  - A run's Dev tools tab has Compare, which asks for the other run by its id or its page's address.
- The console's Dev tools tab draws a run's computers and browser sessions on its time axis. Once the run's usage is read (`computer_intervals` and `browser_sessions` on `GET /runs/{id}/usage`), the overview has a lane for each under the calls, and the Breakdown lists each one: what it is and its size or its provider's id, when it started against the first request, how long it was up, how much of that is in the run's cost, and what else its record says (kept while the run waited for a person, closed by the agent, an attempt that was cut). A computer made before the first request or deleted after the last call is drawn open at that end. A browser session whose start was never recorded (its runner died before its release) has a row with what was charged for it, and no bar. A run with no request and no call lists its computers and sessions all the same, against the run's start. One with no end recorded says how long it had been up when the run ended. One that lies wholly outside the trace's time (a session opened after the last span a long run's trace holds) has its row and no bar. A run with neither shows no lane. <!-- changes/dev-tools-computers-browser-lanes.md -->
- A call in the console's Dev tools tab and the recording made while it ran open each other. A tool call's details offer "Show on the recording" once the run is over and a finished recording has the call as a step: the Screen tab then plays that recording from the call's time. Under a recording's steps, "Open this step in Dev tools" opens the Dev tools tab on the details of the call the video is at; it is off, and says why, while that step is not a tool call. A step opens the very call it is, by its span, though another conversation made a call of the same id. A call past the trace's first 2,000 requests and calls opens no details, and the tab says so. Neither is offered where the run's trace can't be read. <!-- changes/dev-tools-recording-link.md -->
- `agentrun-serve eval-template`: a fake MCP server's answer can match an argument by a regular expression, and a case can seed its runs' work folders. In a fixture's `when`, a value `{"$pattern": "<regex>"}` (that key alone) matches a call whose argument is a string the regex matches whole, anchored by the eval even when the pattern has no `^` or `$`, so a fixture answers keys made of a run's random stem (`{"submission_key": {"$pattern": "ns-[a-z0-9]{8}-voice-cold-open"}}`); every other value is still compared by equality. A `$pattern` that is no string, does not compile, or sits beside another key fails the case when it is read, naming the tool and the answer. A case's `case.yaml` takes `files`, a mapping of a path in the run's work folder to its text: the eval's runner writes each one at the run's claim, before its computer and its first turn, and leaves a file the folder already holds, so a case can start a run where an earlier one left off (a resume that reads `media/run-keys.json`). A path that is absolute, empty, has an empty, `.` or `..` segment, or lies under `inputs/`, and a text that is not a string, fail the case when it is read. Only the eval's own server honours `files`, so a case with it refuses `--server`. <!-- changes/eval-pattern-files.md -->
- A live run shows what it waits on while it waits, not only once it answers (GRE-4835): a model request from the moment it is sent, on every harness, and each tool call until it returns. A slow local model reading a long prompt shows "inkling-2-mini thinking · 2:13" under the run's header, ticking; a slow `web_fetch` shows "web_fetch · 0:41". <!-- changes/in-flight-requests.md -->
  - The kernel stamps each model request's record (`runner.request`) with when it left (`at`) and the input it was admitted with (`inputTokensMax`), written before the request leaves, as the record already was. `ModelPortOptions.now` sets the clock.
  - `GET /v2/runs/{id}/timeline` pages carry `in_flight` (`inflight/1`, this server's own beside the vendored contract): each model request with no answer yet (its model, `started_at`, `input_tokens_max`, and `for_tool` for a tool's own request) and each tool call with no result yet (its tool, `started_at`, `tool_use_id`), oldest first; empty once the run is final. A request sent or answered is a change of the page, so a long poll or the event stream wakes for it.
  - Not yet: tokens counted while a model streams its answer; the Dev tools trace still lists a model request once it answers.
- `GET /v2/marketplace/templates` (serve's `marketplace/1`) answers the list marketplace.agentrun.ai publishes (GRE-4834), each entry with `here`, the id of the package on this server that it is. The server reads it only when a page or a caller asks, keeps it 5 minutes, keeps the last good list through a failed read (`stale`), and answers `unreachable` with an empty list when no read has worked, always with a 200. Each entry is checked field by field; nothing on it is imported or run. An entry carries its `source` (the package an install reads, pinned to a commit) and its package's `harness` preference list when the list gives them. `agentrun local list-marketplace-templates` reads the same list. <!-- changes/marketplace-templates.md -->
  - `AGENTRUN_MARKETPLACE=off` reads no marketplace; an https address (http on loopback) reads that site's list; any other value stops the start. Under `--faux` it is off unless it names an address. A service keeps it: `agentrun service install --env AGENTRUN_MARKETPLACE=off` (or an address), and `AGENTRUN_MARKETPLACE=` removes it.
  - Failure behavior: the read takes at most 10 s, 4 MiB and 1000 entries and follows no redirect; a failed read is retried after a minute, not on every page.
- The models of this machine's Ollama run on every harness on Anthropic's Messages, not just pi: claude-agent, Goose, and a harness module on that wire. They go through the same translation pi's requests take, so they get the same `/api/chat`, `num_ctx`, tools as text where a model needs it, $0, and no count toward `AGENTRUN_FREE_MODEL_REQUESTS`. They are listed in those harnesses' models and free models, and a run's page shows "<tag> · local (Ollama)". codex and opencode, on OpenAI's Responses, don't list them. The trust rules are unchanged: Ollama at the default address only on one owner's own server, and elsewhere only where `OLLAMA_HOST` names it. <!-- changes/messages-wire-ollama.md -->
  - On upgrade: on a server with no model key and Ollama running, claude-agent and Goose now start the runs they refused before, on Ollama's first model that calls tools, as pi does. A saved agent on either harness that names no model follows that default. Name the model to pin it. Any key wins.
  - With no model, their words name Ollama first, as pi's do: "No model yet for claude-agent: start Ollama and pull a model with tools, or add an OpenRouter or Anthropic key".
  - A Messages client's token count (`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens`) is answered by the translation, without asking the model. A request that doesn't ask to stream gets its answer whole, or a 500 error with words when part of the stream doesn't read. Every model id the client sends, Claude Code's small model included, runs the one tag.
  - A Messages `tool_choice` that forces a call (`any`, or one naming a tool) is refused with a 400: Ollama can't be made to call a tool. `auto` and `none` are taken.
  - On these models claude-agent turns off its own tool search and gets the server's `tools_search`, and it offers no provider web search. So `web_search: native` reads unavailable there, in capabilities and at a run's start, and `auto` uses Parallel or keyless Firecrawl.
  - A harness module's launch (`ModuleLaunch`) gains `fetch`. When it is set, the module's model proxy forwards with it to the route's origin.
- Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and every run exports a GenAI trace: model calls, tool calls, tokens with cache, no content. Each run on a pi or CLI harness is one trace through the official OpenTelemetry SDK, its spans named by the GenAI semantic conventions (`invoke_agent`, `chat`, `execute_tool`), its token counts on chat spans only, with `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` inclusive of the cache. A run's end never waits on the collector, and no `OTEL_*` setting (an OTLP header holds a backend's key) reaches a run's harness, tools or computer. Unset, no OpenTelemetry code loads. `@parcha/agentrun-import` adds `otelUsage` (a request's counts as a trace carries them) and an `openrouter` format to `normalizeUsage`. <!-- changes/otel-genai-traces.md -->
- A template package with triggers no longer needs a `budget` when every trigger has its own spend cap (`target.max_cost_usd`, a number above 0). `agentrun template validate`, an import and an apply take such a package. With no budget, one trigger without a cap of its own is refused, and the error names it (`triggers[1] (evening) has no max_cost_usd of its own, and the package has no budget`). A cap of 0, a negative, NaN or Infinity counts as none. `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/package` and `agentrun export` follow the same rule. An agent with no `max_cost_usd` whose triggers each have a cap now exports a package that validates. Before, any trigger blocked the export (`budget max_cost_usd`). Now only a trigger with no cap of its own blocks it, as a `trigger` note that names it. The agent such a package makes has no cap of its own, so a run its person starts has none, as on any agent made without `max_cost_usd`. Each run a trigger fires is capped at that trigger's cap. A package that reads today reads the same. <!-- changes/package-trigger-caps.md -->
- `GET /v2/capabilities` says, for each harness, which of its `models` a run takes now: `ready_models`, those whose provider is connected here (its key set, or the ChatGPT sign-in where that is how the harness runs them). A model that lacks only its key stays in `models` and is not in `ready_models`. The console's Model picker (the agent editor and the API playground's agent requests) lists the ready ones, each tagged with its provider, shows the others on "Show models that need a key", and says where to connect a provider when none is. <!-- changes/ready-models.md -->
  - Breaking: a client that validates capabilities against `harness/5` refuses the new `ready_models` field; the shape's mark is now `harness/6`.
- A scrubber for what leaves the machine: `agentrun scrub <run>` counts what a share of a run would cut, per rule, and never prints a value. The rules live in `secret-rules.ts` beside the existing cut (`secret-cut.ts`), and `scrub(text, { mode })` runs one rule set two ways: `count` (how many, of what kind, where) and `cut` (the text with each match replaced). Cut mode fails closed: any error gives `{ ok: false }` and no text. <!-- changes/scrubber-beta-1.md -->
  - Every rule is anchored: a known key format (the learning guard's shapes and secretlint's preset), a value the server holds, or a label beside the value (`PGPASSWORD=`, `sshpass -p`, `mysql -p`, `--password`, `Authorization:`, `curl -u`, a key-named variable). No rule fires on randomness alone.
  - New cuts: passwords typed in commands, whole dumps (`env`/`printenv` output, `.env*` files, `~/.ssh` contents) dropped as one marker, credential files (`.netrc`, `.pgpass`, docker and kube configs), emails, private IPs (RFC 1918, CGNAT, ULA), and home paths, whose user segment becomes `<user>` (`/root` names no one and stays).
  - Each cut carries its rule, its kind (`format`, `held`, `dump`, `label`, `personal`) and whether a person may restore it: label and personal cuts may be restored, a known-format key, a held value or a dump never. `keep` restores only the first two.
  - A JSON-escaped text gets the same cuts as the text it encodes, up to three levels deep, and a cut never splits an escape. Placeholders and references (`$VAR`, `$(cmd)`, `op://...`, `<your-key>`, `REPLACE_ME`, `sk-...`) are never cut.
  - After cutting, the result is checked again for a held value or a known key format; cut mode fails closed if one is left, and `agentrun scrub` says a share of the run would be refused. Long texts are read in overlapping pieces, never truncated.
  - A key longer than any real one (a 70,000-character `sk-` key, say) is now cut whole, and the share goes through; it used to make the share refuse.
  - A quoted password that holds a shell operator (`redis-cli -a 'pa&ss'`) is cut whole, a query or form password longer than 1,024 characters (`?new_password=…`) is too, and so is a curl password after a command substitution (`curl -H "X-Time: $(date)" -u admin:…`); before, part or all of each stayed visible.
  - `packages/serve/test/fixtures/scrub-negatives/` is a frozen set of 489 things that look like secrets and are not (git SHAs, UUIDs, content hashes, lockfile integrity strings, base64 images, code, prose, the shapes a sweep of real runs found cut wrongly). A cut in any of them fails CI.
- A launch hook's host can release a firing it answered 2xx but will start no run for: `POST /v2/triggers/{trigger_id}/firings/{firing_id}/release` with `{ "error": "<plain words>" }`. The firing is `failed` at once (`host_released`, with the host's words) and its trigger's place under `max_active_runs` frees. Before, the firing held that place until its `start_by`, 10 minutes later, so the next firings waited. When a release waits and what it refuses are stated once, in the route's OpenAPI description; how it meets a run's `trigger_firing` start, in that field's. The CLI has `agentrun triggers release-firing`, and the TypeScript and Python clients have `triggers.releaseFiring` / `triggers.release_firing`. <!-- changes/trigger-firing-release.md -->
- `@parcha/agentrun-web` is new: the machinery behind `web_search` and `web_fetch`, moved out of `@parcha/agentrun-serve` with no change to what a model is sent or told. It holds the providers (Parallel, keyless Firecrawl, keyless Exa, a hosted search given as a function, and the direct fetch), a breaker per provider, the per-run page cache read in parts, and Parallel's prices. It imports no server, browser or vendor SDK code. The provider order, keys, public-host guard, run cap and refusal words come in through `WebConfig`. `createWeb(config)` answers a search or a fetch together with a receipt of the providers tried and the fees sent. `@parcha/agentrun-web/text-urls` exports the link finder alone. `@parcha/agentrun-serve` now depends on it and answers both tools through one `createWeb` per run, with pi-browser's `publicFetch` and `publicCheck` as the guard. `@parcha/pi-browser` exports `publicCheck(url, { lookup, signal })`, the check `publicFetch` makes on every hop, without dialling. Both refuse a loopback, `.local` or `.internal` name written with one or more trailing dots before any lookup, as they refuse it without them. <!-- changes/web-extract.md -->

  Two things a server's users can see change:

  - A workflow's call node that runs `web_search` now gets its answer held to 100,000 characters, as an agent's `web_search` already was. Past that, the least relevant results are left out and `omitted` counts them. Before, a call node got the whole answer.
  - The MCP client keyless Firecrawl and keyless Exa are asked through now names itself `agentrun-web` in its `initialize` request, in place of `agentrun-serve`.
- `web_search`'s default, `auto`, is now agentrun's own search on every harness: Parallel where the server holds a Parallel key, else keyless Firecrawl with keyless Exa behind it. Before, `auto` on codex was Codex's own live search, and on pi with a direct `anthropic/*` or `openai/*` model it was one request to that provider's hosted search. Both now go through agentrun's `web_search` instead. This changes what a codex or pi search costs and returns: Parallel's fee per search on the server's key, or keyless Firecrawl at no charge, in place of the provider's per-search fee, and those providers' results in place of Codex's or the model provider's. <!-- changes/web-search-auto-ours.md -->
  `native` stays a provider you can pick, for an agent (`definition.tool_settings`) or the server (`PUT /settings/tools`). Picked, it still turns on Claude's WebSearch, Codex's live search or pi's hosted search, and it is unavailable where it was before (behind a gateway, on OpenRouter, under a spend cap). To keep the old behaviour on codex or pi, pick `native`. claude-agent's `auto` is unchanged.
  The openapi document's `web_search` provider list is unchanged (`native` stays in it). Only `auto`'s description and capabilities' `resolves` and `why` change: on codex and pi, `resolves` reads `parallel` or `firecrawl-keyless` where it read `native`. A run that started before the upgrade keeps the plane it launched with, `native` included, for its life.
  A claude-agent session now also names the claude CLI's WebFetch in its `disallowedTools` (`CLAUDE_AGENT_ALSO_OFF`), as it names WebSearch. WebFetch was already off three ways: the session's tools list is empty, the PreToolUse hook denies it, and the CLI's sandbox network is deny-all. Naming it keeps the host's `web_fetch` the session's only fetch even if one of those changes.
- The agent editor keeps a harness whose default model needs a key it lacks as a choice. Its card says "Needs a model key", since a save of it is taken with a warning. A harness off for another reason stays greyed out. <!-- changes/b42-agent-editor-needs-key.md -->
- Each saved harness key is bound to the recipe file it was saved for (its sha256) and to the seal key it was sealed under. A later recipe file that takes the same id never opens it. That holds even for a claim that read the first file's binding while a save for the later one landed: the binding holds the digest of the sealed bytes it was written with. It also holds for a run's process that loaded a recipe file swapped since its runner started, because the process asks for the keys bound to the file it loaded itself. The Harness keys page lists such a key to paste again and says why (`reenter`: `recipe_changed`, `seal_key_changed` or `file_unreadable`). <!-- changes/b42-harness-keys-binding.md -->

  A recipe the server is no longer started with keeps its keys, sealed and cut, and nothing runs them. The page lists them under the recipe's id (`named: false`, `kept`), and `DELETE` removes each one. It also removes a key that no recipe runs on any more, or one that no longer opens. Capabilities name each such id (`features.harness_keys.kept`) to the owner's session or a token holder, and to no other caller, so the console keeps offering the page until those keys are removed.
- The share-card renderer draws what it is given: <!-- changes/b48-card-and-sign-in-followups.md -->
  - A columns chart of a year by day draws every column. Past about 268 bars it drew none.
  - Under a title that wraps, the rows drop from the end, in reading order. Before, the 3rd and 6th rows went missing from the middle. `cardCapacity` says how many rows draw, beside each chart's bar count.
  - The image's alt text reads only what is drawn, each value as its bar shows it.

  A ChatGPT sign-in that fails with an authorize code that neither OAuth, OpenID Connect nor OpenAI sends (any local process can answer the sign-in's callback) is said on the terminal as `authorize_other`. `agentrun-serve` run on its own still logs the code; under `agentrun start`, the terminal line is all that is kept. A sign-in's change that the server failed to take is taken again one read at a time, so reads at once no longer each relist and probe.
- A ChatGPT sign-in reads signed in once it is saved, while the server still relists what it offers. A pasted sign-in that a sign-out, a newer start or the 10 minutes cut off says so, in the words Settings shows, never that the log says why. A sign-out whose relist fails still signs out. A relist that failed is taken again at the next read, even when an earlier one finished after it, and reads at once relist once. <!-- changes/b49-plan-refresh-followups.md -->

  `agentrun start` keeps the server's line of a ChatGPT sign-in that did not finish in `start.log`, its authorize code whole; the terminal still says a code the authorize step never sends as `authorize_other`.

  The share card's alt text reads at most 365 bars of a chart, then how many more there are.
- A browser `run` call the browser refused before it ran (pi-browser's typed failure `code: "refused"`, such as code sent to a local Chrome that takes only actions) now reads on its Timeline row as what the browser refused: "The browser refused the code to open iana.org/help/example-domains: run code is not available on this browser …". Before, it read "Opened iana.org/help/example-domains failed: …", as if the page had failed to open. Any other failure of the call reads as before. `registerLabel`'s `saysFailure` also takes a test of the errored result, for a tool whose label says only some of its failures. <!-- changes/browser-refused-code-label.md -->
- A run's claim now lays its model keys where only a read by name finds them. A copy or spread of the tools' environment, and every process a tool spawns from it (the browser, the CLI tool plane, a workflow's call nodes), no longer carries the server's model key; the run's own route still reads it by name. A run's own process is now handed its pinned model's key alone: before, it also got a second claim's key, its revision's model's or the host's default's at the time of the hand-off, which could be another provider's saved since the run started. A `--faux` start still gets its revision's model's key, as before. <!-- changes/claim-model-keys-scope.md -->
- A claude-agent run on a clock the host set (the adapter's `now`; in serve, a template eval case's `now:`) is now told that clock's day by the Claude CLI too. The CLI dates the session from the machine's clock in its own lines ("Today's date is 2026-11-24.", and "Today's date is now ..." on a later day), and has no setting for it. On a case clock set to another day, the model was told both days and went by the CLI's, so every date a grader checked against the case clock failed. The session's model proxy now rewrites those two lines to the clock's day in the run's zone (`zone`), in the CLI's own `system` message only, where the CLI puts them. The person's prompt, the model's replies, tool results and the app's system prompt are never rewritten, so a date someone wrote, quoted or read reaches the model as it was. A run with no `now`, which is every production run, is unchanged. <!-- changes/claude-agent-case-clock-date.md -->
  A session on a person's Claude login has no model proxy, so there the CLI's lines keep the machine's date. Run clocked cases on the provider route (an API key or gateway).
- A computer whose every tool is set to deny is no longer started, so its provider no longer bills you for a phone, desktop, sandbox or browser the agent can't use. Saving such an agent answers a warning on `definition.computer`: "Every tool for this agent's phone is set to deny, so a run never starts it: allow one, or set the computer to none." Its runs go on without the computer, and the run's start no longer asks for that computer's keys or host setup. A computer with even one tool allowed starts as before. The console's agent editor lists such a warning under "Saved. A run of this revision goes on, as each line says:", apart from the warnings that refuse a run until the server has what they name. <!-- changes/computer-all-denied.md -->
  Once a run's first call of its desktop, phone or browser tools is refused for a deny (a setting changed while the run goes), that computer is off for the rest of the run: the refusal says so once, and every later call of its tools is refused at once, in short words, without reaching the computer, even if the setting is allowed again. This holds when the run resumes later (after a park, an approval or a runner's restart): the computer is not started again, and the run's timeline says why. A desktop, phone or sandbox kept through that park is deleted at the resume rather than 10 minutes later, and its mount of the run's folder is removed with it, so the resumed run can write its folder. A person turning down an asked call does not turn the computer off.
- A run whose kept computer its provider refuses to attach again (a Docker computer with network allow or open made before the egress bridge) goes on with a new one, as before, and its timeline now says why: "The sandbox kept before could not be taken back: …", in the provider's words, before "It's a new sandbox". <!-- changes/computer-kept-refused-says-why.md -->
- A run's `computer.state` can now be `released`: the run is stopped, or parked on a question or an approval with no desktop, phone or sandbox kept for its resume. Before, such a run read `ready` though its computer was gone, so Settings → Computers' Running now listed it. `GET /v2/computers/running` leaves released runs out. A client that switches on `computer.state` should treat `released` as a computer the run no longer has; its next turn starts a new one. <!-- changes/computers-released-order-tab.md -->
  - A run's recordings list its computers in the order they started recording, not by computer id. The recorder now writes each file's start into its MP4 header (mvhd's creation time), and the order holds while a computer records on.
  - On a run's Screen tab, Tab leaves the live viewer while the agent drives, and the viewer takes the focus on load only for a person who holds the computer.
- Console: on the Connect agent page, the "Connect agent" hand-off for This server heads its section, at the right of "Discover on this server", as it does for Another machine. On a wide window it stood on the tabs' line: it touched the last tab with no gap, was 32px high beside 40px tabs, and its bottom edge sat 7px above theirs. <!-- changes/console-connect-agent-tabs-line.md -->
- Console: labels and layouts say what a control does, and like things look alike. <!-- changes/console-handoff-labels.md -->
  - Buttons that hand a prompt to your coding agent say what they are for and show when they leave the console: "Query" reads "Ask about runs", or "Ask about this session" when Mission Control is scoped to a connected session; "Connect agent" reads "Connect your agents"; and a trailing arrow marks the main action when it opens another app (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor).
  - Mission Control's getting-started card: its toggle reads "See templates" in place of "Run an agent here", since it shows the templates rather than starting a run, and each starter card says what it does once (the line that repeated its description is gone).
  - Templates page: every card's buttons look the same (Configure in outline, Run the main action); a template whose setup is only parameters no longer swaps them. A card's MCP servers are an "Apps" row of the apps they reach, as icons (HubSpot, Slack, Gmail, GitHub and others), named on hover and for a screen reader with where their tools come from, in place of "MCP hubspot (Composio, optional)"; a toolkit with no icon to be had is its name in words.
  - Build page: the composer, its coding-agent prompt and the templates share one column, and every template card shows "Use this template" without being clicked open first (its version, which choosing a template never needs, is left to the Templates page).
  - Learning tab: each of the four figures at the top says one short line under it, with its whole basis (interval, bar, audits) on hover and to a screen reader; under them the loop's five stages show their values alone, since the figures say their numbers, and each stage's state is its icon (its word on hover and to a screen reader), so a narrow stage's title stays on one line. "Since it learned" is a row of the same figure cells, lined up with the four above. The learned workflow takes a full-width row of its own under the cost of a run, its words beside its graph where there is room, and its name never breaks mid-word; it was a 17.5rem column beside the chart at some widths.
  - Back arrows: an agent's page, its editor and a connected agent's page go back to the console page you came from, as a run's page already did, and to their parent page when opened from a link. An editor opened from its agent's page went to the agents list.
  - A connected agent's panel says its facts a line each (the whole value on hover), keeps verification and capabilities in one closed disclosure of short rows, and says what Verify and Disconnect do on their buttons, and what Disconnect kept once it has.
  - A list filter's count ("3 of 5 shown") stands inside its box, so picking a filter never changes the box's width.
  - Mission Control: a failed group's square, time and Run all again stay on its first line when its list of runs opens.
  - An agent's page shows the same icon in its top bar as its card on the agents list (its runtime's: pi, Codex, Claude Code, a workflow), where it showed a generic robot.
  - Connect agent page: This server's hand-off heads its Discover section, at the right of its title as Another machine's does, where it stood touching the tabs on their line.
- Console, from a first local run of AgentRun (GRE-4829): <!-- changes/console-local-test-feedback.md -->
  - An agent's page has its run box again: type, Run, and the run's page opens. Handing the run to a coding agent and the API playground are the box's second line; the bar's Run agent hand-off stays for native, SDK and CLI agents, which run where they live.
  - "Approvals" reads "Tool approvals" (in the editor and a template's setup): "A tool set to ask waits for your OK before it runs." The editor says it is not about questions, and lists ask_person first among the tools, as "Lets the agent stop and ask you a question" (its blurb on `GET /v2/capabilities` too).
  - Connecting GitHub takes the organization as people paste it (its github.com address, its own page at `github.com/orgs/<login>` or `github.com/organizations/<login>/…`, or @name) and says so in words when what was typed is no login or one of github.com's own pages, sending nothing.
  - An agent card draws its harness or runtime as its icon alone: the chip in words beside the name ("pi", "Codex") is gone, and the icon is named on hover and for a screen reader ("Pi", "Claude Code"). A template's Harness line shows the same icons, each named, in place of the harness ids.
  - One icon rule across the console: a card that stands for an agent or a template leads with its harness's icon (a template's, the harness it prefers first, named with the others). The Templates page's template icon and the Build page's icon picked per template are gone. Where a harness is named, its icon and name show in place of its id: an agent's Harness or Runtime fact, a connected session's Harness, a key's harnesses in Settings, and What runs here. "claude-agent doesn't run on this server" reads "Claude doesn't run on this server".
  - The API playground's Start a run has one row: the operation, the agent beside it, and the request's path once.
  - The Suggested page's Created agents are cards, as its suggestions are: when each was made, its harness, what it takes and answers, and how far along it is (the agent, its pull request, its first call, once the client its pull request adds is wired in at the line the scan named and its variables are set, then its runs), with reviewing the pull request (or opening it, when it did not open) as the one main action.
  - The Suggested page's line on what a repository's app is spans the width of the suggestions under it, both columns.
- `agentrun deploy` checks the package as the target's import checks it before it sends anything, and refuses one the target would refuse: exit 2, the target's own words, no request made and no lock written. A `category` the platform does not have (`category: productivity`) is one, as is an answer's schema it would not read or a package over its limits. Before, the package was uploaded and the target refused it (`input_invalid`). The check is the import's own: the server installed with the CLI runs it (`agentrun-serve check-upload`, the upload's `{files}` body on stdin), so the two never disagree. The CLI starts it with its own node, not the server's shell launcher, so it works on Windows too. `check-upload` decodes stdin whole, so a character split between two reads stays intact. <!-- changes/deploy-checks-package.md -->
  - The refusal of an unknown category names the value it got: `category is one of engineering, security, sales, marketing, research, finance, operations, compliance, personal, not "productivity"`.
- Three things the console's Dev tools said wrongly of real runs. A recording's step that was clicked is now the step marked and the one "Open this step in Dev tools" opens (of two steps at the same millisecond, still the later): Chrome reads a video sent to 4.023 s as 4.022999 s, and the step before was taken for it. "Show on the recording" lands on the call's own step for the same reason. The compare page says a run's cost as "at least" what is priced where one of its charges has no price, as the run's own tab says its cost so far, where it said the cost was not known. A run whose model was told to wrap up for its spend cap with no tool call refused reads "The run was told to wrap up for its budget", in the plain colour, and no longer in red that it stopped short near its cap: such a run may have done all it was asked, well under the cap. A run with refused calls still reads, in red, that it stopped short. <!-- changes/dev-tools-live-fixes.md -->
- A server whose Docker host-address read failed at the start now cuts a retry's read in flight at its close and removes that read's helper container within the stop's deadline. A read whose docker client an outside signal killed removes its container too. The retry also starts when `AGENTRUN_DOCKER_HOST_ADDRESSES` is set, and there it only removes the containers the failed read left. <!-- changes/docker-host-read-cleanup.md -->
- An export of a revision applied before an apply kept its key names names none, and says so: a `remade` note of kind `secrets` that names the package it came from and asks for the keys to be saved on the target and named under `secrets`. This corrects 0.1.0-beta.55's note, which said `report.remade[].kind` no longer lists `secrets`: it lists it for such a revision. An export of a revision whose apply kept its key names names them, with no note, as in 0.1.0-beta.55. <!-- changes/export-unkept-key-names.md -->
- A fal job is priced at the rate its settings are billed at. fal bills some endpoints at a rate that depends on a setting but get_pricing states one rate, so a job at a setting that costs more, or one that leaves out a setting whose default costs more, was held, and booked, under what fal bills: an Ideogram v3 job with no `rendering_speed` renders at BALANCED and was held at half its price. Such a job is now held and booked at get_pricing's live rate times the ratio fal's model page gives its settings (read 2026-11-23), a setting it leaves out at its default, so a price change at fal moves every tier. Where the page and get_pricing disagree, the higher rate is held. A setting value the page names no rate for is refused unsent under a cap, and with no cap it runs booked as an unknown charge. <!-- changes/fal-rate-settings.md -->
  Every endpoint fal's catalog lists in these families (Ideogram v3 and character, Nano Banana Pro and Gemini 3 Pro Image Preview, Nano Banana 2 and Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Preview, Veo 3 and 3.1, Kling v3, sync-lipsync v2, Fabric 1.0) is decided: priced by its settings, or at one rate. An endpoint in one of them that is not decided, such as a variant fal adds later, is refused unsent under a cap ("fal bills <family> by its settings and <endpoint> has no rate decided here"); before, it was held at get_pricing's one rate, under what fal bills when its settings cost more. Endpoints outside these families are priced at get_pricing's one rate, as before. Ideogram v4 is such a family with no rate decided: its pages bill by `rendering_speed` and megapixels, so each of its endpoints is refused under a cap. Before, its tiling endpoints were held at get_pricing's $0.04 or $0.045 an image. Ideogram v4.5 and v4.6 (billed by quality, and v4.6 by size) and Nano Banana 2.1 (`google/nano-banana-2.1`, by resolution), each with its edit, are such families too: refused under a cap whatever unit get_pricing states them in, so a change of unit at fal can't hold them at one flat rate.
  Some of the video endpoints below have no reader for the length fal bills: Veo 3.1 `first-last-frame-to-video`, `reference-to-video` and `extend-video`; Veo 3.1 `fast/image-to-video`, `fast/first-last-frame-to-video`, `fast/reference-to-video` and `fast/extend-video`; Veo 3.1 `lite` and its `image-to-video` and `first-last-frame-to-video`; Veo 3 and its `image-to-video`; Veo 3 `fast/image-to-video`; Kling v3 `pro/text-to-video`, `standard/image-to-video`, `standard/text-to-video` and `4k/image-to-video`; Fabric `text` and `fast`. These endpoints' rates are decided, but their holds aren't yet: under a cap, a job on one is refused until its length can be read.
  `fal-ai/ideogram/v3` (and its edit, remix, reframe, replace-background and generate-transparent): TURBO ×1 (get_pricing's rate), BALANCED, the default, ×2, QUALITY ×3.
  `fal-ai/ideogram/character` (and its edit and remix): the page states $0.10 an image at TURBO, $0.15 at BALANCED (the default) and $0.20 at QUALITY; get_pricing states $0.05, which the page names for no setting. Held at the page's rates: ×2, ×3 and ×4 on $0.05. Before, a job was held at $0.05 an image, a third of the default's price.
  Veo 3.1 and its `image-to-video`, `first-last-frame-to-video` and `reference-to-video`: get_pricing's rate is 720p or 1080p with audio; audio off ×0.5, 4k with audio ×1.5, 4k without ×1. Its `extend-video` takes 720p only: audio off ×0.5. Veo 3.1 `fast` and its `image-to-video`, `first-last-frame-to-video` and `reference-to-video`: audio off ×2/3, 4k with audio ×7/3, without ×2 (the `reference-to-video` page names no 4k rate though it takes 4k, so it is held at the fast tier's). Its `fast/extend-video`, 720p only: audio off ×2/3. Veo 3.1 `lite` and its `image-to-video` and `first-last-frame-to-video`: 720p with audio ×1 ($0.05), without ×0.6, 1080p with audio ×1.6, without ×1. Veo 3 and its `image-to-video`: audio off ×0.5; Veo 3 `fast` and its `image-to-video`: audio off ×2/3; both at 720p or 1080p. Audio is on by default. A resolution an endpoint's page names no rate for (4k on Veo 3 or lite, 1080p on an extend) is refused under a cap.
  `fal-ai/kling-video/v3/pro/image-to-video` and `pro/text-to-video`: get_pricing states $0.14 a second, the page $0.112 with audio off, $0.168 with audio on, the default (×1.2), and $0.196 with voice control, an element with a `voice_id` (×1.4). Audio off is held at get_pricing's $0.14 (×1), the higher. Voice control with `"generate_audio": false` names no rate, so it is refused under a cap. `standard/image-to-video` and `standard/text-to-video`: the page states $0.084, $0.126 and $0.154, get_pricing $0.14; held at the higher: ×1, ×1, ×1.1. `4k/image-to-video`: $0.42 with audio on or off; voice control names no rate, so it is refused under a cap.
  One rate whatever their settings, as their pages state: Kling v3 `4k/text-to-video`, `turbo/pro/*`, `turbo/standard/*` and `*/motion-control`; Ideogram v3 `layerize-text`; `fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2/pro`.
  `fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2`: `lipsync-2`, the default, ×1; `lipsync-2-pro` ×5/3.
  `fal-ai/nano-banana-pro` and its `edit`, and `fal-ai/gemini-3-pro-image-preview` and its `edit` (the same model): 1K, the default, or 2K ×1; 4K ×2; `enable_web_search` adds $0.015 an image (the page doesn't say per image or per request, so the higher is held; Gemini 3 Pro's page names no charge for the web search it takes, so it is held at Nano Banana Pro's). Before, a Gemini 3 Pro job was held at $0.15 an image whatever its settings: 4 images at 4K with a web search were held at $0.60 against $1.26.
  `fal-ai/nano-banana-2` and its `edit`, and `fal-ai/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview` and its `edit` (the same model): 1K, the default, ×1 ($0.08); 0.5K ×0.75; 2K ×1.5; 4K ×2; `enable_web_search` adds $0.015 an image and `thinking_level` `"high"` $0.002 an image (Gemini 3.1 Flash's page names no charge for the high thinking it takes, so it is held at Nano Banana 2's). Before, a 4K job was held at $0.08 against $0.16.
  An image job whose `limit_generations` is anything but `true` or left out is refused under a cap: `false` lets its prompt ask for more images than `num_images`, and fal bills each one. fal's OpenAPI gives it `true` by default wherever it was read (Nano Banana Pro, 2, 2.1 and lite, the Gemini image previews, Ideogram v3 `layerize-text`). Before, `{num_images: 1, limit_generations: false}` was held at one image.
  `veed/fabric-1.0` and its `text`: 480p ×1, 720p ×1.875 ($0.15 against $0.08). `fabric-1.0/fast`: 480p ×1 ($0.10), 720p ×2. Before, a 720p Fabric job was refused under a cap; on `fabric-1.0` it is now held at its voice's length, and `text` and `fast` have no length reader yet (above). A job with no `resolution` is still refused: their resolution has no default.
  ElevenLabs Music and dubbing are held, and booked, at their length rounded up to a whole minute, as fal bills them ("rounded up to the closest minute"): a 30 s track or a 4 s clip is a whole minute. Before, a 30 s track was held at half what fal bills.
- A run with a spend cap can send fal's talking heads, `veed/fabric-1.0` at `"resolution": "480p"` or `"720p"` and `fal-ai/bytedance/omnihuman/v1.5`: each job is held at its voice's length, read before the call from the audio at its `audio_url` alone (on fal's own media, `fal.media` or a subdomain: a voice fal made, or one uploaded to fal; the URL written exactly as it parses, so `V3.fal.media`, a space, a `..` segment or `:443` is not priced), in whole seconds as fal bills them, at get_pricing's rate. The length is what the voice plays: every audio frame of an MP3 (a first frame holding a Xing, Info or VBRI header is skipped, as a decoder skips it), or a PCM WAV's samples at its sample rate, every byte after its data header counted. It is never read from the job's image, from a length its input states, or from a length the file's own header states (an MP3's Xing, Info or VBRI frame count, a WAV's byte rate or data size), which whoever made the file could write short. Only a voice on fal's own media is priced because fal fetches the `audio_url` again after this read, and another host could serve fal a longer voice than the one measured. The voice is read https only and following no redirect (fal.media serves its files directly), so a fal.media URL can't send the read to another host, through the same public-host guard as web_fetch and web_save, and at most 32 MiB. A job is still refused unsent under a cap, as before, when its voice can't be read (an `audio_url` that is not https or not on `fal.media`, a private host, over 32 MiB, a timeout, a WAV that is not integer PCM or float with one format chunk whose fields agree, an MP3 with bytes that are not frames, or any other format: an mp4 or m4a voice states its length only in its header), and for Fabric with no `resolution`: its resolution has no default, so send `"480p"` or `"720p"` (720p is held at $0.15 a second against 480p's $0.08, as fal bills it; see the fal setting tiers note). With no cap such a job runs, booked as an unknown charge, never $0. Fabric's reply states no length, so it is booked at its hold: the ledger books the voice's length, read before the call, not a length fal reports. OmniHuman settles at the length its reply states, in whole seconds. LatentSync, infinitalk and `ffmpeg-api/merge-audio-video` stay unpriceable under a cap. <!-- changes/fal-talking-head-price.md -->
  `publicFetch` and `publicDownload` take `httpsOnly`, which refuses http on the first hop and at every redirect, and `maxRedirects` (a whole number from 0 to 5, default 5; with 0 any redirect is refused before its target is dialled; any other value is a `RangeError` before a lookup).
  A job billed by length is priced from a length its input names only on the endpoints whose input sets the length fal bills, and only from that field: `duration` on Kling v2.5 turbo pro (text and image to video), Kling v3 pro image to video, Hailuo-02 standard text to video, Veo 3 fast, Veo 3.1 (fast, image to video) and ACE-Step; `seconds_total` on Stable Audio 2.5; `music_length_ms` or `composition_plan` on ElevenLabs Music. Before, any per-second or per-minute endpoint trusted a named `duration`, `duration_seconds`, `seconds_total` or `music_length_ms`, so a capped run could send `fal-ai/sync-lipsync/v2` with a 10 minute video and `duration: 0.001` and be held at about $0. Now dubbing, voice isolation, speech-to-text and sync-lipsync v2 are always priced from the media they are given, and any other endpoint billed by length (LatentSync, infinitalk, a merge, Fabric fast, OmniHuman v1, an endpoint this server doesn't know) is refused unsent under a cap, whatever length its input names. A listed endpoint that names no length, or another of the length fields, is refused unsent too.
  An ElevenLabs Music job with a `composition_plan` is priced from its sections' `duration_ms`, never from a `music_length_ms` beside it: before, `music_length_ms` was read first, so a job naming 10 s beside a 10 minute plan was held at 10 s and billed for 10 minutes. A job naming both is refused unsent under a cap (send one: a plan sets the length, and `music_length_ms` goes only with a prompt), and so is a plan with `respect_sections_durations` other than `true` or left out (its default), since the model may then change the sections' lengths.
- fal jobs: three fixes to how a run sends and books them. <!-- changes/fal-tidy.md -->
  - A `submission_key` longer than 111 characters is refused before anything is sent, in words that give its length and the limit. fal takes keys up to 128 characters, and the run adds 17 to keep its keys its own. Such a key used to be shortened with a hash. After a resume, replies gave the agent that shortened form, not its own key, so a later lookup or retry with it missed the job fal already held. Send a shorter key.
  - A job whose reply is lost after it left (a dropped connection, a timeout) is now booked at the hold it was sent at, as a job still running is. It used to be booked as an unknown charge. A job that had no price is still booked as unknown, never as $0.
  - An approval card for a fal job now reads "priced by usage", as a monid endpoint's does. It used to show no price.
- A replay or audit run in a process of its own now grades on the saved key of its grader's provider. Its grader runs on the fast tier (the revision's `modelTiers.fast`, else `AGENT_MODEL_FAST`), which can be another provider's model than the agent's, with that provider's key saved in Settings → Model keys alone. The run's process asks its runner for saved keys, and the runner answered only a subagent's, a learning run's or an SDK run's ask, so a replay of an Anthropic agent whose fast tier is OpenAI's found no OpenAI key, logged "learning: no grader route (No OpenAI key here …)", and compared the answers whole. The runner now answers a replay's and an audit's ask with that one provider's saved keys and no other (through a model gateway, the gateway's key alone), filtered on the runner, since the agent's tools run in the run's process tree. A replay or audit of a revision with no fast tier, or one that names `agree_on`, gets none (a revision that grants the subagent tool keeps the subagent path's keys, unchanged), and a run whose launch brings its own model key still gets none of the server's keys. <!-- changes/grader-key-replay.md -->
- A run created with `hold: true` whose model can't run here now takes no end-of-run learning step either, on pi and on the CLI harnesses: its claim builds none, even when its agent learns, and a runner that starts each run in a process of its own refuses one if that process asks. No saved key is read, no draft is compiled and no audit starts for a run whose model runs nowhere. <!-- changes/held-run-end-of-run.md -->
- A run created with `hold: true` is no longer refused at its create when only its model blocks it: no key here for the model, its harness refusing it (a CLI harness such as codex, claude-agent or opencode that runs here but for want of a model key among them), or no price for it under a `max_cost_usd` cap. The run opens and holds its computer, so a benchmark that only sets a task up, calls the computer and releases it works on a server with no model key. The model check now runs at the start instead: `POST /runs/{run_id}/start`, and any message to the run, answer `409 agent_not_runnable` with the same message, fields and details the create would have given, and the computer still takes calls until it is released or its hold lapses. On pi and on the CLI harnesses, the run's model route chooses no model and reads no key: any model request that reached the run's model proxy would be refused in those words and never sent. Its claim lays only the keys any claim of the run lays (its tools' keys, a key handed with the run), and a runner that starts each run in a process of its own hands that process no model key and no saved gateway key; the claim routes no subagent tier and runs no learning step. A key saved after the create does not unblock that run; start a new one. Any other blocker (a tool's missing key, the computer, the box) still refuses a held create as before, and a server whose model gateway holds no key still answers it `422 model_key_required`. <!-- changes/held-run-model-key.md -->
- The money rule's by-hand cost no longer counts a compile turn as the agent's. An agent run whose end compiled a workflow was read on the by-hand side at its job plus that compile turn, so one compile could raise the agent's by-hand mean far above what its runs cost, and a workflow that cost more a run than the agent kept serving. The rule now reads each run off the served paths the way `GET /runs/{id}` reads it: its compile turns are charged to the revision they drafted, and its other learning (a follow-up's rounds, its audit shadow) stays on the run. The served side is unchanged. `GET /agents/{id}/learning/cost` `workflows[].by_hand` and the decision a run's launch reads both change. <!-- changes/money-rule-by-hand-no-compile.md -->
- Saving or removing a key no longer waits on a stuck Ollama. Once the kept Ollama listing was more than 30 s old, each save asked Ollama about every model it lists, one at a time, up to 10 s each, before it answered. The offers and the model check a save makes again now read each Ollama model from the kept listing, and ask Ollama nothing. A run still asks Ollama about its own model once the listing is 30 s old. <!-- changes/ollama-key-save-hung.md -->
  - `agentrun service install` now takes `--env OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=<tokens>`, so a service can run on a context lower than 65,536. `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=` with nothing after it removes it.
- A hidden file or folder is no part of a package anywhere in it, and nothing reads or keeps one. <!-- changes/package-hidden-paths.md -->
  - A package whose `output.schema` names a hidden file (`.answer.json`, `evals/.cache/answer.json`) is refused, and the error names it. `agentrun template validate`, an import and an apply refuse it alike. Before, the reader took it, and `agentrun deploy` sent it as the answer's schema.
  - An upload (`POST /v2/templates/import`) leaves out every hidden path before it is stored: a `.env` at the top or in a skill folder is neither kept nor read back. The upload's `sha` is the package's, its files without the hidden ones. Before, a hidden file at the top of an upload was stored with it.
  - `agentrun deploy DIR` names each hidden path it leaves out before it sends anything (`Left out, hidden: .env, skills/check/.DS_Store`), a hidden folder once, never what it holds. Its own `.agentrun/` is not named.
- A ChatGPT sign-in that OpenAI never sends back now says why, long before its 10 minutes run out. When a workspace's admin has turned off open-source apps, OpenAI shows its refusal on its own page and never returns to the server. The server can't tell that from a tab left open, so the sign-in sat on waiting for 10 minutes, then said only that it timed out. <!-- changes/plan-signin-wait-hint.md -->
  - From its first minute on, while no code has come back, GET /settings/chatgpt's pending view carries a new `hint` field. The `@parcha/agentrun-client` types have it too. The hint names the likely cause first: the workspace admin's setting (External access → OSS → Use ChatGPT plan). The console's waiting page shows it under the paste step.
  - The timeout's words name the same cause first, then say to start the sign-in again.
  - Once a code is in (the browser's return or a paste), no hint shows while OpenAI answers it. If the 10 minutes cut that exchange off, the words say so, with no guess about the admin setting.
- The API playground's Agent picker shows an agent's name whole. The field was 14rem wide whatever the names, so a longer name was cut with an ellipsis beside an empty row. The field is now as wide as its longest agent's name needs on one line, and keeps that width whichever agent is picked (the console's `Picker`, `steady`, as the operation picker above it). On a phone it is held to 60% of the window's width and cuts a longer name with an ellipsis. A real-browser flow (`playground-agent-width` in `npm run test:e2e`) measures it at 1280 and 390 px. <!-- changes/playground-agent-picker-width.md -->
- A harness recipe's install is checked by one rule, its tree, in harness-check, harness sign-in, a server's harness entry and each start. The tree digest covers every file, the binary among them, so an install no longer writes a separate first-seen binary record: it records its first tree alone, and a recipe's own binarySha256 is still checked at install. An install with no tree record is refused with the line that installs it again, and an install folder holding any link that leads out of it, as the filesystem resolves it (a chain of links included), or that leads to nothing (the tree digest holds a link by its target's name, not the bytes behind it: the executable behind a linked folder, or code beside it) is refused at the install, before anything is put in place, and at every check; an old install that holds one is not taken as already installed, so installing it again says why. The check note keeps the recipe, the tree and the platform. A recipe's keyMethod is checked by the ACP package's AUTH_METHOD, the adapter's own definition. <!-- changes/recipe-install-tree.md -->
- The redactor now finds a held value written with JSON's `\uXXXX` escapes, every character or some, and withholds the text, as it does a value split by whitespace or percent encoded. Where a call's result is read only to a point, the read past that point counts an escape as the character it decodes to, so escaped whitespace there never hides the rest of a value split at it. <!-- changes/redact-escaped-web-split.md -->

  A web_search or web_fetch result has each string of its JSON redacted on its own, its property names now among them. A held value split across two of its strings (a name and its value included), or across its JSON and the lines after it, used to show both halves. It now withholds the result everywhere it is read: the answer the runner stores and hands the agent, a timeline row's preview and summary in the run's view and its timeline, and a read with `calls` (a template eval's grader, `calls=whole`). Each reads `[redacted]`. A held value whole in one string is still cut in place, and the result stays its JSON.
- The redactor now finds more of a held value that a text shows only in part or written another way, and more of a private key: <!-- changes/redact-held-value-parts.md -->
  - A held value of many lines, such as a private key, is found by its lines too: a text that prints its first lines (`head -n 11 key.pem`) or its body with the armor stripped shows `[redacted]` in place of each line. A key's last body line, mostly shorter than the others, is held with its END line, so its last two lines (`tail -n 2 key.pem`) are cut too.
  - A string of a held JSON value, at any depth, is held as a value of its own when it has a line break (a service account's `private_key`) or its key names a secret: with its separators dropped and lowered, the key holds `secret`, `password`, `passwd`, `token`, `private`, `credential` or `apikey`, or ends in `key` (`client_secret`, `aws_secret_access_key`, `SessionToken`, `signing_secret`, a one-line `private_key`), or is a name a URL's credential parameter goes by. A key that ends in `uri`, `url`, `id`, `type`, `email`, `endpoint`, `expiry` or `expires`, a public key, `page_token` and `next_token` name none. A JWK's private members (`d`, `p`, `q`, `dp`, `dq`, `qi`, `k`) are held beside its `kty`. Printed alone, it is cut. An array's items have no key, so only the line-break rule holds them. The value's other strings (an id, a project, its URLs) are not, and its own lines are no parts of it, so a pretty-printed service account's public lines (`"token_uri": "https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token",`) show.
  - The view that reads JSON's escapes now reads all of them (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\"`, `\\`, `\/`, `\b`, `\f` and `\uXXXX`, not only `\uXXXX`), and reads them twice, for JSON inside JSON. A held value of many lines escaped twice, or with its line breaks written as `\r\n`, withholds the text. Escaped once, it is still cut in place. A text with an escaped backslash is read one level deep too, so a held value that holds a backslash before `n` or `u` (the characters `\n` as written), with its backslash escaped as `\\` or `\`, is still found.
  - A held value with a zero-width space, a soft hyphen or another character that renders as nothing between its characters withholds the text, as a value split by whitespace does. A held value that itself holds one is found without it too.
  - A held value glued to the end of a run of text too long to read is found, and the answer reads `[redacted]`. Padding the matcher reads as nothing between the value and the run's end (zero-width spaces, soft hyphens, `\n` escapes, `%E2%80%8B`) does not hide it: the run's end is read by the characters the matcher sees, and padding longer than a piece withholds the answer.
  - Where a call's result is cut at its read stop, the read past the stop counts JSON's escapes, percent-encoded bytes and characters that render as nothing as the views read them (a zero-width space written as `%E2%80%8B` counts as nothing), so padding of them never hides the rest of a value the stop split.
  - A private key block is cut whole, from its BEGIN line through its body to its END line, not its BEGIN line alone, with no held value to cut it by. With its END line within 16 KiB, all between is cut, whatever wraps the body's lines (a code string literal on each, a `#` or `>` before each, an XML or HTML line break, an escape, an armored key's headers). With no END line in reach (a key cut short), it is cut through its body's lines: LF, CRLF or CR line ends, maybe escaped in a quoted string up to four strings deep, blanks and escaped tabs around each line, blank lines, Proc-Type, DEK-Info, Version and Comment headers, at most 1,024 lines of at most 16,384 characters. Text after the body that is no such line stays. A header with no body line after it is cut alone, as before. An answer or a call's result is read in pieces of about 8 KiB, and a piece never ends inside a block whose END line is in reach: it ends before the block's BEGIN line, so the next piece cuts the block whole, and a block longer than a piece is read as one run and shows as `[redacted]`.

  An id or hash holding "aba" and nine digits (a run id's last group, a short sha) is no longer cut as a routing number in what learning serves: the routing word must stand alone, as in `ABA 123456789`, `ABA: 123456789`, `ABA#123456789` or `routing number 123456789`, which are still cut.
- Two more web_search and web_fetch answers with a held value split across two of their strings are now withheld. The runner stored one as it came when its redactor did not list the values it holds and the answer's strings ran past 8,192 characters; it now stores `[redacted]`. A timeline row's preview, a read with `calls` and the stored answer showed one whose halves sit side by side only in the order the answer was written (a property name of digits alone, which a JSON object reads first, or a name written twice, whose first value only the text keeps); each now reads `[redacted]`. <!-- changes/redact-web-split-reads.md -->
- A cut read of a run's file (`GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/files/{path}?cut=run`, which a template eval's grader reads) now cuts what the run's caller handed it: its own model key (`model_key`), its tool keys and its MCP servers' credentials. Before, the cut held only this server's values and the run's sign-in refs, so a file that held the run's own key read with the key in it. While the run holds them, the read cuts them by value. The run's end erases them, as before, and now first counts where they sit in each of the run's text files: each file's MAC (HMAC-SHA256 under a key derived from the seal key) and the byte ranges to cut, never the values or a hash of one. Each file is named by a MAC of its path too, never the path, so a file the run named by a key (`cache/<key>.json`) leaves the key nowhere in the stored count. After the end, a file still byte for byte as counted is cut at those ranges.
