A caller that pushed a folder into a synced computer and stamped each file with `PUSHED_MTIME` itself now calls the new `FolderSync.push(entries, options)`: it gives each file the pushed mtime, pushes the tar, and takes the baseline, and its failure says which of the two steps failed. `baseline()` stays for a folder pushed some other way. <!-- changes/b26-sync-record-cleanup.md -->
  - `GET /v2/computers`: a kind's `record` is now one of `{ available: true }` and `{ available: false, why }`, `why` always present when `available` is false (it was optional). A client that read `record.why` as possibly absent can drop its fallback, and the generated TypeScript and Python types narrow on `available`.
  - The `path` option of `createComputerRoutes` is gone: a kind's `record` looks for ffmpeg on the PATH of the `env` option, the server's own when it has none.
  - The synced folder's serve test no longer waits a real second to prove a pushed file is not racy; it reads the pushed mtime from the computer.

**Changes:**

- A Groundbox provider: `providerFor("groundbox", { apiKey })` makes each computer a Groundbox sandbox, a Firecracker microVM started from the box image (the public tag its `prepareImage()` answers, which Groundbox turns into a disk at the first create), or from a spec's own image: `"default"` (the team's default template, else Groundbox's own Ubuntu image), a template of the key's team, or any other public image. It is a `MachineHost` on the shared adapter: `src/groundbox.ts` calls Groundbox's REST API with `fetch`, and the daemon runs as a child of one resumable command of the WebSocket command stream, handed to `framedExec`: when a socket closes, as every one does within the hour, a new one attaches from the last output position read, so no output is lost or read twice, and each stdin write is one answered call that writes the command's fifo. The daemon is uploaded through the files API. Network none, open and a list are init's, and the run's folder is a synced folder. Its lifetime is the janitor's, by the deadline label, and Groundbox's own timer ends every sandbox at the adapter's backstop; a computer may live up to 30 days less 6 minutes, a day by default. `list` is one call, filtered by `live=true` and the labels as metadata. A spec's `cpus` (whole, 1 to 16) and `memoryMb` (whole GiB, at most 4 a CPU) are the sandbox's size. With `kind: "desktop"` a computer is a desktop: the box image's Xvfb and xfwm4, started through the daemon as on E2B and boxd (Groundbox's own image, which lacks xfwm4, is refused for it). No Archil mount yet. Groundbox's own image keeps toolchains under `/opt` deeper than the isolation probe searches, so `isolation.vendor-agent` can't pass on it; on the box image it does. Settings takes `GROUNDBOX_API_KEY`. `AGENTRUN_COMPUTER_LIVE_GROUNDBOX=1 COMPUTER_GROUNDBOX_API_KEY=... npm run conformance -w @parcha/agentrun-computer -- --provider groundbox` runs the conformance kit on real Groundbox, and `sweep.js --provider groundbox` checks it left nothing behind. <!-- changes/computer-groundbox-provider.md -->

  The provider's `apiUrl` must be https; http is taken only to a loopback host (127.0.0.0/8, `::1` or `localhost`), so the key never crosses a network in cleartext.
- Console: a run's live screen on the Screen tab has the run's steps so far beside it, in the Timeline tab's words, so what the agent is doing is read next to where it does it. The list stays at its newest step as steps come, until you scroll up to read an earlier one; under it a line says the run is working. With its steps beside it the Screen tab's panel is wider than the reading column, so the live view (and a finished run's recording) keeps the size it had alone; on a narrow window the steps sit under the screen. <!-- changes/console-live-screen-steps.md -->
- Runners that are replicas of one deployment (Kubernetes pods, a platform service's instances) now relay dial computers and serve live views across hosts: `AGENTRUN_RUNNER_LIVE_HOST` and the server's `AGENTRUN_RUNNER_HOSTS` take an IPv4 block, such as a private pod network's. A runner given a block answers at its own one address in it, and the server dials any IPv4 address in a block it lists, never one outside. Such runners had no host name the server resolves, so their relay stayed on loopback and a dial computer they made could not attach. A block names its network address and a prefix from /8 to /32. <!-- changes/runner-hosts-ipv4-block.md -->
  - A runner whose block holds none, or several, of its machine's addresses is refused at its start in words, and `runner --check` fails `AGENTRUN_RUNNER_LIVE_HOST` the same way; where the setting names a host, the check now says where the server reaches the runner.
- The console's "set up with a coding agent" prompt for a template tells the coding agent that the package's instructions and skill files are what the new agent will be told, not instructions to it. An imported package's text is a third party's. <!-- changes/template-prompt-package-is-data.md -->
- The README's MCP section says a loopback URL, `http` or `https`, is taken only by a server started with `AGENTRUN_MCP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK=1`, as the refusal already said. <!-- changes/readme-mcp-loopback-switch.md -->
- Suggested agents: connect a GitHub repository, and AgentRun finds where its app needs an AI agent. The console's new Suggested agents page (Agents → Suggested) scans a repository with the bundled `agent-scout` template, on a read-only checkout, and shows each suggestion with the lines of code behind it, the typed input and answer, and where the app would call it. Discard hides a suggestion for good (with an undo). Create pushes the agent's template package and a dependency-free client to a new branch `agentrun/<key>`, makes the agent on this server from those same files, and opens a pull request that only adds files. New routes: `GET /v2/suggestions`, `POST /v2/suggestions/scans`, `GET /v2/suggestions/{id}`, `POST /v2/suggestions/{id}/discard`, `.../restore` and `.../create`, and `GET /v2/integrations/github/repositories`. <!-- changes/suggested-agents.md -->

  - GitHub permissions: a scan needs only what every App holds (metadata and contents read, a token for that one repository, revoked after). Opening a pull request needs Contents write, which Connect GitHub now asks for only when the owner ticks it (`POST /v2/integrations/github/connect` takes `contents: "write"`); an App made before is not widened, and Create says what is missing and links the App's permissions page and the installation's. Each create mints one token for the one repository with contents and pull requests write, and revokes it.
  - An agent definition, and a template's manifest, take `checkout: repository`: the server checks out the head of the default branch of the repository the run names, one commit deep, in `repo/`, and lists its files in `repo/.git/agentrun-files`.
  - New error codes, all 409: `github_not_installed`, `github_permission_missing`, `github_file_exists`, `suggestion_decided`.
- The anonymous usage counts (`docs/telemetry.md`) say how suggested agents are used, with three new events: `suggestions_scanned` (a scan of a repository starts), `suggestion_discarded` (a suggestion is discarded) and `suggested_agent_created` (a suggested agent's pull request opens, once per suggestion). Each is its name alone, with the fields every event already holds; it never says the repository, the suggestion, its agent or its pull request. The same settings turn them off (`AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY=0`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, CI, a test runner, `--faux`), and the start that prints the notice sends none of them: a use that day is not counted. `startServe` takes `onUsage`, which hears each event's name. <!-- changes/suggestion-usage-counts.md -->
- A live run on your Claude plan (or a ChatGPT plan) no longer reads "not priced" while a request is in flight: the run's cost counts that request at $0 on the plan, as the ended run does, so the header reads its tokens and "On your Claude plan" and the timeline's "Cost so far" counts no plan request as not priced. <!-- changes/plan-cost-live.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.53 (2026-11-22)

- An agent can be exported as a template package: `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/package` answers its current revision as the files of a package (`agent.md` with the instructions as its body, `skills/`, `rules/`, an output schema) and their sha256, and `agentrun export AGENT --out DIR` writes them as a folder that `agentrun template validate` reads and any AgentRun applies. `agent.md` always names the model and approvals. MCP tools become needs by their saved server's source and toolkit, and triggers carry no agent and no secret. What names this host (its box, its computer's provider, its pins of this server's tool listings, its place) is left out. The answer's `report` names what can't travel as it is: `blocked` (an MCP server saved nowhere here, on this machine's loopback, or sending its own auth header) and `remade` (webhook, GitHub, Composio and email triggers, browser sign-ins, a paired computer, what the agent learned). `agentrun export` prints both, and with anything blocked it writes nothing and exits 2. A native, CLI learning, SDK or another system's agent, or a workflow, answers `409 not_exportable`. <!-- changes/agent-export.md -->
- `agentrun deploy DIR --to URL` deploys an agent package folder to another AgentRun (`--to cloud` is the hosted one; `AGENTRUN_CLOUD_URL` overrides its address). It uploads the package, prints the apply's plan (create or revise, the keys and MCP servers the target lacks, each trigger made, kept or removed, the computer), asks before it applies (`--yes` off a terminal), and writes a lock to `DIR/.agentrun/deploy.json`. A second deploy of the same files says it is up to date and sends nothing that writes; changed files make the agent's next revision. A target the package needs keys or connections on exits 3 with nothing made, and an agent edited on the target since the last deploy exits 2 unless `--force`. `agentrun deploy rollback` makes the previous revision current, and `agentrun deploy delete` deletes the agent and the lock. `agentrun deploy AGENT_ID` deploys an agent from this install by its package; `--pause-source` turns its schedules off here once it is deployed. <!-- changes/agentrun-deploy.md -->
  - `POST /v2/templates/import` takes `{files}`, a package uploaded whole, checked under the GitHub import's limits and in its words, stored as `upload:<name>` with the package's sha256, and replaced by the next upload of that name. An upload asks no publisher trust. A server that serves the API alone takes an upload and refuses a GitHub `source`.
  - `POST /v2/templates/{id}/apply` takes `dry_run: true`: it answers `{plan}` from the apply's own reads and checks and writes nothing.
  - `POST /v2/templates/{id}/apply` takes `revision` (with `agent_id`) and `sha`, what the caller read: the apply, or its plan, is 412 when the agent's current revision or the package stored under that id is another, with nothing changed. Its answer names the revision it wrote, or kept, as `revision_id`. A plan whose keys are missing lists them even where the model needs one of them, and a plan on a server with no public URL says a Composio trigger is skipped, as the apply does.
  - `agentrun deploy delete` removes the lock only when the agent is gone from the target: a 404 to the archive or the delete is followed by a read of the agent, and one still there exits 2 with nothing deleted and the lock kept. `agentrun deploy AGENT_ID` exits 2 for an agent this install does not have or does not export. `--to` takes an address whose path lacks `/v2` (`https://host/api` is `https://host/api/v2`).
  - A folder's lock comes with the folder, so its target gets the API key only where this CLI has deployed before, or when it is AgentRun cloud: any other address needs `--to`, and nothing is sent until then.
  - A plan lists `MONID_API_KEY` as missing where the package grants a monid tool and the server has no monid key, as the apply refuses it.
  - A deploy whose apply skipped a trigger (a connection or a feed the target lacks) leaves a lock that names no package, so the next deploy of the same files applies again and makes the trigger once it can.
  - One deploy, rollback or delete at a time per source: another one of the same folder or install agent exits 2 with nothing sent, and a hold left by a process of this machine that has ended is taken. The CLI's own deploy record is changed under a lock. A folder whose `.agentrun`, or its `deploy.json`, is a symbolic link is refused with nothing sent.
- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) takes a deploy from the backend in front of it, with the server's token: a template's apply (a redeploy with `agent_id`), the agent's read, its revisions, a rollback (`POST /agents/{id}/current`), and its archive (which its delete needs first) and unarchive. Every run there starts through the backend, on its keys and budget: with the launch hook set, the apply makes the package's schedule and feed triggers and each firing goes to the backend, which starts the run through the API (the unarchive turns them on again); without the hook it makes neither (`not_set_up_here`). A webhook, GitHub, Composio or email trigger is never made there (`not_an_option`). Each skipped trigger is a warning under `warnings` (`triggers.<i>`), and the dry run plans it as `skip` in the same words. Every other agent, template, trigger, hook and settings route stays refused. <!-- changes/api-only-deploy-routes.md -->
- The computer package ships a documents image (`packages/computer/documents`): the default image plus python-pptx, python-docx and openpyxl for `python3` and pptxgenjs, docx and exceljs for `node`, built as the serve README's "The box's image" says and named in `AGENTRUN_DOCKER_IMAGE`. `computer.needs` may now name a Python or Node library by its pip or npm name, and a box that lacks one fails its run in words naming this image's build. <!-- changes/documents-image.md -->
- The console's Learning tab opens on what learning did, once a learned workflow has taken a run over: one sentence, then four figures, each with the count it stands on. The cost ratio is the server's own; how often the serving revision's answer was the agent's on its promotion check, and how many of the runs it ran first it finished alone, are shares with their 95% interval; the last is the bill's break-even run. <!-- changes/learning-tab-glance.md -->
  - A new chart, cost against agreement, draws each promoted revision as one point: what a run it served cost, all in, against how often its answer was the agent's on its check's inputs, with that share's 95% interval, the bar it had to clear to serve, and the agent as the reference at what a run cost it before takeover. A hollow mark beside each point is the same revision's audits since. It sits beside the bill on a wide page.
  - The learned workflow, with its revisions to step through, stands beside the cost of a run where the tab has room for both, and under it otherwise: the steps that take a run over are next to the line that falls when they do.
  - Who finished each run is drawn a run a column wherever the chart is wide enough to give each run one, so a hand-back shows on its own run; a narrower chart keeps blocks of runs.
  - Every figure is one count the API already gives: a check's `agreed` of its `alone`, the audit ledger's rows, the cost summary and the bill. A check's count and an audit's are never added together, and agreement is never called accuracy: the agent's answer is the reference, not the truth. The tab reads the audit ledger once for the figures, the chart and the audit line. No API changes.
- A harness recipe now covers an outside agent's release as its vendor ships it (Google's agy CLI among them), and the owner's own sign-in, made by the agent itself: <!-- changes/recipes-outside-harness.md -->
  - `.zip` releases install, unpacked in Node with no `unzip` on the host. An entry that leaves the folder (`..`, an absolute path, a backslash), a symbolic link, a device, an encrypted entry or a duplicate refuses the whole archive before anything lands.
  - An archive is pinned by one digest, its `sha256` or, where the vendor's manifest lists that, its `sha512` (Google's agy CLI manifests). `release.registry` is optional, for a release that is the vendor's own rather than the ACP registry's.
  - Every file the archive unpacks to is pinned, not the binary alone: the tree's sha256 is recorded at the first install (or given as the release's `treeSha256`), and a check or a sign-in refuses a sidecar that changed since.
  - A release may give its own `args` per platform, over the recipe's.
  - `model.id` picks a plan-billed agent's model among those its `session/new` lists (`session/set_model`); one it does not list is refused before a prompt.
  - A key may be handed under the name the agent reads: `keys: [{ "name": "ANTIGRAVITY_GEMINI_API_KEY", "env": "GEMINI_API_KEY" }]`. It is read by its saved name, so the server's own `GEMINI_API_KEY` never reaches the agent. `keyMethod` is the method the agent's ACP `authenticate` signs in with on it (`gemini-api-key`).
  - One list in the kernel, `launchEnv` (`LAUNCH_ENV`, `LAUNCH_ENV_PREFIXES`), names the variables that change what a process loads or runs before its own code: `PATH`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `NODE_PATH`, `PYTHON*`, `BASH_*`, `ENV`, `GIT_*` and a few shells' and interpreters' start-up variables. A key is never handed under one of them, nor a recipe's `env` or `model.env` named one. The recipe loader and the ACP adapter both refuse them.
  - A key's saved and handed names follow the kernel's `KEY_NAME` (capitals, digits and `_`, at most 64) in the recipe loader as in the ACP adapter, so `harness-check` no longer refuses a lowercase key name the loader took. Other variable names keep `ENV_NAME`.
  - `signIn: { "args": [...], "homeArg": FLAG }` names the agent's own sign-in, as T3 Code runs agy: `agentrun harness sign-in --recipe FILE` starts the installed, unmodified agent on your terminal with its arguments, `args` (`--login`) and `homeArg` naming its own folder (`--gemini-dir DIR`). The agent prints the address, reads the code you paste and keeps its sign-in in that folder; exit 0 is signed in (`HARNESS_SIGN_IN_FAILED` otherwise).
  - harness-check runs on the recipe's keys alone, never the sign-in, so a plan-billed recipe names a key beside any `signIn`. A run on the sign-in hands the agent `homeArg` and its folder, no key, nothing it prints kept.
  - AgentRun never reads, refreshes or sends the sign-in's token, and has no usage reader: it never opens the folder, and a test keeps every credential file and Google account or quota endpoint out of the harness sources.
  - The ACP adapter's `stderr: "none"` (`AcpRecipe`) keeps nothing an agent prints, for a run on a sign-in: a failure says its exit status and AgentRun's own code, and an error the agent answers says its JSON-RPC code alone.
- A template's apply keeps the names of the keys the package declared (its `secrets`, and those of the model choice it took) on the revision it writes, never their values, so `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/package` names them after the server's copy of the template changes, as a bundled template does on every upgrade. Applying the same package again still writes no revision. Only an agent applied before this keeps its `report.remade` entry for keys that can't be recovered. <!-- changes/revision-secrets.md -->
- A run says when it stopped short for its spend cap. Every run read and list item carries `stopped_for` and `budget_refused_calls`. `stopped_for` is `"budget"` on a `completed` run that wound down to stay under its `max_cost_usd`: its model was told to wrap up near the cap, or its tool calls were refused there. It is null on every other run. `budget_refused_calls` counts the tool calls the cap's wrap-up refused, each call once, and is 0 when none were. Before, such a run read `completed` like any other, and nothing on it said the cap had cut it short. The status stays `completed`, so a reader that sets "budget exhausted" reads `stopped_for`. A run paused at its cap (`pending.kind` `budget`) and one its cap ended (`failed`, `spend_cap_reached`) read as before. The server keeps each refusal on the run's journal as it happens; a run that ended before this server reads `stopped_for: "budget"` when its model was told to wrap up, and 0 refused calls. <!-- changes/run-stopped-for-budget.md -->
- A sandbox can list the programs its agent needs on the box's PATH, `computer.needs` (such as `["chrome", "ffmpeg", "ffprobe", "hyperframes"]`), and the computer package ships a media image that has them. Each run's claim asks the box it started before the run's first model request, searching the folders the agent's shell searches, not a PATH the image sets; a box that lacks one, or that cannot be asked, is let go and the run ends `failed` (`run_failed`) in words naming what is missing and how to give the box an image that has it. The field never picks an image: a Docker box's image is still `AGENTRUN_DOCKER_IMAGE`'s. A setting that has `needs` but is no sandbox (a stored body or a launch's computer the validator never saw) fails the run at claim the same way, before anything is started. An agent without `needs` is checked for nothing. A template states them as `needs` in its agent.md, read only beside `computer: [shell]`: apply writes them onto the sandbox it picks as the agent's `computer.needs`, and where the shell here is no sandbox (Archil's serverless exec, or none) it refuses (`409`) in words naming them and `AGENTRUN_DOCKER_IMAGE`, making nothing. `GET /v2/templates` shows them as `needs`. A server before this release refuses a template that names `needs` as an unknown field. <!-- changes/sandbox-needs-media-image.md -->
  The media image's recipe is `packages/computer/media/Dockerfile`: the default image's base and programs, plus Node 24, Chromium as `chrome`, FFmpeg and FFprobe, Noto (CJK, colour emoji) and Liberation fonts, and the HyperFrames CLI at an exact version, with its usage reports off and the image's fonts compressed for it at build, so a render with no network doesn't spend a minute of its compile compressing Noto Color Emoji. Build it and name its tag in `AGENTRUN_DOCKER_IMAGE`; the serve README's "The box's image" has the commands. It is not published.
- Keep newly connected Codex and Claude Code setups in sync by default, and move a supported complete setup to AgentRun from the existing agent page. Move preserves the agent's identity, history, source capture and unified usage, and checks destination tools, accounts, model, policy and project restoration before switching execution. <!-- changes/source-sync-move.md -->

  Managed runs retain project checkpoints for later runs. Source and managed changes produce reviewable conflicts;
  uncertain saves require review before another run. Existing connections require an explicit export grant, native
  credentials stay at the source, and unsupported capabilities remain named prerequisites. See
  [source sync](../../docs/source-sync.md) for compatibility and recovery behavior. Automatic notes and learned skills
  remain retired; authored source skills retain their files and modes.
  Owner skill edits after Move produce a new immutable project for future runs while preserving existing runs and
  unchanged companion assets. Git checkpoints exclude ignored dependency trees before applying project limits and
  file checks. An upload refused before project seeding releases its write receipt only after destination and upload
  cleanup have both settled; unknown or dispatched writes continue to block deletion.
  Completed checkpoint reads that refuse staged Git changes, secrets or unsupported files release their write receipt
  only after scratch, cache, tools and provider cleanup settle under the original claim. The rejected save remains
  visible and unpublished. Failed commands, changed files, lost write acknowledgments and uncertain cleanup retain
  their receipts and continue to block deletion.
  Terminal moved runs whose child crashed before checkpointing now require project review instead of silently starting
  from an older saved project. Recovery reads the committed end, or the exact terminal claim when no end could be
  written; it never invents a checkpoint or publishes orphan files. Missing-end reviews use `entry_id: null` and the
  required `attempt_epoch`, so reviewing an earlier failure cannot acknowledge a later one. Active and queued runs
  are not classified as failed merely because their checkpoint is still pending.
  Moved projects on local storage now place attachments before restoring project files, pin their exact input paths,
  and refuse collisions before admission. Claims and follow-ups reuse the placed files; checkpoints exclude those
  attachments while retaining authored files in the same inputs directory.

  Moved agents can learn checked workflows on the server using their existing learning settings. Replay and eligible
  shadow-audit runs receive isolated copies of the reserved project; their results remain learning evidence, while
  their settled file changes are explicitly discarded rather than published to the saved project. Uncertain writes
  retain recovery receipts, and the existing restrictions on auditing write-capable agents still apply.
  An audit that stops at an approval can still settle its private project under its original held claim, so that
  refused tool call does not falsely block later runs. Parked runs gain no new tool-dispatch permission; superseded
  claims and unresolved writes still refuse settlement. The bounded host-settlement model covers this transition;
  the DSL effect-admission and recovery-driver models are unchanged.

  Supported HTTP MCP connections retain source tool selections and denials, with explicit destination account binding.
  Resource lists, templates and reads use the same pinned grants, credentials and permission gate; resource-only servers
  are supported on managed AgentRun; native Codex 0.171.0 has a resource-only discovery limitation. Incomplete resource listings fail visibly, and resource bodies that echo connection credentials are
  scrubbed or withheld before filing. Three upstream tool names are now reserved for these generated resource operations:
  `agentrun_list_resources`, `agentrun_list_resource_templates` and `agentrun_read_resource`. A conflicting upstream tool
  must be renamed before its server can connect. Stdio connections and unsupported native capabilities remain prerequisites.

  Unknown source storage-write outcomes retain receipts and block deletion until independently resolved; restarting
  or acknowledging a run checkpoint does not clear a source write receipt.

  The Codex adapter preserves native rollout ordinals when recording an approved tool's result before resuming. This
  fixes pinned Codex 0.164.0 rejecting the resumed thread after approval. Existing mixed or invalid ordinal histories
  remain retained and fail before another tool dispatch; they are not silently rewritten or retried. Older wholly
  unnumbered journals retain their format. This serialization fix leaves recovery admission, intent and result ordering
  unchanged, so the recovery models do not change.
- An ACP run (Cursor, Goose, or a harness recipe) no longer stalls after many turns. Before, the adapter copied the agent's whole session store into the run's records at every turn, so the records grew with the square of the turn count. After about 20 Cursor turns they no longer fit the 32 MiB channel to the run's process: an approval answered 204, and the run then waited for good. Now the mirror stores each file as 64 KiB pieces, each written once per session, so a store that grows by appending costs only its new bytes. It never copies SQLite's `-shm` file, and holds at most 8 MiB per session. Past that, the run's timeline says "The agent's session state passed 8 MiB, so a resume starts it fresh with the conversation so far." and the mirror stops. A run whose records no longer cross to its process now fails at once, naming the size and the limit, and the approval that woke it is answered that the run failed. Adapters get a `notice` event, which serve shows as a step on the run's timeline. A session store mirrored before this version is not restored: such a run resumes fresh with the conversation so far. <!-- changes/acp-state-mirror-bounded.md -->
- The console's trigger forms make a trigger for a connected agent: a new schedule, webhook, GitHub trigger, app trigger, feed trigger or email trigger asks such an agent for no cost cap and sends none, and says why in place of the field ("None. A connected agent runs in its own CLI, which keeps its own limits: AgentRun cannot cap its runs."). Before, each form required a cap the server refuses on a connected agent's target (422 `target.max_cost_usd`), so no such trigger could be made from the console. <!-- changes/console-trigger-connected-agent-no-cap.md -->
  - A schedule edited onto a connected agent drops its cap, and the effort it carried, which the server refuses there too.
  - A trigger's page reads the same words under Cost cap for a connected agent, in place of "Agent's default".
  - For every other agent the forms are as they were: a cap is required unless the agent has a default one.
- `agentrun deploy DIR` uploads the folder's package and nothing else of it: `agent.md`, the `skills/`, `rules/` and `evals/` trees, and the answer's schema file `agent.md` names (`output: {schema}`) at the folder's root. A `.env`, a key, a README or any other file or folder beside them stays on this machine. A folder with no `agent.md` exits 2 with nothing sent. <!-- changes/deploy-upload-custody.md -->
  - Deleting an agent (`DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}` once archived, as `agentrun deploy delete` does) also removes the uploaded package (`upload:<name>`) it was applied from, in the same write, when no other agent on that server, archived or not, was applied from it. A package imported from GitHub stays. Before, an upload stayed until the next upload of its name, and a server that serves the API alone could never remove one.
  - A deploy, rollback or delete that waits for another CLI to finish saving its deploy record says so on stderr.
- The dial conformance script accepts `AGENTRUN_BIND_HOST` so local verification can bind to `127.0.0.1` without exposing a public listener. Its local fixture tests use this setting; leaving it unset preserves the public listener used by remote machines. <!-- changes/dial-conformance-bind-host.md -->
- `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/package` no longer copies a credential in the clear into a package. A trigger's source (a feed URL with a `?token=`, `?key=`, `?sig=` or `?password=` query, an address with a user part), its run input (an `api_key` field) and an MCP tool's pin are read the way a composio trigger's config is sealed, and each credential is a `report.blocked` entry of kind `trigger` or `pin` named by its field (`Status: source.urls.0`, `slack: pin.post.api_key`), never by its value. The trigger or pin is left out, and `agentrun export` and `agentrun deploy` write nothing and exit 2, as they do for any blocked entry. A query such as `?page=2` still exports. `report.blocked[].kind` and `report.remade[].kind` are now an enum in the OpenAPI document, so the generated clients type them. <!-- changes/export-custody.md -->
- A run a paid call stopped for good (a fal job or monid call settled above its hold, taking the run past its cap) now stays stopped when a call that passed the tool gate beside it is admitted after the stop and refused for room. Before, that refusal replaced the stop, so a script's next call ran; the run still ended failed at its next model request. <!-- changes/fal-cap-stop-sticky.md -->
- A fal job whose output states more than its input asked for (a larger image, a longer clip) is still booked at what its output states, and when that takes the run past its spend cap, the run now stops at once in the cap's words: no tool runs after it, a script's own calls included. Before, the run went on until its next model request. The stop reads only what the run has been charged: a job still running counts toward whether a new call is let through, never toward stopping the run, so one that settles above its hold beside another still running stops the run only if the charges, once in, pass the cap. A fal job priced by the length of the media it is given is now only one of the endpoints fal bills that way (ElevenLabs dubbing, voice isolation and speech-to-text, and sync-lipsync v2); another endpoint billed per second whose input names no length, such as a talking video made from a voice or LatentSync, which fal bills by its output video, is refused under a cap and booked as an unknown charge without one. <!-- changes/fal-cap-stop.md -->
- A connected agent's held draft is now revised as its hold says. Before, its run's end never found the held workflow (the task never matched it as the run's input), so a check's hold never asked its one recompile and a hold after five give-backs stayed held for good. The held workflow is now the one the task fits, as the start reserves a check. A hold after five give-backs asks its revise only once the agent has `compile_after` completed runs of its own started since the hold, the same wait as a first compile, so a client that never sends a shadow check costs one compile per `compile_after` runs. That revise prompt says nothing was checked and there are no disagreements to show, and no longer says that nothing compiles again. <!-- changes/give-back-hold-cadence.md -->
- A monid call charged above the estimate it was held at no longer stops a run that can still afford it. It is booked as charged and logged, and the run stops only when that charge takes it past its spend cap, in the cap's words, as a fal job's does. Before, any such charge stopped the run, failed, in the words "monid charged $X, more than the $Y held; the run stopped", even far below its cap. <!-- changes/monid-overrun-cap.md -->
- A stored agent body refuses a sandbox's `computer.needs` of more than 32 programs, as the API already did, in the API's words: the store, the API document and a template's `needs` now read one rule. <!-- changes/needs-store-cap.md -->
- A run's purge (`DELETE /v2/runs/{run_id}`) now takes the run's text off its agent's learning folder's current files: its diff files go, and the feedback lines its merges added to `corrections.md` leave main in one commit by the host per merge (none when nothing is left to take off; a line a person edited since stays). Another merge's diff that shows such a line as context is written without it. The folder's history reads (`GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/learning`, its `/log`, a workflow's `/revisions`, and a champion read by its digest in `/promotions`) no longer serve the purged run's merges, and a log page read before the purge is followed by the next with no change skipped; a champion whose revision was the run's (or that it changed last on main) reads as one no commit holds. Each merge's scrub lands once, so a `DELETE` sent again after a stop takes no other run's same line, and a merge of the run made since is scrubbed by it. It covers the learning folder on the server; a Mode 2 agent's folder on an Archil disk keeps the text until a reset or the agent's purge. The bytes stay in the folder's `.git` until a learning reset (`DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}/learning`) or the agent's purge, which delete the folder whole; a promotion record keeps its commit ids. A second `DELETE` of a purged run does this again, so a run purged before this release loses its text the same way; it is `204` with no body as before, and `503 unavailable` while the learning folder can't be written. <!-- changes/purge-learning-text.md -->
- Run ids minted in one millisecond now list and claim in creation order: every run id comes from the monotonic UUIDv7 minter uploads already use, so two runs started in the same millisecond list newest first and a runner claims the older first. Before, a run id's bits after its time were random, and such runs listed and were claimed in either order. A purge on SQLite now writes its scrub marker (`store.sqlite.scrub`) before it changes a row, so a full disk refuses the `DELETE` (500 `internal`) with nothing purged and the retry purges whole. A retried `DELETE` of a purged run or agent does no checkpoint and writes nothing. A purge that commits and then fails (a Postgres commit left unanswered) no longer keeps the run's answer and input in the server's memory. <!-- changes/purge-marker-first.md -->
- A learned workflow whose `workflow.json` a purged run changed last is refused by every read, however old its merge: its file read is `410 purged`, a champion read by its digest reads no commit, a later merge's diff shows the file as added (never the purged text), an SDK start sent again whose receipt pinned it is `410 purged`, and no run lays or serves it, so the agent takes the run. Before, the file read, the diff, an SDK receipt and a run's seed served the purged text, and a champion read served it once the merge was older than the log's newest 200 changes. <!-- changes/purged-workflow-refused.md -->
- A run can bring its own tool keys: `keys: {"PARALLEL_API_KEY": "..."}` on `POST /v2/runs`, `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/runs` and a message, for the tool keys its revision reads (422 at `keys.<NAME>` otherwise). <!-- changes/run-keys.md -->
  Each one is sealed with the run's launch, opened at its claim for its tools alone and erased from the store when its turn ends; the runner's redactor keeps the value in memory to cut it. It is never in the run's body, timeline, view or logs, and the runner cuts it from what the run writes.
  `AGENTRUN_RUN_KEYS=1`: a template's apply makes its agent though a tool key it declares is not set here, with a warning, and each run of that agent must bring the key in `keys` (409 `agent_not_runnable` at `keys.<NAME>` without it). Keys the server holds are still used by runs that bring none. The monid key stays the server's: an agent's monid tools are checked with it when the agent is saved, so with none on the server a template granting them is still refused at its apply.
- A run's purge takes each learned workflow whose `workflow.json` it changed last off main, its README.md too, so both file reads are `404`, the learning view no longer lists it, and the next compile turn is never asked to revise its text. Before, its README.md and description were still served and a held revision of it went into the next run's compile prompt; a run purged before this takes its workflows off when its `DELETE` is sent again. <!-- changes/purge-takes-workflows-off-main.md -->
- Console: a finished run's recording on the Screen tab has the run's steps beside it. Each step the run took while the file was recorded is listed at its time on the video, in the Timeline tab's words; clicking one moves the video there, and the step the video is at is marked as it plays. A step's time is its timeline time since the row that says the recording began, so a run whose timeline has no such row plays its recording alone, as before. The steps sit beside the player on a wide window and under it on a narrow one. <!-- changes/console-recording-steps.md -->
- Launch hook: with `AGENTRUN_LAUNCH_HOOK_URL` and `AGENTRUN_LAUNCH_HOOK_SECRET` set, each trigger firing that would start a run is POSTed to the host instead, signed as Standard Webhooks (`{firing_id, trigger_id, agent_id, revision_id, input, fired_at}`), and the host starts the run through the API with its own keys and cap. The host passes the new `trigger_firing` (`{trigger_id, firing_id}`) on `POST /agents/{agent_id}/runs`, so the run is the firing's: it carries the trigger, its title and input origin, and the firing reads `started` with it, counted by the overlap check and `max_active_runs`. The host may start the run before or after it answers: a 2xx without the run records the firing `sent` with `start_by`, 10 minutes after that answer, and it takes that one start until then. The 10 minutes run from the answer, not from `fired_at`, so a catch-up, a firing that waited on `max_active_runs` or one handed again after a restart gets the same time. Any other answer, or none in 10 s, records it `skipped` with why. The hook URL is https, or http to 127.0.0.0/8, `::1` or `localhost` alone; any other http URL stops the start. On an API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`), the hook is what lets a template's apply make its schedule and feed triggers. Unset, firings start their runs as before, and `trigger_firing` is refused. <!-- changes/trigger-launch-hook.md -->
- `GET /v2/settings/mcp-server-names` answers the names of the MCP servers saved here, `{names}`, and nothing else of them: no URL, auth type, header, tool or Composio record. It takes the server's token and is served on an API-only server too (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`). <!-- changes/mcp-server-names.md -->
- A Composio user id may now hold a `:` (a team's, say), in a save's `user_id` and a run's `mcp_auth`. A space, a slash and a `~` are still refused. <!-- changes/composio-team-user.md -->
- A key a run brings in `keys` or `model_key` is text of 8 or more characters with no space or control character: a shorter one could not be cut from what the run writes, so it is now 422 `invalid` at `keys.<NAME>` or `model_key`, the value never echoed. With `AGENTRUN_RUN_KEYS=1`, no trigger is made whose firings would run an agent without the tool keys each of its runs must bring: a template's apply skips such triggers with a warning at `triggers.<N>` (`not_set_up_here`, the apply still 201) unless the launch hook is set, and `POST /v2/triggers`, or a `PATCH` that moves a trigger, is 409 `agent_not_runnable` naming the keys for one that would start such runs with no hook, or message one of them. <!-- changes/run-keys-hardening.md -->
- A run's view, and so every runs list, is several times faster for runs with long timelines: redacting a timeline's rows no longer derives every held value's forms again for each row (its path spellings, base64 at three alignments, percent forms, hex and folded patterns). What is derived of a set of values is kept per array and derived again when the array's values change, so a value a caller adds is still cut, and what is cut is unchanged. On a store of code-review runs of about 2,500 journal writes each, one run's view went from about 3.2 s to 0.7 s, and a list of ten runs from about 22 s to 5 s. <!-- changes/redact-derived-once.md -->
- A server runs a harness recipe it is started with: `agentrun-serve --harness-recipe FILE` (repeatable, or `AGENTRUN_SERVE_HARNESS_RECIPES`), and `agentrun-serve runner` takes the same flag. The harness is listed, and a run starts, only once a `harness-check` passed on the data directory for that recipe file, binary and tree (`<id>.checked`; else `HARNESS_NOT_CHECKED`); each start digests the binary and tree again. A proxy-billed agent runs on the server's model proxy. A plan-billed one runs on keys saved for its harness, which no server saves yet (`HARNESS_KEYS_NOT_SAVED`), or, on a server its owner starts with `--harness-sign-in` on their own machine (loopback, its own SQLite store, its runs as its own user, one owner; else `HARNESS_SIGN_IN_NOT_LOCAL`), on the owner's own sign-in for a run a person starts; a scheduled or triggered run on it is refused at its claim, and a `message_run` trigger to a run on it is refused when made and skipped at each firing. `harness-check` runs on a recipe's keys alone, never the sign-in, and a plan-billed recipe must name a key. `agentrun harness sign-in` prints one warning line that the vendor's terms (the recipe's new `signIn.terms`) may not cover use through AgentRun. A run's agent reaches beyond loopback only through the server's egress proxy, to the recipe's `model.hosts`. The loader now refuses a key whose name is not shaped as a key (`FOO_CRED`: `RECIPE_KEY_NOT_OWN`). <!-- changes/recipe-run-path.md -->
- A template package can be read on its own: `GET /v2/templates/{template}` reads one package, bundled or imported, as `GET /v2/templates` lists it, with its instructions and every skill file in full (placeholders unfilled) and its apply page as `console_url`; an unknown id is `404`, an imported id is URL-encoded. CLI: `agentrun template get TEMPLATE`; clients: `template.get(id)`. <!-- changes/get-one-template.md -->
- A backend SDK run (`POST /agents/{agent_id}/sdk-runs`) can now run longer than an hour, be reported after it began, and carry its own title and labels. <!-- changes/sdk-run-start-fields.md -->
  - Each events batch, an empty `events: []` one included, moves the run's deadline to an hour after that batch, up to 24 hours after its start. A run that misses its deadline still ends with an unknown outcome, as before.
  - The start takes optional `started_at` (RFC 3339, at most 60 seconds ahead of the server's clock and 7 days behind it), which becomes the run's `created_at`. The deadline is still counted from the start request. Those bounds apply to a new start only: a retry under the same `Idempotency-Key` and body of a start that was made gets that run's receipt, however late it comes.
  - The start takes optional `title` (trimmed, 1 to 200 characters), used instead of the input's first 80 characters, and `labels`, under the same rules as `RunCreate.labels`, so `GET /runs?label=<key>:<value>` finds the run. A label holding a server secret is refused.
  - `GET /capabilities` says so in `features.sdk_runs`: `{ started_at: true, title: true, labels: true, max_open_s: 86400 }`.
  - A start without these fields behaves as before. They are for SDK runs; a CLI learning turn takes none of them and keeps its 24-hour window.

## 0.1.0-beta.52 (2026-11-21)

**Breaking:**

- The apply answer (`POST /v2/templates/{template}/apply`) no longer carries `trigger_ids`: read each trigger's `trigger_id` from `triggers`, which lists the same triggers in the same order with their names, kinds and on or off. The TypeScript and Python clients' `ApplyTemplateResponse` drop the field. <!-- changes/apply-drops-trigger-ids.md -->

**Changes:**

- An agent can limit its own runs' requests on free models: `definition.max_requests`, a whole number, under the server's limit (`AGENTRUN_FREE_MODEL_REQUESTS`, 60 by default), so a run stops at the lower of the two. A dollar cap can't stop a free model, so before, the server's limit was the only bound, for every run on the server alike, and one run looping on a free model could spend a person's whole daily free quota under it. The run that reaches the agent's limit ends `failed` with `spend_cap_reached` in the server limit's words, naming the number it stopped at ("Not sent: this run reached its 20-request limit for free models."). It counts what the server's limit counts, and a paid request never counts. Above 0 sets it, 0 clears it, and an edit that leaves it out keeps it. A template sets it with `budget: { per_run_usd, max_requests }`: the manifest refuses 0 or a fraction, the template list shows it, and the console's template card says "Free-model requests: at most N a run". <!-- changes/agent-max-requests.md -->
- `GET /v2/computers` says per kind whether a run of it can record its screen on this server, and the console's Recording switch reads that alone. <!-- changes/computers-say-record.md -->
  - Public API addition: each of `kinds[]` carries `record`, `{available: true}` or `{available: false, why}`. A desktop, a phone or a browser is available when this server has `ffmpeg` on its PATH (read at each call, as a save of `computer.record: true` checks it); without it, each says "ffmpeg isn't installed on this server (no ffmpeg command on PATH)". A sandbox and no computer are never available, in their own words. The TypeScript and Python clients' `ListComputersResponse` gain it.
  - The agent editor's Computer step shows the Recording switch for every kind but no computer, from the kind's `record`: where a run can't record here, the switch is off and disabled with the server's words for why (a saved `record: true` can still be turned off). It used to show the switch only for a kind whose `settings` list `record`, and offered it on a server with no ffmpeg until the save was refused. A switch of kind or provider drops `record: true` where the new kind can't record, in the same words.
- The console filters Composio's actions, the agent editor's Tools step and an app trigger's events by name, slug or description; events list A to Z with their Markdown descriptions rendered; a new trigger marks Agent, Each run is asked and (with no agent default) the cost cap with *. Every list search in the console (agents and connected coding agents, an agent's runs, templates, a run's trace) now keeps a row holding each word typed, in any order. <!-- changes/console-list-filters.md -->
- A run counts fal's jobs: `run_model`, `submit_job` and `submit_jobs` on a fal MCP server (toolkit `fal`, or `mcp.fal.ai`) are priced before they are sent, at fal's `get_pricing` unit price times the units the job's input states (images, megapixels, characters, seconds, or the length of its input media), held under the run's spend cap and booked as tool cost. A job the cap can't take is refused unsent, as is one whose price can't be known beforehand; with no cap that one runs, booked as an unknown charge. The figure is an estimate at fal's list price. Agents saved before this are metered when their server is at `mcp.fal.ai`; save an agent again to pin a fal server at another address as metered. <!-- changes/fal-spend-metered.md -->
- `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage` (`runusage/5`) now says which charges were the infrastructure's own redo. A turn is worked again when the claim working it is cut: its runner drained for a deploy (SIGTERM), its runner died, it lost its lease, or the turn was tried again. Each line, browser session and computer interval carries `attempt` (1 for a turn's first, 2 for its first redo, and so on) and `billable`. A turn's charges are split into one line per attempt. `billable` is false only for the model requests a cut attempt sent and never finished, which the attempt that takes the turn over sends again. Answered requests, paid calls, browser and computer time stay billable: the next attempt reuses them. The run also reports `infra_usd`, the sum of the lines that are not billable: 0 for a run with no such request, and null when one has no known cost, which a request cut in flight never does. This is data only: `total` and `cost.usd` still hold every line, and nothing is charged differently. A run from before this read keeps `attempt: null` and `billable: true` on every line. <!-- changes/run-attempts.md -->

  Each claim writes its turn and attempt in its own transaction to the store's new `run_attempts` table. Postgres gets it from migration `0025_run_attempts.sql`, which is additive (a runner of the earlier version never reads it). A SQLite store gets it at the server's open, and a runner waits for that server. Each row holds `cause`, why the attempt before it was cut: `drain`, `crash`, `lease_lapse` or `retry`. A runner's release writes the cut attempt's own word for `drain` and `retry`. A runner that loses its lease writes `lease_lapse` while it can still reach the store. A lapse with no word reads as `crash`. A claim's `turn` and `attempt` are on `Claim`.

  Each model request a claim sends to the server's model gateway carries the run, turn and attempt as LiteLLM's spend-logs metadata, in the header `x-litellm-spend-logs-metadata` (`{"agentrun_run_id":…,"agentrun_turn":…,"agentrun_attempt":…}`). That lets a gateway's spend logs be matched to the run's lines call by call. "The server's model gateway" means `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL`, or `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on its origin. The header is sent on pi's routes and Claude Code's, never to a vendor's own endpoint. Codex's adapter takes no extra headers, so its requests carry none yet.
- `web_save` answers a saved audio or video file's length in seconds as `duration_s` (to the millisecond), read from the file's own bytes: mp3, wav, mp4 and m4a. An agent can then fit a cut to a voiceover, or price a job billed by its input's length, without another tool. Any other file, or media whose length its bytes don't give (ogg, webm, a file with no header), answers no `duration_s`. <!-- changes/web-save-duration.md -->
- A connected SDK agent's learned workflow is promoted only after compile_after checked turns, like a managed agent's, not after one. Each reserved native turn is one row of the check: the agent answers it, the caller's shadow runs the draft, and the server keeps the compared turn on the promotion record (`check.turns`) and waits for the next turn the draft takes. The turn that makes `learning.compile_after` decides once on every turn collected, on the same `agree_min` and `alone_min` bar; a disagreement no longer holds the draft on its own turn, and a turn the backend never completes within an hour is one failed row of the check instead of its decision. <!-- changes/sdk-check-evidence-bar.md -->
- A synced folder now sees a file rewritten to the same size in the push's own clock tick (a command that lands tens of milliseconds after the claim's push, on a filesystem whose timestamps come from the kernel's coarse clock). Before, such a file kept the size and mtime the baseline listing recorded, and the runner's copy kept the old bytes for good. The claim's push now gives every file `PUSHED_MTIME` (2000-01-01T00:00:00Z) in its tar header, so any later write moves its mtime, and nothing is read back after the push. <!-- changes/sync-sees-push-tick-rewrite.md -->
  computerd's `tar.push` now gives each file its tar header's mtime, as tar and the macOS computerd already did, instead of the time of the extraction. `TarEntry` takes an optional `mtime` for the header, whole seconds from 0 to `MAX_TAR_MTIME` (ustar's 11 octal digits; any other value throws a `RangeError` before the entry is written); without one it is the time the entry is written, as before.
- In the console, a webhook trigger's once-shown signing secret after a template apply that skipped a trigger (a feed given no feeds, a GitHub or Composio trigger not set up here) is labelled with its own trigger's name, and its warning opens that trigger. Before, the console matched the package's trigger index against the answer's list, which a skipped trigger shifts: the secret carried the skipped trigger's name, and the warning's "Open … (Rotate)" link went to another trigger or to none. The console now finds each trigger by its name. <!-- changes/webhook-secret-name.md -->
- `DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}/learning` resets an agent's learning without deleting the agent: its learning folder whole (corrections, learned workflows, their history and the audit ledger), on this server and on every Archil disk its runs used (`503` while one can't be reached, nothing deleted), then its promotion records and grades. Deleting an agent now also deletes its learning folder on a disk a run's launch named. The agent, its runs and their files stay, and the run list, `GET /stats` and `GET /usage` read the same; the next run takes the agent path with nothing learned. Learning reads only the runs after the reset: they alone count toward `compile_after` and feed a compile, a check's replays and audits. A run whose start read the agent's learning before the reset learns nothing at its end, its learning `dropped` with the new reason `reset`. Learning-only runs in flight (replays, audit shadows) are cancelled first; while a run of the agent's own is still going it answers `409 learning_busy` naming the runs, and nothing is deleted. `204` when done, idempotent (an agent that never learned is `204` too), with the owner's session or the token as deleting an agent takes (any other console session is `403 forbidden`), in the API-only profile as well. The TypeScript and Python clients add `learning.reset(agent_id)`, and the CLI `agentrun learning reset <agent_id>`. <!-- changes/reset-agent-learning.md -->
- A run on a disk its launch names (`archil_disk`) learns nothing: it starts with no seed, no learned corrections and no learned workflow, and every learning read of the agent's runs (a compile's traces and its `compile_after` count, a check's replays, an audit's draw, the money rule, the cost page's ledger) skips it. Before, such a run read and fed the one learning of its agent, so a self-hoster's customers could see each other's traces in a learned workflow. A later change that lets named disks learn adds a per-disk key to the learning records. <!-- changes/learning-per-disk.md -->

  Upgrading: runs gain a `disk` column, filled from each run's launch (Postgres migration `0026_run_disk.sql`; SQLite store version 15, which the server applies when it opens the store, and a runner waits for that). A run purged before the upgrade has no launch left, so it reads as the default disk's. A run on the agent's own disk, or on no disk, learns as before.
- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) serves `DELETE /v2/runs/{id}` for a run of an agent an inline run made (`external`): a backend erasing one user's runs of a shared external agent purges each run, where deleting the agent would take every user's runs. The purge is the full server's: `204`, and `204` again once purged; `409 run_not_final` while it or a run made from it is live; every other route of it `410 purged`; its cost kept in every total. A run of an agent made here stays refused there with the profile's `404`, as before. <!-- changes/api-only-run-delete.md -->
- A run's fal jobs no longer collide with another run's: fal's hosted MCP server (`mcp.fal.ai`) keeps one `submission_key` journal per fal account and refuses a key it has seen with another request, so the same task run twice in a day, which makes the same keys, had its second run refused. The run's gateway now sends fal each `submission_key` of `run_model`, `submit_job`, each request of `submit_jobs` and `get_submission` with a suffix derived from the run, so a retry within one run still reaches fal with the same key and is deduped, and two runs never share one. Replies read back with the agent's own key. A key too long for fal's 128-character limit with the suffix is shortened with a hash of the whole key and marked apart from unshortened keys, so it never becomes another key. A server saved with the toolkit `fal` at another address (an eval's fake) receives the agent's keys unchanged. <!-- changes/fal-run-scoped-key.md -->
- A `DELETE` of a run or an agent retried after its purge committed and could not write the SQLite scrub marker (the 500 `internal` a full disk answers) now arranges the scrub again: it answers 204 as before, and it also runs the purge's WAL checkpoint again, writing `store.sqlite.scrub` when another connection still holds the log back, so the next start's scrub truncates it. Before, the retry answered 204 and wrote nothing, and the log could keep the purged bytes until some later checkpoint. A `DELETE` of a purged run or agent with the marker already there writes nothing new, and an agent's retried `DELETE` also drops the purge-in-progress mark its failed one left. <!-- changes/purge-retry-marker.md -->
- On Postgres, a run whose input or text holds an escaped NUL (`\u0000`) or a lone surrogate no longer breaks the store's reads of its launch body, its commands or its journal. The affected reads were an agent's learning starts, the runs made from a run, a run's purge, a reopen, a claim, a trigger's queued message and the start sweep of runs of unknown cost. Postgres keeps such text, but its json functions refuse the whole document over one escape, and a read that scans every launch failed for every run. Outside a transaction, each read retries on that refusal against a copy with those escapes blanked. Inside a transaction, where a refused statement can't be retried, the read uses the copy from the start. Learning starts come back as written: a run's `learning` member is never taken from a blanked copy. <!-- changes/launch-json-unicode.md -->
- `DELETE /v2/runs/{id}` on a run whose launch named a caller's Archil disk now also deletes the agent's learning folder on that disk, together with the run's own folder. Before, the folder stayed until the agent's learning reset or the agent's delete, and the run's merge diff and its correction line stayed in it after the purge. Nothing reads that folder: a run on a named disk gets no learning seed. <!-- changes/purge-learning-folder.md -->
- A connected agent's workflow check now holds only after five give-backs in a row, never counts a cancelled turn, and starts the count again when a turn lands. A check held that way is never stopped for good: the agent's next compile revises the workflow and checks the revision afresh. <!-- changes/sdk-check-give-backs-in-a-row.md -->
- A backend SDK run's compile ask now stops at the agent's own max_requests on a free model, as every other run of the agent does, when that is under the server's AGENTRUN_FREE_MODEL_REQUESTS. <!-- changes/sdk-compile-max-requests.md -->
- Two files uploaded in one millisecond now list newest first in `GET /v2/files`. Upload ids are minted by the same monotonic UUIDv7 as agent ids, so each sorts after the one before it; before, two ids in one millisecond carried random bits after the time and could list in either order. <!-- changes/uploads-monotonic-id.md -->
- A run's claim-time lay of its skills no longer depends on the class of a `NOT_FOUND` error to tell that a fresh folder has no `.agents/skills/` yet: it asks `stat`. On beta.50 a Mode 2 run in its own process lost `WorkspaceError`'s class over its channel and failed at its claim with `".agents/skills" is not there` whenever it had a skill (its own, or a desktop or phone computer's); beta.51 registered the class, and the lay now holds without it. A lay that fails says so (`laying the run's skills in .agents/skills/: …`), and an Archil listing or exec of a folder that is not there names the disk's key and the disk. <!-- changes/run-skills-lay-reads-no-error-class.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.51 (2026-11-21)

**Breaking:**

- A pending approval says why a call its setting allows asks in a field of its own, `asks_because` (on `pending` of GET /runs/{run_id} and the run list), and no longer among the call's arguments: `args_preview` is the model's arguments alone, with no `asked_because` key, and `summary` no longer ends "Asks because ...". A client that read the reason from `args_preview`'s `asked_because` (or from the end of `summary`) breaks: read `asks_because` instead, absent on a call that asks by its setting. The console's approval card, on the run page and on Mission Control, says "Asks because <why>." above the arguments' box. <!-- changes/approval-asks-because.md -->
- A runner can run on a disk of its own, and `runner --check` checks its environment by name. A runner with `AGENTRUN_STORE_URL`, `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY` and a local `--data` never reads the server's data directory: in Mode 2 (Archil settings saved) it runs every run; while the server is in Mode 1 it claims nothing and says why, on its log and to the server, which refuses a new run in those words (`503 runner_refused`) while no runner on its own data directory is there. The mode is the server's (its saved settings, or the Archil settings in its own environment), never the runner's. The runner never fails the run itself. The server tells the disks apart by an id it keeps in `/data/data-root.id` and says in the store at each start, beside the names (never the values) of its run-facing environment. <!-- changes/disk-free-runner.md -->
  What breaks: `runner --check --data D --name N` now also checks the runner's environment (the store opens, the seal key is the store's, the runner holds every run-facing name the server holds, an upstream on loopback answers) and fails on any gap. A health check run with an empty environment (compose's `env -i`) now fails: run it with the container's environment (the check prints names, never values), or use `runner --check --heartbeat --data D --name N` for the heartbeat alone. `runner --check --env [--data D]` checks the environment alone, before a runner starts. Not yet on a disk of its own: screen recordings. See deploy/README.md, "A runner on a disk of its own".

**Changes:**

- A disk removed at Archil while a run is on it now fails that run's next disk call as the disk being gone (`UNAVAILABLE`, in Archil's words), not as a missing file. <!-- changes/archil-disk-gone-midrun.md -->
- Email: Save signs in before it keeps the account, and the console opens and makes email triggers. <!-- changes/email-save-signs-in.md -->
  - Behavior change: `PUT /v2/settings/email` signs in to IMAP and SMTP first, as Test does, sending nothing. If either refuses or can't be reached, it answers 424 `upstream_failed` with `details.imap` and `details.smtp` (each `{ok, message}`) and saves nothing, keeping any account saved before. It used to save any password. A body that doesn't read is still 422 by field, before any sign-in. The console's Save shows the refusal beside the form.
  - Public API addition: the apply answer (`POST /v2/templates/{template}/apply`, Apply and Update) carries `agent_change`: `made`, `updated` (a new revision written) or `unchanged` (an update with `agent_id` whose package and parameters the current revision already holds, no revision written), with `revision_version` the agent's current revision once it is done. It also carries `triggers`, every trigger the apply made or kept, in the package's order, each `{trigger_id, name, kind, enabled}`; `trigger_ids` is unchanged. The TypeScript and Python clients' `ApplyTemplateResponse` gain both. The console's Apply and Update result lists each trigger by its name and kind in words, on or off, an email trigger beside its schedules (a schedule keeps its line and next time); it used to list the schedules alone.
  - An email trigger's page opens in the console: the account and mailbox it watches, how often, its last check, its filter, its agent and its firings, with Pause, Run now and Delete. It carries the same "Waits for your approval" warning the other triggers' pages do when its agent has a tool that asks (refused, with accounts off), and Run unattended. It used to say the page didn't open it yet.
  - Triggers → New makes an email trigger (`#/triggers/new-email`), beside the schedule, webhook, GitHub, app and feed forms: its agent, mailbox (INBOX unless changed), how often it reads, what each run is asked, its cost cap and whether it is on, with the same approval warning and Run unattended. With no account saved it says so and links to Settings → Email. An email trigger used to be made through the API or a template alone.
- A template's apply result, on Templates and in the API playground, says from the answer's `agent_change` what the apply did: an update that changed nothing reads "Nothing to update: rev 2 is current.", never that the agent is made or applied. <!-- changes/lookback-tidy.md -->
  The console also:
  - Takes a run with only a field for an agent whose `input_schema` fields are all optional, as the server does, and says a refusal of neither at the message box. Filling a field clears the server's issue at the message only where the message is optional; a required message keeps its issue until it is fixed.
  - Offers the Grade form on an ended run whose learning reads `reflecting`, and says a `409 run_learning` in the server's words, keeping the choice.
  - Says on every tool row of a template's install page that the template asks you to grant it, and on a tool whose `asks` is `ask` that each call waits for your OK unless you allowed it in Settings or pick Never ask; no listed tool reads as one the template does not ask for.
  - Says on a Triggers row, of any kind, whose agent has tools that ask "Waits for your approval: <tools>" (or "Refused without your approval" with accounts off), as the trigger's page does, reading each agent once.
  - Names each trigger's agent on Triggers when the agent was made after the console opened (a template applied from a URL makes one with its triggers): the agents' names are read again each time Triggers opens, as Runs and Mission Control read them. It used to show the agent's id.

  A look-back cut by a stop or cancel is said as "a stop or cancel cut it while it wrote what it learned", and the learning state's `reflecting` description names the run's end it reads.
- A run whose revision ships skills no longer fails at its claim on a fresh Mode 2 (Archil) folder with `".agents/skills" is not there` when it runs in its own process. A `WorkspaceError` now crosses the run's channel as a `WorkspaceError` with its `code`, as the other run errors do, so `layOwnSkills` (and every other check of `instanceof WorkspaceError` in the run's process) reads a missing folder as `NOT_FOUND` again. Runs in the runner's process were not affected. <!-- changes/run-process-workspace-error.md -->
- A runner that holds many customers' runs keeps per-run users without putting its own user in 256 groups, and its operator can stop owners from allowing private-network hosts (`AGENTRUN_PRIVATE_HOSTS`). See [docs/multi-tenant-runners.md](https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun/blob/main/docs/multi-tenant-runners.md) for the threat model. <!-- changes/runner-per-run-users-one-group.md -->

  - In the image, the server's user (node) is now in one group, its own, and in no slot's group. A platform that reads a user's groups at start (Northflank's environment injector refused node's 257 groups) can run the image with per-run users on, so `AGENTRUN_RUN_USER=same` is no longer needed there.
  - A run's folders are given to its slot before it starts (`agentrun-runas own <slot>`: the slot's uid, node's group, folders `2770` with the setgid bit) and back to node at its end (`own runner`). The server reads a running run's files through its one group; no other slot can enter them, nor the slot's next run. The helper gains `cap_chown` (kept alone while it gives folders, each entry changed through a descriptor opened without following a link); `reown` and `reap --fix` are gone. A give-back that fails retires the slot, as a reap that does not hold does.
  - A run that shuts one of its folders (`chmod 700`, which drops its setgid bit) hides it from the server until the run ends.
  - `AGENTRUN_PRIVATE_HOSTS` bounds the private-network hosts an owner may allow an MCP server or a calendar on (Settings → MCP servers). Unset, the owner's list holds, as before. `none` reads no owner's list and saves only an empty one (422, naming the switch, otherwise): set it on a server or runner many customers share, and on each runner, which reads its own environment and says the bound at its start. A comma list of address ranges (`10.20.0.0/16,fd12:3456::/32`) allows a listed host only inside them. A value that is neither reads as `none`. `GET /v2/capabilities` lists it under `switches`.
- `GET /v2/capacity` (`capacity/1`) says how much room the runners have, read from the store alone, so a server with no runner beside it (`--no-runner`, `AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`, where it is served too) answers for every runner on its store. It gives the runs waiting for a runner (`runs.queued`: queued, handed back, or with a claim that ran out, past any backoff) and the runs a live claim holds (`runs.executing`). It lists each live runner by name with its build's `version`, its `slots` (the most runs it holds at once), what it holds (`executing`) and its `free_slots`, plus the total `free_slots`. It counts the runs handed back still running within `?window=` minutes (`hand_backs`: 1 to 1440, default 15). It names no run, agent or address, and it takes the server's token like every route but capabilities and health. An operator or a scaler reads it to size the runners by backlog, not CPU. <!-- changes/runner-capacity.md -->
  Each runner's row now says its version and slots (`runners.version`, `runners.slots`), and every release that leaves its run running writes a row to a new `hand_backs` table, kept for a day. Postgres migration `0024_runner_capacity.sql` adds both, and a SQLite store gets them at the server's open. Both are additive. A runner of an earlier build that is already running keeps working, with its version and slots read as null. On SQLite, one also starts again as before. On Postgres, a runner of an earlier build that starts after the migration refuses the store, as for any migration it does not know: upgrade Postgres runners with the server. A runner of this build waits on SQLite for a server that added them.
  A runner prints metric lines in the server's log format (`at=… event=… key=value`), so a log-based metric can count them: `runner_claimed`, with `took_over=1` when it took over a run whose lease ran out; `runner_hand_back` with a `cause` (`drain`, `interrupted`, `end_retry`, `give_back`, or `claim_lost` with its `why`); `runner_drained` (`ms`, `held`, `left`), once per close that held a run; and `runner_gauge` every minute (`active`, `slots`, `rss_mib`). The existing `Runner … claimed` and `ready` lines are unchanged. A runner beside a server prints the same lines where the server prints its own.
- A runner on Postgres no longer needs the store's schema to match its own version exactly. The server can migrate first while the earlier release's runners keep running, as long as the migrations are additive. Each store keeps a runner floor: the oldest schema version a runner's build must know. A migration marked `-- runners: breaking` raises the floor to its own version. Every runner reads the floor again every 10 s, whether or not it holds runs. When the floor rises above its version, it claims nothing more, drains, hands its runs back and exits 3. A runner that starts below the floor exits 3 and says to run a runner of the server's release. A runner on a store its server has not migrated yet still exits 3, as before. Runners of earlier releases still need an exact match, so roll this release's runners with its server as before; from this release on, a runner keeps running beside the next releases' additive migrations. <!-- changes/runner-floor.md -->
  - `agentrun-serve store-schema [--data DIR]` prints the store's schema version and runner floor beside this build's version, and what this build's server and runner do on that store, as one line of JSON. It reads only: no lock, no migration. `--build` prints the build's own versions with no store. `GET /v2/capabilities` carries the same live values in `store_schema` (`version`, `runner_floor`, `known`), for a deploy check that refuses a build older than its store.
  - A Postgres migration that drops or renames anything, changes a column's type, makes a column NOT NULL, or adds a NOT NULL column with no default must carry the `-- runners: breaking` header. A test fails one that does not. Migrations up to 0022 predate the rule and count as breaking; 0023, the first the lint reads, is additive. A SQLite runner still opens only its own schema version.
- With Archil on (Mode 2), uploads live on Archil and the server places a run's files in its folder at the run's start, so a runner reads no upload and needs no disk of the server's. `POST` and `PUT /v2/files` keep each file on the server's own uploads disk, `agentrun-<server id>-files` (made by the first upload), at `files/<file_id>/`, and listing, reading and deleting read it there. A run started with `file_ids` has each file copied into its folder at `work/inputs/<path>` before it is queued (2 files at a time across every start on the server, at most 45 s). Its launch records `files_placed` and the disk it used, and its claim copies nothing. A copy that fails refuses the start with `424 upstream_failed` in words, and no run is made. <!-- changes/uploads-on-archil.md -->
  In Mode 2, an uploaded file that no run names is deleted after `AGENTRUN_UPLOAD_RETENTION` (default `7d`, or `off`), swept hourly (`event=uploads_expired`). Mode 1 is unchanged: uploads stay in `DIR/files/`, are copied in at the claim, and are never deleted. Files uploaded under one mode are not seen under the other.
- Connect independently started Codex CLI and Claude Code sessions with `learning connect`, without <!-- changes/existing-cli-learning.md -->
  an SDK wrapper or replacing the source task launcher. Hooks record completed prompt windows and
  reported usage; later prompts receive pinned owner corrections from AgentRun. Source task dialogue
  never becomes a standing correction automatically. Source hooks do not expose a workflow execution
  bridge or launch extra native reflection sessions. Retired automatic notes and skills stay on disk
  but are not served or converted to owner corrections. Existing CLI profiles with a stored
  `learning: "notes"` setting read as enabled under the current learning model; new definitions use
  its boolean or loop settings.

  Connection credentials are scoped, installation preserves unrelated hooks, and disconnect removes
  only its own hooks. Incomplete evidence and cancellations stay explicit. The console offers capture
  and correction delivery enrollment for existing applications while execution and editing stay in
  their original setup. Initial enrollment requires a local AgentRun server and the selected CLI's
  sign-in; metadata observation alone does not enable it.

  Private pending capture journals are bound to their destination and credential generation. A reconnect
  starts a fresh journal; prior or unbound records remain on disk and are not automatically migrated,
  uploaded or deleted. `learning retry` reports `blocked_journals` and exits with status 1 when those
  records need review.

  Disconnect disables local capture before removing hooks or contacting the server. If server revocation is
  pending, loaded hooks and retries stay disabled until disconnect completes; status exposes `capture_enabled`.
  Retries advance across retained sessions, queued hooks and unfinished turns so older entries cannot indefinitely
  hide later uploads. Interrupted connection commands recover an abandoned lock while a live owner keeps it.
  Recovery also recognizes a proven previous kernel boot on the same host. A different namespace from the
  same boot, or an unknown boot identity, stays protected until its owner's death can be established.
  Project installer and shared Codex hook locks now keep private owner records and recover after a proven
  owner death. Legacy empty or malformed installer locks stay protected regardless of age; the error names
  the lock and requires stopping and verifying all relevant installers before manually removing that lock.
- Observe token usage from already-running Codex sessions without restarting their native processes. Polling subscriptions follow loaded interactive, exec and delegated sessions; explicitly selected historical sessions remain available. Input, output and reported cache counters use native model metadata and source UTC dates, with cumulative baselines, atomic local checkpoints and sequence deduplication preventing duplicate accounting. <!-- changes/existing-codex-polling-usage.md -->

  Polling usage requires the receiver’s advertised capability. Existing lifetime totals are not backfilled; missing counters, tail gaps and queue drops remain partial coverage. Conversation content stays local, existing learning consent is unchanged, and OTLP ingestion keeps its existing behavior.
