  Selected failed sessions remain eligible for bounded usage polling, so counters flushed after Codex reports a system error are retained. Acknowledged counters are not counted again after another poll or a connector restart.
- The CLI capture API uses `agentrun cli-learning enroll|list|revoke|start|get|events|complete`. <!-- changes/cli-capture-command-routing.md -->
  Its earlier generated `CLI learning` group was one word internally and did not accept the documented
  invocations. The generated TypeScript resource is `cliLearning` with the same verbs, and Python uses
  `cli_learning`; API paths and operation IDs are unchanged. The local `learning connect`, `status`,
  `disconnect`, `retry` and `hook` commands and the existing learning API commands keep their routes.
- Keep delayed CLI hook retries in source order. An older queued submit or session ending cannot <!-- changes/cli-capture-retry-boundaries.md -->
  interrupt a newer prompt. When earlier dialogue cannot be ordered safely, retain it privately and
  mark the capture incomplete instead of presenting it as prior context.

  Bound newly captured prompts, answers and dialogue to the server's text and event limits, including
  after secret redaction. Truncated evidence remains explicitly incomplete and can be uploaded instead
  of retrying an oversized request indefinitely. Already frozen historical requests remain unchanged
  because an uncertain earlier upload may have committed their immutable payloads.

  Serialize session journals with the existing token-fenced ownership lock. Concurrent recovery of a
  dead owner cannot remove a new owner's lock. Legacy empty or PID-only locks remain pending rather
  than being removed on age alone; remove such a lock only after confirming no hook or retry process
  still owns that journal.

  A pending local disconnect no longer advertises learning as ready while hook removal or remote
  revocation is blocked. The connector withholds its readiness proof until the connection is active.
- Install Codex learning hooks in linked worktrees through the main-checkout `hooks.json` that native <!-- changes/cli-learning-worktree-hooks.md -->
  Codex actually loads. Reconnecting migrates unchanged owned hooks without changing the learning
  connection or credential. Shared-file locking and stable hook group positions preserve other enrolled
  projects and their native trust keys; worktree-local TOML stays untouched. Observation readiness checks
  the derived shared configuration and does not mark ignored local hooks ready. Modified configuration,
  invalid Git ownership and size overflow fail without replacement; interrupted migrations retain both
  ownership records for safe disconnect. Loaded Codex project configuration requires a new or reopened
  session before hooks activate. A nested linked worktree cannot also learn through its enclosing checkout.
- Capture reported token usage for new Codex and Claude Code CLI learning prompts, deduplicating native response records within each prompt. The dashboard's unified `analytics.usage` includes retained source observations and recorded runs, using verified session identity to group potentially overlapping usage. When exact overlap is unavailable, the total keeps the larger coherent source or recorded view as a lower bound, with incomplete coverage explicit. A stale or zero source report cannot erase a larger completed prompt total; distinct immutable CLI turns can sum, while upload dates alone do not prove separate native execution. Range and session filters apply to the combined total; unavailable cache breakdowns, partial boundary days, missing reports and the 90-day source retention limit stay explicit. Unbound observation identities cannot be matched to separately recorded runs. Missing, ambiguous or incomplete prompt usage remains unknown; existing run completions are not rewritten. An enabled CLI learning profile with no recorded prompts explains that its next source prompt starts capture and that earlier conversations are not imported automatically. <!-- changes/cli-prompt-usage-coverage.md -->

  The dashboard and Agents page share one connected-agent inventory. Source sessions and AgentRun agents appear together, including profiles awaiting their first captured prompt, and the separate observed-session sections are removed. Selecting a source session filters its reported usage without treating the session as a completed run or requesting a server-agent run endpoint.

  Ordinary analytics reads project the saved accounting and identity fields instead of transferring full CLI policies and SDK replay records. Historical identity still selects the right source usage across date ranges. PostgreSQL records containing unsupported Unicode escapes retain the earlier JavaScript parsing path for that record, preserving their counters and exact native identity. Unexpected accounting read failures are surfaced by the usage endpoint.
- Show connected coding agents in the same searchable inventory and count as registered agents, with <!-- changes/connected-agent-inventory.md -->
  project, session, model, activity and token details. Preserve loaded cards when another source is
  loading or unavailable, and exclude nonarchivable connections from the archived view.

  Identify coding sessions by their native title, project basename or delegated task name, with a stable
  ID suffix for unnamed sessions. Names refresh even while idle. The observer sends bounded labels only
  to receivers advertising support; prompts, conversation previews, full paths and obvious credentials
  are excluded. Token accounting and selection scopes stay unchanged.
  Unicode labels respect queue and delivery byte limits so long multilingual names cannot stall delivery.
- Give connected coding sessions the same card layout and coding-agent Run/Edit handoffs as other <!-- changes/connected-agent-learning-controls.md -->
  agents, with learning status and setup or settings actions. Project learning connections remain
  available in Learning Dojo but no longer appear as duplicate agents in the active inventory.

  The connector can associate a session with an existing project/runtime learning connection using
  its installed hook receipt and a scoped proof. Learning is shown as on only after that exact session
  has reported a hook window and the server and project settings allow learning. Missing setup,
  unverified activation and unsupported delegated sessions remain explicit. Revoked or invalid proofs
  do not grant access or prevent ordinary activity and token reports. This does not install hooks,
  enroll additional projects, import conversations or change how coding sessions are started.
- Dashboard and agent analytics show exact, comma-separated token totals, input and output counts whenever they fit. Counts adapt to the actual column width and font, using compact notation only when needed. The full number remains available on hover and to screen readers when abbreviated. <!-- changes/console-exact-token-counts.md -->
- The dashboard and agent analytics show Input and Output counts beneath the token total. Input includes cached tokens, including when a connected source reports total and output usage without a cache breakdown. Missing counts display a dash, and genuine zero counts remain zero. The token card no longer shows cache percentages or model-request diagnostics; incomplete coverage and history limits remain visible. <!-- changes/console-token-breakdown.md -->
- Show Mission Control's activity and token-usage charts directly below the main agent and run counts, <!-- changes/mission-analytics-placement.md -->
  before the observed-session summary.
- Keep verified session identity privately beside retained observation usage, independently of current <!-- changes/observation-usage-identity.md -->
  learning readiness. Disconnecting, replacing credentials, or receiving an older client's activity
  no longer counts observed tokens separately from the same session's captured runs. Existing verified
  associations migrate when another observation arrives; the accounting identity grants no learning
  authorization and is removed with the retained session.

  If an earlier disconnect already discarded the verified identity, it cannot be reconstructed. Where
  unidentified observations may overlap recorded native runs, usage compares the complete native view
  with each collector's complete observation view and reports a conservative total with incomplete
  coverage. It does not add possibly overlapping collectors or infer an identity from unverified fields.

  A verified report that tries to assign a different native identity to an already identified observed
  session is refused with `409 connector_session_identity_conflict`. The entire batch remains uncommitted,
  including its usage and receipts; distinct native sessions must use distinct external session IDs.
- Template packages such as Inbound Lead and KYB accept and retain their `learning.agree_on` settings through import, apply and later edits. A learned workflow's promotion check and shadow audit compare the declared answer fields, with each dotted path required in the template's output schema; a missing path disagrees. Without `agree_on`, the existing whole-answer comparison remains. The console and API describe which fields the check compared. <!-- changes/template-learning-compat.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.50 (2026-11-20)

- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) serves four learning reads with its token: an agent's loop, promotions and cost per run, and a run's learning. <!-- changes/api-only-learning-reads.md -->
- Computer time is priced the way providers bill it: by the resources a computer holds, never by a size. An operator copies its provider's per-resource rates from the provider's price sheet into `AGENTRUN_COMPUTE_USD_PER_VCPU_SECOND_<PROVIDER>`, `AGENTRUN_COMPUTE_USD_PER_GIB_SECOND_<PROVIDER>`, `AGENTRUN_COMPUTE_USD_PER_GPU_SECOND_<PROVIDER>_<GPU_TYPE>` and `AGENTRUN_COMPUTE_USD_PER_DISK_GB_MONTH_<PROVIDER>` (a month of 730 hours). A priced computer's time is held on the run's ledger under its `max_cost_usd`, one 5-minute stretch ahead, as browser time is: a claim's computer, made while the run is set up, has its first stretch held as soon as the run's cap can judge, so the run's first request is judged beside it (a cap with no room parks the run there); a computer made later in the run (a lost sandbox's new one) has its first stretch held before its create, and a cap with no room makes nothing and fails the run in the cap's words; a cap with no room for a later stretch pauses the run for a raise; and the time it ran is booked before the run's end is written, so the end's `cost.usd` holds it all. The run's ledger tells a caller whether its cap can judge yet (`RunLedger.judges`), and a paid step asked while the run's spec is built waits for it instead of failing. With no price set nothing changes: the computer runs outside the cap, as a tool call with no price does, and is never refused. A resource set to `0` is booked at $0 and reads $0, never `unpriced`. `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage` gives `compute_time` lines (`runusage/4`), one per provider and resource, with the raw quantity, its unit, its basis and the dollars the run's ledger booked, so `total` stays the run's `cost.usd`; the time no claim held (a computer kept for a follow-up, one deleted after its run, one whose delete failed) is said apart as `unheld_quantity` and is in no cost. Each computer interval gives `disk_gb` and `booked_seconds` (Postgres migration `0023_computer_interval_resources.sql`; a SQLite store gets both columns at the server's open). A computer's figures are its provider's own where its answer gives them: `CreatedComputer.resources` in `@parcha/agentrun-computer`, filled from Daytona's sandbox (vCPUs, memory, disk and GPUs), E2B's `getInfo` and Fly's machine guest (vCPUs and memory), and `Machine.resources` for a hosted provider's read of its machine. <!-- changes/compute-prices.md -->
- The file viewer shows images and plays video and audio from the run's file route, which now serves `.webm`, `.mp3`, `.wav`, `.m4a` and `.ogg` inline with their types. Settings → MCP servers has two fal presets, fal (key) and fal (sign in); fal bills your fal account, and a run's spend cap does not count it. <!-- changes/console-media-viewer-and-fal-preset.md -->
- A template eval case can name `previous: fixtures/previous.json`, the earlier completed results of the package's schedule trigger, each checked against its own `output_schema` (else the package's) when the case is read; the eval writes them in its own server's store as completed runs of the run's agent, each started by a firing of that trigger, then fires the trigger on its clock, so the run is handed its last result whole, as its `x-carried` fields with the first entries dropped and counted, or nothing, said so, exactly as a scheduled run is. What the run was handed is on its report as `handed_previous`, and a new `handed` grader checks it (`expect: whole | carried | too_large | none`, with `dropped` counts for carried arrays). <!-- changes/eval-previous-run.md -->
- A workflow decision Parallel answered on its own API (the `parallel` provider on the server's `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, booked at Parallel's list price, $0.001 a request) now counts as a paid call Parallel charged, beside `web_search` and `web_fetch`: it is in the run's `cost.tools_usd` (`toolsusd/2`), on the `parallel` `tools` line of `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage` (`charged_by` and `provider` `parallel`, one call each, `basis` `estimate`), and on the `tools` meter of `GET /v2/usage`. It used to be on a `tokens` line under its model (`parallel-fast`). It moves; it is not added: `total` is still the run's `cost.usd`, and `cost.usd` does not change. A `parallel` decision sent through OpenRouter (no `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, on the OpenRouter key) is OpenRouter's to charge, at the cost OpenRouter reported, and stays a `tokens` line, as Jev's and other decision models' do. <!-- changes/parallel-decision-tool-lines.md -->

  A Parallel search is now priced by its `mode`, from [Parallel's pricing page](https://docs.parallel.ai/resources/pricing) (read 2026-11-20): `turbo` or `fast` $0.001 a request, `basic` or `advanced` $0.005, each with 10 results included, and $0.001 for each result past them. `web_search` always searches `fast`, so what it books does not change. A search body in a mode with no price here, or naming none, is never sent, as a request to an endpoint with no price is not: it is never booked at $0 or at `fast`'s price.
- SDK runs accept externally executed agents through `sdk: {runtime: "external", platform: "OpenClaw"}`. Use `"Capy"` or another platform label without adding a runtime. The required label is 1–80 Unicode characters with no leading or trailing whitespace, control characters or unpaired UTF-16 surrogates; it is preserved in the console and on each recorded run. Registration and run start must name the same runtime and platform. Other SDK runtimes reject `platform`. See [Report runs from an external platform](../../docs/tutorials/platform-sdk-runs.md). <!-- changes/sdk-runs-openclaw-capy.md -->
  Execution stays on the platform: managed launch, stop, cancel and follow-up requests are refused. External sources receive the owner's corrections when learning is on, with no workflows. Starts carrying `workflow_tools` or `workflow_adapters` are refused (422) before recording a run. `BackendLearningClient`, imported from `@parcha/agentrun-client/learning`, accepts the external binding and refuses a `workflows` bridge before any request. Existing Claude Agent SDK, Codex SDK and eve integrations retain their behavior.
  The generated TypeScript `StartSdkRunBody` is now a union. Consumers that extend it with an interface or index its workflow fields must use a type intersection or select the SDK branch; the [client README](../client/README.md#learning-for-existing-backend-sdk-agents) describes the migration. `BackendLearningStart` remains extensible, and existing Python TypedDict constructors and CLI flags are preserved.
- `web_save {url, path}`, a new host tool, saves one public file (at most 200 MiB) into the run's `work/`, a bare name under `media/`. It downloads through `web_fetch`'s guard, never overwrites, and saves media only when the bytes, the declared type and the extension agree. An agent gets it by naming it. pi-browser adds `publicDownload`, the bytes version of `publicFetch`. A template eval's `web:` fixture takes an optional `save` section. <!-- changes/web-save-tool.md -->
- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) now serves `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage`, a run's usage lines. It answered `404` before, so a backend could read a run and its `cost.usd` but not the lines that make it up. The route reads only that run, takes the server's token, and cuts the host's secrets out of its names as `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}` does. Every other route the profile refused is still refused. <!-- changes/api-only-run-usage.md -->
- A run on an Archil disk that Archil no longer has fails at its claim, before any file call, saying so: the agent's disk is read at Archil at every claim (one GET), as a launch's disk already was, and a disk that is gone, or one in another region than the key's, refuses the run naming the disk, the region and the way out (`DELETE /v2/agents/{id}/archil` drops it, and the agent's next run makes a new one). No new disk is made in its place: the agent's learning and its runs' folders were on it. Before, such a run failed at its first claim with `".agents/skills" is not there`, since every call on the missing disk answered 404 and a 404 read as a folder that was not there. <!-- changes/archil-disk-gone.md -->
  - An Archil run folder makes its folders before it writes: Archil can answer 404 to a put whose folder is not there (it made no parent for an expert run's `.agents/skills/` on a fresh run folder, so every expert run failed at its claim with `".agents/skills" is not there`). A write, an append, a mkdir, the run folder's own put and a synced folder's push now make each missing folder above the key, from the highest down, and put again; a folder already there is left as it is.
  - An Archil workspace keeps Archil's own words in a failure: a missing file or folder is still `NOT_FOUND`, naming the call (list, read, write, append, mkdir, put) and what Archil said after it, and a disk Archil has no record of is `UNAVAILABLE` naming the disk and its region, never a missing folder.
  - A run's folder on its Archil disk that can't be made fails the claim with the reason, where it was a log line; a folder already there is not put again, so a later claim whose kept computer holds it opens at once.
- With `learning.repick: true`, a learned workflow whose answer is written by a composed workflow now re-picks from the pages in that composed workflow, where before it was committed as compiled without a word. A re-pick the rewrite still does not reach (one that is not a single model step, or whose marker names are taken) is kept as compiled, and the server's log says so. <!-- changes/learning-repick-reach.md -->
- `POST /v2/templates/{template}/apply` now answers `revision_version`: the number of the agent's revision the apply wrote, its current one now (`1` for an agent it made; on an update with `agent_id`, the new revision's). This is a public API addition: the TypeScript and Python clients carry the field, and the console says "Updated: rev N" from it with no second read of the agent. A purged run's answer and input no longer stay in the server's in-process caches after its `DELETE` (or its agent's): the purge drops them, and a read under way when the purge lands keeps none of them. A SQLite purge whose WAL checkpoint another connection holds back now leaves the store's scrub marker (`store.sqlite.scrub`), and the next start's scrub truncates the log before it serves, a crash in between included; it no longer retries or logs a warning. A secret rewrite running beside the purge never removes the marker the purge left. When that marker cannot be written (a full disk), the purge has still committed: the `DELETE` answers 500 `internal`, saying so, and the server logs it; the run's cached answer and input are dropped all the same, and the next `DELETE` answers 204. <!-- changes/purge-tidy.md -->

  Upgrade note: a retried apply whose answer was saved before the upgrade replays without `revision_version`; it ages out within a day.

## 0.1.0-beta.49 (2026-11-20)

- `learning.repick: true` (off by default) has a learned workflow's quote re-pick read the pages its run fetched, sent as untrusted data to a step with no tools; `learning.repick_max_chars` (150,000 by default) caps what it sends. It reaches workflows compiled after it is set, and agents on an SDK bridge ignore it. <!-- changes/learning-repick-pages.md -->
- A purged run's or agent's content no longer stays in the SQLite store's file bytes: every store connection writes with `secure_delete` on, so a deleted or overwritten row's bytes are zeroed in its page, and a purge checkpoints the WAL (`TRUNCATE`) once it commits, so neither `store.sqlite` nor its `-wal` keeps an earlier copy. The checkpoint waits a few milliseconds for another connection, never the store's 10 s busy wait, so it holds up no other request. One another connection holds back is retried once, then logged (the next purge's checkpoint or the server's stop clears it), and never fails the `DELETE`. Postgres is not covered: `VACUUM` only makes a purged row's space reusable, so its bytes stay until a later write overwrites them; `VACUUM FULL` rewrites the table; Postgres's WAL, archived WAL and backups keep the old values for their own lifetimes. <!-- changes/purge-secure-delete.md -->
- `DELETE /v2/runs/{run_id}` purges a run that is not live: its launch, journal and timeline, messages, outputs and files, folders, kept answers, its agent's grades of it, its kept learning's content and what its agent's promotion records copied from it (a disagreement's input and answers; each record's decision, numbers and run ids stay) go, with the runs made from it (its audit's shadow run, the replay runs of its input, a learning run that grades it); no replay or shadow run of a purged run is started. Its row stays as a tombstone (id, agent, state, times, cost, purge time): `/usage`, `/stats` and a cap's spend read are unchanged, every route of the run answers `410 purged` with the tombstone in `details`, and no run list shows it. A second `DELETE` is `204`; a live run (queued, working, waiting on a person, or held by a runner) is `409 run_not_final`, nothing purged; a purge stopped part way is finished by the next `DELETE`. A message, a trigger's message or a grade sent to the run while its `DELETE` runs waits for it and is then `410 purged`. `DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}` now purges an archived agent made here the same way (its definition, learning, triggers, sign-ins, computer, disk and folders go, its runs become tombstones, its row is a tombstone answering `410 purged`); one not archived is `409 agent_not_archived`, which replaces `agent_not_external`. An unarchive or a write sent to the agent while its purge runs (its home, its definition, a move of its current revision) is `410 purged` once it ends, as is a definition edit or a template update whose body arrives after it, and a trigger made for a purged agent or moved to it: nothing of a purged agent is written again; after a purge stopped part way, each is `409 agent_not_runnable` until a `DELETE` finishes it. An agent another system owns is deleted whole, as before. Both deletes take the owner's session or the API token: any other console session is `403 forbidden`. The TypeScript client, the Python client and the CLI (`agentrun runs delete`) carry the new operation. <!-- changes/run-delete.md -->
- `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage` (`runusage/1`) says what one run cost, line by line, and whose invoice each part lands on: `tokens` per model (`model`, and `provider` where the server sent the requests itself; null behind a gateway), `tools` per charger (`charged_by`, with calls of unpriced tools in `not_metered_calls`), and `browser_time` per browser provider (`provider`, seconds). Each line has its quantity as measured, its dollars as the run's booking holds them, and its basis (`reported`, `estimate`, `unpriced`). It reads the same for a pi run, a CLI-harness run and a workflow run (its decisions on the model that answered them). The lines join to `total`, the run's `cost.usd`; a charge of unknown cost is null with what is known beside it, never $0. `ended_at` is the end the lines cover: a follow-up can reopen an ended run, and a later read with another `ended_at` says it moved. The console's Dev tools tab shows the lines as "Cost by line". In the kernel, a paid request may say `reported` (it settles at the provider's own figure), written on its `runner.request`. <!-- changes/run-usage-lines.md -->
- `GET /v2/computers`' `folder` field is described by its rule alone, naming no vendor: `bind` a folder of this machine (Mode 1), `archil` the owner's Archil disk where the provider takes an Archil mount, has Archil's image and does not dial this server, `sync` a synced folder the runner keeps for any other computer that takes a folder in Mode 2, null none. The computer package's README no longer says a program of the user can join the window manager's namespace with nsenter: root made it, and the user holds no capability there. A Daytona desktop on exec is refused in the shared refusal's words alone. `runConformance` takes `onScreenshot(png)`, called with screen.screenshot-size's last whole screenshot. <!-- changes/computer-untangle-16.md -->
- In the console, updating an agent from a template (Update <agent>) now says it was updated and names the new revision ("Updated: rev 2"). It used to say the template was applied and "The agent is made", as if the apply had made a new agent. Only an Apply that makes a new agent says "made". <!-- changes/template-update-says-updated.md -->
- A scheduled run handed its previous result's `x-carried` fields is told how many entries each carried array lost from its front, "the first N entries" (the template keeps the array oldest first), no longer "the N oldest": the engine drops from the front and reads no dates. A stored `x-carried` the save would refuse (a repeated, unknown or empty name) is read as none, so its run gets the too-large line. `submitParameters` leaves every `x-` keyword out of submit tool schemas, as it does `criteria`, not only `x-carried`; a property or definition so named keeps its name. <!-- changes/x-carried-first-entries.md -->
- A run's look-back (its own after its job, or the feedback round a grade opens) keeps the run's end, so GET, the list, SSE and the console show it completed or failed with its answer and `ended_at` while its learning reads `reflecting`, it tells `run.ended` once, a stop or cancel that lands mid-round drops only the round, and `PUT /v2/runs/{run_id}/grade` meanwhile is `409 run_learning`, a new error code. <!-- changes/grade-keeps-run-end.md -->
- `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage` gives `browser_sessions` (`runusage/2`): one record per browser session the run opened, with the provider's session id, when the server opened it and let it go, why it ended, the seconds charged for it, and the provider's own record of it (`provider_record`: its start, end and proxy bytes), read once when the session is let go. With it a person running AgentRun sees how long each session ran, spots one that ended late or was lost, and finds each on the provider's own dashboard and invoice by its id. A provider that keeps no record, or a read that fails, says so in `provider_record_status`, with the record null, never zeros. In the computer package, a browser provider may offer `sessionUsage(ref)`, the vendor's record of a session; Browserbase's reads `GET /v1/sessions/{id}`. <!-- changes/run-usage-browser-sessions.md -->
- `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}/usage` gives `computer_intervals` (`runusage/3`): one record per computer the run made through its provider (a sandbox, a desktop or a phone), by when each was made, with the provider's own id for it (`provider_id`), its `kind`, what its create asked for (`gpu`, `cpus`, `memory_mb`; null where it asked none, never a guess), when the create answered (`started_at`), when the provider's delete of it answered ok (`ended_at`), and whether the run's park kept it past its claim (`kept`). With it a person running AgentRun sees how long each of a run's computers lived, finds one left running after its run (`ended_at` null: no delete was proven, never a guessed end), and matches the provider's invoice by its id. The server writes the store's new `computer_intervals` table (Postgres migration `0022_computer_intervals.sql`; a SQLite store gets it at the server's open) at the claim's create, the park, and every delete that answers ok: the claim's release, a later claim letting an earlier one's go, the run's end, a kept computer's end, and the janitor's sweeps. A write that fails is said on the runner's log and never fails the run. The agent's own computer, a paired one and `--faux`'s have no record. Computer time is not priced: it is on no line and not in `total`. A `tools` line now names its `provider` too, the same vendor as `charged_by`; a `tokens` line behind a model gateway keeps `provider` null, since the server does not know the gateway's upstream. <!-- changes/computer-intervals.md -->
- An agent whose `input_schema` fields are all optional takes a run that gives one of them and no `content` (`{"pr_number": 3318}` was refused 422). An input with neither is still refused at `input.content`. <!-- changes/input-content-or-field.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.48 (2026-11-20)

- A harness module builds its harness the way the built-in harnesses are built: `entries(builtins, kit)` now gets a kit with `kit.adapterEntry(facts, adapter)` and `kit.acpEntry({ facts, recipe, proxy })`, so the harness is offered its wire's vendor's models, named on that vendor's and OpenRouter's key rows, and gated and named by its own facts. [HARNESS.md](../../HARNESS.md) is the guide, and `examples/harness-module` is a whole module (Goose under an id of its own). <!-- changes/harness-modules-kit.md -->
  - The built-in harnesses read the same facts as before, with or without a module loaded.
  - An adapter harness that loads skills itself gives `kit.adapterEntry` a `skillCheck`: the run's skills it accepts are taken out of the prompt and handed to its adapter as `launch.skills`.
  - `kit.acpEntry`'s offer promises resume `"restart"` unless given `resume: "load"`, which its recipe must declare (`declares.load`); otherwise its first launch is refused (`HARNESS_RESUME_UNDECLARED`).
  - `missing(env)`, on either builder, says what no model key fixes (a binary, say). It is asked before the key, so the harness's offer says it and names no key. An error it or the adapter throws with a `code` refuses the harness with its facts' install fix for that code, as the built-in Goose's are.
  - `@parcha/agentrun-serve/conformance` adds `suiteHostTools`, and `@parcha/agentrun-harness-acp/testing` exports the fake ACP agent (`FAKE_ACP_AGENT`, `fakeAgentRecipe`), so a module's author runs the conformance suite with no binary, model or key. The run spec a subject hands `createAdapterLoop` names its harness's `facts`.
- A schedule trigger's next run keeps what its last answer carried when that answer is over 32 KiB. An agent's `output_schema` may name, in `x-carried`, the top-level fields its next run reads back (a watch's `seen`, a digest's `open_urgent`). When the last completed result is over the limit, the next run is handed those fields alone, read from the schema of the run that produced it (its revision's, not the agent's current one), with words naming them and the whole result's size. A carried array is kept oldest first by convention; the template owns that order and the engine reads no dates. When the carried fields are themselves over the limit (UTF-8 bytes), the largest carried array gives up its oldest entry, one at a time and measured again after each (a tie goes to the first in `x-carried`), until they fit, and the words say per field how many were dropped (`seen: 12 oldest entries dropped`). A scalar or object is never cut. With no `x-carried`, or carried fields still over the limit with no entry left to drop, the run is told the result was too large, as before; under the limit it is handed whole, as before. <!-- changes/x-carried-previous-result.md -->
  A save refuses an `x-carried` that is not an array of unique names of the schema's root `properties` (`422 input_invalid`, field `definition.output_schema.x-carried`). `submitParameters` leaves `x-carried` out of a submit tool's schema, as it does `criteria`, so a learned workflow that copies the agent's output schema never sends a provider a keyword it does not know.
- Keep compiled workflow drafts out of connected agents' reusable workflow lists until a shadow check compares them with an independent native answer. Claude Agent SDK, Codex SDK and Eve use the same reserved candidate, caller-side execution and server promotion decision; native and remote runner tools also withhold unchecked drafts. <!-- changes/connected-workflow-shadow-checks.md -->

  The first check uses one fresh native turn and reports that sample count. It compares the full answer exactly, or the owner's configured agreement fields. A mismatch, missing evidence, expired check, ambiguous input or failed execution never promotes a draft. Original native results remain unchanged. Shadow writes use only that turn's matching recorded results; an unrecorded write stops the check. Reads also use recorded results by default; `shadowReadFallback` explicitly opts into missing read-only observations under the host's existing policy, never retries failed calls. Complex input mappings can supply `resolveCheckInput`; the default does not guess fields from prose.

  Write-bearing checks require complete serial native tool lifecycles and a serial candidate preserving every original call once and in order, including reads. Unknown tools, overlapping calls, buffered Codex write traces and parallel write candidates remain unpromoted. Read-only turns retain recorded-read reuse and reordering. Raw callback results preserve their values and types; only SDK-confirmed MCP envelopes are decoded, and ambiguous or error responses stay held. Asynchronous schema validators are rejected before invocation.

  Eve now uses the shared durable delivery client and an in-process workflow binding. Old pending delivery failures remain recorded without blocking new native turns. Context says compiled workflows and leaves selection to the agent; it no longer claims owner approval or instructs the model to prefer a workflow. The unused Eve mount threshold options are removed; existing server agent learning settings remain authoritative.

  Agent Learning and Learning Dojo now show when the selected learning model lacks server access, name the model, and link to API Keys. Readiness checks the actual learning route rather than accepting any saved key or an unrelated default model. Native connections keep their own sign-in. SDK background compilation requires server-owned model access; a per-request gateway key alone is insufficient. The read-only readiness fields make no paid request and do not verify quota.
- An ended run whose end could not read its booking now heals by the end's own rule: a booking that holds a charge at its hold heals as an upper bound (`cost.upper_bound: true`), so `GET /v2/usage` and `GET /v2/runs/{id}` read the same figure, and the store writes it only over an unknown cost with no bound. The start sweep no longer rereads runs that can never heal (a native run, a person's stop of an agentic run, a run with no booked answer), so the `cost_heal` line's `read` counts only runs that could. SQLite and Postgres alike; no schema change. <!-- changes/cost-heal-reads-only-healable.md -->
- `agentrun-serve check-harness` cuts the recipe's keys and the server's secrets from its report and its output, so an agent that prints its key on stderr as it fails leaves it in neither. <!-- changes/harness-check-redacts-keys.md -->
- Only a built-in harness owns a key. A harness module's entry that names a run secret in `ownKeys` no longer withholds it from other harnesses' runs; Cursor's `CURSOR_API_KEY` still goes to Cursor's runs alone. <!-- changes/module-own-keys.md -->
  - A built-in's own key goes to the built-in that owns it and to no other harness, built in or not. A harness module whose entry names one in `ownKeys` (`CURSOR_API_KEY`) refuses the server's start with `HARNESS_KEY_OWNED`, naming the module, the id and the key.
  - A module's ACP recipe (`kit.acpEntry`) that names a key this server holds in its `keys` (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, any `AGENTRUN_*` or `AGENT_MODEL_*` setting) is refused with `RECIPE_KEY_NOT_OWN` when its run would launch, so the harness's offer says so and no run of it starts. A recipe names only keys saved for its own harness.
- The console's API playground rules the Request pane and the Code/Response pane at the same heights: the line under <!-- changes/playground-pane-lines.md -->
  their headers and the line above their footers (Send request, the code's note, Open this run) run straight across the
  divider instead of stepping at it. The footer's "Sends a real request to this server." note wraps beside the buttons
  instead of pushing them onto a second row.
- A run's views no longer show a `Bearer` token or the value of a URL parameter named like a credential (`?api_key=`, `&access_token=`, `&client_secret=`, a signed URL's `sig=` or `X-Amz-Signature=`) when the server holds neither value. Both are new secret shapes, cut to `[redacted]` wherever a run's text is served: its Timeline, its trace (`GET /v2/runs/{id}/trace`) and the Dev tools tab, its answer and its error. The scheme and the parameter's name stay, so `Authorization: Bearer [redacted]` and `?api_key=[redacted]` still say what was sent. Learning refuses a draft that holds either, as it does every other secret shape. <!-- changes/redact-bearer-token-and-url-credential.md -->
  A token is twenty characters or more with a digit among them, and a parameter's value sixteen or more, so a placeholder (`Bearer <token>`, `Bearer $TOKEN`), a challenge (`Bearer realm="x"`) and a parameter that only resembles a credential's name (`page_token`, `sort_key`) are left as written.
- A connected agent's shadow check now reserves a native turn only when the draft takes its input: a JSON task must pass the draft's input schema, and a start whose task or instructions held a protected value reserves nothing. A turn that cannot be the check's baseline (cancelled or failed, a learned workflow in it, redacted evidence, no shadow report, or a shadow that failed or stopped at an unrecorded write) gives its reservation back instead of holding the draft, and the next turn the draft takes is checked. The fifth given-back turn stops the check with nothing checked, which asks no recompile. A start that could not be admitted gives its turn back uncounted. <!-- changes/sdk-check-release-and-deadline.md -->

  A turn the backend never completed within the hour is decided like any other check, as one failed input: its hold asks the one recompile, and a recompile's check that ends the same way stops instead of compiling again. A draft still waiting for a turn when a newer revision lands is set aside, and the newer revision is checked.

  Promotion records of connected checks say `via: "sdk"`, and their check records count `released` turns and the shadow's `fresh_reads` (live read-only calls it made where the recording had none, which the client now reports). A failure to settle a check no longer skips the run's own end or its learning.
- The code-review template no longer asks for GitHub's `get_repository_tree`. That tool is in the GitHub MCP server's `git` toolset, which its hosted server leaves off by default, so applying the template with its suggested tools ticked was refused with "The MCP server github has no tool get_repository_tree". The review reads the repository from its checkout, or through `get_file_contents`, which lists a directory. <!-- changes/code-review-no-repository-tree.md -->
- When a codemode script stops at a call that waited for a person's answer, its answer now gives every call's value whole. Before, each value was cut at 2,000 characters. In QA, an approved Hacker News item of about 9 KB reached the model without its title. The whole answer is still held to the host's bound on every tool answer. <!-- changes/codemode-stopped-whole-values.md -->
- Console: the "Set up GitHub App access" link under a template's missing tool, and "Browse history" on Start here, are underlined all the time, not only on hover. In light mode the link's orange and the warning box's amber are nearly the same colour, so the link read as plain text. <!-- changes/inline-link-underline.md -->
- Applying a template that grants `issue_write` on a GitHub App whose installation has only Issues: read now warns that GitHub refuses it on a private repository, and says a public repository takes it anyway. The warning said GitHub always refuses it, but on a public repository anyone who can read it may open an issue, App tokens included, so release-notes opened its draft issue there. <!-- changes/issue-write-warning-public-repos.md -->
- After an agent is created in the API playground, "Open agent" sits beside the response status, above the definition, instead of below it. A long definition no longer pushes the link out of view. <!-- changes/playground-open-agent-top.md -->
- The console's Tools step lays out an MCP server's tools and the monid row across the whole width, in the same columns <!-- changes/tools-step-mcp-full-row.md -->
  as the built-in tools. They took two columns before, so on a wide window a server's tools sat in two middle columns
  with empty space on both sides.
- A run's trace (`GET /v2/runs/{id}/trace`, `agentrun runs trace`) no longer shows a model request's or a decision's cost with floating-point noise: a request that cost $0.001893 reads `0.001893`, not `0.0018930000000000002`. A tool call's charges already read so. The amount is unchanged, and the Dev tools tab, which rounds for display, shows what it did. <!-- changes/trace-span-cost-no-float-noise.md -->
- GET /v2/computers says, on each provider's row, the run's folder a computer of it holds on this server now: `folder` is `bind` (Mode 1's folder of this machine), `archil` (the owner's Archil disk mounted), `sync` (a synced folder the runner keeps on the disk) or null (none). It is read by the rule a run's claim picks the folder by, in this server's mode and with the provider's keys and image as this server has them, so a caller no longer guesses from DAYTONA_ARCHIL_EGRESS. The API-only profile serves it too. <!-- changes/computers-folder-kind.md -->
- An operator's backend can show a run's live view and let its user take over: on an API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`), `GET /runs/{id}/computer`, `POST /runs/{id}/computer/take-over` and `POST /runs/{id}/computer/hand-back` take the server's token, and `POST /runs/{id}/computer/viewer` mints a 5-minute link on `AGENTRUN_PUBLIC_URL` that opens that run's live page and socket for the backend's user, until the run ends. <!-- changes/operator-live-view.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.47 (2026-11-19)

**Breaking:**

- Daytona no longer offers a desktop on any connect (none ever started: its sandboxes block the tool user's namespaces); `{ kind: "desktop", provider: "daytona" }` is refused with the reason. A descriptor may name the setting kinds it doesn't serve and why (`unserved`). <!-- changes/computer-daytona-no-desktop.md -->
- Upgrading from 0.1.0-beta.46 or earlier: a run-list row that server cached is not rebuilt for the new `path` and `workflow` fields, so `GET /v2/runs` and `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/runs` can show such a run without them until the run changes. `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}` has both. <!-- changes/run-list-rows-not-rebuilt.md -->

**Changes:**

- `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}` carries `run_blockers` (this server's own property of the contract's Agent, marked `x-agentrun-serve: "runblockers/1"` in the OpenAPI document, and in the generated client types): what the run's own check would refuse now (`409 agent_not_runnable`), as `{message, fields}`, or null when a run would start. The console's agent page shows each blocker as a warning before Run ("A run of this agent is refused until this is fixed: …"), so an agent that can't run (an agent imported with empty instructions or a model no key here reaches, a harness this server doesn't run, a key a granted tool needs) says why on its page, not only after Run. Native and SDK agents, archived agents, and a revision whose MCP tools its first run would pin read null. The read asks no other service: under the agent's spend cap, an OpenRouter decision model's missing price is named once a save or a start has read OpenRouter's catalog, and a catalog that could not be read is named by the start alone. <!-- changes/agent-page-run-blockers.md -->
- A Composio preset server saved with `user_id: "per_run"` keeps no account. Each run names one in `mcp_auth.<server>` as `{composio_user_id, connected_account_id?}`, sealed in the run's launch and erased at its end; a binding to the preset's default user `agentrun` is refused `422`. A run that names none has its calls refused unsent. Such a server makes no Composio trigger. <!-- changes/composio-per-run.md -->
- `PUT /settings/mcp-servers/{name}/composio` takes `price_usd` and `auth_config_id`. `price_usd` prices every granted action at that amount a call, held under the run's cap and booked in `cost.usd` as any priced MCP tool; a re-save that names none keeps the prices. `auth_config_id` (`ac_…`) makes the server and its connect link against an auth config you already have, read first and never deleted; its triggers run as an account under that config. A server saved before this keeps the managed config's link. <!-- changes/composio-save-options.md -->
- A smol cloud provider: `providerFor("smolcloud", { apiKey })` makes each computer a smol cloud machine, a microVM booted from an OCI image (by default the box image, which its `prepareImage()` answers), as a sandbox. It is a `MachineHost` on the shared adapter: `src/smolcloud.ts` calls smol cloud's REST API with `fetch`, and the daemon runs as a child of a resumable interactive exec, its output read by offset and its stdin sent as numbered frames. The daemon is uploaded through the files API. Network none, open and a list are init's. Its lifetime is the janitor's, by the deadline label; the idle stop is off and smol cloud's delete timer ends every machine at the adapter's backstop. Machines are named `agr-<computer name>` and placed on amd64 nodes. No mount and no desktop yet: smol cloud binds each machine's storage disk at `/workspace`, so the run's folder is not a synced folder there. Settings takes `SMOLCLOUD_API_KEY`. `AGENTRUN_COMPUTER_LIVE_SMOLCLOUD=1 COMPUTER_SMOLCLOUD_API_KEY=... npm run conformance -w @parcha/agentrun-computer -- --provider smolcloud` runs the conformance kit on real smol cloud, and `sweep.js --provider smolcloud` checks it left nothing behind. The shared REST client takes a raw body (`bytes`) for an upload. <!-- changes/computer-smolcloud-provider.md -->
- `GET /v2/computers` lists each kind's `settings`: the fields an agent's computer of that kind may set beside its kind and provider. The console's Computer step reads what a kind takes from it. <!-- changes/computers-kind-settings.md -->
- A model gateway can be saved in the console: Settings → Model keys → **Use a model gateway** takes the address of a LiteLLM or other OpenAI-compatible proxy you already run, its key (optional), how it takes model ids, and the default model of each tier, and **Test** lists the models the gateway serves to pick from. It takes effect at once, with no restart, and removing it puts the provider keys back in force. <!-- changes/console-model-gateway.md -->
  - The API: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /v2/settings/model-gateway`, and `POST /v2/settings/model-gateway/test`. Saving, removing and testing take the owner's signed-in session; the API token gets 403, with `details.console_url` linking to Settings → Model keys.
  - The address follows the rule `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL` does (https, or http on this machine; no user, query, fragment or dot segment), and the test follows no redirect.
  - The key is sealed under the seal key, never shown again, kept off every run's tool environment, and goes only to the origin it was saved for: it is sealed with that origin, a new origin asks for the key again, and a key read beside an address of another origin (a change caught between its two writes) is not sent. The test leaves out a model id that holds the key, and `api_key: null` tests with no key.
  - `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL` set where AgentRun starts still wins, whole: the saved gateway is not used, and its save and removal answer 409 `key_set_by_server`. `AGENT_MODEL`, `AGENT_MODEL_FAST`, `AGENT_MODEL_STRONG` and `AGENT_MODEL_GATEWAY_IDS` set there win over the saved fields; an `AGENT_MODEL_API_KEY` set without a base URL is never sent to the saved gateway.
  - The clients and the CLI treat the save and the test as secret writes: the CLI takes their body from stdin or a file only, and the SDKs cut the body's key from what they show.
- A finished run's Screen tab plays its screen recording where the live view was: a muted video with controls, sized as the desktop or the phone was, read from the run files route inline so it seeks by byte range. A run with several recordings has a picker beside Export. A run still going keeps its live view and its Recording chip. <!-- changes/console-run-recording-player.md -->
- Cursor runs as a harness (`cursor`), over ACP, on its owner's own Cursor API key: install its pinned release with `agentrun harness install cursor` (or `agentrun-serve install-harness cursor`), set `CURSOR_API_KEY` where AgentRun starts, and restart. Each run is billed to your Cursor plan, under Cursor's terms, with no spend cap of AgentRun's: it stops after 20 turns or 100 tool calls (`AGENTRUN_CURSOR_MAX_TURNS`, `AGENTRUN_CURSOR_MAX_TOOL_CALLS`), and capabilities show its card (`harnesses[].card`). <!-- changes/cursor-harness.md -->
  - Cursor makes no file edits: every Write is denied in its CLI config until Cursor asks before an edit, as it asks before a shell command or a tool. Its own shell commands, and any other call of its own, are asked first, of a person who can approve them, and refused where no one can (they run on AgentRun's host, never on the run's computer, so bash's setting is not theirs); AgentRun's tools over MCP go through the agent's tool settings.
  - `CURSOR_API_KEY` is handed to Cursor's runs alone, read by name at each start. The credential Cursor derives from it (`auth.json`, which would hold its tokens and the key itself) is never written: its path is a folder Cursor cannot write a file at, and Cursor runs on the key in its environment, so a killed run or server leaves no credential on disk. Cursor's warning that it could not save one is left out of a failed run's words (a recipe's `quiet`). Its whole private HOME is deleted when its process ends.
  - A model is `cursor/<model-id>` (`cursor/gpt-5.4-nano`; `cursor/default` for Cursor's own default), checked against the models Cursor lists for the key (`ACP_MODEL_UNLISTED`). A key whose Cursor team administrator turned headless CLI use off is refused as `CURSOR_HEADLESS_DISABLED`.
  - The release is pinned by its archive's sha256, its launcher's, and a digest of every file it unpacks to; a drift in any of them refuses the run (`ACP_BINARY_MISMATCH`). The archive installer takes tar.gz as well as tar.bz2 (`ARCHIVE_FORMATS`), and so does a harness recipe's loader. A recipe may not take any id the server's harness table already has, `cursor` and `goose` included.
  - Cursor's release is pinned for linux-x86_64 alone. On any other host, a Mac included, Cursor is refused `ACP_BINARY_UNPINNED` before any install is looked at. `cursorRelease(platform)` gives the release pinned for a platform, or none.
  - A new Cursor pin needs a key walk on it first. The walk runs a turn, a hard kill mid-turn and the close on the real binary. At each point it counts the files of the session folder that hold the key or a JWT-shaped token, and it never prints them. CI refuses a pin that the walk's record does not name, so a release that starts saving its key somewhere else fails before it ships.
- `dial-conformance.mjs` gives a desktop run the computerd-fixture binary, which the server's image now builds into `packages/computer/dist/computerd-fixture-linux-amd64`; without it a desktop's screen and input cases skipped and Core could not pass. <!-- changes/dial-conformance-fixture.md -->
- An agent's description can be edited. `PUT /v2/agents/{agent_id}/definition` with a new `definition.description` makes the next revision and changes the description in the same commit, so an edit refused by its check or by a stale `If-Match` (`412`) changes neither; an edit that leaves the description out keeps it, and the same description sent again writes nothing. It was refused `422` before, so an agent the setup import made kept its project folder's path as its description for good. The name and id stay fixed: a changed name is still `422 input_invalid` on `definition.name`. In the console, Edit agent's Description field (and the request editor's) is editable and sent with the save. <!-- changes/editable-agent-description.md -->
- An ended run whose end stored its cost unknown, because its read of the run's booking failed or ran past its bound, no longer reads `cost.usd: null` on `GET /v2/runs/{id}` (and the runs list's `RunSummary`) while that booking is priced. The run read reads the booking itself, as it already does for an ended run's figures since v0.1.0-beta.39, so the next read gives the booked total, with `all_in_usd` beside it. A charge of no known cost still reads `usd: null` with `unpriced` and `so_far_usd`, as before. When the booking has no request to read either, the run's `Cost` says why in a new field, `unknown: "booking_unread"` (costunknown/1), never a bare null: a reader that bills holds the run, as on any null. The console says "Unknown · cost not read" for it. <!-- changes/ended-run-cost-reads-booking.md -->

  The store heals too. When a run read finds such a run's stored cost unknown and its booking priced, it writes the booked figure back in one conditional write, so `/stats`, `/usage`, the runs list and the learning cost and bill (`unknown_cost_runs`, `unattributed_usd`) read it as well. Only an unknown becomes a figure: a stored figure is never written over, and a run reopened or ended again since keeps what its end wrote. At start the server sweeps the store for ended runs whose stored cost is still unknown, a page at a time and in the background, so a run nobody reads again heals too, and when it read any it logs one `cost_heal` line counting the runs it read, healed and failed to read, with no ids; a run whose read fails is passed, and its next read heals it. A run whose booking cannot be read keeps its unknown cost there, counted unpriced as before. SQLite and Postgres alike; no schema change.
- Connect an existing eve 1.0.0 agent through an additive extension, preserving its model, tools, <!-- changes/eve-learning-extension.md -->
  permissions and durable execution. AgentRun records the actual eve runtime, compiles workflows from
  complete task evidence, and supplies owner corrections and served workflows to subsequent turns. Stable turn
  keys and bounded event replay handle eve's buffered step writes without duplicate records on retry. Learning Off supplies no
  learning to a new turn. The extension is held from publication while its integration is reviewed.

  Optionally reuse checked workflows over the existing application's explicitly approved read-only
  callbacks through a private local MCP bridge. Admission remains bound to the current turn and
  pinned revision, with one workflow invocation per turn and Learning Off checked before dispatch.
  Mutating tools and model/judgment callbacks are not supported in this initial eve workflow mode.
  The cookbook includes a fresh-session workflow reuse and Learning Off comparison.
  Workflow context names the original native callbacks found by inspecting each pinned workflow,
  so the agent can compare it with its existing task and standing tool policy.
  Keep host-configured delegation guidance separate from learned reference data. Matching workflows
  are preferred only within the original policy; explicit direct-tool requirements take precedence.
  SDK compilation describes when a workflow matches the task and what its input fields mean, without
  adding a manual-invocation requirement. The existing agent can select it for an ordinary request;
  execution still requires its explicit MCP tool call and the original permissions. This applies to
  new drafts, revisions and compiler retries, not a rewrite of already-committed learning.

  Show the actual harness mark beside connected agents and observed sessions, including eve,
  Claude Code and Codex. Workflow agents keep a distinct workflow icon.

  Keep the workflow schema discoverable by production dependency tracers when embedding the interpreter in an eve application.

  Package the extension with its runtime asset requirements and include it in release archive verification.
  An existing eve application can install the candidate archives and add one extension mount without
  workspace links or changes to its model, tools or build options. Document corrections onboarding and
  the additional explicit read-only bindings required for executable workflows.
  Enabling learning on an Off eve agent preserves the server's current learning model. Without
  workflow bindings, turns receive the owner's corrections; automatic workflow compilation requires
  explicit bindings. Preserve an already-enabled learning configuration when another client saves it
  before the switch's update.

  Support configurable full-learning settings for Eve registration and workflow execution, and preserve
  an already-enabled loop configuration when the console refreshes before saving. The fresh-agent
  cookbook opts into a five-run compilation threshold without changing acceptance thresholds.
  Resuming the owner-correction example stops before changing learning if the owner has edited
  the saved setting; it does not overwrite a custom schedule with its On or Off control.

  Scope bounded native evidence to the recorded turn boundary, so an invalid or oversized buffer
  does not disable future turns. Skip unverifiable learning without inventing a completion, and
  resolve workflow input schema references before advertising them in the native context.

  Label tool credentials as API Keys in console settings and retain all repository and third-party
  attributions in the package archives.
  Browser archive verification recognizes both required vendor provenance manifests and continues
  to reject unlisted files.
- Bring your own harness, door 1: a recipe. A JSON file names an ACP agent's registry release (the archive's URL and sha256, the binary inside it), its model billing (through AgentRun's model proxy, or the owner's plan with turn and tool-call limits), its literal env, files and session folders in the private HOME, and what it declares. `agentrun harness install --recipe FILE` installs the release, and `agentrun harness-check --recipe FILE --model PROVIDER/MODEL` runs it for real: the agent's own tools off, its environment an allowlist, the cap or plan limits, the pinned binary at every start, no side request (stage 2); a SIGKILL then resume, a denied call, one of AgentRun's tools over MCP, a second runner (stage 3). It writes a JSON report and prints the three facts a harness row carries: `resume`, `tool_gate`, `billing`. See [docs/harness-recipe.md](https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun/blob/v0.1.0-beta.47/docs/harness-recipe.md) and [HARNESS-SCORECARD.md](https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun/blob/main/HARNESS-SCORECARD.md), which rates 25 agents. <!-- changes/harness-recipe-door-one.md -->

  The loader refuses a recipe that breaks one of five rules by its code: a key that is not the harness's own (`RECIPE_KEY_NOT_OWN`), a binary not pinned to a registry archive (`RECIPE_BINARY_UNPINNED`), a file or folder outside the private HOME (`RECIPE_PATH_OUTSIDE`), an install step of its own (`RECIPE_INSTALLS_ITSELF`), an environment beyond the allowlist (`RECIPE_ENV_NOT_ALLOWLIST`). A release whose registry entry lists no binary digest is pinned to the first one its owner's install records; a later binary that differs is refused, at an install and a check alike (`HARNESS_BINARY_MISMATCH`). A recipe's keys reach the agent the way a run's do, read by name at its start: `harness-check` on a host without one is refused before the agent starts (`ACP_KEY_MISSING`). The ACP adapter logs each permission the agent asks for (`acp: the agent asked permission`).
- A learned workflow's check and its shadow audit compare two answers by their decision when the definition names no `learning.agree_on`: the replay run, or the shadow, asks the agent's fast model (`model_tiers.fast`, else AGENT_MODEL_FAST) once at its end whether its answer and the other one reach the same decision, and its reply `{"same": boolean, "differs_on": string | null}` decides that pair. Answers equal as JSON still agree with no call, and an `agree_on` revision asks no model. The request runs through the run's own session under its cap and is booked as its spend, so it counts as the check's cost (`check_usd`) or the served run's learning cost. A reply that is not the verdict, a request that failed twice, one cut by its 60 s deadline, or a cap refusal counts as a disagreement and says why. A person's stop or cancel of the run cuts the request at once. A verdict holds only for the two answers it read: if the agent's run answers again after its replay was compared, that input counts as a disagreement ("the comparison read an earlier answer"). The check record keeps `grader` (the model) and each disagreement's `differs_on`. A hold says "its answers reached a different decision from the agent's on k of n (for example: …)", and the console's check line says "compared by the fast model". With no fast model the whole answer is compared as before, and the hold words say a learning agent with no `agree_on` wants one. <!-- changes/learning-grader-compare.md -->
- A run (GET /v2/runs/{id}) and each row of a runs list carry one `path` and a `workflow: { name, digest }` (the learned workflow that served it, null on any other run) in place of `served` and `handed_back`; the cost read's `bill` drops `baseline` and `promoted` (`summary.before` and `summary.takeover` say the same). Upgrading: read `path` and `workflow` where you read `served`/`handed_back`, and `summary.takeover`/`summary.before` where you read `bill.promoted`/`bill.baseline`. <!-- changes/learning-simplify-1119.md -->
- The server remembers its public address (`AGENTRUN_PUBLIC_URL`) in its data directory once a start serves, and warns when a start changes it. A start that fails remembers nothing. The warning is one log line, `event=public_url_changed from=<old> to=<new>`. It says that the owner signs in again at the new address and that links in earlier webhook messages point to the old one. Before, the change signed the owner out with no word. <!-- changes/public-address-moved.md -->
  When the old name still reaches the server, a browser that opens the console there is redirected (308, `no-store`) to the new address, keeping the link's `#/runs/<id>`. On a loopback listener the rest stays refused, as before. The API and webhooks get a 403 `forbidden` that now names the new address, and another browser page gets a page that links to it. The redirect and the page apply only when the server has a public address now. Every other name is refused as before, and its Host is never repeated.
- A served run's `workflow.repick` (`found`, `missed`, null) says whether its answer re-picked after a quote miss; its run page shows it. <!-- changes/repick-label.md -->
- `GET /v2/runs/{run_id}` gains `cost.tools_usd`: the part of `cost.usd` its paid tool calls cost (monid, priced MCP tools, Parallel, browser time), never added to it. A paid call in a learning turn is in `learning_usd` instead. Null while a charge is unknown, while the run is at work, for a learning run a follow-up opened again, and for an imported, native or SDK run. <!-- changes/run-cost-tools-usd.md -->
- A run's cost (`GET /runs/{id}` and each `GET /runs` row) carries its model requests' `tokens` (`input`, `output`, `cache_read`, `cache_write`, `requests`, `unmetered`), and its `basis` says how the figure was reached instead of always reading `estimate`: `reported` when every priced request had the provider's or gateway's own figure (LiteLLM's `x-litellm-response-cost`, OpenRouter's usage `cost`), `estimate` when any was priced from a price table, `unpriced` when no request was priced. A run through a model gateway (`AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL`) now shows its tokens, not only an estimated cost. <!-- changes/run-tokens-cost-basis.md -->
  `GET /stats` (`cost.basis`) and `GET /usage` (`basis`) say the same words over the runs they sum. A run that ended before this change counts as `estimate` when it cost anything, and so does an imported session read at the model catalog's estimate; an imported session with neither a recorded cost nor an estimate reads `unpriced`. The console shows the tokens beside a run's cost and marks a reported figure `reported`, as it marks an estimate `est.`.
  A native or SDK run's cost (its harness's own figure for its whole task) reads `estimate`, with that task's tokens and no request count. A client that treated `basis` as always `estimate` (or `charge`) must accept `reported` and `unpriced`. A run with no model request now reads `basis: "unpriced"` (it read `estimate`).
- A secret write refused to the API token now says where to finish it. The refusal is the same `403 forbidden`; its message ends "Finish it in the console: <link>", and `error.details.console_url` is that link: the console page for the operation (Settings → MCP servers, Model keys, GitHub, Email, Computers, Workspace, Webhook, a trigger's page, an agent's page). For an MCP server's save or sign-in, the link opens the add form (or a saved server's Change form, `?change=<name>`) filled with the server's name, its URL, the kind of credential (`none` for a save that sends no auth) and its toolkit, so the person pastes only the secret and saves; a Composio save opens the Composio form with its toolkit and actions, and one over a saved server's name saves under that name (`?change=<name>&preset=composio`). A save of a kind of credential the form can't fill (`per_run`) links to the page alone. The link never holds a token, a header, a client secret or a key. A URL with a user or password, a query parameter named like a credential, a key-shaped path segment or value, a key that spans path segments or a query's `+`, or a host label that could be an id (20 or more letters and digits with a digit, or a UUID) is left out of the link. The calendar and Claude Code login routes have no console page yet, and their refusal has no link. The setup skills now say that the person saves secrets in the console, and that an assistant opens this link for them instead of asking for the secret in chat. <!-- changes/secret-refusal-console-link.md -->
  Clients that compared the refusal's message to the exact sentence should check that it starts with that sentence: "Saving, replacing or removing a secret takes the owner's signed-in session in the console; the API token can't write secrets."
- A run a learned workflow answered alone says so where runs are read: `GET /v2/runs/{id}` and every row of `GET /v2/runs` carry `served: { workflow, digest }`, and a run the workflow ran first and handed back carries `handed_back: { workflow, digest }`, both read off the run's record as `GET /v2/agents/{id}/learning/cost` reads its `path`. A run by the agent, a check's replay run and an audit's shadow carry neither. The console's runs list reads "Learned workflow" in the Kind column for a served run, and its run page header reads "Learned workflow <name> · rev N"; a handed-back run reads "agentic · handed back by <name>". <!-- changes/served-run-label.md -->
  In this release `served` and `handed_back` became `path` and `workflow` (the bullet on them above), and a run-list row an earlier server cached is not rebuilt for them until the run changes (Breaking, above).
- The first visit needs nothing looked up: `--open` (on by default in `npx @parcha/agentrun`) opens the setup page while the server has no owner, with the setup code already filled in when setup takes one, and Settings → Webhook copies its signing secret with one press. Before, the browser opened the console's front page and the person had to find the code in the server's log, and the webhook secret shown once had to be selected by hand. <!-- changes/setup-opens-filled-in.md -->
  - The opener gets the same link the log prints (`Set up this server: <address>/setup#code=<code>`), or `<address>/setup` on loopback, where setup takes no code. The code works once and lasts 30 minutes, so the opener's arguments and the browser's history hold nothing that outlasts the setup; the API token still never goes to the opener. Once the owner is set, `--open` opens the console's address as before.
  - The setup skill (`docs/SKILL.md`) has the assistant open that link in the person's browser itself, with `open`, `xdg-open` or `start` on their computer or with its client's browser tool, instead of handing over a link to click or a command that prints the code. It sends the link only when it can open no browser. For a server the installer or `agentrun service` started, it gets the link from `agentrun open`.
  - The installer (`curl -fsSL https://agentrun.ai/install | sh`) and `agentrun service install|start|restart` end the same way: until the owner's password is set, they open the setup page with the code filled in, and print that link for when no browser opens. `agentrun open` does it at any time, and opens the console once there is an owner; with no server answering (a record a crash left behind included) it says so and exits 1 (`--setup-only` opens nothing then). It reads the code from the service's log (for the server in that service's data folder only; another `--data` opens without a code and says where that server's log is) and asks the server for a new one (`POST /v2/setup/code`) when the last has run out. The opener is started and left running, so a browser that stays open never holds the command; on the tailnet (`--tailscale`) the page opens once `tailscale serve` is on, since the link names that address. The setup page's hint names `agentrun open`, `agentrun service logs` and `journalctl --user -u <unit>`.
  - **Copy secret** beside the secret in Settings → Webhook says Copied, or, where the browser won't copy, to select the text. The console's copy button is now the `CopyButton` primitive, shared with the webhook trigger's Copy URL and Copy secret.
- The server posts run notices to Slack itself: paste a Slack incoming-webhook URL under Settings → Slack (or `PUT /v2/settings/slack` with `{url}` from the owner's signed-in session), and each run's end (`run.ended`), each wait on a person (`run.needs_input`) and each trigger that could not start its run (`trigger.failed`) is posted as a readable message: the agent's name, the status in a word, the run's title and a link to the run, what a waiting run waits on, or the trigger's name and error. No relay is needed. A message never carries a run's input, its output or a tool's arguments. <!-- changes/slack-destination.md -->
  - The URL is the credential, so saving it is a secret write (the API token is refused `403`, with `details.console_url` opening Settings → Slack); it is sealed, never shown again but for its last four characters, kept out of the log and the deliveries, and cut from what a run shows.
  - Every string of a message (an agent's or a trigger's name, a run's title, an error) is cut of the server's secrets before it is saved or posted.
  - With the outbound webhook set too, each gets its own message for the same moment, under its own id.
  - Every event is on by default; `{"events": {"run.needs_input": false}}` turns one off, and the API token may change events.
  - Delivery is the outbound webhook's outbox: the same retries, one message per moment, deliveries at `GET /v2/settings/slack/deliveries`, redelivery and a test send (`POST /v2/settings/slack/test`). Slack's `404` or `410` (`no_service`, `channel_not_found`, `channel_is_archived`) turns Slack off with Slack's word until a URL is saved again; a test or redelivery is then `409 slack_off`.
  - Only `https://hooks.slack.com/services/...` is taken.
- `GET /v2/capabilities` lists the switches only the operator sets at the server's start, under `switches`: `AGENTRUN_MCP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK`, `AGENTRUN_WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_TARGETS`, `AGENTRUN_BOX_ALLOW` and `AGENTRUN_BOX_CPUS`, `_MEMORY` and `_PIDS`, each with `on`, the `value` the server read (never a secret) and what it `allows`. A refusal one of them causes now names the variable, the value that allows it and the restart it takes, with the same error code as before: a webhook URL on a private network or this machine (`PUT /v2/settings/webhook`, 422 `input_invalid`) says `...which this server does not send to; restart the server with AGENTRUN_WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_TARGETS=1 to allow it, only on a machine you alone use`, and so does a try's log entry; an MCP server on loopback says `restart the server with AGENTRUN_MCP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK=1 to allow it, only on a machine you alone use.` in place of `set ... when starting the server, ...`; a computer that needs a network under `AGENTRUN_BOX_ALLOW=none` says `restart the server with AGENTRUN_BOX_ALLOW set to a host list`. A client that matched the old words should match the error code, which is unchanged. The switches stay environment-only: no route or console page sets them. The README has a table of them ([start-time switches](https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun/blob/main/packages/serve/README.md#start-time-switches)). `agentrun service install --env` also takes `AGENTRUN_MCP_ALLOW_LOOPBACK=1` and `AGENTRUN_WEBHOOK_PRIVATE_TARGETS=1`, keeps them through restarts, upgrades and later installs as it keeps a local model's variables, and `KEY=` removes one; a switch at any value other than `1` is refused, since the server would read it as off. <!-- changes/start-switches-named.md -->
- The server now sends anonymous usage counts ([docs/telemetry.md](https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun/blob/main/docs/telemetry.md)): `server_started` from its second start, a `heartbeat` every 24 hours, and `first_run_completed` once per data directory. Each holds a random id made for the data directory, the version, the platform (`os`, `arch`, Node's major version) and how many runs ended there as a range: never prompts, files, keys, names, paths or addresses. <!-- changes/telemetry-on.md -->
  - The first start that can send prints a notice on stderr and sends nothing until its first heartbeat a day later. A first run that completes before then is said with that heartbeat or at the next start, so the notice comes before anything leaves.
  - Turn it off with `AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY=0` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` where the server starts. It is already off in CI (`CI` set), under a test runner (`node --test`), under `--faux`, and in every command but the server's start.
  - `agentrun service install` writes `AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY` or `DO_NOT_TRACK` from the shell it runs in into the service, which never sees that shell, and `AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY=0` under CI. `--env` takes both names, and `--env KEY=` removes one. The installer's `--vps` writes them into `/opt/agentrun/.env` the same way: a value set where it runs replaces the line `.env` has, so running it again with `AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY=0` turns the counts off.
  - `AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY=debug` prints each event on stderr in the form it would be sent, sends none and writes nothing.
  - Events go to `telemetry.agentrun.ai`, PostHog's managed proxy under this project's own name, and land in a PostHog project on its US cloud that holds these counts and nothing else. The project is set to discard the sender's address, and its location lookup is off.
- The console's trigger forms (schedule, webhook, GitHub, app and feed) and a trigger's page warn when the trigger's agent has a tool whose permission is ask and the agent's approvals are not "never": "A run from this trigger stops and waits for you when it calls <tools>." A schedule's warning adds "later firings are skipped while it waits". On a server with accounts off, where no one can approve a call, it says instead that each such call is refused. The warning offers one fix, Run unattended, which saves a new revision of that agent with `approvals: "never"` on the revision the page read (its ETag), as the agent editor saves one. The tools named are those `GET /v2/agents/{id}` lists with `permission: "ask"`; the server's defaults and the gate are unchanged. A workflow agent, which has no approvals to set, is never warned about, and a failed read of the agent shows no warning. <!-- changes/trigger-ask-tools-warning.md -->
- `@parcha/agentrun-harness-acp`, the adapter that runs an Agent Client Protocol agent as a harness (Goose's among them), is no longer held: the next release publishes it, after the kernel and before the server. `@parcha/agentrun-serve` now depends on it, so a server installed from npm has the Goose row: its owner installs Goose's pinned binary with `agentrun-serve install-harness goose --data <dir>`, restarts the server, and Goose is offered. The package's archive holds `dist`, Goose's recipe (`recipes/goose.json`), the README, LICENSE and NOTICE; `scripts/verify-packages.mjs` imports its root and `./facts` in the clean consumer and reads the recipe from the installed package. <!-- changes/unhold-harness-acp.md -->
- The outbound webhook's signing secret can be rotated for the same URL: `POST /v2/settings/webhook/secret`, and Rotate secret in the console's Settings → Webhook, which asks first and then shows the new secret once, in the same box a save shows it in, with Copy secret, and moves the focus to it. It is a secret write, so only the owner's signed-in session may make it; the API token gets the same 403 as every other secret write, and the secret is kept. The old secret is retired at once: every try after the rotation is signed with the new one, a message queued before it included, so the receiver needs the new secret before its next message. `404` when no webhook is set; `422` for any body. A `PUT` with the API token now tells the person to rotate the secret in the console, in place of removing the webhook and saving it again. <!-- changes/webhook-rotate-secret.md -->
