- A follow-up to a Codex or Claude Code run a person stopped while a tool call ran is now the run's next turn. Before, the run first finished the stopped turn without the message, then answered the follow-up as one more turn. <!-- changes/cli-stop-follow-up-settles-cut-turn.md -->
- Only a schedule trigger's run is handed its trigger's last completed `result.output`. A Composio, GitHub or webhook trigger's run no longer is, as an email's or a feed's already wasn't: each of their firings is a different event, so one sender's answer was reaching the next sender's run. A source opts in with its adapter's `previousResult: true`. <!-- changes/composio-no-previous-result.md -->
- `PUT /settings/mcp-servers/{name}/composio` takes an action slug of at most 128 characters: a longer one is `422 input_invalid` with reason `invalid` under `tools` (and `maxLength: 128` in the schema), before Composio is asked anything, in place of a `not_found` that named it by its first 64 characters and its length. A slug the toolkit doesn't list is still `422` `not_found`, now with a guess only when it is a listed slug in another case ("linear_list_issues (did you mean LINEAR_LIST_ISSUES?)"); a slug a letter or a `_WORD` off is named without one. <!-- changes/composio-slug-bound.md -->
- The agent editor's Computer step keeps image, persistent, GPU, surface, exec and record across a switch of kind or provider where the new pick can take them; the kind's card names each one it drops. Before, any switch dropped all of them but record. <!-- changes/console-computer-fields-kept.md -->
- A workflow run's Graph names a map's item by the head of its label when the label is text. Before, a label with a slash in it showed only what came after its last slash: a release note that ended "Send event queries to /v2/events instead." read "events instead.". A file's path or a page's URL still shows as its name alone (`invoices/2026/acme-march.pdf` reads `acme-march`), and the cell's hover still gives the whole label. <!-- changes/console-graph-item-name.md -->
- The OpenAPI document requires what this server always sends: an agent's `kind`, `revision`, `revisions` and `archived_at` on every agent answer (a read, a list's, a create's and an edit's), and `harnesses` in `GET /v2/capabilities`. The generated TypeScript and Python client types follow. The console reads its agent and capabilities types from the generated ones instead of its own hand-written copies, so a capabilities `models.source` of `managed` or `env` and a save warning's `reason` are typed as the server sends them. <!-- changes/console-served-type-aliases.md -->
- console: two fixes to the run page's Dev tools tab. <!-- changes/dev-tools-panel-width-cache-finding.md -->
  - With a call's panel open, the calls table no longer scrolls sideways. Beside the panel the table showed its time axis and its Size column from a window 1536 px wide, where it had 740 px and needed some 900, so the tab scrolled sideways until the window was some 1700 px wide. The two columns now show by the width the table has: the time axis from 896 px, Size from 1024 px. Where the panel is under the table (a window under 1280 px), a table wider than its box still scrolls in that box, and the tab no longer scrolls sideways with it.
  - "A request read nothing from cache" no longer names a subagent's first request. A subagent is a conversation of its own, so its first request reads nothing by design. A request is now compared only with earlier requests of its own conversation. A workflow run's trace does not say which requests share a conversation, so the finding is left out there.
- `agentrun harness-check`'s `tools_off` stage passes when the agent's first model request reached the provider. The model proxy refuses a request that offers a tool its policy does not allow, so the check no longer applies Goose's tool rule a second time, and the report drops `proxyAllows`; the agent's tools that are not AgentRun's are still listed (`notOurs`), and the proxy's refusals beside them (`proxyRefusals`). The variables the adapter and the model proxy set in the agent's environment are one list, by part (inherited from the host, reserved for the private HOME, the proxy's), which the recipe loader refuses and the check's `env_allowlist` expects. <!-- changes/harness-check-one-variable-list.md -->
- `agentrun harness-check`'s gate refuses every call that is the agent's own (`acp_<kind>`), as a server's gate does, so a call of AgentRun's tool whose title the adapter can't tie fails `mcp_tool` instead of passing; the report's `gate.asked` and `denied_call` drop `about` and `askedAs`. <!-- changes/harness-check-untied-title.md -->
- `import` says what it is doing and what it did. On a terminal it shows one progress line (looking for sessions, checking them for keys, importing N of M), cleared before the summary. The first Ctrl+C stops it after the session being saved, says so, prints the summary with a `Stopped: imported N sessions …; run the import again for the rest` line, and exits 130; a second Ctrl+C quits at once. A Ctrl+C that comes once the sessions are saved, while the summary is read back and printed, no longer ends the import with nothing printed: the summary is printed whole, and the exit code is 130. The summary says how many sessions this import took and into how many agents (`Imported 76 sessions into 3 of 7 agents`), or `Nothing new to import` when every session is held already, instead of `Imported into 7 agents` on a run that took nothing. With no `--port`, the last line no longer promises port 7340, which a server passes over when it is taken: it says to start the server and open the address it prints. An import refused because a running server holds the store says to stop the server first. <!-- changes/import-cli-progress-stop.md -->
- An imported session its source did not price, such as a Codex session, now reads at the model catalog's estimate the import kept for it, wherever a run's cost is shown: the run's `cost.usd` (basis `estimate`, "$0.0016 est." in the console), the runs list, its timeline's usage row ("Cost: $0.0016 est. over 2 model requests"), `GET /stats` and its analytics (the cost tile and the per-harness rows), and `GET /usage`. The run's stored cost stays unknown, a recorded cost always wins, and a session the catalog cannot price stays unknown. An imported run's usage row now says the run's own cost: a Claude Code session priced at $0.0421 read "$0 known, 4 not priced" there. <!-- changes/import-cost-estimate-read.md -->
- `import` no longer says `Stopped: … run the import again for the rest` when a Ctrl+C left nothing to import. A Ctrl+C that comes while the last session is being saved finishes that session, and the summary now says `Imported N sessions into …` as an uninterrupted import does; the exit code is still 130. A Ctrl+C with sessions left (while they are listed, checked for keys, or between two of them) reads `Stopped:` as before. <!-- changes/import-stop-line-last-session.md -->
- A command running when its sandbox is lost is no longer run a second time on the new sandbox. Before, a bash call cut by a hosted provider's delete (Daytona's `not_found` "was deleted" words) was read as "bash is not there", re-sent as `sh -c` and routed to the replacement sandbox. It then ran from the start and ended `success`, with nothing in the tool result saying so. Now the call in flight when the loss is confirmed, and any call alongside it, fails with code `gone`: `the computer <name> was lost while this call ran, and it was not run again: <the provider's words>. A new computer starts at the next call.` The next tool call starts the new sandbox as before. The bound of 2 new sandboxes a claim and the `computer_unavailable` end past it are unchanged. <!-- changes/lost-sandbox-call-not-replayed.md -->
- A schedule (or any other) trigger can now start a connected agent's runs (`native connect`, Claude Code or Codex). Before, every trigger run had to be capped in dollars, and a connected agent refuses a cap because its own CLI keeps its own limits, so a trigger on one was refused at creation without a cap and every firing was refused with one. A trigger whose target is a connected agent now needs no `max_cost_usd`, and refuses one (on the target or as the agent's default) with `422 not_allowed`. Its runs start uncapped, as a connected agent's runs started by hand already do. An `effort` on such a target is refused the same way, as the run start refuses one. Every other trigger's runs are still capped. <!-- changes/native-schedule-triggers.md -->
- A pi run's model requests that answer at about the same time are each priced at their own cost. When one turn started several `subagent` calls, the child whose answer asked first was given every child's booking and the others $0, so the run page's Timeline and Dev tools tab and `GET /v2/runs/{id}/trace` showed one request at the sum (three requests of the same tokens at $0.02163, $0.01266 and $0.04326, say) and others at $0. Each answer now reads the bookings of its own conversation's requests. The run's cost was right throughout and does not change; a run already recorded keeps the per-request figures it was written with. <!-- changes/parallel-request-costs.md -->
  The session's model proxy takes a new request header, `x-agentrun-conversation` (`CONVERSATION_HEADER`, exported from `@parcha/agentrun-kernel/host`): a client may name the conversation a request is asked in, an id-shaped label of its own. The proxy tells the host with the request (`ProxyRequest.conversation`, `ModelRequest.conversation`) and never sends the header to the provider. A request that names none is asked as before.
- A pi run that compacted its context no longer reads its cost as unknown. pi sends the compaction's summary request through the run's model port, which marks the request and books it at its price, but pi stores no answer for it: the summary's cost rides on the answer pi stores beside it. The Timeline's usage row counted the summary as a request cut with no answer, so it read `usd: null` with `unpriced` equal to the number of compactions. Every reader built on that row read the same: a running run's `cost.usd` on `GET /v2/runs/{id}`, its live spend on the runs list and in `GET /v2/usage`, its `/usage` tokens meter, and the usage line on its run page. pi's compaction entry now answers that summary request. The row reads the run's priced total and counts the summary as a request whose tokens pi did not report. A real charge of no known cost beside a compaction (a request cut with no usage) still reads `usd: null`, with `unpriced` counting it. <!-- changes/pi-compaction-summary-priced.md -->
  The cap's own reading of a run's journal (`spentFrom`, behind the runs list's live spend) is fixed the same way. Where request marks hold the cap's figure for each request, it left the summary's mark open and counted it a second time at its hold, so the spend it read was too high. No runner in this server writes such marks, and a run's cap gate reads its booking instead, so no run here was stopped early by it. A store or host whose marks hold figures read it high.
- A run whose answer a composed workflow's own quote re-pick wrote reads `workflow.repick` `found` or `missed`, no longer null. <!-- changes/repick-composed.md -->
- A server whose runners all refuse to claim (their run isolation refused, for one an `AGENTRUN_RUN_USER` the runner does not know, or the image's helper unable to switch users on the platform) now says so instead of queueing runs forever. Before, on Render with `AGENTRUN_RUN_USER` removed, a person started a run, got 202, and watched it sit `queued` for good while `/v2/health` said `ok`; the reason was only in the service's log. Now the start is 503 `runner_refused` with the runner's words and their fix (`set AGENTRUN_RUN_USER=same`), a run already queued ends `failed` with error code `runner_refused`, `GET /v2/capabilities` has the words in `runner_refused`, and `GET /v2/health` answers 200 `degraded` with its `runner` check `refused` (200, so Render's health check does not restart the service in a loop over a setting). A message to a run and a backend SDK run's start are refused the same way. Once a runner that can claim starts, it all clears. Both shapes count: the runner beside the server, and runners in processes of their own, on this host or another over one Postgres store (each runner now keeps a row in the store saying it is there). A runner in a process of its own says on that same row, under the same incarnation, where its relay takes the dials the server relays to it, so the relay's table `runner_relays` becomes `runners`, and whether a relay is there is judged on the store's clock (the database's on Postgres): a runner on another host whose clock drifts from the server's is no longer refused as not running. Postgres migration `0020_runners.sql` renames the table in place and keeps its rows. On SQLite the server's start drops `runner_relays` and makes `runners`, with no store version change: its rows are heartbeats each runner writes again within 10 s, so none is copied. Start this build's server before its runners: a runner waits until the server has done it, and a runner of an earlier build with a relay does not start against a store this build's server opened. A server with `--no-runner` and no runner started yet still queues runs for its runner to come. The failed run's error code `computer_unavailable`, served since the computer-loss end, is now in the OpenAPI document's `RunErrorCode` too. <!-- changes/runner-refused-says-so.md -->
- A runner started before its server has upgraded the store now stops with exit 3 on SQLite and Postgres alike: `The store in <place> is behind this runner: start the server first, which upgrades the store in place, then the runner.` Before, a Postgres runner said to run a runner of the server's release, and a SQLite runner exited 1 with the store's own words. `agentrun-serve import --dry-run` on such a store now says to start the server first too, not to start on a new, empty data folder. The known issue beta.45 and beta.46 shipped about this no longer applies. <!-- changes/runner-waits-for-server-upgrade.md -->
- A desktop's or phone's live viewer already open on the run page's Screen tab now hears a Take over and a Hand back made from the page's header, and drives once the person holds the computer, with no reopen. A run in a process of its own committed its hold's changes there, and the viewer, which is the runner's, never heard them: the change now goes to the runner first. <!-- changes/screen-take-over-heard.md -->
- The SDK compile prompt calls a learned workflow compiled and unchecked and no longer tells the agent to prefer it: the agent decides whether one fits under its original instructions and permissions. The client's workflow context now opens "Compiled workflows for this task (not checked):". <!-- changes/sdk-compiled-wording.md -->
- A synced folder's new sandbox, started in place of one its provider lost, no longer puts the whole folder back on the run's disk at the next changing call: the claim's sync goes on from the new sandbox's own listing. A loss that a sync finds now starts the new sandbox at the run's next call; before, that call failed on the lost one. <!-- changes/serve-synced-folder-lost-sandbox.md -->

  Two parts of the synced folder are gone. A run whose folder moves from a synced folder to an Archil mount loses the modes and links the synced claim recorded: the mount never reads sync.json. A kept synced computer whose keep lapses is deleted without a read-back, so writes made while it was parked are lost. A kept computer that holds the run's folder another way than the resuming claim is not taken back: it is let go as one of another kind or provider is.
- `agentrun import --help`, `agentrun native discover --help`, `agentrun reset-password --help` and `agentrun runner --help` print that command's own usage (and for import, what it reads and what `--dry-run` does), exit 0, and touch nothing in the data folder. Before, the launcher answered every one of them with its own three-line usage, which names none of their flags, and `agentrun-serve <command> --help` failed with "Unknown option '--help'" (exit 2). The same holds for `-h`, and for `agentrun-serve install-harness`, `validate-template` and `eval-template`. `agentrun-serve --help` now lists `native discover|connect` beside the other commands. `native` called wrong answers with that same line, and takes only the flags it names: `--base-url` (the same as `--url`) and `--json` (which changed nothing) are refused, exit 2; use `--url`. <!-- changes/server-command-help.md -->
- A server listening on every address (`--listen 0.0.0.0` or `::`) with no public URL now prints its setup link at this machine's own IPv4 addresses too, `From another machine: http://192.0.2.10:7401/setup#code=…`, after the loopback `Set up this server:` line, each time a new code is printed. Before, the only link named the loopback address, which does not open from another machine. Loopback, link-local and container-bridge addresses are left out, at most three are printed, and none are printed inside a container, whose addresses are not the ones its host publishes. The launcher passes these lines on as it does the setup line. <!-- changes/setup-link-other-machines.md -->
- A run stopped while it waited on a person (a tool call waiting for approval, a browser or desktop hand-over) reads `input_required`, `idle` and `pending` kind `stopped` from the stop's answer to its end, in `GET /v2/runs/{id}` and in its item in `GET /v2/runs`. Before, it read `working`, `working` and no `pending` for the half second or so the runner held the run to take the stop, between two reads that said stopped, so a client polling after the stop could see the run start working again. <!-- changes/stop-reads-stopped-while-taken.md -->
- The serve README and the setup skill say how to run claude-agent through an Anthropic-compatible gateway, such as LiteLLM's `/v1/messages`, with no Anthropic key: set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` to the gateway and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` to its key, or any placeholder when the gateway adds its own. The README lists what the gateway must accept (`x-api-key`, Anthropic's own model ids, the CLI's `anthropic-beta` headers) and notes that a run's spend cap holds each request at a size bound there, since Anthropic's token count is asked only on `api.anthropic.com`. <!-- changes/claude-agent-through-a-gateway.md -->
- The server README's Direct Particle-1 section records that a run's estimated cost matched Particle's own usage page <!-- changes/particle-bill-match.md -->
  (2026-11-19, one workflow run of three requests): the same token counts and the same cost. A rate limit or server
  error from Particle is still not seen live.
- The OpenAPI document now lists `403 forbidden` on the four secret writes that left it out: `DELETE /v2/agents/{agent_id}/sign-ins/{key}`, `POST /v2/settings/mcp-servers/{name}/oauth/start`, `POST /v2/integrations/github/connect` and `DELETE /v2/integrations/github`. The server already refused each one to the API token. <!-- changes/secret-writes-document-403.md -->
- A run on a computer that mounts its folder attaches again when the run is a process of its own (every runner since v0.1.0-beta.46). The run's process hands its mount check to the runner's Workspace across the run channel, where the check's read-back is a handle answered as a promise; attach compared the computer's read-back against that unawaited promise, so every such run was refused about 25 seconds in with `does not hold this run's folder at /workspace: it mounts <the right folder> ..., not undefined:/undefined in undefined`. Attach now awaits the expected read-back. <!-- changes/attach-readback-across-run-channel.md -->
- A run paused at its spend cap shows one raise form in the console. The header's Raise the cap button now takes you to <!-- changes/one-raise-box.md -->
  the form under the pause banner, where it was opening a second form above it. From the Graph and Dev tools tabs,
  which show no banner, the button opens the Timeline and goes to the form there. A working run's header still opens its own.
- The console's API playground no longer says an empty `max_cost_usd` means no cap. When the agent has a default cap, <!-- changes/playground-cap-default.md -->
  the box shows it (for example `$0.25`) and says an empty box uses it, as the agent page's run bar already did.
  With a revision picked, the box shows that revision's default cap, since a run takes the cap of the revision it runs.

## 0.1.0-beta.46 (2026-11-18)

- The agent editor's Computer step has a Recording switch for a desktop, a phone or a browser: on, it saves `computer.record: true` (a video of each run), with a note that it records everything on the screen, including what a person types after taking over and any password shown. A switch of provider, or of kind to another that records, keeps the recording on; a switch to a sandbox or to no computer turns it off and says so on that kind's card. Before, any switch dropped `record`. A server without ffmpeg refuses the save, and its words show in the Computer step. <!-- changes/console-computer-record-toggle.md -->
- console: the Dev tools tab reads as a browser's network panel does. Each row of the table carries its bar on the time axis, the overview above it is compact, and the run's six figures take one line, so more calls show at once. <!-- changes/dev-tools-network-panel.md -->
  - Zoom in, or drag across the overview, and the table lists only the calls that ran in that part of the run.
  - A call's panel has a Timing section: what it waited before it started, how long it ran, and how long the next request or call took to start.
  - The Breakdown view opens with run vitals: first answer, first tool call, largest input, most calls at once and longest pause. It also says when a request read nothing from cache after the cache was written.
  - The table is one stop for the Tab key. The arrow keys move from row to row, Enter opens a row's panel, Tab goes into it, and Escape closes it from the table or the panel and returns to the row.
  - The time axis shows under a forced-colours (contrast) theme, a failed call is striped as well as red, the smallest labels are 11px, and each run-page tab is tied to its panel for a screen reader.
- A learned workflow's check and its shadow audit compare two answers on the fields that carry the decision, not word for word. A definition's `learning` takes `agree_on`, dotted paths into the answer's JSON object (e.g. `["verdict.decision"]` or `["mcc", "riskTier"]`; 1 to 16 distinct paths, each up to 128 characters and 8 non-empty segments, kept in the order given; a bad one is a 422 under `definition.learning`): each path must resolve in both answers to equal values, and a path missing on either side disagrees. Left out, the whole answer is compared as before, and a check that agreed on none says to name the fields. The kyb template declares `verdict.decision` and inbound-lead `next_step.action`; a template's `learning` takes the same object, each path a required field of its output schema. The check record keeps `agree_on`, and its reason says "said what the agent said on mcc and riskTier"; the console's check line says "compared the whole answer" when there was none. <!-- changes/learning-agree-on.md -->
- The server README's Direct Particle-1 section records a live pass against Particle's API (2026-11-18): what it covered, <!-- changes/particle-live-pass.md -->
  and what was not seen live (a rate limit or server error, and the estimate against Particle's own bill). It replaces
  the sentence that said live validation was outstanding.
- A host that won't let the runner start a run as a user of its own (a spawn `EPERM`, as on Render) leaves the server up: the runner says why and claims no runs (`AGENTRUN_RUN_USER=same` lets it), instead of stopping the container. Any refusal of the runner's isolation does: the image's `runner` process says so once and waits, holding no claim and writing no heartbeat, until it is stopped (exit 0), and a server with its runner in its own process says so once on stderr and serves with no runner. A server whose runner refuses still serves its console and API, and its runs wait queued until the setting is fixed and the server restarts. <!-- changes/runner-isolation-refusal-stays-up.md -->
- An imported agent now runs as imported. Before, a project with no CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md was imported with empty instructions, and a Codex session's model was pinned as it was named (`openai/gpt-6.1-codex`, the Codex app's own model, which no key here reaches). Every run was refused with 409 `agent_not_runnable`. Now such a project's agent gets short instructions of the import's own ("You work on the project <name>. Your past runs are its Codex sessions, imported. …"), and a session's model is pinned only when a model catalog here lists it. Otherwise the agent runs on the server's default model for its harness, and each imported run still names the model it ran on. The import says so for each one: `model not kept: <project> (codex) ran on openai/gpt-6.1-codex, which no model catalog here lists; its agent runs on the server's default model until you pick one`. Agents imported before this change keep their revisions: set their model and instructions on the agent page, or import into a new data directory. <!-- changes/imported-agent-runs-as-imported.md -->
- Outbound webhook messages name their agent, so a receiver no longer reads the trigger or the agent back to know whose it is: `trigger.failed` adds `agent_id` and `agent_name`, and `run.ended` and `run.needs_input` add `agent_name` beside `agent_id` (the agent's id when it has no name). No field is removed or renamed, and a message still carries no run output or input (#3130). <!-- changes/webhook-payload-names-agent.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.45 (2026-11-18)

**Breaking:**

- An agent learns two things now: its owner's corrections and its compiled workflow. Notes, learned skills, the end-of-run look-back turn and the learning grader are gone. <!-- changes/delete-notes.md -->
    - Corrections: an owner's words after a run (a grade's words, or a message after the job's first) become one line of the agent's `corrections.md`, with no model turn. Every run reads the file whole under `# Learned`. It holds at most 2048 bytes; a line that would pass the cap, or that holds a secret, a secret's shape or a hidden character, is refused whole and the run's learning says why. `GET /v2/agents/{agent_id}/learning/corrections` reads it with its ETag, and `PUT` replaces it whole under `If-Match` (CLI: `agentrun learning corrections`, `agentrun learning write-corrections`; client: `learning.corrections`, `learning.writeCorrections`).
    - The compiled workflow is committed as soon as its checks and dry run pass, with no grader: its one promotion check against the agent's own answers decides whether it serves.
    - A grade's `feedback` round is `correction` (was `look_back`). The run's learning carries `corrections` (lines added) and `workflows`; `given`, `read`, `learned`, `pending` notes and the grader's `verdict` are gone, and so are the `proposed` state and the `unparsed`, `propose_failed`, `grader`, `grade_failed` and `reflect_timeout` reasons.
    - Removed routes: `GET .../learning/notes`, `PUT .../learning/files/{file}`, `POST .../learning/workflows/{name}/promote`, the learning batches and the learning evals. `GET .../learning` answers `{agent, main, corrections, workflows, log, counts, impact}`. `approve`, `retire` and `restore` act on a workflow's `README.md`.
    - Removed server options: `--learning-budget` (`AGENTRUN_SERVE_LEARNING_BUDGET`) and `--grade-model` (`AGENTRUN_SERVE_GRADE_MODEL`); `capabilities.learning.grade_model` is gone. A definition's `learning: "notes"` is refused.
    - A native source (Claude Code or Codex, local or through the connector) is handed no learned skills and runs no grader turn: the connector's remote `grade` command is gone. A native target's `capabilities.notes` and `capabilities.skills` are one `capabilities.learning`: whether its runs may learn.
    - Upgrading: read a native target's `capabilities.learning` in place of `notes` and `skills`; move what an agent should always follow into its `corrections.md` (one `- ` line each) with the PUT (JS client: `learning.notes` and `learning.write` are now `learning.corrections` and `learning.writeCorrections`; Python client: `learning.notes` and `learning.write` are now `learning.corrections` and `learning.write_corrections`), and stop reading `learning/notes`, a run's `given`/`read`/`learned`/`pending`/`verdict`, and `feedback: "look_back"`. Existing notes and learned skills on an agent's `main` are no longer served; delete the flags above from your start command.
- The Learning tab tells one story: one run numbering, one takeover, one cheaper ratio and one figure for what learning costs a run, each read from the server once. <!-- changes/learning-tab-one-story.md -->
    - `GET /agents/{id}/learning/cost` numbers the runs that do a job as the bill does: a run's `n` is its job's number and a replay run's is null (it does no job). `summary.takeover` is the bill's `promoted` run, the first run a learned workflow served, alone or handed back, found by its place in the series, never by a start time two queued runs can share. Each run has `digest`, the workflow revision that ran it (null for the agent's own), `took_over`, true on the first run its revision served (over every run, `limit` aside: where a promotion's flag stands), and `audited`, whether an audit's shadow run checked it, in place of `learned_revision` (the learning folder's commit, which moved with every audit). The CSV has `digest` and `audited` columns. `bill.learning_usd` is what learning booked beyond the jobs' own cost, and `bill.revisions[].served` counts every run a revision served, not only the ones that carry its spend.
    - `GET /agents/{id}/learning`'s `impact` sides are `runs` and `median_duration_s` only: `median_cost_usd`, `cost_runs` and `median_learning_usd` are gone. What a run costs is the cost read's all-in `summary.before` and `summary.after` (a median of the job's own cost left learning out and said a second ratio, -86% beside 2.0x cheaper), and what learning itself costs a run is the bill's `learning_usd` over its runs, which counts the audits' shadow runs and replays a median of mostly-zero rows read as $0.
    - The console's Learning tab: the cost chart, its table and markers number jobs only (the replays between two jobs are spread across the gap, unnumbered, each hovered on its own), and the takeover line is its P marker's line, the P on the run the server marks `took_over`; the cheaper stage says the chart's ratio ("7.7x cheaper", never "About 8x"); the "Since it learned" card has no cost of a run of its own; answer times show to a tenth under 10 seconds, with the change of the times shown; "Learning itself" is the bill's figure a run, booked; the levels and the bill's end labels sit in a gutter right of the plot, off the lines; the bill's dollar axis tops out just above its largest figure; an audited row says so in the table; the audit card counts the audited runs the ledger has not scored yet; and the captions say compile turn and audit shadow run, not look-back, grade or notes.
    - Upgrading: read a cost run's `digest`, `took_over` and `audited` instead of `learned_revision`, allow a null `n` on a replay run, read a run's cost before and after learning from the cost read's `summary` instead of `impact`'s `median_cost_usd`, and what learning costs a run from `bill.learning_usd` instead of `impact.after.median_learning_usd`.
- The container image's default command now starts the server and its runner as two processes, so a busy runner's journal writes no longer hold up the API's reads. The command is `server-and-runner --data /data --listen 0.0.0.0 --port 7340 --drain-timeout 6s`: the server with `--no-runner`, and one runner on the same data once the server answers `GET /v2/health`, with the server's `--faux`, `--faux-browser`, `--max-runs` and each `--harness-module` (a runner takes `--faux-browser` now, with `--faux`, as the server does). `render.yaml` and the Railway template run that command too. A `docker stop` reaches both, and if either exits, the other stops and the container exits non-zero. <!-- changes/run-list-rows-image-two-processes.md -->
  Who breaks: an operator who gives the image server options of their own (`docker run IMAGE --data /data --port 7340`) still gets one process with the runner inside it. Put `server-and-runner` before those options to get the two processes. `runner ...` and the other commands run as before.
  A paired computer needs the runner in the server's process: an operator who uses one gives the image the server's options alone, without `server-and-runner`. On a server started with `--no-runner` (the image's default included), the pairing code, the pair answer and each paired computer in `GET /v2/computers` carry `runs_refused`, which says no run there can use it and gives that fix; the console shows it with the code and on the computer's row. A run that names such a computer is refused in the same words. So is a run on a provider whose machines dial the server (Fly Machines and Cloudflare): a runner in a process of its own has no socket to take them, and its create refuses naming the same fix. Such a server says it before any run: each dial provider's row in `GET /v2/computers` carries `runs_refused` (every provider row has the field, null where runs can use it), the console shows it on the row, and the provider's test (`POST /v2/computers/{provider}/test`, the console's Test connection) fails in those words with no call to the vendor. The computer package says whether a provider's machines dial from its descriptor (`connect`, read by `connectOf(descriptor, options)`), the same answer its host's `facts.connect` gives; `connectOf` replaces the internal `hosted/values` helper of that name.

  - `GET /v2/runs` (and an agent's runs) reads each run's listing from its row: the status filter, the order, the limit and the cursor are one query, so a list costs the same at 10 runs and at thousands, however long their journals. Each item is what `GET /v2/runs/{id}` gives for the run, as before. The SQLite store goes from version 11 to 12 and Postgres takes migration 0017. The server brings the store up at its first start; a runner refuses a version 11 store until the server has. After the upgrade the server builds each run's listing in the background, runs no runner holds first; a list that reaches a run not built yet builds it then.
- `GET /settings/tool-keys` (`listToolKeys`) names a key row's harnesses by harness id: `items[].harnesses` is an array of strings (a harness id, `HARNESS_ID_PATTERN`), no longer of the four built-in names, since a harness its owner installs (`goose`) is named there once it is installed. The TypeScript client's and the console's types say `string[]`, and so does the Python client. <!-- changes/tool-keys-harnesses-ids.md -->
  Upgrading: a caller that switched over the four names (`pi`, `claude-agent`, `codex`, `opencode`) handles any other id too, for example by showing it as given.
- `GET /v2/agents/{id}/learning` says of each workflow whether it serves: `workflows[].status` is `serving`, `checking`, `held` or `stopped` (the state `GET .../learning/promotions` gives it, from the same records; one with no promotion record yet reads `checking`; a champion the cost rule stopped running first reads `stopped` in both, never `serving`), else `pending` or `retired` as its README.md says. `active` is gone: a reader that tested `status === "active"` for a workflow given to runs tests that it is neither `pending` nor `retired`. <!-- changes/learning-view-status.md -->

**Changes:**

- `DELETE /v2/agents/{id}` deletes an agent another system owns (one an inline run made with `external`), whole, and answers 204. <!-- changes/agent-delete.md -->
  - The order is fixed. First the agent refuses new runs, and that refusal is stored, so a run POST, a message that would start a run, a trigger firing, a schedule and an SDK run are all refused (409 `agent_not_runnable`, "being deleted"); then its runs and learning runs are cancelled and waited on until each is final. Then its learning is deleted: every file of its learning folder, then its promotions and grades. While learning work is in flight that delete refuses, and the DELETE answers 409 `learning_busy`, naming the work in `details.runs`, with the agent left refusing runs. Last, its triggers, sign-ins, own computer, disk, folders, kept idempotent answers, runs (journal, launch records, channel posts, changes) and revisions are deleted, then the agent.
  - Nothing the agent owns elsewhere is left behind: a trigger's registration upstream, a saved sign-in at its vendor, its own computer and its Archil disk are each deleted there before the record here that names them. While one is not (the vendor or Archil failing, or Archil turned off on this server with a disk still stored on the agent), the DELETE answers 503 `unavailable` (retryable) with the agent kept and refusing runs.
  - A run whose launch named an Archil disk (`archil_disk`, the caller's) kept its folder there: that folder is deleted on the disk before the run's launch record, and the disk and everything else on it are kept; a disk Archil says is gone has nothing left to delete. While Archil refuses (a computer still holds the folder, Archil is not reached or is off), the DELETE answers 503 the same way.
  - From the first step the agent also takes no new trigger, not even one made off (Composio registers those too), no trigger moved to it or turned on, and no write to its home or its learning (a home file's write or delete, a corrections.md edit, a learned workflow's approve, retire or restore, a run's grade, a replay): each is 409 `agent_not_runnable`. Such a write sent while a DELETE runs waits for it, then finds the agent gone (404), so none lands after the learning went. A trigger that reached it anyway keeps the agent (503 `unavailable`) until the next DELETE removes that trigger upstream and here. A kept idempotent answer whose removal failed to save is removed by the next DELETE, and a request still at work under its key when the DELETE removed its run keeps no answer, so a key never replays a deleted run, a restart included.
  - A trigger's adapter settings (a webhook's secret, a poll's cursor) are removed before its row, on this delete and on `DELETE /v2/triggers/{id}`, so a failure between the two leaves the trigger for the next DELETE to find.
  - Sending the DELETE again finishes the job after a crash at any step; once it has finished, the agent is 404.
  - An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) serves it too, for the backend that made the agent.
  - An agent made here is never deleted: 409 `agent_not_external`, pointing at `POST /v2/agents/{id}/archive`. A run that cannot be ended from here answers 409 `runs_in_flight` (retryable).
  - Shared things stay: MCP servers, sealed keys, paired computers, tokens and uploaded files.
  - The clients gain `deleteAgent` (TypeScript and Python) and `agentrun agents delete-agent`.
- The runner now writes a warn line when a paid model request bills more input than the bound its spend-cap hold was priced on: the one way a cap can be passed, a hold that was too small. <!-- changes/cap-bound-warn.md -->

  The line is `event=cap_hold_short`, in the same logfmt shape as the server's other log lines, written to stderr once for each such request as its answer is booked: by an agent's run, by a workflow run's model nodes (harness `workflow`), and for a request that answered after its run's claim was lost, by the booking that writes it later. It carries the run id, the request's session and turn, the harness, the model, the bound and the billed input in tokens (input, cache reads and cache writes together), and in USD what was held, what the answer billed and the shortfall (billed less held) when the answer was priced.

  No line is written for a request billed at or under its bound, for one whose answer reported no usage, for one billed to a ChatGPT plan or on a free model (held at $0 whatever its input), or for one with no hold (no cap). The line carries ids and figures only: never any prompt or answer text, header, key or token. Billing, holds and refusals are unchanged.
- The console's Settings → Model keys has the row "Use Claude Code's login on this machine". Off, it asks where the login is (AgentRun's own by default, this machine's `~/.claude` by choice) and for the owner's word that only they run agents on the server. On, it shows the account and plan the CLI reports, or the command that signs the CLI in, plus a button that starts the CLI's own sign-in when the console is on the server's machine. A server that refuses the mode shows its one-line reason, and a server with the mode switched off shows no row. A run on the login reads "On your Claude plan" with no dollars. The Anthropic key's row says which Claude plans include monthly API credits. <!-- changes/claude-code-login-console.md -->
- A self-hosted server one person runs can run Claude Agent on that person's Claude plan through the Claude Code CLI's own login on the same machine: `PUT /v2/settings/claude-login` with `only_me: true` turns it on, and the CLI keeps the login and calls Anthropic itself. AgentRun only asks the CLI `claude auth status`; it never reads, stores or relays the login. A run on it gets no model key, endpoint or proxy, books its tokens and no dollars (`cost.plan.on: "claude_code"`), and fails in words when the login is signed out. A server where more than one person can start runs refuses the mode. It exists only on a server that listens on loopback: one bound to `0.0.0.0` or another address has it off by default. `AGENTRUN_CLAUDE_CODE_LOGIN=off` removes it anywhere, routes and all, and `on` allows it past loopback. <!-- changes/claude-code-login.md -->
- The server and the runner make every computer provider's vendor call through the standard `HTTPS_PROXY` (or `HTTP_PROXY`), with `NO_PROXY`'s hosts, loopback and the server's own public address direct: fetch and WebSocket providers through Node's own proxy support, Modal and boxd through gRPC's `grpc_proxy`, E2B through its SDK's `proxy` option, and Morph's SSH gateway through a CONNECT tunnel. Unset, nothing changes. Archil's SDK takes no proxy, so the Archil mount still connects direct. <!-- changes/computer-https-proxy.md -->
- `curl -fsSL https://agentrun.ai/install | sh -s -- --vps` sets up AgentRun on a Linux server you rent (Ubuntu or Debian, as root), with a shell for its agents in Docker sandboxes. It runs the release's published image (`ghcr.io/parcha-ai/agentrun-server:v<version>`, the server the launcher depends on) with Docker Compose in `/opt/agentrun`, and gives it the server's Docker socket. It prints the address, the setup link with its code, and the line that reads the code again later. <!-- changes/installer-vps.md -->
  - Docker: one already on the server is used as it is (Docker Engine 26 or later with the compose plugin) and never changed. With none, the installer installs Docker Engine and the compose plugin from Docker's apt repository.
  - `/opt/agentrun/.env` (mode 600) holds `AGENTRUN_TOKEN` and `AGENTRUN_SEAL_KEY`, made once with `openssl rand` and kept on every later run, with the lines you add, which reach the server too. `compose.yaml` is written again on every run; a `compose.override.yaml` of your own stays. Running it again upgrades to the release it names. `--version V` picks a release and `--image IMAGE` names an image.
  - Private by default. With Tailscale logged in, AgentRun is served on your tailnet only, through `tailscale serve` and never Funnel, by the same step as `--tailscale`, run in the server's image. Without Tailscale it listens on the server's loopback, and the installer prints the steps to add Tailscale and exits 0; it never installs Tailscale or logs in. `--public` listens on every address, port 7340, over plain HTTP, and says what that exposes first. If the first visit would not ask for the setup code, the installer stops the server.
  - `lib/tailscale.mjs serve` takes the place of the setup code's line as a fifth argument.
  - Server: under `--faux`, a server whose own environment names `AGENTRUN_SERVE_FAUX_MOUNTINFO` hands it to the runner it starts beside it, so a test server in a container runs Docker sandboxes as the real one does.
- Run Particle-1 directly on Pi with `particle/particle-1` and `PARTICLE_API_KEY`, available in Settings → Model keys <!-- changes/particle-direct-provider.md -->
  and the model picker. Keys use provider-scoped custody. Native streaming tools, reasoning continuation and cache
  affinity travel through Pi's local proxy; existing OpenRouter support and its text-tools workaround remain separate.

  Token accounting distinguishes cached input and includes reasoning in output once. Costs use regular peak list-price
  estimates, not Particle's account bill. Missing or malformed usage fails with unknown cost; cancellation and errors
  do not silently resend a paid request. Pi claims with a Particle route disable automatic conversation retries,
  including mixed-provider claims with a Particle subagent tier.

  The direct route supports Pi and workflow model nodes (including nested learned workflows). Side calls inherit
  the live port's model metadata; calls with no conversation ID use route-local cache affinity. HTTP Responses gateways
  and CLI harnesses are unsupported; configuring Particle as `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL` is refused with setup instructions.
  Live validation requires a key and explicit spend authorization; see the server README's Direct Particle-1 section.

  The Compose files (`compose.yaml`, `deploy/compose.yaml`) pass `PARTICLE_API_KEY` through to the server.
- Each run is a process of its own under its runner, and in the image a user of its own; `GET /v2/capabilities` says which as `run_isolation` (`"uid"` or `"process"`). <!-- changes/run-process-and-user-of-its-own.md -->
    - The run's process is handed its own keys on a pipe and a channel to its runner. Over the channel it reads and writes its journal, under the runner's fence, and the store's rows of its own run and agent, each call checked against its claim. What the seal key opens for the run, the runner opens and hands over; the seal key, the API token and the store's URL stay in the runner. A run's own model key (`model_key`) is opened by its runner, at its claim and for each message that hands one; a run that holds one is handed none of the server's model keys. A frame past 32 MiB, or one that is no message of the channel, fails the run.
    - In the image, slot `s` of a runner runs as uid and gid `1001 + s`, through `agentrun-runas` (root:node `0750`, file capabilities `cap_setuid`, `cap_setgid`, `cap_setpcap`): its slot's group alone, no capability, `no_new_privs`. The data directory is `0711` (the Railway template's start command sets its volume so too) and the store's files `0600`. At a run's end every process of its uid is killed and its files in `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/dev/shm`, `/run/lock` (`/var/lock`) and `/dev/mqueue` are removed (SysV IPC objects are not), and its runner sweeps the run's scratch folder, its temporary folder with it.
    - A platform that strips file capabilities or sets `no-new-privileges` makes the runner refuse to claim, in words naming the setting; `AGENTRUN_RUN_USER=same` runs every run as the runner's own user instead, said on its log. Runners in containers of their own on one `/data` volume take slots from an `AGENTRUN_RUN_SLOT_FIRST` of their own (`deploy/compose.yaml`: 0 and 128); a runner told to hold more runs than the slots from its first to 255 refuses to start, and each run's slot is locked on the volume (`run-slots`) until its reap, so runners whose ranges overlap never run two runs as one user.
    - What a run's process is handed is bound to its claim: a GitHub token only for its own pull request's repository, contents read; decision and tier model keys only for the learned workflows its runner chose for it; of the settings, the server's shared configuration and its own run's and agent's rows; its runner's live address with a proof key of its own run alone. Its uploads and opening message are placed by its runner before it starts, and the learning its end takes (a check's replays, a promotion) is its runner's. A slot is reaped before its first run too, and a reap that does not hold retires the slot. The server started with its runner beside it in one process (the image's default) runs each run as a process of its own. A run that runs no agent's code on the runner stays in the runner's process: a learning run, an SDK backend run (its agent runs in the caller's application) and a native run (its agent is the source machine's own sign-in). So does a workflow run on a server started with `--documents` (its reads and pages are rooted in a folder the server's user alone reads, and its nodes run the server's own tools alone). Where each run is a user of its own, a `claude-agent` run on Claude Code's login on this machine, with no `model_key` of its own, is refused at its claim: it fails in words naming the login and `AGENTRUN_RUN_USER=same`, which runs every run as the server's own user and lets such a run go on the login. A run handed its own `model_key` runs on that key, as a process of its own. An installed harness (`claude-agent`, `codex`) is readable by every user and writable by none, one installed before this release too. A computer made for a run is let go by its runner at the run's end even when the run's process never let it go.
    - A local install has no helper: each run is a process of its own as the user who started the server (`run_isolation: "process"`).
- A run's trace: `GET /v2/runs/{id}/trace` serves each model request that answered and each tool call of a run as one span, and the console's run page has a Dev tools tab that reads it. Use it to see where a run's time and money went and why a call failed. <!-- changes/run-trace-dev-tools.md -->
  - A span has its kind, its name (the model or the tool), when it started and ended, how it ended, and the span it ran under. A model request also has its tokens (input not read from cache, cache read, cache write, output, and thinking tokens where reported), and its cost. A tool call also has the head of its arguments and of its output, as the Timeline shows them, and what was charged under it (a browser session's time, a paid tool's fee), or that its tool has no price set.
  - The trace says only what the run's record keeps, in `model_requests`: `priced` (each request has its cost), `tokens_only` (a workflow run: its model nodes' requests carry tokens and no cost, since the cost is booked for the run, and each of its decisions is a span with its own cost), or `not_recorded` (a CLI harness's record keeps no request, so the trace is its tool calls). A computer's own time is billed by its provider and is in no span. One read serves the run's first 2,000 spans and counts the rest in `dropped`.
  - The Dev tools tab shows the run's totals, every request and call on one time axis and in one table (filter by kind or words, sort by duration, size or cost, zoom the axis), and a panel for the span you open: its tokens by line and the share read from cache, its cost, the request that called it and the calls it made, and a call's arguments and result. Its Breakdown view says what stands out (what failed, the slowest call, the most expensive request), where the time and the cost went, each request's input and cost in order, and the same by model and by tool. Export JSON saves the trace as served.
  - The TypeScript client has `runs.trace(runId)`, the Python client the same operation, and the CLI `agentrun runs trace RUN_ID`.
- In Mode 2, a sandbox or desktop whose provider takes no Archil mount here, or whose image has no Archil client, now holds the run's folder as a synced folder instead of being refused: hosted Daytona (no `DAYTONA_ARCHIL_EGRESS`), a Daytona sandbox with an egress but no `AGENTRUN_DAYTONA_SNAPSHOT`, and Daytona's and Modal's GPU computers. The runner keeps the folder on the run's Archil disk as it does today, pushes it into the computer's `/workspace` when the run claims it, and lands each change on the disk before the call that made it answers. <!-- changes/serve-synced-folder.md -->
  - A folder over 20000 entries or 2 GiB refuses the claim before anything is rented, in words naming its size and the cap. A change the disk refuses fails its call with "`<method>` ran, but the run's folder could not be made durable: ...", and is sent again at the next change.
  - The folder's modes and links are kept beside it, in `runs/<run>/sync.json`, since the disk's file API keeps neither. A run synced before and claimed again on an Archil mount (its provider now takes one) has them put back over the mount before any tool runs.
  - A park lands the folder's changes before the computer is kept, and keeps nothing if they don't land. A kept computer attached again by a new runner is read back whole, as is one whose keep runs out on the runner that parked it, before it is deleted. A computer kept holding the folder another way (an Archil mount, a bind) is deleted, not taken back. A claim that doesn't take a kept synced computer back ends it, or waits for its end already under way, before it reads the folder, so no old write lands after a new one. At release a final sync runs before the computer goes; if it fails, the release says "writes since the last sync may be lost".
  - A provider whose machines dial this server (Modal, E2B or Daytona with its connect setting on `dial`) holds the folder as a synced folder in Mode 2 instead of an Archil mount its check refuses.
  - The claim reads each provider as the run's start does (the keys that turn on its mounts, and whether its image is named here), so it holds the folder the start said it would.
  - Conformance: `mount.sync-durable`, `mount.sync-push`, `mount.sync-delete` and `mount.sync-cap` check a provider's synced folder (need `mount:sync`). `FolderSync.adopt(held)` starts a sync of a folder whose copy in the computer may be newer than the sink's.
- Applying a template again can update the agent it made instead of making a second one. `POST /v2/templates/{name}/apply` takes an optional `agent_id`: the apply writes a new revision of that agent, answered 200 with the same id, and its runs and its learning (corrections and workflows) stay. The parameters and grants are checked as a fresh apply checks them. Its triggers are matched by name: one the agent has is changed in place (a feed trigger keeps the items it has seen, a webhook trigger keeps its secret, and one the owner turned off stays off; a trigger setting its new version leaves out, `catchup_window_s` or `max_active_runs`, goes back to its default, as a fresh apply would make it; a source the new version leaves as it was is not rewritten, so a schedule keeps its next time, and an every-N-seconds one with no `start_at` keeps the grid its first apply set), a new one is made, and one the package made or kept and no longer lists is removed. Each trigger now records which template package made it, which no API body can set and which moving the trigger to another agent clears: a trigger the owner added, one moved in from another agent, and one made before this release are left alone, and a removal that fails is done by the next apply. A Composio trigger an update removes goes at Composio first: if Composio does not delete its instance, the trigger is kept here as it was (on or off, its config sealed) and the next update removes it; a dropped one is named in the answer's `warnings` with what is left at Composio. Updates of two agents at once that remove triggers sharing one Composio instance delete it with the last of them. A trigger moved to another agent while an update runs is neither changed nor removed. A trigger without that record that has the name of one of the package's triggers (the owner's, or one an apply made before this release) is taken over only when it can be changed in place, and is the package's from then on. If it would have to be removed and made again (another kind, or another Composio server, event or config), or another template package made it, the update is refused with 409 `name_taken` under `triggers.<i>.name` before anything changes: rename or delete that trigger, then apply again. A Composio trigger whose config seals a key from a parameter keeps it sealed when the update sends the same key; a different key, or another server, event or config, makes it again, as a change of source kind does: the old trigger and its Composio instance are removed first, and the new one stays off if the owner had turned the old one off. If Composio does not delete the old instance, the new one is not made, the old trigger is kept as it was, and the apply answers 424 `upstream_failed`; the next apply, once Composio deletes it, makes the new one off where the owner had turned the old one off. A source the package leaves as it was is compared with its defaults filled in, so a feed whose package gives no `every_s` is not polled again by an update that leaves it alone. What the package sets and its new version leaves out (an input or answer schema, a checkout, a default cost cap, learning) is removed from the agent; the harness, computer and sdk references the host set are kept, and an agent in the box keeps the shell tools a fresh apply gave it when the package names none. The store gains a nullable `triggers.template_id` column: SQLite adds it when the server opens the store (a runner waits for the server), and Postgres adds it in a new migration. Two updates of one agent run one after the other, and an update whose read of the agent went stale before it wrote (an edit, or an update on another server) answers 412 `precondition_failed` with nothing changed. An agent not made from that template is refused with 422 under `agent_id`, saying where it came from, and an unknown id is 404. A fresh apply of a template whose same parameters already made a live agent still makes one, with a `duplicate` warning naming that agent. The agent keeps only a keyed digest of the parameters it was applied with, never the parameters. In the console, a template that already made an agent shows "Update <agent>" next to Apply. <!-- changes/template-apply-update.md -->
- The Composio preset reads a toolkit's actions at its latest version, and a save refuses an action Composio doesn't list before it makes anything there. <!-- changes/composio-save-slug-check.md -->
  - `POST /settings/mcp-servers/composio/tools` asks Composio for `toolkit_versions=latest`. Without it Composio lists the toolkit's base version, which leaves out actions added since (on 2026-11-18 Linear listed 21 of 48 and Stripe 33 of 435), so the picker didn't offer actions templates use, such as `LINEAR_LIST_ISSUES_BY_TEAM_ID`.
  - `PUT /settings/mcp-servers/{name}/composio` reads the same list, every page, before it makes an auth config, an MCP server or a connect link. A slug that isn't on it is `422 input_invalid` with reason `not_found` under `tools`, naming each such slug and the likely one when it is obvious ("ad (did you mean add?)"; a slug past 128 characters by its first 64 and its length), and nothing is made at Composio. `not_served`, for an action Composio allows but its server leaves out, is unchanged.
- The console's run timeline reads a link in a step's one-line preview as its words: an answer whose first line has `[example.com](https://example.com)` shows "example.com", and `<https://…>` shows the address. Opened, the answer still shows the link as a link. <!-- changes/console-answer-links-picker-description.md -->
  - Every picker in a console form is described by its field's note and error, so a screen reader says them with the picker (the agent's Model field's refusal, for one). Before, only text fields were.
- The console's Dev tools tab no longer scrolls the whole page on its Breakdown view. The switch beside the per-request chart has hidden radio inputs that were positioned against the page instead of the tab's own scrolling section, so on a long breakdown the page grew a second scrollbar and showed empty space under the message box. The tab's scrolling panes now hold their own out-of-flow content, and only the section scrolls. <!-- changes/dev-tools-breakdown-scroll.md -->
- A held computer's run released before its owner started it now always ends cancelled with its agent never run. Before, a release that reached the runner just as it took up the run (after the hold began waiting, before the runner's wait for the start) was missed: the agent ran and the run ended as a plain completion. <!-- changes/held-release-before-start.md -->
- The console's API playground names an agent's model with the agent editor's Model picker, in both "POST · Create an agent" and "PUT · Edit agent": the models the server offers for the form's harness, the server default first and Custom... last, the free-text box only once Custom... is picked. A model the harness can't run is refused at the field in the editor's words. In both the playground and the editor, what the server said of a model shows at the field only while the form names the harness and model it was said of: a switch of harness hides it, an answer that arrives after the switch included. <!-- changes/playground-agent-model-picker.md -->
- A server started while the one it replaces is still closing its store no longer exits with "database is locked". Its check for an earlier version's store read the store file before taking the owner lock, with no wait, so a read that landed during the old server's last checkpoint failed and the new server exited 1. The check now waits for that lock as long as the store's own connection does (10 s by default). <!-- changes/replace-waits-on-closing-store.md -->
- SDK compile asks are held to the run's cap. <!-- changes/sdk-ask-cap-hold.md -->

  A backend SDK run's end-of-run compile ask is judged by the run's cap before it leaves, as every other paid step is: on the run's whole spend (the job its backend reported and every ask before it) and at its whole output bound. One that would pass the cap is not sent and books nothing; its learning is dropped as "Skipped: no budget left in this run to write what it learned.", and the run keeps the job's cost and outcome. Its requests on free models now count toward the run's limit of them (`AGENTRUN_FREE_MODEL_REQUESTS`).
- A synced folder keeps its links and modes when the run moves off an Archil mount, and a runner that lost its claim can no longer write the run's folder. <!-- changes/serve-synced-folder-reverse-fence.md -->
  - A run whose folder was on an Archil mount and whose next claim syncs it (Daytona's `DAYTONA_ARCHIL_EGRESS` removed, or a provider moved to connect `dial`) now finds its links and modes there. Before, the claim failed on a link an exec made (`read "go": 501`), and every file came back at 0644. An Archil computer's park and release record the folder's modes and links in `runs/<run>/sync.json` (read through computerd, which sees the mount, for at most a minute), and the synced claim pushes them, then removes the exec-made link objects from the disk.
  - Every write a claim makes to the run's folder on the disk (each put, mkdir, remove and sync.json write) first reads the run's row from the store. Once a later claim has taken the run, whether it still holds it or has ended, the write is refused and never sent: "this runner no longer holds the run's claim, so its write to the run's folder was not sent". Before, a runner whose run was claimed by another went on writing the folder.
  - `FolderSync.recordMeta()` writes a folder's modes and links, as the computer lists them, to its sink, and nothing else.
- A run a person stops no longer reads as waiting on them with nothing to answer. Before, for up to half a second after the runner cut the turn and before it ended the run stopped, `GET /runs/{id}` could read `input_required` and `idle` with nothing pending. Now a stop that is accepted and not yet applied reads stopped as soon as nothing in the run is working: at once for a run waiting on an approval, a person or a browser, and from the turn's cut for a run mid-request (until then it reads working, so its cost is never the known sum while the cut request is still unbooked). <!-- changes/stop-reads-stopped-at-once.md -->

  While the stop is not yet applied, every tool call still waiting for approval reads withdrawn in the timeline, as an answer sent then is already refused with `withdrawn`. The `run.needs_input` webhook tells the stop once, after the run's end, as before.
- Goose is a harness in serve's table (`goose`), run by `gooseAdapter` on the host's Anthropic Messages provider, the same origin and key claude-agent's proxy takes, priced and capped by the same hooks. Its owner installs it with `agentrun harness install goose` (`agentrun-serve install-harness goose`), never a run: nothing on a run's path downloads anything. <!-- changes/goose-install-and-harness-row.md -->
  - The install downloads the pinned archive for this platform (`GOOSE_PIN`) with node's fetch, checks its sha256 before unpacking, unpacks it with the system `tar -xjf` (a fixed argument list, no shell) into a fresh folder beside `<data>/harnesses/goose`, checks the binary's sha256, then renames the folder into place and makes it read-only. A crash part way leaves the old folder or none, and the next install sweeps what it left. Every failure is named (`HARNESS_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED`, `HARNESS_DOWNLOAD_FAILED`, `HARNESS_ARCHIVE_MISMATCH`, `HARNESS_UNPACK_FAILED`, `HARNESS_BINARY_MISMATCH`, `HARNESS_INSTALL_BUSY`) with the command to try again. Run again with the pinned binary in place, it downloads nothing. No provider key reaches it.
  - Capabilities list Goose (label, its promises `resume: load`, `tool_gate: permission`, `billing: proxy`) only once the pinned binary is installed and verified, read at AgentRun's start: restart AgentRun after installing it. Before then an agent on goose saves with a warning, and its run is refused (`agent_not_runnable`), each naming `HARNESS_NOT_INSTALLED` and the install command.
  - `@parcha/agentrun-harness-acp` exports Goose's facts (`gooseFacts`), its install command (`GOOSE_INSTALL`) and its code (`GOOSE_NOT_INSTALLED`). The package is held from npm for now, so a serve installed from npm has no goose row until it ships.
- A provider whose machines dial the server (Fly Machines, Cloudflare, and E2B, Daytona or Modal set to dial) now works under a runner in a process of its own, the image's default `server-and-runner` included. The server stays the one public address: a machine dials its `/v2/computers/attach` as before, and the server relays the socket to the runner that made the machine. Give the runner the server's public address (`AGENTRUN_PUBLIC_URL`, as the server reads it; the image passes the environment to both); across hosts, give it `AGENTRUN_RUNNER_LIVE_HOST` and list that host in the server's `AGENTRUN_RUNNER_HOSTS`, as for a run's live computer view. Nothing changes on the machine. <!-- changes/dial-relay.md -->
  The runner mints each machine's token into the shared store with its name and incarnation on the token's row, and serves its own attach hub on a private listener (loopback beside its server, its live host across hosts). The server opens a socket to that listener with a proof under the seal key that binds the token, the runner, its incarnation and a time within 10 seconds, taken once: the listener answers nothing without it, and takes only a token its own runner minted in this incarnation. The relayed socket keeps the server's attach limits (frame size, binary refusal, idle timeout), and a close on either side closes the other. A dial whose runner is gone, does not answer or restarted since is answered 503 in words that name its run, `a dial for run <run> (machine <machine>)`, and never its token; the server's log line says the same, and the run makes a new machine at its next claim. The server keeps those words on the token's row, and the runner's create, waiting for the machine to dial, ends at once in them (`the server refused a dial for run <run> (machine <machine>): ...`) instead of waiting out its create timeout; the machine is deleted. `MachineTokens` gains `refused(machine)`, which a hosted provider's dial wait reads. A hosted provider's create names the machine's run in its token's mint (`MachineMint.run`, from the create's `agentrun.run` label), and the token's row keeps it.
  With such a runner, each dial provider's `runs_refused` in `GET /v2/computers` is null and its test reads the vendor's account again. A runner with no public address relays nothing, and the row, the test and the runner's create keep their words.
  The SQLite store goes to version 13 at the server's first start (from 11 or 12), and Postgres takes migration 0019 (`minted_tokens.runner`, `.incarnation`, `.run` and `.refused`, and `runner_relays`). A runner refuses a version 12 store until the server has upgraded it.
  - A runner started beside its server in the image (`server-and-runner`) no longer gets the server's own API tokens (`AGENTRUN_TOKEN`, `AGENTRUN_TOKENS`, `AGENTRUN_API_KEY`); it still gets every other secret the launcher hands over.
- A webhook try's bound can be set: `Webhooks`' `timeoutMs` option, and the server's `webhookTimeoutMs` (15 s by default, as before). It is whole milliseconds, refused at zero, in part of a millisecond, or at or past the 60 s claim a try holds its message by, so no try outlives its claim. A try cut by it says the bound it had (`no answer in <n> s`). <!-- changes/webhook-try-bound-option.md -->
- A learning pi run that compacted its context two or more times now reads its stored cost on `GET /runs/{id}` and in `GET /agents/{id}/learning/cost`, instead of `cost.usd: null` beside a known figure and a count in `unknown_cost_runs`. The job's cost its learning keeps (`job_cost_usd`) is read from the run's booking by the same rule its end stores its cost by, so with no compile turn after the job it is the stored cost, and a compile turn's spend is that cost less the job's. <!-- changes/learning-job-cost-booked.md -->
- CI's store-on-Postgres job runs the database `test/pg/compose.yaml` runs locally: its data on tmpfs, `fsync` and `full_page_writes` off. With a schema per test, a checkpoint on the runner's disk synced 80k-150k files over 90-180 s, and a commit behind it went past the store's 10 s deadline. A lock wait past 1 s is now logged with its holder. <!-- changes/ci-postgres-test-database.md -->
- An API-only server (`AGENTRUN_API_ONLY=1`) now serves `GET /v2/computers` and `GET /v2/workspace/archil` with its token, so a backend in front of it can read which computer providers are ready and whether runs' folders are on Archil before it launches. Both answer key names and whether each is saved, never a value. Their writes, tests and key choices (`PUT`, `DELETE` and `POST .../test` on either, `PUT /v2/computers/{provider}/keys`, `GET /v2/computers/{provider}/choices`) are still refused there. <!-- changes/api-only-computer-reads.md -->
- A Linux box with no display pairs with `computerd pair` as a sandbox, and in Mode 2 holds a run's folder as a synced folder in its `/workspace`: serve pushes the folder in at the claim, syncs each change back before the call that made it answers and once more at release, all through the claim's epoch fence, and the next run on the box finds its folder. Its network is `open`; any other is refused. Mode 1 runs a sandbox only on Docker, as before. <!-- changes/paired-linux-sandbox.md -->
  - `/workspace` is a directory of computerd's user's own, mode 0700, never a link, made once as root with the tmpfiles.d line in spec/computer/attach.md (`d /workspace 0700 <user> <user> -`). A claim refuses a box whose `/workspace` is missing, a link, not a directory, another user's or open to others, in words naming that fix, and lets the box go. Each claim first ends every program an earlier run left running there and empties it of that run's files.
  - The synced folder writes only under `/workspace` and never through a link: init extracts the push opening each name `O_NOFOLLOW`.
  - `attachedProvider` gives a Linux box daemon `child`, `mount: ["sync"]` and no vendor agent ports, and reads its folder back as `{ kind: "sync", epoch }`.
  - A desktop or a phone named as a sandbox computer is refused saying only a Linux box paired with no display can be one.
- The fake calendar (`startIcsFaux`, which calendar tests and a template's eval read) counts the requests for its own paths only: the calendars it serves, the paths it moves and their targets. A request for any other path is answered 404 and not counted, so a host process that polls every loopback listener (GET /) no longer fails a test that counts the calendar's reads. <!-- changes/ics-faux-own-paths.md -->

## 0.1.0-beta.44 (2026-11-17)

- A run can bring its own model key, such as a LiteLLM virtual key minted for it: `model_key` on `POST /v2/runs`, `POST /v2/agents/{agent_id}/runs` and `POST /v2/runs/{run_id}/messages`. Every model request tied to the run carries it in place of the server's key, through the model proxy: its turns, subagents, learned workflows' nodes, workflow model nodes and end-of-run look-back. AgentRun never mints, lists or revokes it.
  - Custody follows `mcp_auth`: taken out of the body first, sealed with the run bound to the gateway's origin, opened at each claim (a reclaim after a crash too), erased by the write that ends the turn, redacted, and never seen by the harness, its tools or its sandbox. A message's key replaces the run's from the turn it starts.
  - No setting: a server with a gateway (`AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL`) and no model key of its own starts and reads ready, and its callers bring their own. A run whose model goes to the gateway with no key to spend is 422 `model_key_required` at its start, as is a message that would start a new turn without one; a trigger's firing on such a server fails the same way.
  - Behavior change for a gateway that takes no key: a server with `AGENT_MODEL_BASE_URL` and no `AGENT_MODEL_API_KEY` used to send `none` as the key; its runs now need `model_key`. Set `AGENT_MODEL_API_KEY` to any value to keep the old behavior.
  - claude-agent with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` on the gateway's origin no longer needs a standing `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: it runs on the run's key.
  - `model_key` where the run's model never goes to the gateway (no gateway, a native run, a model routed elsewhere) is 422 at `model_key`.
  - Spend after a run's turn ends is never sent on the run's key or the server's: a run that brought its own key queues no learning grade (dropped `grade_failed`, in words), starts no shadow audit or replay check, and a server with no key skips them, refuses an owner's replay (409) and learning from a CSV, and opens no grade feedback round.
- A harness is one entry in serve's harness table: capabilities, a revision's save check, the runner and the console all read the table. An owner can add harnesses with a harness module. Start the server (and any separate runner) with `--harness-module MODULE` (repeatable) or `AGENTRUN_SERVE_HARNESS_MODULES` (comma-separated). MODULE is a path, or a package installed with `npm install --prefix <data>/harnesses <package>`, that exports the `entries(builtins)` shape test tables already use.

  A module adds whole entries of new ids. A module's harness runs on its own runner's adapter, and a run of it reserves the memory its entry declares (`runMib`). A module's harness without adapter facts runs pi's tools, and capabilities list it on each of those tools (`tools[].harnesses`, now ids of the table, not an enum) and on MCP grants, so an agent on it keeps its tool choices. A module that gives an id outside `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`, names an id serve's own runs carry (`learning`, `sdk`, `workflow`, `claude-agent-sdk`, `codex-sdk`) or every object already has (`constructor`), names a built-in harness (pi, claude-agent, codex, opencode), names an id another module adds, or leaves out a member refuses the start of the server or of a separate runner, naming the module and the id.

  Capabilities' `harnesses` now carry each harness's `label` and `promises`: `resume` (`exact`, `load`, `restart`), `tool_gate` (`every_call`, `permission`, `config`) and `billing` (`proxy`, `plan`). The built-in harnesses promise exact resume, every call gated, and proxy billing. A harness id in the API is now a string (pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$`), not an enum of the four built-in ones. The console offers a harness the server adds after the built-in ones, under the label the server gives it; one named `decision` stays a harness, never the Decision starter.
- An agent whose computer is a browser can record its runs: `computer: {"kind": "browser", ..., "record": true}` makes a video of each browser session's page, `recordings/<computer>.mp4` with one file per session, under the same caps, pause and stop rules as a desktop's or a phone's, listed in the run read's `recordings` and served by the files route. A browser with `record: true` was refused with 422 before.
    - The video is the live view's own CDP screencast of the session, shared with a person's viewer (one screencast per session, never a second); each frame is stamped as it comes, so a page that sits still does not shorten the video.
    - `@parcha/pi-browser`'s live view takes a host's watch of a session's frames, with or without a viewer: `liveView.watch(tag, { frame, ended })`. A viewer that joins a stream already running is sent the page, any dialog and the newest frame.
- The server can count itself, anonymously: `server_started`, a daily `heartbeat` and `first_run_completed`, each with a random id kept in the data directory, the version, the platform and how many runs ended as a range. **This release sends nothing**: the receiver's key is not set, and the release that sets it will say so. `AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY=0` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns it off, as do `CI` and `--faux`; `AGENTRUN_TELEMETRY=debug` prints each event and sends none. [docs/telemetry.md](https://github.com/Parcha-ai/agentrun/blob/main/docs/telemetry.md) lists every field.
  The start that first could send prints one notice on stderr and sends nothing at that start.
  A send never delays a start, a run or a stop; a failed one is dropped.
- On an agent's page in the console, shown side by side (1024 px and wider), the agent's name, description and id stay in place and the details under them (its facts, tools, configuration and live jobs) scroll in their own box; the workspace beside them (runs, versions, learning, analytics) scrolls by itself. The whole page scrolled before, taking the name with it. Each box's scrollbar is slim, sits in a gutter of its own beside the cards, never over their edge, and shows only while the box is being scrolled or the pointer is on the bar; an edge the content goes on past fades out. The name, description and id take at most half the column: a description longer than that scrolls in a box of its own between the name and the id, so the details under them can always be reached.
